in writing. the fight against all forms of discrimination has always been at the heart of my various commitments, including my political commitment. but the defense of the family and freedom of conscience also. i voted against the lunacek report. as a supporter of the fight against homophobia, i have regretted that this text, by its lack of clear definitions and therefore by the ambiguities it contained, in particular on freedom of conscience or on the mutual recognition of civil status documents between the member states of the union, weakened the noble cause it was intended to defend. subsidiarity and the sovereignty of the states were not sufficiently respected in this text, despite a paragraph at the end of it which claimed the opposite. i am not opposed to a road map at european level, of course. i am in favour of this if it defends the fight against homophobia in a measured way, without threatening in particular freedom of conscience and subsidiarity. i believe that these policies are best implemented at national, regional or local level, as close as possible to the problems encountered and in accordance with the legal traditions of each member state.
in writing. this eu roadmap against homophobia and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity , proposed by ms lunacek, defines the individual on the basis of his sexual orientation and not his biological sex in order to confer on him special rights. however, the defence of rights and freedoms is not conditional on behaviour or orientation, and there is therefore no need to create specific rights for a category of the population. this report also aims to muzzle the divergent opinions to give voice only to self-proclaimed lgbti rights defenders and gender advocates. the principle of non-discrimination at european level is being misused, as is freedom of movement, two principles which are almost dogmatic in brussels and on which the lunacek report is based. it is high time to get rid of the ideological and normative invasion of the union. with the support of the europe of freedom and democracy group, i tabled an alternative resolution to remove references to gender identity and to recall that the defence of the fundamental rights of the human person must not be sectoral or community-based .
in writing. i voted for this report, of course. the massive shielding of european ultraconservatives against this text, based on false arguments, is incomprehensible. article 10 of the lisbon treaty states that the european union is obliged to combat discrimination in the definition and implementation of its actions. however, according to a study by the european agency for fundamental rights, 47% of homosexuals in europe say they are victims of discrimination or harassment. therefore, and following the example of the european strategies for gender equality, disability and anti-discrimination against roma, this report calls on the european commission to develop a roadmap to combat homophobia. ulrike lunacek, the austrian environmental rapporteur for the text, worked closely with the other political groups and put forward a text with a broad consensus for the vote. as a member of the lgbt intergroup, i took a stand and spoke in favour of this text.
in writing. i voted against the lunacek resolution and in favour of an alternative motion because, while the fundamental rights of all citizens must be respected, i would also like to stress the need to respect the principle of subsidiarity. it considers that family and education issues are not a matter for the european union but for the member states. all forms of discrimination are of course reprehensible and must be firmly combated. however, i reject the communitarian and ideological approach to this report, which would lead to the emphasis being placed on a particular community or category of citizens. in the face of the attacks and stigmatisation of those who advocate a protective family policy, i would like to reiterate my attachment to family values and the responsibility of parents in the education of their children. in the midst of the economic crisis, our citizens expect more from europe than the production of a chain of relations which are stigmatizing and non-binding.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report which calls on the commission to draw up a roadmap against homophobia because i believe that we must put an end to the fear, isolation, harassment and discrimination which lgbti people are facing today in europe, most often with impunity. unfortunately, in our countries, we have to admit that the march towards equality is still very long and must continue because lgbti people are still too often the target of unacceptable stigmatization. suicide cases among lgbti youth are all signs that we need to act urgently to address this phenomenon. just as europe fights discrimination based on disability or ethnic origin, it is important that it also tackles discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender. while it is essential to tackle the economic and social challenges facing our continent, the role of the european parliament is also to conduct these debates in such a way as to build a european society that is faithful to the values of freedom and equality. it is high time that european texts were adapted to changing customs and promoted the universality of rights.
in writing. the economic crisis is a breeding ground for a retreat in identity and a crisis of values. history has provided us with a shocking testimony. the last few weeks have shown us how attempts to deconstruct the bedrock of values that make up a nation can exacerbate tensions. i therefore call for an urgent and necessary withdrawal. my rejection of the report on homophobia should not be seen as a denial of such discrimination. on the contrary, they exist and must be combated. however, i am convinced that this report, far from soothing the conscience, is only inciting anger and pits individuals against each other. i do not believe that individuals should be categorised according to their sexual orientation and that an identity should be reduced to that criterion alone. a peaceful debate must take place. it must not, however, be a matter of opposing one set of values to another, of destroying family values and family policy in order to impose a caricatured social pattern by force. the european parliament must continue to protect the rights of all but must never offend some to favour others.
in writing. the report on a roadmap against homophobia and discrimination was the subject of a crude disinformation campaign by the 'manifesto for all' organisations. what does this report say? a reaffirmation of the will to combat discrimination and to guarantee equal access for all to employment, health, education, goods and services, free movement, freedom of expression and assembly... the fight against discrimination is the "trade union minimum" in terms of equal rights. nothing very controversial or new (at european level, these rights are already guaranteed by the treaties (article 10 tfeu) and by the charter of fundamental rights). but today, for some movements, the mere words "homosexual" and "gender" are enough to stir up hatred and occupy the public debate, distracting attention from the real problems of society. criticism of the fight against discrimination, whatever its origin, is to call into question the very principle of equality. we are born free and equal in rights. if we have to fight this fight in 2014, we will fight it, and today and tomorrow, lies and hatred will not win.
in writing. i voted against the alternative resolution proposed by the epp to replace the own-initiative report by my colleague ulrike lunacek on the european roadmap against homophobia and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity. while the proposal improved the original text, it left ambiguous legal provisions, such as the principle of mutual recognition of the effects of civil status documents between member states or the mutual recognition of registered partnerships or marriage for same-sex couples. i can only regret that the noble objective which justified this report, namely the fight against homophobia and any other discrimination based on sexual orientation, has been diverted for partisan purposes in an attempt to open the way to a questioning of policies which are exclusively within national competence. although not binding, this text could be used to influence national debates that have nothing to do with the fight against homophobia. the alternative resolution was adopted by 394 votes to 176, with 72 abstentions. i'm sorry about that.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which will help to strengthen the fight against discrimination which still affects lgbt people in large numbers across europe. with the vote on this resolution, we ask that the european union finally adopt an action plan to combat homophobia and transphobia, in the same way as it already fights discrimination on grounds of sex, disability or ethnic origin, while respecting the principle of subsidiarity, as provided for in paragraph 5. i also want to support this report because a retrograde wave is currently blowing across europe to challenge the fundamental rights acquired by both women and lgbt people, by organising intensive disinformation campaigns. it is essential to be mobilised and not to give in to this rise in conservatism and extremism across europe.
in writing. i voted against this text, as did almost all my colleagues from the ump in parliament. the reason for this choice was that, in this text, under the guise of combating discriminatory behaviour which still occurs today in the european union and which is unacceptable, the rapporteur wished to introduce provisions which trample on the sovereignty of states in areas of civil law which are absolutely not within the competence of the eu. i voted in favour of an 'alternative resolution', which unfortunately was not approved by the full house, calling for all eu citizens to be able to enjoy their fundamental rights fully, including the right not to be discriminated against.
in writing. i strongly condemn any discrimination, including on grounds of sexual orientation. article 10 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union states that the union shall endeavour to combat all forms of discrimination in its policies. however, i cannot support the request that a member state recognise civil acts, such as same-sex marriage, entered into in another member state, even though it does not recognise them in its own legislation. the issue of same-sex marriage is a sensitive subject which must be left to the discretion of each member state, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. i cannot support the promotion of any kind of sex education in the european commission's programmes for young people. the issue of sex education must be approached with great vigilance and above all the central role of the family must be recognised.
in writing. given the reactionary climate, this text is welcome. it gives a fairly comprehensive overview of all areas of homophobic and transphobic discrimination, and represents a breakthrough for many european countries. however, it is regrettable that there is no mention of equal access to ldc for lesbian couples. finally, although the report is mainly concerned with negative rights to non-discrimination, it places the fight against homophobia and transphobia in a universalist framework. i vote for it.
in writing. the european union is committed to combating all forms of discrimination in its policies. this is a fundamental principle which must be safeguarded at all costs. it is absolutely unacceptable that many people are discriminated against in the member states of the union because of their sexual orientation. however, each member state is able, under the principle of subsidiarity, to create its own legislation to remedy this problem. the european parliament has a duty to ensure that the european parliament is not undermined by the council's decision. i voted against this report because it supports ideas on family law, such as the european promotion of sex education, and this right is a matter for the member states. it is not incompatible to protect european citizens from discrimination and to safeguard the sovereignty of the member states in certain matters.
in writing. in order to promote a republican approach to the issue, there is an important balance to be struck between the defence of the family and the various forms of discrimination based on sex, sexual orientation and gender identity. all homophobic behaviour and discrimination must be firmly condemned, but we must not forget the traditional family model which is one of the pillars of our society. the lunacek report does not in any way correspond to our view of this balance. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. i voted against the joint resolution which took up the main elements of the lunacek report and called for the development of a 'roadmap against homophobia and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity'. while i strongly condemn any discrimination based on sexual orientation, i did not wish to support this report, some of the passages of which were outside the competence of the european union. the text required each member state to recognise civil acts concluded in another member state, even if they were not recognised in its own territory. civil status and family law are sensitive subjects which fall within the sphere of national sovereignty.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the fight against homophobia because discrimination against lgbt people (lesbian, gay, bi and transgender) is still very much present in the european union. according to a recent study by the human rights agency, one in two lgbt people have been discriminated against or harassed and one in four have been physically assaulted because of their sexual orientation. this report calls for a new eu action plan to combat homophobia, in the same way that the eu already fights discrimination based on sex, disability or ethnic origin. it also respects the principle of subsidiarity on family law and does not require member states to adopt legislation on registered partnerships, marriage or adoption. these decisions are the responsibility of the member states' authorities and there is obviously no question of the european union interfering in this area!
in writing. i voted in favour of the lunacek report. this report has been the subject of a vast campaign of disinformation from the most reactionary fringes of our societies. this text is an opportunity to reaffirm our opposition to all forms of discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex people in europe and around the world, whether in the field of employment, education, health, access to goods and services or freedom of movement and expression. we cannot tolerate crimes and hate speech against our fellow citizens. this is a non-binding own-initiative report which recommends that member states coordinate their policies to combat discrimination against lgbti people. it reminds us that the road to equality is still long and that all member states must make progress along this path. i deeply regret that the ump voted against this text. it is a very bad signal in view of the current situation in some member states and the international situation, and it is also a further blow to the values of respect and equality which weakens the wall between the republican right and the extreme right.
in writing. the european union must lead by example on lgbti rights: this is the signal that the european parliament has sent today by adopting this roadmap against homophobia and discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity. we need to do more to eliminate discrimination against lgbti people in europe: just as the european union is fighting discrimination based on disability or ethnic origin, it is important that it also tackles discrimination based on sexual orientation, and this is the main thrust of this report. lgbti people are still too often discriminated against in the labour market, in schools and in the health sector. the report calls for existing laws against discrimination and violence to be systematically applied throughout the union in order to ensure freedom of movement without any unrest. i regret that too many members have succumbed to the pressure of the fallacious arguments of conservative lobbies.
in writing. i deplore the very principle of this vote, which gives easy angles of attack to europe's opponents to make citizens believe that the european union is no longer useful. i have always fought against discrimination based on sexual orientation, as the european charter of human rights proclaims. my negative vote is therefore not an objection to those who want to fight these practices of another age, but a warning to make it clear that if the eu continues to want to take care of everything, it will end up taking care of nothing! it is high time that the role of each individual was redefined and that it was made clear that social issues such as family policy and sex education are the responsibility of the states alone. what message are we sending when we spend hours debating a hypothetical roadmap, while europeans expect us to provide solutions to the consequences of the crisis, to increasingly porous borders and to an environment threatened by climate change? we expect europe to deliver concrete results and not to be the scene of a clash over cultural values.
in writing. this report calls for better enforcement of the rules applicable to protect citizens against unfair commercial practices, which are a scourge and a real danger to citizens. the european union must therefore act to reduce this risk, including by taking into account new developments on the internet. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the application of the unfair commercial practices directive to promote cross-border trade and consumer confidence by combating misleading advertising and unfair practices in business-to-consumer ('b2c') relationships across all sectors and by ensuring that consumers are properly informed to make informed choices.
in writing. i voted in favour of the rochefort report for an amendment to the directive on unfair business practices. the new challenges facing the union, due to the development of new technologies, require improvements to this directive. i am in favour of effective and genuinely dissuasive sanctions for companies that engage in this kind of practice.
in writing. this text rightly begins an assessment of the application of legislation on unfair commercial practices in the member states. the importance of this legislation in ensuring consumer protection and consumer confidence in the internal market is underlined. if this legislation appears to be adequate, improvements in its implementation are nevertheless possible. more effective and dissuasive sanctions to prevent unfair trading practices should indeed be encouraged within member states. the penalties imposed for non-compliance with eu law should therefore never be less than the benefit derived from a practice considered unfair or misleading.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report to combat misleading advertising and other unfair practices affecting consumers. the european parliament recalls that consumers continue to be victims of many misleading practices, for example on websites selling airline tickets. for example, there is a surcharge applied to credit and debit cards when booking online. in addition, there are many complaints from users of online ticketing sites who have been victims of what is commonly known as 'ip tracking', a practice which aims to keep track of the number of connections a user has made via the same ip address and then artificially raise the prices of a property based on the interest shown by several similar searches. the european commission must urgently investigate the frequency of this practice, which creates unfair competition and constitutes a misuse of users' personal data. the report also calls on the member states to redouble their efforts in this respect and stresses the need for closer cooperation between national authorities within the framework of the consumer protection cooperation network.
in writing. in line with its commitment to consumers, parliament approved the report on the fight against unfair commercial practices in the european union. the legislation came into force in 2005, but the deadlines for transposition in the member states were not always met, so the european commission could only make a first assessment of its effectiveness in 2013. the aim is to promote cross-border trade and to encourage consumer confidence by combating misleading advertising and unfair practices in business-to-consumer relations and ensuring that consumers are properly informed. the legislation applies to unfair commercial practices from the stage of advertising and marketing, but also during and after the commercial transaction. although some shortcomings were noted, i am pleased that, overall, this first inventory was conclusive. the aim now is to better control 'hidden' advertising practices on the internet, which are very concretely characterised by the manipulation of professionals posing as consumers on forums and social networks, and to ensure effective, fast and inexpensive redress for deceived consumers.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague robert rochefort on the implementation of the unfair commercial practices directive (2005/29/ec). the report stresses the need for full application and proper implementation of the directive by the member states. it also called for the strengthening of surveillance operations, the imposition of appropriate sanctions against companies and the regular updating of the european commission's guidelines. the hidden advertising on the internet is also taken into account, as is the need to strengthen the application of the directive to vulnerable consumers, to emphasise the importance for consumers of effective, fast and inexpensive redress and to adopt a cross-cutting framework for class actions. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of an own-initiative report on the application of the misleading commercial practices directive, which recalls the urgency of implementing all its measures to protect consumers from certain unscrupulous or even completely fraudulent sellers and traders. parliament stressed in particular the new fraudulent practices on the internet, but also the issues related to false declarations about the environmental quality of products.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the evaluation of the application of the unfair commercial practices directive. progress is possible in the application of this directive adopted in 2005, which had to be transposed from 2007. it is therefore necessary that appropriate penalties are applied to undertakings, as provided for in the directive, where consumers are misled or exposed to aggressive marketing.
in writing. this report, which has no legal standing, commends the european commission for its implementation of the 2005 directive on the fight against unfair and deceptive trading practices. for the future, the text expresses moving intentions that range from pious wishes ("to make businesses aware of consumer rights") to charitable incantations ("to take better account of vulnerable people"). it is entirely consistent with the logic of intensifying trade and publicity. it therefore pays no attention to relocating production and encouraging short supply chains, which are fundamental levers for integrating the ecological imperative into trade that today has no boundaries. taxation and reduction of advertising are also not part of the recommendations of this report, which is part of the pure productivist and consumerist logic of the current european union. the report will therefore bring no real improvement to consumers, workers and citizens. i vote against it.
in writing. directive 2005/29/ec aims to protect consumers from unfair business practices and to increase consumer confidence in transactions in the internal market, while ensuring greater legal certainty for businesses. the provisions of the current directive are satisfactory and no major revision was necessary, but it is essential that member states implement it fully and apply it correctly. however, even if member states implement the directive fully and correctly, full compliance by businesses will only be more effective if prevention is strengthened and if they clearly see the prospect of being sanctioned in the event of infringement. i voted in favour of this report because i found in it these broad lines which i believe are essential.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which aims to establish a benchmark for the judiciary and to contribute to the development of national judicial systems by enhancing their quality, efficiency and independence. it deals only with civil and commercial matters, since these are closely linked to the economy. it collects data from member states and evaluates it to help member states improve their justice systems.
in writing. i voted for the report on the eu justice scoreboard which is an important report for european justice.
in writing. this comparative table provides reliable data on the judicial systems of the member states of the european union. this will in particular enable exchanges of good practice between member states for a more independent and efficient judiciary. the achievement of this objective will strengthen the confidence of european citizens in their judicial system. it is rightly emphasised that an efficient and trustworthy judicial system encourages businesses to develop and invest at national and international levels. legal certainty is therefore inseparable from the recovery of competitiveness and employment in europe.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which takes stock of the european judicial systems for the year 2013. on the basis of these conclusions, several options are preferred for the coming year, starting with reducing the length of procedures, in order to improve the operating environment for companies and thus make it more attractive to investors. in addition, ongoing training of judges is essential as national legislation is changing rapidly as a result of european legislation. all these measures are part of a genuine european judicial area, which i can only encourage.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report which follows the publication by the european commission of a justice scoreboard, a non-binding comparison tool for assessing the effectiveness of national justice systems in the areas of civil, commercial and administrative justice. this tool is important for enhancing the quality of national justice systems and contributing to improving the business and investment climate within the eu.
in writing. this report supports the european commission's proposal to create a reliable tool for comparing national legal systems. it aggregates quantitative as well as qualitative statistical data to enable better assessment of each country's improvements and setbacks. the aim is not to rank but to understand each other's systems. a better understanding of complex crossborder cases, in particular, would be very useful for many of our citizens who are increasingly faced with them. however, some of the rapporteur's main points are very vague and indicate a view with which i totally disagree. thus, legal systems should contribute to economic growth and stimulate competitiveness . the introduction of liberal mantras spoils this report which should have remained scientific in nature. i'll hold off.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which welcomes the paradigm shift in the way regions produce and consume energy. it also highlights the opportunities that geographical (or territorial) changes bring to the energy network of disadvantaged regions and invites member states and regions to invest in local smart grids through the european structural and investment funds. the deployment of smart grids requires a stable long-term policy framework and this is the call of this report.

in writing. i welcome the adoption of this resolution on the implementation of smart electricity grids. these networks are tools that ensure better coordination between energy production and consumption systems in order to optimise costs. the modernisation of the electricity grid has become essential for the distribution of energy from renewable sources. these technologies are therefore a major asset in meeting today's energy challenges. they also represent an undeniable potential for growth and innovation for all the countries of the union. i welcome the fact that my amendment on raising awareness among users to become producers-consumers aware of the possibilities offered by these networks has been adopted in the final text.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague elisabeth schroedter on the local and regional consequences of the implementation of smart grids. the report welcomes the change in energy production and consumption patterns in the regions and calls on member states to invest in local smart grids to meet future energy needs. the report was adopted by a large majority, with 571 votes in favour, 87 against and 22 abstentions, which i welcome.
in writing. smart grids are based on decentralised energy production and consumption models and enable a stable and secure energy supply. the report before us proposes to strengthen these mechanisms. it is regrettable that these good intentions are reflected in an increased use of individual consumer responsibility, whereas the objectives pursued (reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, stable supply, etc.) are collective. moreover, the apology for public-private partnerships prevents me from supporting this text. the naivete of green capitalists is affecting ecological progress. for these reasons, i vote against.
in writing. the european economy needs local and regional energy initiatives to become increasingly self-sufficient in this area. for some time now, we have seen the creation of smart grids for renewable energy, which have the potential to create sustainable development and jobs. i voted in favour of this report as it stands. although environmental protection is very important, we should not be deceived into setting binding environmental standards that are not achievable for most member states. it is true that such developments as smart grids must be supported, but it must be borne in mind that the european energy sectors must move closer to these objectives without losing their competitiveness vis-à-vis the rest of the world.
in writing. - the eu member states have few energy reserves of their own and therefore import more than half of their energy consumption (54.1% in 2010). so the price of energy that we pay every day depends on the situation in the world market or on the demand of the exporting country, and we have no other way to pay it. the only way to reduce costs at present is to reduce consumption and increase energy production within the eu. the eu is already implementing several successful pilot projects in which local communities and citizens have become productive consumers. this means that they produce energy for their own use by selling part of it to the grid or by receiving a discount for the additional electricity consumed using net accounting. the development of smart grids and virtual power stations, which provide for flexible supply and could store small amounts of electricity produced from renewable energy sources, is necessary to establish such a two-way system. the resolution stresses that the implementation of smart grids should draw on the resources of the european structural and investment funds by establishing partnerships with entrepreneurs at local, regional and national level. the network would help consumers to adapt their consumption to their needs, saving energy, improving energy efficiency, reducing peak hours, etc. this would reduce energy costs for businesses and increase consumer purchasing power. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. i abstained on the very technical own-initiative report on the local and regional consequences of the development of so-called smart electricity grids. while i can only support a more sustainable approach to electricity consumption, this report has not gone in the right direction. it stresses competition and proposes to develop, as usual, public-private partnerships. he emphasises the role that regions could play in becoming electricity producers. this is not in itself a bad thing, but it may lead to a disengagement of the states, which is already well advanced, by liberalizing public network services. there are still considerable uncertainties about the use of 'smart meters' which are supposed to 'advise the user on his consumption'. the user must be assured that the personal data transmitted will be protected and must not be obliged to provide such data in exchange for services. finally, installation costs must not be passed on to the bill and the benefits in terms of consumption reduction must be real.
in writing. this own-initiative report provides a useful overview of the situation of small farms in the european union and the challenges they face. these small farms are necessary for the harmonious economic, social and territorial development of the european union. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. i voted for the report on small farms. it is aimed primarily at very small farms in the new member states from the eastern bloc. agriculture in these member states is still characterised by traditional structures and a large number of small farms. although they have been on the road to modernisation since the start of their accession process, profound differences remain. the cap reform introduced a flat-rate payment for small farms, to simplify their access to cap aid. the report welcomes the new system but considers that it does not fully address the problems facing these small farms. it therefore lists areas where the union must step up its action, in particular the fight against rural exodus and urban sprawl and the establishment of adequate financial engineering instruments.
in writing. the text calls for action to combat the depopulation of rural areas, where small farms are a real asset. the overall objective is to increase the competitiveness of these farms. this includes a proposal to mobilise the financial resources of the european funds and the necessary encouragement to support specialised production lines to enable job creation. finally, the text rightly encourages the creation of platforms for the exchange of good practice on the regulation and control of processing carried out on small farms.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which aims to rebalance the weight of small farms in the common agricultural policy. it is therefore essential that the union's cohesion policy be used to help finance small farms in rural areas and thus enable them to overcome structural problems.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it will help support the smallest farms, which play a key role in rural areas. first, it provides a clearer definition of small farms and calls for measures for small farms to be simplified and made more flexible under the common agricultural policy, in particular by facilitating access to certain aids. the text also stresses the role that the cohesion fund can play in helping to finance the infrastructure needed to set up small farms in the least populated areas. it has become urgent to tackle this problem in order to combat depopulation and rural exodus.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague czeslaw adam siekierski on the future of small farms. the report calls for better consideration of the needs of small farms in the new common agricultural policy, the preparation of post-2020 guidelines, the establishment of adequate financial engineering instruments and the fight against rural depopulation. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. this report proposes interesting ways of supporting small family farms and better taking account of their specific needs: increasing direct sales through the development of local infrastructure, mobilising 'special aid' for small farms which have opted for a cooperative structure or the sharing of agricultural equipment. he also criticised the 'insufficient' amount of aid provided for by the new cap for smallholders. it also called for the mobilisation of the european social fund and the cohesion fund and for more public subsidies to help rural development. but this report remains a prisoner of liberal europe. he calls for support for livestock but does not say a word about the abolition of milk quotas in 2015. he called for support for small farms but "without distorting competition" which is destroying them. he calls for more money for smallholders but does not criticise the reduction in the cap budget or the benefits of agribusiness. i'm not going to.
in writing. the european union introduced legislation to reform the common agricultural policy at the end of 2013. this is a major development which will ensure farmers a better future. however, it is clear that some definitions and guidelines are missing from this reform, particularly as regards small farms. i am glad that the report on this subject has been adopted. it is a good way of highlighting the particular case of small farms with profitability problems. these are usually small family farms, and there is no guarantee that they will be inherited. in the same way as we are promoting the rejuvenation of european farmers, we must support small farms to tackle the problem of rural exodus and agricultural development. the profitability of small farms must be ensured if an important element of the european agricultural model is to be maintained.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report on small farms. it is a list of good intentions with no legal value and could have been considerably improved. i supported the alternative motion for a resolution put forward by my portuguese colleague, mr joao ferreira, a member of the gue/ngl, which went in this direction. the viability and profitability of small farms must be strengthened. taking account of the agricultural characteristics of the country concerned, regional variations, encouraging the creation of cooperatives or increasing the direct sale of traditional products on local and regional markets are all measures which would reduce the pressure on small farms by giving them economic opportunities in the face of current distribution channels. in view of the guidelines of the failed cap reform, small farms must be supported and their strategic value recognised within the european agricultural model, as they are one of the pillars of rural development. it is not, however, the budgetary choices that have been made, except in a marginal way, and it is regrettable that this text is only a paved road of good intentions, the usefulness of which need not be specified on the eve of the european elections.

in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on an integrated parcel delivery market to support the growth of e-commerce in the union. for a long time, particularly when i was president of the chamber of commerce and industry of tulle and ussel, i have been convinced that e-commerce and home delivery of parcels are a distribution mode that is a good solution both for local businesses and for customers, especially in rural areas. it is important to work on building consumer confidence in the delivery process. i support the need to improve geographical coverage and accessibility to a universal parcel delivery service in rural and remote areas.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on an integrated parcel delivery market to support the growth of e-commerce. internet commerce has been growing for several years. we have to support him.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text, the main purpose of which is to adapt the parcel delivery market to the current digital age. it aims to take better account of the consumer's point of view by giving him access to information, such as delivery options and methods, which is part of a concern to modernise the it tool and to protect the consumer, which i welcome.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague pablo arias echeverria on the establishment of an integrated parcel delivery market to support the growth of e-commerce in the european union. the report aims to ensure fair working conditions in the delivery sector and accessible, affordable, efficient and high-quality delivery services. i'm very happy about the adoption.
in writing. this text contains some positive developments, such as the strengthening of the requirements for transparency but also for the reliability and safety of parcel transport (through measures to control final delivery and better attention to post-delivery services). however, all the measures envisaged in this text are only envisaged in the light of the liberal ideology of the creation of a european e-commerce market. the creation of such a market requires transport over long distances at lower cost, which is not compatible with satisfactory social and environmental standards. it leads to disasters, like the one at mory ducros. transport workers will once again see their working conditions worsen as european competition between companies deepens. the only beneficiaries of this system will be the large express transport companies. the measures envisaged to help smes in the sector are not up to the competition they face from these large companies. i am voting against this text because i do not want to encourage or endorse this sad continuation of a supply policy which denies social rights and is dragging down the whole european economy.
in writing. the economic importance of e-commerce has been widely recognised. in 2012, the european market for this sector grew by around 20% to reach some eur 250 billion, but the figures indicate that it still has significant growth potential in the european union. however, this potential can only be realised if delivery services meet the needs of online shoppers and retailers: accessible, affordable and quality delivery services throughout europe. in addition, recent studies have shown that problems with these services are one of the main reasons for not buying online. in particular, they account for nearly 70% of the abandonment of purchasing transactions. smes also express dissatisfaction with the lack of transparency, the quality of delivery services and the high costs of cross-border delivery, which they consider to be a significant obstacle to their development in the digital single market. i voted in favour of this report because it recognises that the parcel delivery market in europe is evolving rapidly, but that important obstacles remain, which risk slowing down the growth potential of european e-commerce.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which sets out an action plan for the european steel industry to help the sector meet current challenges and lay the foundations for future competitiveness by encouraging innovation and creating growth and jobs. this is the first time since the davignon plan in 1977 that the european union has proposed such an action plan. it is structured around the following main axes: ensuring an appropriate regulatory framework; facilitating restructuring and meeting skills needs; boosting demand for steel; supporting demand by improving access to foreign markets and ensuring fair conditions of competition at international level; and boosting competitiveness through appropriate energy, climate, resource and energy efficiency policies.

in writing. the steel industry in europe, and particularly in france, is in a bad shape. since the creation of the ecsc, steel has repeatedly returned to the centre of public debate, now for the wrong reasons. the industry, which employs 350,000 people directly, has lost 65,000 in recent years. there are several reasons for this. asymmetric trade agreements allow third countries that practice social, economic and environmental dumping to have unhindered access to the markets of the eu member states. another factor is the rise in energy prices in europe, mainly due to massive investments in renewable energy, and wind in particular. we are paying today for the strategic error of having put everything on services at the expense of industry, which creates wealth, and its defence. finally, the european regulatory framework, which is extremely burdensome, is putting a damper on the competitiveness of industries by making their work, innovation and investments more difficult. simplification of the regulatory framework and a return to intergovernmental cooperation would make it possible to take better account of the expectations of this indispensable industry.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it will restore the competitiveness of the european steel industry by helping the sector to face its current difficulties. the european steel industry is of key importance for many other industrial sectors that create jobs (automotive, construction, etc.). i therefore welcome the action plan proposed by the european commission to restore our steel industry to its strategic role. the report adopted today calls in particular for control of energy and regulatory costs, which are a heavy burden on the steel sector. the union must have a climate, energy and environmental policy that preserves the competitiveness of our industry and makes it possible to avoid further relocations. finally, the report intends to combat asymmetrical trade agreements by adopting a reciprocity approach and using the trade defence instrument. the european union is still too often the 'big naïve' of globalisation in trade matters, putting our companies at a competitive disadvantage.
in writing. the steel industry is essential and strategic for the european economy as it is the foundation from which other industries develop and prosper. a plan to support and revive this priority activity, which had been deeply affected by the crisis, was therefore urgently needed. how can we believe that no major action has been taken since the davignon plan of 1977?! i am glad that the european commission has finally proposed a realistic, comprehensive plan adapted to the needs of this industry. tackling high energy costs, better protecting our market against aggressive and unfair practices from third countries, training qualified personnel, research, development and innovation are the major tasks on which the european union must concentrate its efforts. the priority of the union, like that of its member states, must be to boost employment and competitiveness. the role of the union is therefore to create a framework, conditions and space favourable to the flourishing of our industries and businesses.

experiencing in the european union, and in particular in the euro area, since 2008 has provided us with valuable lessons. it is absolutely essential to move towards the banking union which will be the fundamental pillar of economic governance for both the european union and the euro area. i come from a country where i was also finance minister at the worst of the crisis and i know what it means to put into practice a bank rescue mechanism with a bail-out system and i know, from our very close experience in cyprus, what it means to put into practice a bail-in mechanism in relation to bank rescue. the market is waiting and needs the single resolution mechanism. the citizens, depositors, investors expect and need this mechanism. it is very important, given the rapporteur's creative spirit, that we complete this process, if possible, in the current parliamentary term and it is true that we do not have much time. you are aware, honourable members of the european parliament, that two serious institutional issues have arisen which we are called upon to address with full respect for the treaties governing the european union and the institutional role of the european parliament. at council level, we have to reconcile the union's competences with the reservations and sensitivities of many member states, not in relation to their legislative bodies or their governments but mainly in relation to their judiciary and more specifically their constitutional courts, and this because there are many serious budgetary obstacles to the allocation and management of the resources necessary for the functioning of the single resolution mechanism. on the other hand, we must preserve the european union's ability to put in place a mechanism which may not be perfect from the outset but which must not be subject to national judicial challenges - so we must take the first step. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a very good one. i must say that i personally understand and respect the sensitivity of the european parliament, but i respect even more the willingness of the rapporteur to overcome the problems and come up with a workable solution. i am aware, as is the council, of the case law of the court of justice of the european union in relation to the esm and i am also aware of all the problems that have arisen in relation to the legal basis. we must proceed with a method which is compatible with the requirements of the intergovernmental method but which fully respects the substantive and active involvement of parliament, we must complete the dialogue, discuss the issues of substance, find the best possible solution which is certainly a viable and financiable solution, a solution which will of course apply within the logic of the uniform treatment of banks which have the same problems and are in the same situation and, of course, of the systemic banks. in this sense, i believe that we can easily find a compromise, both on procedural and substantive issues, and arrive, with the necessary speed and if possible before the end of this parliamentary term, at the single resolution mechanism. we have the single supervisory mechanism which must prove to be effective. we need, and i will end with this, the single deposit protection mechanism, because in a single banking market higher interest rates operate and attract depositors, and this is of great importance, especially for the periphery of europe, for the countries of the south, for the countries emerging from the experience of the crisis. but the final and highest criterion for any depositor is always the safety of deposits. if there is no single deposit guarantee system there is a deep structural inequality within the banking union. i am therefore glad that this debate gives me the feeling that we are taking an important step towards a compromise and a practical solution.
member of the commission. mr president, i have noted the concern mrs giannakou has just expressed, which is also felt in many parts of europe, because of the number of natural disasters that are happening. but here we are talking about disasters that are not natural: it is the banking crisis. i therefore return to the subject, mr president, to greet the members of parliament who are here and you, mr vice-premier venizelos. the commission, ladies and gentlemen, has broadly shared parliament's aspirations on this matter from the outset. i am not just talking about the six months that have just passed since our proposal was published. long before this, since the non-legislative report presented by elisa ferreira, to whom we also wish a speedy recovery, we were already on the same page. like you, we want a fast, credible and democratic system for managing banking crises in europe. your parliament has expressed its disagreement, through the voices of its president and sharon bowles, with the organization of an intergovernmental conference on a text introduced under the ordinary legislative procedure. the commission's position on this point has been clear from the outset. article 114 is, in our view, the appropriate legal basis for the creation of the single fund. today, more than ever, i stand by that position. however, the political choice made by the council to leave the contributions to the resolution fund provided for by the brrd directive at national level is not, according to the analysis of our legal service, contrary to the treaties. it is essential, however, that the content of the intergovernmental agreement be strictly limited to the elements necessary to manage the transfer and pooling of bank contributions. all other elements, including the establishment of the fund, its governance, its tasks, the calculation of contributions and borrowing between national compartments in the transitional phase, should be laid down by a regulation adopted in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure. it would be a great concession for parliament to accept a limited intergovernmental agreement out of realism. the council, for its part, must fully recognise the role of this parliament as a co-legislator. the aim, once this principle has been established, is now, in a few weeks, to clarify the elements of an ambitious and acceptable compromise. at this stage, there are three major issues that need to be addressed together: funding, governance and the democratic accountability of the single resolution board. as regards financing, which is obviously at the heart of the debate, that is to say the setting up, as mr sánchez presedo has said, of this european fund, i propose four lines of work, if you will. firstly, the sooner we pool the national compartments, the better. i am personally in favour of a five-year pooling instead of a ten-year pooling. alternatively, if we want to maintain a unity and parallelism between the planned period for feeding the fund and the mutualisation, we could consider a period of seven years to achieve stability. in such a case, we might expect increased mutualisation at the beginning of the period. for example, instead of 15% per year over seven years, one could imagine 40% in the first year, 30% in the second, 20% in the third and 5% in the fourth and fifth years. secondly, we must strengthen cross-financing between national compartments. if a national compartment proves to be insufficient for the resolution of an institution, it shall be able to borrow from the other compartments. thirdly, at the end of the transitional period, i.e. when the fund is fully pooled, the board should be able to collect directly from all banks the necessary contributions, including ex post contributions to be raised in case of urgent funding needs. the council presents the intergovernmental agreement as a necessary tool. so, for the sake of realism, but then it must be a temporary solution that will make way for a viable solution, after the mutualisation. fourthly, we must move forward now on the question of financial support, even if it is only gradually being brought together. i think, for example, that we could explore the idea that elisa ferreira has proposed, that of a credit line as a last resort. the risk is limited, since these subsidies will only be in the form of guarantees and loans, which will be reimbursed by private money, without any impact on the taxpayer. finally, as regards financing, we must be careful not to focus the negotiations too much on the question of the fund. we must measure the reforms already achieved with you on supervision, on capitalisation and even on resolution, with the political agreement on the brrd directive. we're not in the same time as before. the guiding principle is now to lease in, not out. the use of resolution funds should therefore remain exceptional. finally, i would remind you once again that this is not public money but money collected from the private sector. i would add a few more points, mr president. we must find a viable and credible compromise on governance. when i put the proposal for a resolution on the table, i emphasized this point, without being an ideologue, but we must find ways of taking decisions quickly and effectively. financial stability and the fate of depositors are too important to be sacrificed in the name of institutional competition which would be inappropriate. resolution decisions must be motivated by technical excellence and not by considerations of national policy or institutional ego. it is in this spirit, again without being an ideologue, that i proposed that the commission be the institution responsible for pressing the button on the motion for a resolution tabled by the independent resolution authority. the council has chosen another path. the question is whether this will be an effective and credible way for the markets and for applying a resolution procedure to a bank. we're not there yet. parliament and the council have asked the commission to be creative, to design a system which is in line with the state of the case law. the court of justice's ruling a few days ago on short selling confirms the validity of the system we had originally proposed. i personally pledge to you, ladies and gentlemen, that i will do my utmost to find this creative solution. finally, the discussions should make it possible to strengthen the democratic accountability of the resolution board. we have already made clear in our proposal the principle of an independent authority, but one which is accountable to parliament for its actions. you have wanted to strengthen the democratic legitimacy of the council of resolution and i fully support parliament's view on this point. i am convinced that the council shares this objective and i hope that the discussions will lead to a satisfactory compromise. in conclusion, i believe that the following are the major challenges facing us in the trilogues which are about to begin or which are still to take place, and some of the solutions which i would like to put forward as constructive proposals. reading the greek presidency's reply to sharon bowles and what i also heard at the ecofin council, it seems to me that the council is in a state of openness and is ready to find - at any rate, i hope so - a credible compromise. the commission, for its part, is there to facilitate the search for solutions, and you can count on my help and that of all my teams and departments. we have a few weeks to come up with a deal. this is too important a subject to risk failure or too long a wait which would undermine the whole structure of the banking union. since the outbreak of the financial crisis in 2008, and even more since the start of the sovereign debt crisis in 2010, europe has been able, we have been able, the citizens have been able to measure the consequences of a certain indecision every time we have had difficulty taking the necessary measures quickly. we are in the final stretch of the banking union on the most ambitious project in recent years and our top priority in order to clean up the financial sector is to restore confidence. so it is not a matter of slacking off as we approach the result. in order to achieve this result in the coming weeks, i want to confirm the full commitment and readiness of the european commission and myself in particular.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fisheries sector is not left behind. this control regulation ensures that the rules of the common fisheries policy are respected. in its proposal, the european commission reclassifies the competences conferred under the old comitology procedure by dividing them between delegated and implementing acts. this is a very formal division, but it is worth thinking about. the criteria for allocating these powers are laid down in the treaty, but in practice we are faced with a vast grey area which requires political arbitration, which is also the prerogative of the legislator. it is often wrongly forgotten that the allocation of institutional powers in the union as redefined in lisbon is an ongoing process and that these technically-appearing alignment regulations are an extension of it. the commission proposal almost always settles on delegated acts, and we are told that since these delegated acts are subject to the ex post control of parliament, parliament retains its competence. i would urge caution, ladies and gentlemen, because parliament does not have the human resources or the procedures at present to carry out such a post-mortem check in a serious manner. without these two conditions, the spirit of the treaty will be misconstrued. we also draw the commission's attention to the opinion which parliament's legal services have given us at our request. the 'lisbonisation' procedure is indeed intended to verify the conformity of the texts with the treaty, but if this conformity concerns articles 290 and 291, it also concerns the charter of fundamental rights annexed to the treaty. i call on the commission to confirm to parliament in its future work on alignment that this legal verification has been made. i have made two points on the fisheries control regulation. the first concerns the need for uniform implementation of the regulation. this need for consistency across europe has led me to defend the commission's proposal to give priority to delegated acts so that fishermen in san benedetto del tronto, loch inver, vigo, baltimore, hull, skagen and guilvinec will not suffer any injustice, thanks to a uniformly implemented control regulation. secondly, i followed the commission and defended the idea that this was merely 'lisbonisation', or legal alignment, and not a pretext for a revision of the fisheries control regulation. this request was all the more justified since the reform of the common fisheries policy entailed a subsequent revision of the control regulation. despite the numerous requests by my colleagues for amendments to the substance, i have stuck to a list of recommendations addressed to the commission so that it takes them into account in its future control regulation. i therefore regret very much, madam commissioner, that the commission is returning to us today with a proposal which does not incorporate any of these requests. the the s&d group is therefore calling for a new directive on the safety of passengers in air transport, which is a very important one. the directive is aimed at ensuring that passengers are not subject to unreasonable restrictions on their rights to travel by air. the commission proposal made a number of improvements over the current text. i think we have succeeded in improving it, and i would like to thank our rapporteur and all my colleagues in the other groups for this result. we are proposing legislation that is actually applicable. there is no point in granting passengers very extensive rights if in practice airlines can circumvent their obligations by invoking some technical problem or if the rules are operationally unviable. we have therefore set very strict limits on the extraordinary circumstances which companies may invoke. the regulation also introduces an important new element: the right to financial compensation in the event of delay. however, we must take account of the diversity of destinations and the material constraints that arise from this, while keeping in mind the idea of a common continental airspace. we must therefore maintain the principle of the three trigger points for financial compensation. it may seem tempting to support amendments which seem to be very beneficial to consumers, but this could lead airlines - and you said it, commissioner - to simply cancel flights rather than try to meet reasonable deadlines. we must also maintain the prohibition on denied boarding in the event of non-use of the outbound or connecting flight. finally, i would like to mention a few important points: the total transparency of the displayed price, which should allow for better price comparability (including hold baggage), the authorization to take along personal effects other than cabin baggage, but also the obligation for airlines to provide contact points at airports in case of problems. all this, in my view, is a balanced text between better rights for passengers and realistic obligations for airlines, which is a good basis for discussion with the council.

on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, madam commissioner, let me first of all congratulate the european commission on its proposal and, in particular, cecilia malmström, the rapporteur, claude moraes, the fictitious rapporteur who was unable to be here today - we regret that - and all the other fictitious rapporteurs for the excellent work and compromise that has been presented to us today. i also welcome the good cooperation between all the political groups. we know that european migration policy is being developed and, in particular, the legal migration framework, which is in its infancy: the blue card, the single permit, posted workers and, today, the directive on seasonal workers. to understand better the progress of this reform, we need to ask ourselves three questions. first of all, why do we need such a directive? we are responding to a need in our economy, namely the need to use seasonal workers from third countries. every year, 100 000 seasonal workers travel to the european union to work. it is essential that the arrangements for their coming be made in a calm manner. then what do we do to maintain our ideal of justice? we guarantee these workers a fair wage and the same working conditions as european workers, because europe is not a purveyor of misery. finally, what are we doing to protect our european citizens and, in particular, their jobs? we avoid unfair competition by imposing the same pay, the same working hours, the same holidays for foreign and european workers. we allow member states to refuse the entry of seasonal workers if european workers are available. each state will thus be able to set the volumes of admission, which is essential to adapt the flow of foreign workers to the needs of each economy. we are thus giving ourselves the means of a competitive economy which can use migration according to its needs without endangering the jobs of european citizens. this is the face our migration policy must have, for a migration that is chosen and not forced. in writing. despite appearances, this text organises a labour immigration not seasonal but sustainable. because a seasonal worker who stays in europe for nine months out of the twelve and who receives social benefits, including family and unemployment benefits, as provided for in the directive, is a permanent immigrant worker. and that permanence will be compounded by your facilitation clause. i cannot be led to believe that the use of seasonal workers from third countries is motivated solely by a shortage of local labour. of the tens of millions of unemployed in the european union, many would no doubt be happy to do these jobs. but it is doubtful whether companies specialising in the importation of extra-european labour under the guise of secondment or seasonality are more efficient than official employment offices. some of them even seem to be able to receive public subsidies for job creation. if the so-called shortage is not the whole story, it is that employers, not just those who exploit the misery of others, are finding a financial interest in it. there must therefore be some possibility of social dumping.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague claude moraes setting out the conditions for entry and residence of third-country nationals for the purpose of seasonal employment. in order to prevent seasonal workers from third countries from exceeding the authorised duration of stay, a maximum duration of stay has been established. the member states will also be able to determine the volumes of admission themselves. the number of restrictions and inappropriate conditions linked to seasonal work has therefore been limited, while ensuring maximum safeguards for applicants against illegal forms of exploitation. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by 498 votes in favour, 56 against and 68 abstentions.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report and i welcome the adoption by a very large majority of a legislative act on seasonal work, a first at european level. the 100 000 seasonal workers from third countries who come to the union every year will have to have the same working conditions as european workers. this is an important step forward, as it fights unfair competition by imposing the same pay, the same working hours, the same holidays for foreign and european workers. at the same time, each member state retains the choice of the number of workers it accepts and may set a maximum duration of stay of between 5 and 9 months. the new provisions will have to be implemented by the member states within a maximum of two and a half years.
in writing. this directive on seasonal workers who are not eu nationals is the first legislative framework on legal migration for low and unskilled workers. it offers substantial advances on the wages of these workers and their right to complain. member states must provide for sanctions against fraudulent companies, and in particular subcontractors, and 'ensure that ... effective and adequate inspections are carried out' and also ensure that they do not use workers from outside the union if the need can be met by our nationals. how can labour inspectorates ensure this effectively, given the many budget cuts to their services? this report does not take account of the consequences of austerity, whose first victims are always the precarious workers, in this case foreigners, who are immediately dismissed from their jobs. however, in view of the minimum rights acquired here for seasonal workers, i shall abstain.
in writing. the problem of seasonal workers from third countries should not be confused with that of posted workers or foreign service providers. most member states currently need seasonal workers from outside the european union and a structure to manage immigration at union level could bring real added value. it should also be noted that the introduction of legal immigration channels can reduce illegal immigration and the exploitation that often follows. it is also essential that this directive should ensure very closely the equal treatment necessary on the union's labour market to ensure respect for wage and working conditions and thus to combat social dumping. i supported this report in the plenary because i think the criteria it sets are reasonable and balanced and because this directive will help to fill the current legal vacuum.
in writing. every year, around 100 000 seasonal workers come to work in the european union. i voted in favour of this directive on the immigration of these workers, with two objectives: to guarantee seasonal workers a fair deal, while ensuring that social dumping and unfair competition are prevented. the rules provide for the introduction of similar working conditions for seasonal workers and european workers (in terms of pay, working time, holidays and housing) to put an end to their exploitation. at the same time, member states remain free to determine the volume of admission and to refuse entry to foreign workers if the posts can be filled by europeans.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the conditions of entry and residence of third-country nationals for the purpose of seasonal employment. seasonal migrant workers are sometimes subjected to intolerable abuses. the european union had to respond by protecting these workers from unacceptable treatment. moreover, by bringing the treatment of migrant workers closer to that of local workers, the european parliament also protects the latter from social dumping and from a race to at least a social status. the directive requires that a person entering the union must have a firm employment contract or offer of employment in order to discourage unscrupulous employers from resorting to covert work. this text is much awaited in our territories to better regulate and protect a workforce useful to the agricultural sector in season, but it is essential that it be subject to the same rules as other employees.
in writing. i supported this text, which bans the import of atlantic bigeye tuna from bolivia, cambodia, georgia, equatorial guinea and sierra leone. this trade sanction was imposed because vessels flying the flag of these countries were declared to be fishing illegally, unregulated and unreported, whereas these species benefit from strictly controlled programmes to ensure their survival. at the same time, we have lifted the ban on tuna imports from bolivia and georgia, since the latter now comply with our law.
in writing. i voted for the report on the import of atlantic bigeye tuna. council regulation (ec) no 827/2004 prohibits the import of atlantic bigeye tuna originating in bolivia, cambodia, georgia, equatorial guinea and sierra leone. this trade sanction was declared by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (icsat) because vessels flying the flag of these countries were declared as fishing illegally, unregulated and unreported. given the current situation of tuna fishing and marketing, in particular with regard to valuable species such as bluefin tuna and bigeye tuna, the complexity of iccat measures to control fishing and marketing shows that iuu fishing is still a significant problem for tuna and related species in the atlantic. cambodia was considered by the commission in its decision of 15 november 2012 as a non-cooperating country in accordance with regulation (ec) no 1005/2008 on iuu fishing.

in writing. the text ends the ban on the import of bigeye tuna from bolivia, cambodia, equatorial guinea, sierra leone and georgia. we are making it easier for european citizens to access a rare species, while protecting consumer health and promoting sustainable fisheries. the european parliament also reaffirms its willingness to strengthen cooperation with these five countries by welcoming the progress they have made in the fight against illegal fishing.

in writing. the global craze for japanese cuisine has increased the fishing pressure on tuna. the most well-known case is that of bluefin tuna threatened by overfishing. this is a different species, the obese tuna, but the same logic. the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas, a recognised intergovernmental body, considers that the evolution of the stock allows the ban on imports of this species from bolivia and georgia to be lifted. the report follows this recommendation. so from a fisheries resource point of view, i could vote for it. i do not, however, agree with the logic of europe consuming fish caught on the other side of the world. i could therefore vote against. but why maintain the ban on bolivia and georgia, when the ban on cambodia and guinea has been lifted? a madman's way of doing it! i'm not going to.

in writing. i voted in favour of the protocol between the european union and gabon, which negotiated a new protocol to the fisheries agreement, which entered into force on 24 april 2013 for a period of three years. it offers opportunities for tuna fishing and for migratory species in gabonese waters. the reference tonnage allocated to 27 european union trawlers and 8 liners is 20 000 tonnes. in return for this fishing, the european union pays an annual compensation of eur 1 350 000, of which eur 450 000 is to be used to support gabon's fisheries policy. these financial compensations have been substantially revised upwards compared to the previous protocol which expired in 2011. both sides indicated that they would respect the recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas, which are in line with the decisions taken at european level under the common fisheries policy.
in writing. i voted in favour of the ferreira report on the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and gabon. this protocol is balanced: substantial financial gains will be derived from the opportunities that will open up for fishing and it offers significant support to gabon's small-scale fisheries policy. finally, as the report states, i support greater involvement of the european parliament in all phases of the preparation of the protocol or its renewal.

in writing. the protocol stipulates that the eu must respect scientific advice and that european vessels must only fish if there is a catch remaining: the idea is that the europeans do not profit from gabonese fish. this is a positive development, even though the protocol is very vague on the control of these commitments. above all, the union has the capacity and the space to be self-sufficient in fisheries resources. the development of semi-extensive aquaculture, which is reversible and has no significant impact on the environment, is possible. this would be more clever than going fishing off gabon, especially since the persistence of a relict requires that the gabonese do not develop their own fishing skills. it is clear that fishing off the coast of gabon is not essential for the union. the report does not propose to provide scientific support for fisheries management and logistical support for the fight against poaching. it leaves the commission free to validate changes in the quantities and species caught. i'm not going to.
