in writing. i voted in favour of modernising the eu's trade defence instruments, including anti-dumping. the objective here is twofold. first, we must adapt these instruments, which have been awaiting reform for 15 years, to the new global trade challenges, whether in terms of social, environmental and commercial dumping or counterfeiting. the commission also found that the chinese exporting producers were not able to provide the necessary information to the commission to enable it to assess the likelihood of continuation of dumping. on the other hand, we wanted to give all our many smes access to these trade defence instruments so that they could face international competition with more tools. this dossier was therefore particularly important, not to take refuge behind new barriers, but to show all our realism and our combativeness in the face of international competition which is intensifying on a global scale, with the assertion of new commercial powers such as china, brazil or india.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which emphasises the access of smes to trade defence instruments, which have been disadvantaged by the cost and complexity of anti-dumping investigations. for example, a helpdesk should help smes to lodge complaints and provide information on procedures.
in writing. what might appear to be a breakthrough in european trade policy in the fight against dumping is far from being up to the challenge of the ravages caused by free trade, of which the european union, and the commission in particular, remains a zealous promoter. the recent treatment of chinese solar panel imports is proof of this: while chinese products occupy 80% of the european market and 25,000 jobs in a strategic sector have been destroyed, the timid commission proposal was withdrawn immediately after china threatened to retaliate. the rapporteur is helping to reduce the few achievements of the text; it opposed the application of the anti-dumping duty in its entirety, even if limited to the raw material market, stressing that most of the goods exported by the companies were derived from imported intermediate goods. in this connection, it does not fail to recall that dumping is not a practice prohibited by the wto, only 'harmful' dumping is. i vote against it.
in writing. it was essential for the european union to modernise its trade defence instruments to adapt them to the current global trading environment. it is not protectionist to want to guarantee that our companies operate in an international environment conducive to fair trade. this instrument, which we so badly needed, will enable the union to act quickly when competition from third countries does not respect the rules of international trade. i am very pleased to have fought for this report to be adopted in such a way that european companies are assured of operating in the best possible commercial environment. the report places particular emphasis on support for smes, which, in the current economic crisis, are particularly affected by unfair competition from third countries. they must be able to use this instrument in the same way as other european companies. ensuring a prosperous future for european businesses also requires the modernisation of the union's trade defence instruments.
in writing. this reform is simply necessary: nothing has changed since 1995. while our trade defence instruments remain relevant in substance, several recent cases, including that of chinese solar panels, have shown that they are no longer always appropriate to the global trading environment. the amendments we have adopted today will better equip our companies against all forms of dumping: commercial, social and environmental. we also wanted to modernise the existing european regulations in a very concrete way. for example, by facilitating access to cids for small and medium-sized enterprises or by reducing the time taken for investigations in order to increase their legal certainty. i now expect the european commission, which started its work very late and imposed a tight timetable on us, and the council to get to work very quickly. our common objective must be to see these modernised idcs come into force as soon as possible.
in writing. i voted in favour of this reform of the 'european trade defence instruments' (etdi) to combat unfair competition from certain imports, the most exemplary case being chinese solar panels. these instruments will enable europe to unilaterally increase customs duties to offset the dumping of highly subsidized products by our commercial competitors. the aim of this revision is also to better equip our companies against all forms of unfair competition: economic, social or environmental.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text on defence against dumped imports. the text thus modernises the european anti-dumping procedure, which is one of the main tools used by the eu to regulate imports and protect its market on the basis of international trade rules. with this text we are strictly regulating this practice, reserving the possibility of introducing or increasing taxes on products when they arrive on the european continent. this will enable european countries to promote products made in europe and to safeguard jobs on european soil.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. european production is in competition with producers in third countries whose social and environmental standards are much lower than ours. the result is unfair competition for our businesses and jobs, downward pressure on our requirements and a deindustrialisation of the union. this report sets out important steps to enable europe to impose stricter duties on imports that do not meet adequate social and environmental standards. in addition, it takes into account the difficulty for smes to participate in anti-dumping investigations by offering a service to help smes. this is a step forward, but there is still a long way to go to protect our industries, our workers and our environment and to ensure the sustainability of the european model of sustainable development: producing efficiently while respecting people and ecosystems.
in writing. under wto rules, dumping is illegal if it is injurious and the evidence of such injury is to be provided by the victim. today, 50% of the eu's imports are intermediate goods and the globalisation of the value chain has exploded in recent years. moreover, the abandonment of our current industries and technology transfers will prevent any return of european competitiveness in the open world market. the european commission is struggling to respond to the damage caused by social or environmental dumping or illegal subsidies as a result of retaliatory measures by third countries, who are supposed to be our trading partners. the basis of international trade as defined by the european commission, the wto's pawn, needs to be revised. while third countries and those considered to be emerging (russia, china) benefit from the wide opening of our markets, theirs remain inaccessible for our products or services.
in writing. i voted in favour of this technical report which, following the many reforms of the common fisheries policy, seeks to put in place effective control mechanisms to ensure that the new provisions are properly complied with both at union and member state level.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on compliance with the cfp rules. the commission has proposed a strict alignment of the control regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 with the lisbon treaty so that parliament can use all the new powers conferred on it by the lisbon treaty since 2009. parliament is keen to ensure that the delegation of power proposed by the european commission is not for an indefinite period but for a limited period of three years. no amendments to the substance of regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 were accepted in the compromise amendments proposed by the rapporteur. the new powers of parliament were underlined.
in writing. the lisbon treaty gave the european commission the power to adopt delegated acts, allowing for amendments to non-essential elements of legislative acts, and implementing acts. in order to ensure the consistency of european legislation, it seems to me important to adapt the legislative act on compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy in accordance with these new powers of the commission. however, the european parliament should have ex-post control over those delegated acts.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague isabelle thomas which aims to improve the methods of monitoring compliance with the common fisheries policy, in particular as regards catch quotas, data collection and traceability. i therefore welcome the broad adoption of this report.
in writing. the proposals in this report aim, on the one hand, to harmonise the rules between european fishermen, a position which i support. the amendments also limit the use of delegated acts to the more technical implementing act, which leaves less room for manoeuvre. however, despite the report's intention to limit the waiver of power, the share left to the commission's initiative for the adoption of delegated acts is far too significant. the scope of those acts can only be reviewed ex post after three years. i'm not going to.
in writing. since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, fisheries policy has been subject to the so-called co-decision procedure of the council and the european parliament. the regulations in this area must therefore be brought into line with the treaties. this is the subject of the regulation adopted by the european parliament on compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy. the main issue is the distribution of powers between the various institutions and the disputes over this distribution of powers between the co-legislators, which are not lacking. the commission's powers are to be defined and to be able to decide when it may make use of delegated or implementing acts. i therefore voted against because, in addition to giving the commission additional powers, the text proposes, even worse, to change several delegated acts into simple implementing acts, which significantly reduces the european parliament's decision-making power. the council has not had the opportunity to play its part as co-decision-maker in this area and has failed to preserve a common fisheries policy worthy of the name.
in writing. following the entry into force of the lisbon treaty on 1 january 2009, european legislation must be gradually brought into line with the new provisions of the treaty. the report is purely technical in nature and ensures that this is done in an appropriate manner. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to adapt existing european legislation on equipment and protective systems intended for use in explosive atmospheres. the european union needs a certain degree of coherence and legal certainty in its internal market, which requires changes in its legislation. i am in particular in favour of strengthening consumer protection for these products, which should include safety information and clear labelling.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which establishes a clear definition at european level of protective equipment and systems intended for use in explosive atmospheres. moreover, the increased requirement for traceability for all economic operators reinforces the basic objective of security, which i welcome.
in writing. i support this text which harmonises the provisions on the placing on the market and control of explosives for civil use at european level. it was also essential to clarify the common definition of the term 'explosives'. in view of the dangerous nature of these products, member states should ensure that the placing on the market of explosives for civil use is subject to appropriate measures concerning their storage and use.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which is part of the 'harmonisation package'. i therefore welcome the safety obligation on member states to inform other states whenever a non-compliant explosive is identified.
in writing. this text, like several others tabled during this part-session of the european parliament, aims to adapt the european framework for the marketing of a number of products to the lisbon treaty. to do this, several previous directives need to be revised. in this particular case, it is the control of explosives for civilian use. it is therefore essentially a technical text which does not alter the previous legislation, particularly as regards the content of the safety requirements. parliament also took the opportunity to remind the various economic operators active in this sector of their obligations with regard to the traceability and labelling of products. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which advocates legal certainty and increased consumer protection, improves technical safety requirements, product instructions and labelling and ensures better market surveillance.
in writing. following the entry into force of the lisbon treaty on 1 january 2009, european legislation must be gradually brought into line with the new provisions of the treaty. the report is purely technical in nature and ensures that this is done in an appropriate manner. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. this text adapts the european legislation on non-automatic weighing instruments. it is rightly aimed at removing previous inconsistencies which could be a source of legal uncertainty on the european market. in order to ensure the safe circulation of non-automatic weighing instruments on the market, member states should take measures against misuse and incorrect application of the rules on ce marking.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which is part of the 'harmonisation package', and i therefore encourage the european union's drive to modernise electronic equipment.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which approximates european legislation on electromagnetic compatibility. however, in the context of the amendment of the legislation in force, it seems to me legitimate to provide in particular for a transitional regime favourable to economic operators for the making available on the market and the putting into service of appliances already placed on the market in accordance with the previous legislation. they should be able to sell their existing stock of equipment, so that they do not suffer from legal instability.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to modernise electromagnetic compatibility. the respect of security requirements and the desire for data transparency reflect a better consideration of this issue by the european union.
in writing. this text aligns european legislation on electrical equipment intended for use within certain voltage limits with the new legislative framework. the need to ensure a high level of protection for the most vulnerable consumers is rightly emphasised. where the equipment is not intended for professional use, placing on the market must be conditional upon ease of use for all.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal, which concerns electrical equipment intended for use within a certain voltage limit. the increase in the safety of these materials and the desire to ensure transparency for the consumer are all positive elements which i welcome.
in writing. i voted in favour of this technical report because it aims to improve the internal market and will allow the establishment of a common framework for the marketing of products.
in writing. i support this text which harmonises the provisions on lifts and safety components for lifts at european level. it seems to me particularly consistent that in the event of non-compliance of these products with the legislation, appropriate restrictive measures, such as withdrawal from the market, should be taken as soon as possible. these measures are necessary to strengthen the protection of european citizens.
in writing. this text adapts the current european legislation on simple pressure vessels. i think it is particularly important to reduce the excessive bureaucratic burden in this area. this requires modernisation of existing procedures so that the eu declaration of conformity is available not only in paper form but also in electronic form.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which contains many safeguards for consumers. the proposal has the effect of improving the competitiveness of notified bodies and undertakings which comply with their obligations seriously, as compared with those which circumvent the system. in addition, this text does not represent a major cost for economic operators and notified bodies, which i welcome.
in writing. i support this text which aligns the measuring instruments directive with the new european legislative framework. in order to strengthen consumer protection on the european market, cases of distance selling by economic operators should also be subject to such legislation.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which is part of the 'harmonisation package'. i welcome the obligation of traceability for all economic operators, including the names and addresses of manufacturers, which will further enhance consumer safety.
in writing. i voted for the eight roithova reports because the technical alignment of these directives mainly concerns: a) measures to combat the non-compliance of products: obligations for economic operators (manufacturers, importers, distributors), traceability requirements, market surveillance; (b) measures to improve the quality of the work of notified bodies assessing compliance with european union requirements (notification requirements, obligation to provide information on refusals, restrictions, etc. on certificates); (c) measures ensuring consistency between directives (alignment of definitions and terminology, alignment of provisions on conformity assessment procedures).
in writing. i supported the eight reports by my colleague zuzana roithova, which follow the publication by the european commission of the alignment package on the new legislative framework. the technical alignment of these eight directives (the directive on equipment and protective systems intended for use in potentially explosive atmospheres, the directive on explosives for civil use, the directive on non-automatic weighing instruments, the directive on electromagnetic compatibility, the directive on electrical equipment for use within certain voltage limits, the directive on lifts and safety components for lifts, the directive on single pressure vessels and the directive on measuring instruments) mainly concerns measures to combat non-compliance of products, measures to strengthen the quality of the work of notified bodies assessing the conformity of products with the requirements of the european union, and measures to ensure consistency between directives. these reports have been widely adopted, and i welcome that.
in writing. i voted in favour of the package of eight reports introducing technical alignment on product safety and enhanced market surveillance. the effectiveness of european legislation on health and safety protection will be enhanced by these amendments for each of the sectors concerned.
in writing. the eight reports in the harmonisation package amend the directives on product harmonisation as part of the implementation of the new legislative framework adopted in 2008. this is to address the shortcomings in the existing union harmonisation legislation. the adoption of these texts will strengthen producer and consumer confidence by clarifying the obligations of economic operators. it will also provide member state authorities with more effective tools to carry out market surveillance checks, which will lead to an overall reduction in non-compliant and dangerous products on the market. nevertheless, the aim is as always to achieve the internal market by promoting competition. i'm not going to.
in writing. the adoption of the bach report confirms the european parliament's strong position in favour of air passenger rights, at a time when the market is now fully open and airlines are benefiting from a strong increase in traffic. parliament called for compensation for delays in proportion to the duration of the flight or for better care to be given to passengers who cannot board. we also ask for greater price transparency when booking, since the price initially displayed must include hand and hold baggage, the price of payment by credit card or check-in. i hope that the council will now follow this ambitious line.
in writing. i voted in favour of adopting this parliament's position at first reading. the growth of air traffic benefits everyone but must not be at the expense of respect for the rights of everyone. of course, there are already rights, but they are still difficult for passengers to understand, who too often find themselves helpless when faced with difficulties such as cancellation or delay of their flight, loss of luggage or denied boarding. today we want to strengthen and clarify these rights. some airlines do not play the game and willfully ignore passenger complaints or misuse "extraordinary circumstances" to evade their compensation obligations. this new legislation must be made for passengers and will put an end to these abusive practices. i welcome the adoption of the position advocated by parliament. i believe that this is the only way to create a 'single european sky' which is both competitive and protective of travellers. i hope that the member states will pay attention to the need to strengthen passenger rights, as we are asking for today.
in writing. i voted in favour of this new regulation to support the introduction of a right to financial compensation for european citizens which airlines will have to respect in the event of delays or cancellations. the airlines will no longer be able to refuse passengers compensation on the grounds of 'extraordinary circumstances' or 'technical problems' which they alone have so far defined, and which in reality lead to widespread abuse. the text also puts an end to the questionable commercial practices of some low-cost airlines in their rules on hand luggage. finally, i very much welcome the special attention given to vulnerable passengers, such as children or disabled people. the ball is now in the council's court and i hope it will be as ambitious as parliament has been.
in writing. who has not been concerned about losing luggage or facing a delayed or cancelled flight, given the difficulties in winning a case? despite improvements in the conditions for reimbursement and compensation, these are not applied uniformly by airlines, which take advantage of the approximation of definitions in european legislation to justify a non-receipt order. i am pleased that the european parliament has supported this new package of measures for better protection of air passenger rights with a large majority. airlines will no longer be able to abuse the 'extraordinary circumstances' to refuse reimbursement. the report provides a clear definition of this concept and also sets thresholds for compensation in the event of cancellation, delay or denied boarding. the report also recommends that passengers be allowed to bring coats, handbags or at least shopping bags to the airport on all flights, in addition to the maximum baggage allowance.
in writing. while the parliament's text makes some improvements to the commission's text, it does not mention or even add to certain provisions of the original text. thus, damages caused by bird impacts are included in the extraordinary circumstances which exempt air carriers from compensating passengers. this is a common cause of flight delays and cancellations. the introduction of the directive in the text therefore means that the users have to bear the costs. above all, parliament endorses the introduction of labour disputes in exceptional circumstances. this means that the financial consequences of social movements are borne by the users and not by the transport operators, and therefore neutralizes the balance of forces established by the outbreak of a strike. this is completely unacceptable. it's a violation of the right to strike. i am voting against this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long delay of a flight. although this report falls short of what might be expected in terms of protecting air passengers' rights, it contains significant improvements over the commission's initial draft. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive on the protection of the environment. this text provides for a better balance between the rights of airlines and those of passengers. the european union must realise that passengers are not only consumers governed by the law of king money alone, but also citizens with rights to assert vis-à-vis the carriers. and the right to mobility must be moved from the logic of competition dominated by the law of supply and demand to a logic of rights, of the fight against discrimination and equality.
in writing. after intensive negotiations, we succeeded in adopting the regulation on air passenger rights by making the positions of my political family prevail. the big winners are all travellers who fly from outside the european union. passengers travelling to the eu on board a european airline will also be able to benefit from these preferential rights. for example, they will no longer have to carry their personal effects and duty free purchases in a single suitcase. this travesty of some airlines, which try to make passengers pay by forcing them to put everything they carry in the hold, will now be banned! in addition, the right to board is now guaranteed to persons who have purchased a return ticket and who will no longer be denied boarding on the return journey on the grounds that they missed the outward flight. the text also clarifies the issue of delayed compensation: for example, all intra-eu flights delayed by 3 hours will be entitled to financial compensation of at least eur 300. i hope that the council will now follow our wishes and not seek to undermine the rights of passengers.
in writing. i voted in favour of the legislative report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the 2000 council regulation on insolvency proceedings. it became necessary to revise that regulation to allow its practical application. its scope does not cover certain national procedures for restructuring a pre-insolvency company or procedures which maintain the existing management. concerns have arisen as to which member state is competent to open insolvency proceedings. the rules on the publicity of insolvency proceedings and the production of claims also needed to be clarified. finally, the specific rules on the insolvency of multinational groups of companies had to be taken into account, as a large number of crossborder insolvency cases involve groups of companies.
in writing. i voted for the lehne report on the proposal for a regulation on insolvency proceedings. the aim is to vote on the european parliament's position with a view to adoption at second reading, since no agreement could be reached with the council at this stage.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to reform european legislation on crossborder insolvency of companies in order to strengthen the internal market of the european union. i support better harmonisation of national legislation in this area to ensure fair competition and legal certainty for businesses in europe. the proposal to create a european insolvency register to check whether insolvency proceedings have been opened in a member state or not seems to me to be relevant.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which aims to clarify crossborder insolvency cases. one of the major challenges of the european single market is to resolve this type of dispute, which is increasingly being resolved through the use of private international law. in addition, the proposal allows for the introduction of standardised forms available in all the official languages of the european union, which facilitates the production of claims for foreign creditors.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague klaus-heiner lehne, which aims to clarify crossborder insolvency procedures, since national laws vary widely from one member state to another. by allowing synergy between the procedures opened in the member states and by establishing interconnected insolvency registers to facilitate the circulation of information, the text promotes better handling of insolvency situations in the european union. i therefore welcome the outcome of this vote.
in writing. the insolvency regulation establishes a european framework for crossborder insolvency proceedings. it applies where a debtor, whether a natural or a legal person, has assets or creditors in more than one member state. the report recommends the creation of a european insolvency register which would enable creditors and courts to determine whether or not insolvency proceedings have been opened in another member state. this includes the introduction of procedures to help debtors in serious financial difficulties recover, so as to help healthy businesses survive and give entrepreneurs a second chance. it also helps to combat organised insolvency. i vote for it.
in writing. ukrainian protesters are facing violent repression from the authorities. the european union must act to ensure that freedom of expression is respected. under the european neighbourhood policy and the eastern partnership, the eu opened up to a ukraine whose foreign and trade policy was swinging either towards russia or towards europe. the radical turn of the yanukovych government in refusing to sign the eu-ukraine negotiating agreement was a bombshell. ukrainians recognise european values and see the eu as a partner capable of improving their daily lives. in addition, the eastern partnership recognises the importance of cooperation with civil society. ukrainian citizens understood this and put it into practice by asserting their right to contribute to the politics of their country. as europeans we must act when a neighbouring people, sharing the same values of freedom of expression and democracy, calls on us for help. violence against protesters must stop, the process of revising the constitution must continue and new free and fair elections must be held. if the ukrainian people want more europe, let us give them the opportunity to get more europe without being threatened by a recalcitrant government.
i call on the presidency of the council and on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, on behalf of the high representative, mrs ashton, i would like to reiterate our deep concern at the crisis in the central african republic (car) and to stress the urgent need to protect the population. this country continues to experience a great crisis. insecurity is widespread almost everywhere, as are human rights violations. the humanitarian situation is alarming. this is a humanitarian crisis. the social fabric has been disrupted, further fuelling intercommunal tensions, which are being politically exploited and leading to 'an eye for an eye' type of killings between the christian and muslim populations. public institutions that were already weak and operating at the limit of their potential have ceased to function completely. we are now faced not with a state which is weak, but with a vacuum in which it is difficult to say that there is a state. as restoring security is the key to protecting the civilian population and stabilising the situation in order to support the political process, it is obvious that there is no military solution to this conflict. the current crisis stems from decades of lack of political consensus, daunting challenges to governance and unbalanced socioeconomic development. the european union has been actively involved, since the beginning of the current crisis in late december 2012, in order to help prevent a full-scale conflict. following the violent seizure of power by seleka rebel groups in march 2013, the european union supported regional and international efforts to find a political solution to the crisis and to help stabilise the country. the european union has responded swiftly and comprehensively to the current crisis, fully supporting the french initiative and intervention. the union's response, which combines support for stability and development, is evidence of the european union's ability to respond to major crises such as this one quickly and efficiently, with all the means at its disposal. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu aid volunteers initiative, in particular through the european solidarity corps, and will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu aid volunteers initiative. let me point out three key elements which we consider essential for a way out of the crisis in the central african republic: firstly, security must be restored, starting with the capital and then extending to the wider region. the union fully supports the african mission mission mission in afghanistan (misca) and welcomes the support provided by the french operation sangaris to restore law and order in accordance with the un security council resolution. we also consider the bilateral assistance provided by member states of the european union to be very important. in view of the urgent priority of restoring a security environment, the eu foreign affairs council has decided to extend the mandate of the eu high representative for foreign affairs and security policy to include the eu high representative for the common foreign and security policy. on 20 january, the council adopted a political decision to begin preparations for an eu military operation in the central african republic. the decision was taken after taking into account the continuing situation of lawlessness and insecurity in much of the country and the common desire to improve security so that urgently needed humanitarian aid can be given to those who really need it. the european operation is intended to complement the efforts of misca and the french forces. it underlines the union's readiness to respond in a comprehensive manner. i am pleased that the un security council unanimously adopted resolution 2134 (2014) on 28 january, granting the authorisation for the eu operation in the central african republic. the african union also welcomed this eu operation under the csdp. i am particularly pleased as greek foreign minister because the headquarters of this operation is in larissa, a greek city, where we have very close and good cooperation with the french armed forces, which are the backbone of this operation, the bulk of the military personnel and know-how. secondly, it is necessary to reconstitute a political process. in this context, the appointment of new transitional authorities, following transparent consultations, and the balanced composition of the new government in relation to the various communities are positive signs. moreover, the head of the transitional authority has a strong background in human rights and mediation, so we have a unique opportunity to advance the political transition process, the cooperation of all parties to end the violence and the country's march towards elections by february 2015 at the latest. the eu stands ready, in good coordination with partners, to assist the new government in advancing the transition process. while elections are necessary to restore the legitimacy of the authorities and constitutional order, the international response should always go one step further to ensure a sustainable response to the instability that is re-emerging in the car; there's a vicious circle. thirdly, these initiatives must be combined with humanitarian efforts to help those in need. on 20 january, the un and the eu chaired an international high level meeting which raised almost $500 million for humanitarian and development assistance. this is a positive development, but i must stress that the improvement of humanitarian coverage and the resumption of development aid are directly linked to positive developments which must be made in security matters. we believe that the speed with which we act is essential to support the transitional authorities, to re-establish order and to normalise the political process. we will continue to support the humanitarian, stabilization and political process and to contribute to the creation of the conditions for sustainable development. the necessary medium-term objective is to rebuild the state structures and institutions and support long-term socioeconomic recovery, within the framework of an overall agenda for consolidating the state and peace in the country. eu action will bring real added value to international efforts to stabilise the country by building on the union's long-standing relationship with the car and its instruments in an integrated approach.

in writing. only 2% of air passengers receive compensation after lodging a complaint: this is the current imbalance between the traveller and the airline. i therefore voted in favour of these new provisions so that passengers who are stuck, whose luggage has been damaged or whose flight has been delayed can be better informed and can get compensation. the text also provides for an increase in the number of bags allowed in holds, including handbags, coats and shopping bags at the airport.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long delay of a flight. europe has already done much to protect the rights of air passengers in the event of loss of baggage or cancellation of flights. however, in many cases airlines refuse to grant these rights or delay compensation procedures. in view of this situation, the report simplifies the procedures for air passengers and obliges airlines to inform correctly and in good time all passengers who are entitled to compensation. the text will help to protect european citizens from airlines which too often show bad faith.
in writing. i welcome the result achieved today, the result of negotiations with all the political groups until the last minute. the increase in air traffic must be accompanied by new rights for passengers, whose numbers are increasing. the text introduces an important new element: the right to financial compensation in the event of delay, in proportion to the duration of the flight. airlines will no longer be able to evade their obligations, particularly by making false claims of technical problems. in addition, when booking a flight, price transparency will be mandatory in the interests of the consumer. the price of the ticket must always include the costs of check-in, boarding pass, hand luggage, hold baggage and payment, such as credit card charges. finally, the rules on cabin baggage will make life easier for travellers. the scandalous business practices of some low-cost airlines had to be stopped. parliament voted a balanced text between better rights for passengers, with particular attention to vulnerable passengers such as children or disabled people, and realistic and effectively enforceable obligations by airlines. we now expect the council to be just as ambitious.

in writing. unfortunately, the texts on the eu's energy and climate policy follow one another and are similar. there is still so much certainty about the benefits of the co2 market, and still so much blindness to the climate catastrophe. the few cosmetic reforms that the european parliament wants to make to the ets are tiny compared to the incredible environmental counterproductivity that the system has already shown. at a crucial moment for the survival of humanity, the european parliament has already abandoned any ambitious energy and climate policy. instead, it is the 'internal energy market' that should initiate the bifurcation of the european energy model and the co2 market that should steer the european economy towards sobriety in this area. the archetype of the stupidity of this european liberal technocracy is the proposal to abandon public aid for certain renewable energies (land-based wind and solar) on the grounds that they would distort the proper functioning of the energy market and that they would be mature enough to face competition. i shall abstain on this text in order not to impede the meagre progress made in this report.
in writing. it is very important for the european union to adopt a common climate strategy so that all member states are held accountable to the common goal of preserving the environment. many european laws have been enacted to this end and member states are doing their utmost to reduce their energy consumption. however, it is essential to take account of the sectors affected by this reduction in energy consumption, such as industry and transport. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the environment is not affected by the new technologies. i voted against this report because the binding objectives it proposed were completely out of proportion and unattainable. reducing greenhouse gas emissions is essential, but it must not be at the expense of certain important sectors of the european economy. there are priorities, and the return to growth is the main one.
in writing. on 23 january 2014, the commission presented its green paper on energy and climate policies for 2030, reversing its previous statements and positions. the european parliament adopted a resolution confirming its previous climate positions, including the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions by 80-95% by 2050 and the adoption of binding targets for greenhouse gas emissions reduction, energy efficiency and the share of renewable energy in energy consumption by 2030. however, its ambitions remain limited, its renewable energy and co2 reduction targets being only marginally higher than those of the commission. i regret that a right-wing majority rejected the amendments which i co-signed in order to increase these objectives. i am particularly sorry that parliament is calling for a reduction in public intervention in all areas of energy and climate policy. how can the necessary public policies be implemented by leaving it to private investors and the 'balance of the market'? this means nothing more than the unleashing of greenwashing, in other words pseudo-green capitalism. so i chose to abstain in the final vote because it is only a very small step in the face of the challenges of global warming.
in writing. climate change is a real threat to people, and that is why i voted today in favour of measures with binding targets: reduction of co2 emissions, development of renewable energy and improvement of energy efficiency. in its proposals for 'energy and climate by 2030', unveiled on 22 january, the european commission has set only one really binding target: a 40% reduction in co2 emissions, coupled with a 27% target for renewable energies at european level, but it does not provide for mandatory national reductions, which makes its implementation uncertain. the commission has also not proposed any measures to improve energy efficiency, which is a source of economic and climate benefits. like the other european socialists, i have today spoken in favour of multifaceted and binding objectives, far from the timid proposals of the european commission. we need a clear and strong european position: the sector needs visibility to make the investment decisions that bind us in the medium and long term today, in order to make the european union the world leader in sustainable development.
in writing. the rapporteur konrad szymański wanted to disavow his own report by postponing it in committee but was unable to do so for procedural reasons. it was a bad text. the issue of global warming/climate change has been in the spotlight for many years, and europeans have been blamed for it at every turn. the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions is the workhorse of the well-meaning commission. yet the eu is responsible for only 11% of these emissions worldwide. despite sound economic sense, in the face of rising energy prices, the commission is proposing only costly and haphazard renewable energy sources such as wind and a reduction in ghg emission quotas for member states, an incentive to pollute elsewhere than in europe. insecurity remains as regards the supply of renewable energy. these resources are not sufficiently reliable or flexible to respond quickly to rapid changes in demand. the european energy policy is not balanced and this is reflected in the commission's irresponsible proposals which only increase the union's regulatory burden.
in writing. after the 2009 energy and climate package, which was one of the greatest successes of the french eu presidency, our parliament adopted an ambitious roadmap to 2030. we know the crucial challenges facing humanity: limiting the rise in temperatures, co2 emissions, sea level rise and preserving biodiversity and our habitat. these are the imperatives which require us to explore the ways of achieving an economy which is resource and energy efficient. two types of energy seem to me to be extremely promising and should be encouraged: renewable marine energy, produced in particular from wind, waves and currents, which are clean, unlimited sources and job creators; and shale gas, which is hotly debated but can be exploited intelligently, provided that sustainable and non-abrasive exploration and extraction methods are developed. these two projects represent the future of energy and are capable of guaranteeing the union an energy supply which respects the balance between industrial development and environmental protection. in this way we can reduce our energy bill, our trade deficit and our dependence on oil and gas from unstable countries.
in writing. we confirmed, by a large majority, the negotiating mandate on the bank resolution mechanism, the last and indispensable step in building a strong and reliable european banking union. we wanted to give weight to the negotiating team of the committee on economic and monetary affairs of parliament which is conducting laborious negotiations with the member states. our fellow citizens need us to endorse the creation of this single resolution mechanism to avoid burdening the states, and therefore the taxpayers, with the bankruptcy of credit institutions. firstly, the european parliament wants the resolution mechanism to be based on a european treaty rather than an intergovernmental treaty, as germany wants. similarly, we believe that we cannot wait for the agreement of 28 member states when it comes to deciding on the bankruptcy of a bank and triggering the resolution mechanism. otherwise, this tool would lose all purpose since its functioning depends on the very speed of decision-making. we hope that this vote will open the way to further compromises.
in writing. i voted in favour of this clear negotiating mandate on the european banking union mechanism, which aims to protect the taxpayer from possible bank failures. the compromise reached before christmas by the finance ministers is far from satisfactory and does not provide sufficient legal clarity to avoid contagion between financial institutions. the member states' position shows significant setbacks compared to michel barnier's proposal, particularly on the complex and politicized decision-making mechanism and the weakness of the bank-financed rescue fund, which must be more credible. the council must accept democratic control of decisions and review its copy for adoption before the european elections.
in writing. for several months now, discussions have been taking place within the union to establish a 'single mechanism for resolving banking crises'. this banking union is supposed to solve crises by stealing from troubled banks. in practical terms, this means setting up a new fund, financed primarily by the banks, whose insufficiency is known in advance and which will therefore be mainly replenished by public funds. as usual, there are few conditions attached to this bank rescue, which has already cost over eur 4.5 trillion, and no question is raised here of the dependence of the states on the financial markets. the european parliament has fought a battle, but it is not to criticize the cruel lack of ambition of this reform, which is being presented as revolutionary in an election period. it is to reject the intergovernmental process that the council favors, a procedure which will give less power to the european commission and more to the representatives of the member states. the position of the gue-ngl is clear: we are voting against this so-called 'reform' which is merely organising the rescue of the banks without any real counterpart from them.
in writing. since 2002, fresh beef has been labelled precisely to inform the consumer of the place of birth, rearing and slaughter of the bovine. in 2011, the european commission was given the task of extending origin labelling to other types of meat: sheep, goat, pig and poultry meat. the european commission proposes very minimal rules with only a mention of the place of slaughter and sometimes the place of rearing. we believe that the european commission should revise its copy and come back quickly with a text that will better inform consumers. that is why i voted for this resolution which i initiated and tabled with my colleague, mrs agnès le brun.
in writing. i supported this resolution to take over the european commission in its application of european legislation on the indication of the country of origin or place of provenance of fresh, chilled and frozen meat of porcine, ovine, caprine and poultry animals. in view of the recent scandals in various european countries over meat labelling problems, i believe it is essential to provide for the mandatory indication on the label of unprocessed meat from pigs, sheep and goats and poultry of the place of birth, rearing and slaughter. only then will we be able to restore consumer confidence.
in writing. a year ago, citizens were astonished and shocked to discover the composition of lasagna made from horse meat. although the european union has steadily strengthened food safety and the traceability of the products we consume, fraud and diversion have been detected. this unacceptable situation calls for a strong, effective and responsible response. this is why i am surprised that the european commission has not been able to come up with a proposal that is up to the challenge. since 2002, fresh beef has been subject to precise and mandatory labelling at the place of birth, rearing and slaughter of the bovine. we owe this clear and transparent approach to information to consumers. however, the commission continues to oppose the generalization of these rules to other types of meat (sheepmeat, goatmeat, pigmeat and poultrymeat) fresh, chilled or frozen. the european parliament therefore called on the commission to revise its proposal in the light of the need for transparency and information for citizens.
in writing. i voted for the resolution in favour of better consumer information on all types of meat with the obligation to indicate on the label the place of birth, rearing and slaughter of animals. the eu's new rules on labelling for fresh beef and veal, which have been in place since 2002, should also apply to pig, sheep, goat and poultry meat, meps said.
in writing. one year after the horse meat scandal in lasagna, the european commission has presented a regulation on the origin labelling of fresh, chilled or frozen pig, sheep, goat or poultry meat. unfortunately, the text on the table is not acceptable. the brussels executive proposes only minimalist rules, according to which a chicken that has lived only one month in france could be called "raised in france", without specifying its place of birth. i therefore voted in favour of the objection and against the commission proposal and called for mandatory labelling indicating the place of birth, rearing and slaughter, in order to provide the consumer with clear traceability information.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution calling on the european commission to review its policy on food labelling. the european commission, under the influence of certain large agri-food lobbies, is seeking to adopt a number of derogations from the labelling rules concerning the indication of the country of origin or place of provenance of certain fresh meat. european consumers have the right to be informed about the origin of the meat they consume. in this text, i have therefore asked the european commission to make it compulsory for the labelling of meat from pigs, sheep, goats and poultry to indicate the place of birth, rearing and slaughter, as provided for in the legislation in force for beef and veal.
in writing. since the bse crisis, the labelling of beef has been subject to strict rules, but not that of pig, sheep, goat or poultry meat. in recent years, however, food fraud has increased. the european commission has therefore proposed a regulation to introduce the marking of the country of production and slaughter of the animal on the packaging. in this resolution, parliament opposed this and asked the commission to revise its copy, including the labelling of the country of birth. i voted for this resolution because we must shed light on the origin of meat. to require the compulsory indication of the place of birth, rearing and slaughter of unprocessed meat of porcine, ovine and caprine origin and poultry in the same way as is done today for beef seems to me quite 'normal'. in the light of the recent food scandals, including the fraudulent use of horse meat instead of beef ('spanghero's case), greater transparency and better information on the origin of all types of meat, including minced meat, seems to me to be the minimum requirement.
in writing. faced with the steady fall in the price of carbon in the european co2 emissions market and its negative consequences for the climate and low investments in carbon emissions, the european commission has proposed to save it by regulating the supply and demand of allowances. behind this technical appearance is the whole of european policy to combat climate change. indeed, with a price of a tonne of carbon dangerously close to zero, the carbon market becomes inefficient and therefore transparent... it no longer protects europeans and their environment from carbon emissions that contribute to climate change and natural disasters. i therefore voted in favour of this recommendation, which calls for the rapid implementation of this emergency measure.
in writing. regarding the implementation of the greenhouse gas auction timetable, i voted against the european commission's proposals in the draft regulation because the commission did not provide an assessment showing, for the different industrial sectors, that no real impact is to be expected on the sectors or subsectors exposed to a significant risk of carbon leakage. this assessment was an essential condition for the consent of the european parliament when it voted, after difficult debates, the decision of 17 december 2013 authorising the commission to amend the timetable by withdrawing 900 million allowances. i also object to the fact that the draft regulation has not been translated into all the languages, which is another intolerable attack on multilingualism. it was not even made available to meps on the parliament's live session website.
in writing. i opposed the european commission's draft regulation to amend european legislation on the determination of the volume of greenhouse gas emission allowances to be auctioned during the period 2013-2020. such a change in the timetable for auctioning co2 emission allowances runs counter to the principle of legal certainty which we want to respect in order to promote competitiveness and employment in europe.
in writing. last december, parliament endorsed the freezing of 900 million co2 emission allowances under the greenhouse gas emission trading system (ghg), otherwise known as the carbon market (cem), in order to make it at least operational. at this session, the only question was to approve the entry into force of this provision in the coming weeks. as in december last year, i abstained because the 900 million co2 emission allowances frozen for the period 2014-2016 and put back on the market in 2019 are only a palliative and are far from matching the necessary reduction in ghg emissions. the aim of the freeze is to increase the price of co2 and thus to encourage manufacturers to change their production methods by investing in technologies and manufacturing processes that emit less co2. i don't believe in that. this decision was adopted by a narrow majority. the right wing as a whole, under pressure from the industrial lobbies, voted against this amendment, showing its opposition to any measure to reduce co2 emissions and its lack of concern for the issues of protecting the planet.
in writing. in view of the tragic situation in ukraine, i voted in favour of this resolution which condemns the use of force, calls for a peaceful solution and, finally, recalls the european union's readiness to help and to come closer to ukraine and the ukrainians.
in writing. the european parliament could not remain silent in the face of the wave of protests in ukraine in recent months, firstly to demand that ukraine sign the final association agreement with the european union, and also to demand the resignation of president viktor yanukovych. i supported the european parliament resolution voted on 6 february 2014. the joint resolution by the various political groups condemns all forms of violence and repression by the ukrainian authorities against peaceful protesters and calls for political dialogue as a solution to this crisis. parliament also called for the fight against money laundering and tax evasion to be continued, for a visa-free regime to be rapidly introduced and eventually a visa-free regime for ukrainians, and for a long-term financial assistance programme to be prepared to help ukraine improve its financial and social situation.
in writing. i supported the motion for a resolution on the situation in ukraine. the resolution condemns the escalation of violence and calls for a solution to the conflict through dialogue. it called on president yanukovych to end the use of riot police, arbitrary arrests and to release all unlawfully detained protesters, including yulia tymoshenko. it also calls for targeted sanctions against ukrainian officials involved in the repression of the pro-european movement. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. i welcome the adoption of this resolution.
in writing. it should be recalled that following the decision of the ukrainian president not to sign the association agreement with the european union, protests began two months ago, which were severely repressed by the riot police and quickly banned by laws that severely restrict freedom of expression and freedom of assembly. the resolution condemns the policy of intimidation, repression and even torture which has been carried out by the ukrainian government against demonstrators, human rights activists and journalists. i welcome this, especially since it also mentions the acts of violence committed by ultra-nationalist members of openly neo-nazi movements. i also welcome the adoption of an amendment by the gue-ngl which recalls that it is the ukrainian people alone who must decide the geopolitical direction of their country, without foreign interference. the resolution does not, however, say anything about the union's policy in ukraine, which is limited to proposing the development of free trade on the basis of a 'deep and comprehensive free trade area'. the ukrainians need democracy and a re-foundation of their institutions, not economic tutelage. that is why i abstained in this vote.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution condemning the very numerous and absolutely intolerable human rights violations currently taking place in syria. the resolution calls for a concerted, peaceful solution but also recalls that "any political solution must preserve the unity, territorial integrity, sovereignty and independence of syria".
in writing. faced with the escalation of terror for the past three years, europe has still not succeeded in finding a satisfactory solution to the syrian crisis. and the last few months have shown us that this response can only be political, to prevent chaos from succeeding chaos. this is why this resolution stresses the role of the geneva ii negotiations. the syrian opposition must use this platform to show itself more united and organized. the resolution also stresses the extremely worrying situation of the syrian people, and we europeans must do everything possible to bring medical and humanitarian aid to these people in distress as quickly as possible. the resolution also stressed the increase in violence on religious or ethnic grounds, which was essential in view of the extremely worrying situation of the minorities concerned, especially christians.
in writing. this is not the first time that parliament has spoken out on the situation in syria and the measures that need to be taken. in the face of the continuing escalation of violence in syria and the growing number of victims, it is becoming increasingly clear that a lasting solution to the current crisis can only be found through a political process led by syria and open to all parties. it is in this perspective that the efforts of the geneva ii conference must be continued and that direct interaction between the warring parties must be maintained. the resolution also provides an opportunity for parliament to pay tribute to the countries neighbouring syria which are absorbing the ever-increasing flows of refugees. the union must of course support the countries bordering syria, in view of the humanitarian, social, economic, political and security consequences of the syrian crisis for the whole region. this assistance to host countries, whether humanitarian aid, development aid or macroeconomic aid, must be articulated and organised in a concerted way.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the current situation in syria, where more than 100 000 people have already lost their lives. the text reiterates its call for a political solution supported by the international community and its concern about the humanitarian situation and its implications for syria's neighbours. i welcome the adoption of this resolution.
in writing. the recent events in syria have had dramatic consequences, both politically and humanitarianally. today, there are over 100,000 dead, over 4 million displaced persons and 2 million refugees in neighbouring countries. an attempt to resolve the conflict peacefully was initiated by the united nations, with the geneva ii conference for middle east peace, which opened on 22 january 2014, but whose positive results are still pending. the urgent need to intervene to enforce international law and minimise human losses, while continuing to seek a political compromise. this resolution perfectly embodies this urgency and affirms that the european parliament continues its efforts to achieve a political and peaceful solution. it also stressed the need for substantial humanitarian support to help syrian families and to ensure the protection of fundamental rights. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. according to the un, more than 130,000 people have been killed since the syrian regime's violent crackdown on peaceful protesters began. 9 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance, 6.5 million are internally displaced and 2.3 million are outside, mainly in syria's neighbouring countries. among them, a majority of children in terrible states of psychological suffering. this is not to say that the situation is dramatic. this resolution rightly calls on the union and its member states to fulfil their humanitarian duty and to do more for syrian refugees. there is little we can do about it, but the international community's apparent inertia is partly responsible for the worsening of the situation. however, i could not vote for a resolution which encourages the opposition to 'form a more united, inclusive and organised opposition front' when we know the influence of jihadist groups within it, which calls for the establishment of free zones on the border with turkey, whose role as a transit country for international jihadists is proven, and which says nothing about the reasons for the non-participation of the democratic opposition in the geneva conference.
in writing. this resolution on the situation in egypt affirms the european parliament's support for the democratic will shown by the egyptian people, while condemning the various forms of violence currently taking place in the country. i am particularly in favour of condemning acts of violence against coptic christians and the destruction of churches. in 2013, egypt had the highest number of incidents involving christians in the world. i therefore welcome the european parliament's call for greater protection of the coptic community.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which stresses the importance of protecting the rights and freedoms of the entire egyptian population, in the context of the adoption of the new constitution by referendum, but with more than 60% abstentions, especially following the call for a boycott launched by the muslim brotherhood. i welcome the broad adoption of this resolution.
in writing. the new constitution adopted in egypt on 14 and 15 january 2014 by referendum marks an important transition that opens the door to the implementation of a real democratic system. it is all the more important because it was more than widely welcomed by the people, who voted 98.1% in favour, although the voter turnout was only 38.6%. many innovative elements are included in this constitution and testify to its stability as well as to the promising future it can offer egypt. this is particularly the case with various provisions which promote greater consideration of the rights and freedoms of the egyptian people. the resolution confirms the european parliament's desire to deepen relations between the european union and egypt, which would make the situation more sustainable. that is why i voted for it.
in writing. the resolution, which is full of goodwill, condemns the violence on both sides and expresses 'its great solidarity with the egyptian people'. however, it did not say anything about the military coup of july 2013 and the brutal repression that followed. nor is there any mention of the economic positions of the military leaders, whose interests are in reality far removed from those of the egyptian people, and in particular those of the workers, the poor and the young, who are demanding social justice and an improvement in their living standards. the economic situation has stabilised only thanks to the massive aid from the gulf countries and unemployment remains endemic. the priority is to restore democratic order as a matter of urgency so that the country can be rapidly equipped with democratic institutions capable of finally responding to the concerns of the population. the european parliament's almost unconditional support for the institutions created by the military coup seems to me to lack nuance and distance, to say the least. that is why i have chosen to abstain on this resolution, as have the members of the gue/ngl.

in writing. this resolution aims to support the european commission's proposal to set up the naiades ii action programme for the period 2014-2020. in this text, the european parliament calls on the commission to allocate sufficient resources to such a programme which promotes inland waterway transport in the european union. it is important to provide adequate support to this sector, which is mainly composed of smes. in addition, water transport has low greenhouse gas emissions and it is worthwhile to develop it.
in writing. river freight is much less polluting than road transport. in my constituency in the south-west of france, i am defending his return to the canal des deux-mers. i am pleased that the group has obtained an amendment on aid for the modernisation of the small-sized fleet, which is the most environmentally friendly, in order to improve its competitiveness. similarly, our amendment calling for compliance with environmental regulations for inland waterways was narrowly adopted, whereas the amendment on the search for intermodal connections was not. in its present formulation, the resolution favours the colossal projects planned on the rhine and the danube. the two largest rivers in europe are often combined in one vision, that of a rhine-danube axis. we as environmentalists are not trying to adapt rivers and streams to larger vessels, but rather to calibrate the fleet according to the characteristics of the waterways. it is this second option that i advocate with the development of a medium-sized freight vessel on the canal des deux-mers. i therefore wish to abstain on the naiades ii programme.
