the topic of today’s discussion, the european semester. first of all, i would like to acknowledge the hard work of the three rapporteurs, philippe de backer, sergio gutiérrez prieto and sergio gaetano cofferati, as well as of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, the committee on employment and social affairs and the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, which allows us to have this timely debate today. i would also like to thank the greek presidency for their commitment and the comments which the minister for european affairs has just made. the european semester goes to the very heart of what has preoccupied us all especially from the outset of the financial crisis – our economy. how can we make our economy recover again? how, in fact, can we work together for employment in europe? these are the issues that our citizens expect us to address – jobs and growth. a year ago, some were still talking of the collapse of the euro, some were even speculating about the disintegration of the european union. i think we can say that, together, we have proved that the prophets of doom were wrong. this is the year in which we are moving away from recession. the recovery is expected to continue and to become more robust during this year and to strengthen further in 2015. consumer confidence and investment confidence is now positive. industrial investment seems to be picking up. instead of expressing concern, leaders outside europe congratulate us on our resilience and for our political willingness to act. they also congratulate us on the necessary, courageous and often painful reforms that several member states have had to put in place. naturally, we know the situation is still difficult. tackling unemployment and the social consequences of the crisis will take time and resolve. but the situation globally is improving and i do not think we should underestimate that fact. in a few hours, vice-president rehn will officially present our latest economic forecasts, and they will confirm that we are on the path of recovery. we have come a long way. the comprehensive response we gave to the crisis is bearing fruit. we have moved from pooled bilateral loans to greece in 2010 – in a situation of real emergency – which was the only possibility available at the time, to the european stability mechanism in 2013, which today has a capital of eur[nbsp ]700 billion! frankly, a while ago it would have been unthinkable to admit that member states could agree to create such a facility. we were able to provide financial assistance to member states in distress, or – in some cases – specifically to their banking sector. were it not for european solidarity, the economies of greece, ireland, portugal and cyprus would have collapsed, with the huge social consequences that such a collapse would have had. we also significantly reformed our financial sector, from new capital requirements to, more recently, the proposal on the structural reform of banks. we are about to conclude – and i certainly expect the strong support of parliament on this – the banking union which is a significant step in the deepening of economic and monetary union. and finally, we have overhauled the system of economic governance in the european union, particularly in the euro area. this has been done through legislation, co-decided with this parliament, giving us a strong foundation for taking both preventive and, if necessary, corrective action in the future. not only was budgetary surveillance strengthened, but the system was widened to cover macroeconomic imbalances. i think we can say that this was a strong set of achievements, which were possible due to the strong involvement of this house. while some of us would have liked to go further and faster, i believe it is fair to recognise progress in this area. the crisis has given us the political will to make the necessary changes that were politically unattainable and simply unimaginable five years ago! and in the most recent years all this has been done in a coherent european framework which is provided precisely by the european semester. throughout the crisis, the europe 2020 strategy has served as our compass, and the european semester as our main delivery tool. by introducing the european semester, we have ensured that coordination of member state economic policies takes place at european level, respecting of course the national competences. in difficult economic and political times, this has allowed for further transparency, effective dialogue and monitoring. the commission has also proposed that the social dimension be developed as an integral part of european union economic governance. a reinforced surveillance of employment and social developments is now a reality as part and parcel of the european semester. and rightly so. because we know how difficult the situation remains in many member states, especially with unemployment and youth unemployment so high. it is true that improvements in macroeconomic conditions are not yet being felt by citizens themselves and by their families in some of our member states. but at the same time, it would be politically inaccurate and, i think, intellectually dishonest to deny the progress we have made. we have, in short, started down the path of a deep and genuine economic and monetary union to fix the structural faults that lay hidden during the good times, and have now put in place a more sustainable model. these renewed foundations were laid down in just a few years and they play a key role in helping europe emerge from the crisis more resilient for the future and stronger. in all of this, and in spite of many of the debates, we have seen more, and not less, europe – in fact we have seen european integration make progress, particularly in the euro area– with calendars of economic and fiscal reporting and evaluation now synchronised, draft national budgets now seen at a european level, and a stronger role for the european institutions, including the commission. this was possible thanks to many of you in this parliament. honourable members have played a vital role in the european semester from the start. you insisted – and rightly so – on making the so-called six-pack and two-pack legislative, despite initial strong reservations by some governments, and you defended the community method on several key occasions. your role has thus gone far beyond improving the governance structures. along with national parliaments, you have brought democratic legitimacy, accountability and ownership. as we said last year in the blueprint for a deep and genuine economic and monetary union, economic governance, social commitments and democratic legitimacy must move forward hand in hand. tighter economic governance needs tighter democratic control. that is why i was delighted to take part in the european semester week in january which brought members of this parliament together with 140 national parliamentarians. and many of my colleagues in the commission, including both vice-president olli rehn, responsible for economic and monetary affairs, and commissioner lászló andor, responsible for employment, social affairs and inclusion, who are with me here today, actively participated in the economic dialogues you decided to organise. the european semester has not simply been about putting new processes in place. i have to insist on the process because it was, in fact, an innovation and it is important to make sure now that it will be consolidated for the future. but more important than the process is that it has led to concrete and significant fiscal and structural reforms that have helped restore confidence. it has added a strong economic dimension to a range of policies – from taxation, energy, transport, research, climate and environment, to judicial systems. this is very important politically because, as i have already said to you, during the most acute moments of the crisis, the big question that the markets and our partners put to us was not so much about the deficit of this or that country but was about our political will to work together, particularly in the euro area. by putting in place a system of increased coordination, i think europe has shown that there was a will – and there is in fact a will – to learn the lessons from the crisis and to avoid some of the mistakes of the past. i think we can say that the need for sound public finances is now entrenched. this was not the case some years ago. some governments believed that they could go on and on and on spending money that was simply not in their treasuries. deficits have been halved and significant structural reforms for more competitiveness are under way: reforms such as the modernisation of our labour markets and public administrations, or the youth guarantees that are being put in place to ensure that all young people under 25 receive a good quality offer of employment, continued education, an apprenticeship or a traineeship within four months of leaving formal education or becoming unemployed. this is a matter which i believe deserves support – strong support – and a sense of urgency, and governments should now implement the programmes on the ground. i very much welcome many of the recommendations in the reports being debated today. we should continue to look at ways to be more competitive: by making further progress on the single market and adopting the remaining proposals under single market act i and ii, in telecoms, transport, energy and the digital sector; by getting rid of the blockages in business and professional services, retail and construction; by cutting red tape and reducing regulatory burdens; and by improving access to finance for our smes. tax systems should be simplified further and the tax burden redirected away from labour. we should be more resource and energy efficient and invest more in research, innovation and development. because we cannot afford to sit back and relax. not only do we remain exposed to external risks, but we still have a long way to go in our own reforms and in deepening the economic and monetary union. we cannot honestly say that we have exited from the crisis whilst unemployment remains so unacceptably high, especially amongst our younger generation. we have a responsibility to deliver. that is why i want to see the european union budget used to its full potential. we must now get down to the business of extracting the biggest added value from every last euro that has been decided. through the european structural and investment funds, through horizon 2020, through erasmus+ and through the youth employment facility, the european budget focuses on jobs and growth, and it is the main source of investment funds for many of our member states. this budget is indeed a very tangible expression of european solidarity at work. i think it is also important from this parliamentʼs perspective. we all know that in many of our member states people now associate europe with austerity. i think that through the european budget and through the very important funds invested by europe in our regions, we can say that europe can be associated with solidarity because the european union is in fact providing very important resources to the regions that most need to achieve territorial, economic and social cohesion. responsibility to deliver reforms and to make the most of available funds now lies with the member states themselves. but all of us here have a responsibility to explain to europe’s citizens the reason for the reforms, and also to listen to them about the effects of those reforms. let me conclude by saying that we should take heart from what we have achieved so far, remembering where we are now and where we were five years ago, and also thinking about what the alternatives could have been. together we are emerging from the crisis united, open and, i believe, stronger. stronger because we are now preparing a new basis for the competitiveness of europe, because we are now drawing on all the lessons from the globalised world and what being ready to confront our partners in this much more competitive world means. but there is still much more to do under the european semester and europe 2020 strategy. and for those who question our approach and who question whether the european union is part of the solution – i believe that all of us who care about europe should welcome and engage in that debate. because europe does indeed need that political debate. because i believe that a renewed consensus will move us towards greater convergence, solidarity and cohesion. we are stronger together and it is together that we can better achieve our common aims: growth and jobs for europe.

in writing. i voted in favour of the häfner report on the amendment of rule 136 of the rules of procedure on the participation of members in sittings. article 136 of the rules of procedure concerns the attendance sheet. in its present form, it only distinguishes between members who are present at the sitting (on the basis of their signature on this sheet) and those who are not. it therefore takes no account of absences authorised by the president (and governed by the quaestors under rule 31 of the measures implementing the statute for members). the purpose of the proposal to amend rule 136 is to record in the minutes of each sitting the names of members whose absence is excused by the president, with the words 'excused' (for example: maternity or paternity leave).

in writing. i voted in favour of this text which confirms the objective of a maximum co2 emission level of 95g per kilometre for new vehicles sold from 2020 and defines the conditions for the application of this provision. so we set the course, and it's essential for our automotive industry and our climate! however, as early as the debates in the parliament's committee on the environment, i had expressed my scepticism about the level of ambition: the criterion for calculating the distribution of effort between manufacturers should also have been reformed and not the "super-credits" to manufacturers multiplied. i also regret that germany, on the part of the member states, last summer thought it appropriate to challenge the agreement in preparation in order to obtain even more flexibility for its manufacturers. in fact, by adding flexibility to flexibility, we clearly run the risk of discrediting the objectives because we help the manufacturers to circumvent them... finally, although i would have preferred a mechanism with a more restrictive framework and less favourable to the most polluting manufacturers, i am pleased that the union is maintaining its overall ambition to reduce co2 emissions. manufacturers need to be prepared for this, especially with electric vehicles.
in writing. i voted for the ulmer report on co2 emissions from passenger cars, which validates the agreement reached in the trilogue. this agreement confirms the target of 95[nbsp ]g co2/km by 2020 but brings additional flexibilities (95[nbsp ]% of the fleet will have to meet this target at the beginning of 2020, 100[nbsp ]% only at the beginning of 2021, manufacturers will be able to use the "super credits" until 2022).
in writing. the purpose of this text is to amend european legislation in order to enable the european union to achieve the 2020 target for reducing co2 emissions from new passenger cars. the road sector is the second largest source of greenhouse gas emissions in europe. efforts must therefore be made in this area. it is essential that the european union empowers itself to achieve a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by encouraging the production of cleaner and more fuel-efficient vehicles, while avoiding legal uncertainty with adverse effects on competitiveness and employment.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which has the effect of reducing co2 emissions by 2020 for new passenger cars. the environmental constraint is at the heart of this text, which reflects the union's will to make a lasting commitment to reducing co2.
in writing. i voted in favour of this agreement because it is a balanced and pragmatic text, free of the unrealistic objectives that some people want, and will benefit the environment, industry and consumers at the same time. the already very ambitious target of limiting co2 emissions to 95g per kilometre by 2020 was maintained, but with an additional deadline to give manufacturers more flexibility. the latter will also have to revise their test batteries in order to measure the consumption of vehicles more precisely. the mechanism of bonus payments, known as super-credits, has also been preserved. it will be in place until 2022 and allows manufacturers to accumulate 'bonuses' when they bring clean vehicles to market. it is a vital incentive mechanism which must encourage research into the vehicles of tomorrow, a field in which europe cannot afford to lag behind. in the face of the deindustrialization affecting our continent, and as social plans proliferate, i am glad that reason has prevailed. our citizens now expect europe to give priority to jobs and growth.
in writing. while cars are responsible for 12[nbsp]% of co2 emissions in europe, the european parliament has set new targets to reduce car-related pollution by 2020. new cars registered in europe will not be allowed to produce more than 95 grams of co2 per kilometre, compared to the current 130 grams per kilometre. this will reduce our co2 emissions by 15 million tons a year. with this measure we also want to encourage manufacturers to innovate in order to maintain the automobile industry in europe. manufacturers will be given time and flexibility to adapt their designs. while these new technologies come at a cost, they also represent a gain for consumers, who will be able to buy cars that consume only 4 litres of petrol per 100 km. i voted for this because i believe it is important to limit co2 emissions from road transport, which is one of the only sectors where co2 emissions are increasing.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which gives substance to the european target of reducing co2 emissions by 95g per km from new cars by 2020. this ambitious target will save 15 million tonnes of co2 emissions per year. for these savings to be effective, however, a new international test procedure for passenger cars will have to be implemented to take account of real driving conditions.
in writing. with this text, the european union is demonstrating a sad persistence in its policy of ecological inaction and the relegation of ecological issues to green capitalism. it is a text devoid of ambition and offers nothing that is relevant to the challenges of the 21st century. it is not enough to call out loud and loud for technical progress to save the day, thus justifying this lack of ambition and making ecological measures conditional on respect for sacred competition and the sound management of public finances. the fight against global warming requires ambitious and immediate objectives, which include measures to reduce the use of private cars. the large manufacturers must not be spared, as this text does, but must be made to face up to their ecological and social responsibilities. i vote against it.
in writing. the initial objective of this report was to further reduce co2 emissions from new passenger cars. the current limit of 160g co2/km will be reduced to 130g in 2015 and then to 95g from 2020. however, these considerations have resulted in a lack of ecological ambition, notably through the proposal for the 'super-credit', a system allowing manufacturers to artificially lower the average co2 emissions of their fleet by any vehicle emitting less than 50g co2/km. i therefore opposed this report.
in writing. i welcome the outcome of this vote which sets out the ways in which co2 emissions from cars can be reduced to meet the targets. co2 emissions per km will be reduced to 95 by 2020, 95[nbsp]% of cars will be affected and a meeting clause is put in place to establish a new reduction target in 2015 for the post-2020 period.
in writing. the european parliament adopted on 25 february the revision of the legislation on the reduction of co2 emissions from new passenger cars, the target of which, adopted in 2008, is to reach 95 grams of co2/km by 2020. this is a revision for nothing because the revised legislation retains a lot of flexibility to achieve this objective. it does not set a new reduction target for the period after 2020. nothing is done to ensure that the co2 emission levels reported by car manufacturers correspond to the co2 emissions level in real driving situations, with emissions and consumption sometimes being 25%[nbsp ] higher than the advertised figures. supported by the two right-wing groups (epp and ecr), the liberals and the social democrats, this status quo benefits mainly the large-cylinder car manufacturers and does not encourage the automobile industry to innovate and reduce energy consumption. like the gue/ngl, i voted against this missed opportunity to demand a strong commitment from an industry that does not hesitate to call on the community for its restructuring and the social plans it is carrying out in this context[nbsp ] also missed opportunity to make a contribution to the fight against climate change.
in writing. brands play a vital role in today's economic world. they are a source of credibility and confidence for many european products, some of which are exported beyond the borders of the european union. the rules on trade marks must therefore be strengthened and modernised, and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the revision of the european trade mark system. it's a good report.
in writing. with this text, we give the national authorities a wide margin of manoeuvre in the protection of trade marks and the fight against counterfeiting. this is in particular to facilitate cooperation between the internal market authorities and the national authorities while leaving the possibility for the member states to apply their legal framework where they consider it more efficient. i particularly appreciate the desire to prevent attempts to bring counterfeits and counterfeits from third countries into the european territory. these provisions are in the right direction, that of greater protection of european know-how and therefore of the member states.
in writing. globalisation of trade means that europe must constantly keep its enterprises up to date with market developments. by deciding to review its system of protection of community trade marks for its enterprises, in particular for its smes, the union has just corrected a legal vacuum in its legislation. customs authorities will now be able to prohibit the entry into the eu of goods bearing a community registered trade mark without authorisation. the new rules will also make registration cheaper, quicker and provide greater legal certainty. this modernisation of the community trade mark system was essential to cope with unfair competition from companies outside the community. this responds to a growing expectation of the 'trademarks' themselves to be better protected throughout the european territory. in 2012, 107 900 applications were filed, double the number registered by the european trade mark office 10 years earlier. as a reminder, the branded goods industry directly accounts for 21% of employment in europe and 34% of european gdp. it should be noted, however, that only generic medicines should be exempted, in view of the trips agreements of the wto allowing them to benefit from a specific regime.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which is about strengthening the community brand within the european union. i fully support the desire to streamline the procedures for applying for and registering european trade marks, given that national offices receive very few european trade mark applications. i also welcome the desire to increase legal certainty by clarifying certain provisions and removing certain ambiguities, as may be the case, in particular, with the affirmation of a clear definition of the community trade mark.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it will encourage innovation and entrepreneurship by making the systems for registering a community trade mark throughout the union more accessible and more efficient. it was important to reduce the administrative burden of registering trade marks and to streamline procedures to enable union entrepreneurs to innovate and invest in the creation of new trade marks. i am glad to see that this report also includes a reinforcement of legal certainty: the protection of intellectual property is a major issue for french and european companies.
in writing. - i am in favour of the revision of the ohim agency for the protection of a european trade mark, as defined and formulated in this report. in a context of sometimes haphazard regulation, there is a need for our entrepreneurs to feel protected and to see their products compete in global markets. i hope that the changes and improvements proposed for the hmis will really be an additional step for european products and strengthen the union's action in this area, as has already happened with the measure on 'made in'.
in writing. on tuesday 25 february, the european parliament set out new rules on trade marks and goods in transit to make the community trade mark more accessible to businesses in the european union. this european trademark simplifies the procedures and reduces the costs of registering the trademark in the various member states of the european union. i voted in favour of this text because european companies using trade marks represent about 34% of the gross domestic product and 21% of jobs in the european union; it is therefore important to simplify the registration of trade marks and to better protect them against counterfeiting.
in writing. a trademark is used to distinguish the products and services of a company. the laws of the member states on trade marks were partially harmonised by a directive in 1988 and then codified in 2008. in parallel with the national trademark systems, an autonomous system of unitary rights registration has been established, which produces the same effects throughout the european union. the community trade mark system and the office for harmonization in the internal market (ohim) are responsible for providing assistance to trade mark and design actors in europe. the aim is to modernise the way in which community trade marks operate by means of legal harmonisation. the report proposes to involve parliament more closely in this procedure, in particular by reducing the number of delegated acts. i do not think that the introduction of these new rules will be a good thing, but i think that the commission should be aware of the fact that the new rules are not being applied in the same way as the old ones.
in writing. the commission presented at the end of march 2013 the proposal for the revision of the trade mark system in europe, which we adopted today. in less than a year we have reached a clear and balanced position. in this vote we have succeeded in restoring the balance broken by the court of justice in its nokia/philips judgment. the commission will be able to monitor goods which are in transit through the territory of the european union without being marketed there. it is important and legitimate for the eu to protect its citizens from goods that may harm their health or safety. it must also be able to guarantee its undertakings the highest degree of protection against the circulation of counterfeit products.
in writing. i voted in favour of the macovei report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the freezing and confiscation of the proceeds from crime in the european union. the main objective is to combat the mafia and the parallel economy of illicit networks. if this money were to be returned to the national budgets, there would be no more debt in europe, given the sums at stake.
in writing. this text takes bold action at eu and member state level in confiscating and freezing the proceeds of crime. we can count on the mutual recognition of decisions by states in this area to prevent and combat crossborder crime. these are the provisions necessary to combat criminal activities, not only at the level of the states but also in the field of cross-border cooperation.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because, at a time when crime is reaching dangerous proportions in the european union, a strong reaction from the european union was needed. i therefore support the obligation on member states to allow the freezing of assets or instruments which are liable to be lost, hidden or transferred outside their jurisdiction, with a view to their possible subsequent confiscation. nevertheless, in the context of fair trial, i welcome the measures which are designed to guarantee respect for the presumption of innocence, the right to access to an impartial tribunal.
in writing. i fully supported the adoption of minimum harmonisation rules on the freezing and confiscation of proceeds of crime, as it is unacceptable that the bulk of the illicit profits made by organised crime should subsequently be reinjected into perfectly legal activities with impunity. it is a particularly useful tool for the return of criminal assets to public authorities. i also defended the provisions to create the possibility of reusing confiscated assets for social purposes, as is already the case in italy or ireland. the directive marks a clear step forward in the fight against organised and financial crime, but it is only the first step. the commission will shortly present a new proposal to harmonise the possibilities for confiscating illicit proceeds without a criminal conviction, a measure which has proved effective in countries such as italy, ireland, bulgaria and slovakia.
in writing. on tuesday 25 february, the european parliament adopted legislation to improve the efficiency of the freezing and confiscation of the proceeds of crime. i voted in favour of this text because i believe that the member states of the european union do not use this tool sufficiently to fight organised crime, whereas the proceeds of crime amounted to no less than us$2.1 billion in 2009. the european parliament has therefore adopted rules to extend the confiscation powers of the member states. we've authorized the forfeiture of property acquired by a convicted person in connection with all of his criminal activities, including those for which he has not yet been convicted. we have also harmonised european legislation to allow all member states to confiscate the assets of a third party who hides the property of a convicted person. finally, assets can be frozen without waiting for a court order in an emergency to prevent criminals from taking the proceeds of their crime.
in writing. i voted in favour of the directive to strengthen the rules on confiscation of criminal assets. robin hood stole from the rich to give to the poor; with this bill, we confiscate from the mobs to redistribute to the citizens. confiscation is the most effective way we have of cutting off the grass under the feet of criminal and mafia networks. for all they care about is the profit they make from their illegal activities. money is always the lifeblood of war. and the millions of euros they accumulate are still at the expense of honest citizens.
in writing. the most effective method of combating organised crime is through severe legal consequences and effective detection and seizure and confiscation of the instruments and proceeds of crime. this directive lays down minimum rules for member states concerning the freezing and confiscation of assets of criminal origin by means of the following measures: direct confiscation, confiscation in value, extended confiscation, confiscation in the absence of a conviction and confiscation of assets of third parties. the national laws are unequal and therefore require appropriate harmonisation, if only to ensure full enforcement of confiscation. the adoption of these minimum rules will harmonise the freezing and confiscation regimes in force in the member states, thus enhancing mutual trust and the effectiveness of cross-border cooperation. the commission will also take steps to strengthen the mutual recognition of freezing and confiscation orders, an important aspect of the fight against serious crossborder organised crime within the union. i vote for it.
in writing. this report concerns the european commission's proposal for a directive of 12 march on the freezing and confiscation of the proceeds of crime in the european union. this directive lays down minimum rules for the member states in this field by means of direct confiscation, confiscation in value, extended confiscation, confiscation in the absence of a conviction and confiscation of assets of third parties. these minimum rules will make it possible to start harmonising the systems in force in the 28 eu member states. they will make progress towards the mutual recognition of freezing and confiscation decisions, which are important aspects of progress in the fight against organised crime. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. organized crime, which knows no borders and is increasingly international, is primarily driven by profit. the fight against this crime, if it is to be effective, should therefore add to the serious legal consequences for criminals the effective neutralization of the related gains made through crime. yet, today less than 1 percent of the proceeds of crime - drug trafficking, counterfeiting, human trafficking, and small arms trafficking - are frozen and confiscated. sending criminals to jail while letting dirty money circulate is unacceptable! the purpose of this text, which i supported in today's vote, is to facilitate the confiscation of criminal assets in the eu. the new provisions include that member states must allow the confiscation of criminal assets following a final conviction, including where the convicted person is ill or has absconded; may confiscate assets acquired through criminal acts related to child pornography, cybercrime, or active or passive corruption in the private or public sector; must consider measures to enable confiscated property to be used for public or social purposes.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report because this dossier is a good example of the active role of the european parliament in the institutional game. the proposal for a directive was announced by the european commission after the adoption in 2011 of a report by the european parliament calling for effective regulation of asset forfeiture. the adoption of these minimum rules will harmonise the freezing and confiscation regimes in force in the member states, thus enhancing mutual trust and the effectiveness of cross-border cooperation. the commission will also take steps to strengthen the mutual recognition of freezing and confiscation orders, an important aspect of the fight against serious crossborder organised crime within the union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text on the confiscation of assets of organised crime. it is a very important text because it will enable the european union to better combat the activities of organised crime which, as many europol reports show, are on the increase within the european union. the assets of these mafia groups, obtained illegally, can now be more easily confiscated by the police following a conviction. all confiscated property will then be used for public benefit or social purposes. the amount of these earnings and related assets is estimated to be several hundred billion euros in the eu. currently, only 1[nbsp ]% of these assets are subject to confiscation. we must strike organized crime where it hurts, by attacking its profits!

in writing. the european parliament, by adopting this directive on the laws of the member states relating to trade marks, intends to combat counterfeiting. a trade mark registered in a member state may prevent the importation of counterfeit goods into the european union; however, it will not be able to prevent the transit of counterfeit goods through the european union if the trade mark is not registered in the country of final destination. i voted in favour of these new rules, which do not impede international trade but allow for better control of goods entering the union. the protection of european consumers is essential, as a large proportion of counterfeit goods are everyday consumer goods, such as cigarettes or medicines.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the european union agency for law enforcement cooperation and training (europol). it aims to bring europol in line with the requirements of the lisbon treaty by establishing a mechanism for monitoring its activities by the european parliament, in association with national parliaments, and to ensure a robust data protection regime. the report also opposes the merger of europol with the european police college.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to amend the legislation applicable to europol, the european union agency for law enforcement cooperation and training, in order to bring it into line with the provisions of the lisbon treaty and to give it new responsibilities. in view of the increase in organised crime in europe, it is important to equip the european union with the appropriate instruments to combat this phenomenon. it is right to stress that effective cooperation between member states and law enforcement agencies is essential. however, i felt it was essential to put in place a strict framework to ensure a strong regime for the protection of personal data when they are transmitted to europol by the member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which relates to the creation of the european union agency for law enforcement cooperation and training. in the present day, when crime is playing out across borders, it is essential to set up european training and exchange programmes for all law enforcement professionals. finally, i welcome the intention of this text to improve the governance of europol in the interests of greater efficiency.
in writing. by voting for this report, i opposed a proposed merger of europol and the european police college, proposed by the european commission, under the pretext of budget cuts but without proving the real benefits, and taking the risk of sacrificing the quality of the training provided. i also support the strengthening of democratic control of europol, as this is a recurrent demand of the european parliament, which would be achieved by the creation of a parliamentary control unit bringing together meps and national meps. unlike the epp rapporteur on this matter, i am particularly opposed to giving europol direct access to the personal data of our citizens. on the contrary, through the various amendments i have supported a strengthened personal data protection regime, thus taking into account the concerns expressed by the european data protection supervisor.
in writing. given the transnational dimension of crime, genuine european cooperation has become necessary to solve cases that are no longer purely national in scope. europol was created to bring together national police forces and coordinate their efforts. this agency is one of the concrete manifestations of what europe can do to fight crime, mafia networks and protect european citizens. however, up to now the european parliament has had little control over this agency and its objective, in the context of the negotiations on its statute and its tasks, is to restore the democratic legitimacy of europol, whose actions are unfortunately not recognised. the house also called for the commission to be given the power to adopt legislative proposals to improve the quality of the information it receives from the public. i would like to see europol given all the means it needs to carry out its tasks successfully and without hindrance. the protection and security of citizens must be the cardinal principles of the negotiations now under way between parliament and the council.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a directive to improve the efficiency and strengthen the monitoring of the activities of europol, whose role is to support the action of national law enforcement services and their mutual cooperation in the fight against serious crime and terrorism. the european parliament, in association with national parliaments, will now have to scrutinise the agency's accounts, be consulted on europol's multiannual work programme and hear its executive director. we have also taken several steps to improve cooperation between member states and europol so that the agency can facilitate information exchange and increase the efficiency of european intelligence. we have, however, put in place a number of safeguards to protect the data and privacy of citizens. finally, training activities for police forces will be strengthened and improved, in particular in the fight against cybercrime. i voted in favour of this text because it will make the fight against crime more effective, while ensuring the proper management of the europol agency and respect for the rights of citizens.
in writing. the mission of europol, as set out in article[nbsp ]88 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, is 'to support and strengthen the action of the police and other law enforcement authorities of the member states and their mutual cooperation in preventing and combating serious crime affecting two or more member states, terrorism and forms of crime which affect a common interest which is the subject of a union policy'. europol provides the exchange of information and intelligence on crime between law enforcement agencies in the member states (potentially very large personal data) and provides expertise and technical support. he also cooperates with the fbi (exchange of information, etc.). the aim is to extend europol's scope of application and give it greater operational autonomy vis-à-vis the states in line with the stockholm programme, an open and secure europe that serves and protects citizens . the report also proposes to allow access to private databases. i vote against it.
in writing. europol (european police office) is an intergovernmental criminal police office that facilitates the exchange of information between national police forces on drugs, terrorism, international crime and paedophilia within the european union. the report endorses the commission's proposal to increase europol's powers by increasing its powers and exchanges of information and by enhancing its independence. nevertheless, some interesting amendments have been made to make these changes more relative. the most significant concerns a strengthening of the protection of private data and the independence of europol, which is tempered by a strengthening of the powers of the ms authorities. the rapporteur also rejected the merger of europol and ecpol (european police college) following pressure from a majority of groups. although the report has thus been improved, i regret the weakening of europol's control over the protection of personal data. i therefore abstained from voting.
in writing. i abstained on the european parliament's report on the european union agency for police cooperation and training (europol). while european police cooperation may be necessary for a number of crimes and offences, it must be done in a way that respects the rights of citizens. the text adopted by the european parliament does not seem to me to provide the necessary guarantees and may be worrying. europol will now have almost total autonomy with relatively limited control by the member states and will de facto constitute a kind of supranational police. moreover, at a time when the prism nsa case has revealed to the world the capabilities of widespread surveillance by states, the issue of data protection is essential. this text opens up new possibilities for the collection of personal data at european level without the necessary guarantees being provided to european citizens. i welcome the rejection of an amendment by the european right which would have opened up additional possibilities for access to private sources. the european parliament's report seems to me to fall far short of what might be expected and even short of what is already in place.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report which sets out the conditions for entry and residence for more than 3 months for third-country nationals for the purposes of research, studies, pupil exchange, training, voluntary work and au pairs. to remain competitive, the european union must attract the best students and researchers, while ensuring that working conditions are sufficiently regulated to prevent such a workforce from creating unfair competition in the european labour market. this directive updates european legislation by extending it to trainees and au pairs. it also provides for simplification of admission procedures and reduction of response times for researchers in order to make emigration more attractive for highly qualified people. students and researchers will have the possibility to stay in the member state for 12 months after the end of their studies or research to look for work or to set up a business. however, we have imposed many conditions to verify the validity of applications for residence permits: documents to be provided, proof of means of subsistence, health insurance, etc.

in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report which provides a legal framework that is both safe and virtuous with regard to the conditions of entry and residence of non-european nationals. the idea is obviously not to decide whether to open or close our borders. europe has historically been a land of transit and reception, and the eu's humanist values forbid us from turning in on ourselves. it is really a question of focusing on the mobility of socio-professional categories which are strategic for the european economy and for the economies of our neighbours: students, researchers, academics and business tourists. the report does not grant indefinite residence permits or unlimited travel, but sets out clear rules: anyone who wants to come to europe to study, teach or do business is welcome for a certain period of time. i have always been opposed to community practices which would lead, for example, to condoning the brain drain of young people from the countries of the southern mediterranean: to welcome students from the maghreb for the duration of their studies, yes, but not to deprive our mediterranean partners of their vital forces!

in writing. volunteering is a concrete and visible expression of solidarity which allows individuals to devote their knowledge, skills and time to the service of others without financial motivation. the idea of the european voluntary humanitarian corps is to enable citizens of the union to provide practical support to people affected by natural or humanitarian disasters around the world. or even to meet the needs of organizations that are already working in the field. in the first phase, for the period 2014-2020, this programme could involve 10,000 volunteers. in concrete terms, the commission will develop european standards for the management of volunteers involved in humanitarian projects, as well as a european training programme. after training, the volunteers will be sent out to serve in the world. a network will be set up to enable them to exchange experiences and support each other before, during and after the interventions. others will also be able to participate in these projects through online volunteering (to support volunteers already on the ground or to help humanitarian organisations by working from home). i welcome this initiative which is in the direction of a people's europe and the promotion of our values.

in writing. in 2012, the european commission adopted a proposal for a regulation on the establishment of the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps (eu aid volunteers). these volunteers will be deployed in humanitarian aid operations in third countries following man-made crises or natural disasters, excluding the contexts of armed conflict and internal unrest. for once, it is about promoting solidarity, but at a low cost. instead of calling into question the union's policies at the root of humanitarian crises or sending in people who are really trained (doctors, educators, etc.), we will send our young people, who are paid little or nothing, to look for a soul mate. i'm not going to do this charade.
in writing. this report concerns the proposal for a european commission regulation on the establishment of the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps (eu aid volunteers). this effective and visible humanitarian corps should contribute to strengthening the union's capacity to respond to humanitarian crises in third countries. this is the number of people to be deployed over the period 2014-2020. these volunteers will receive a specific training programme to prepare them for their assignment. the report proposes to grant these young people the status of 'certified eu aid volunteers' at the end of their first deployment. an interim evaluation report is also planned, assessing the impact of eu aid volunteers in the humanitarian aid sector and the cost-effectiveness of the programme. this voluntary programme will strengthen european solidarity with regions in difficulty, while providing volunteers with a most enriching human experience. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. this report is above all an expression of the union's humanitarian values and its solidarity with people in need. it shall thereby contribute to strengthening the union's capacity to respond to humanitarian crises. the aim is to ensure that volunteers bring real added value as their deployment will be based on identified needs in the field and their role will be clearly defined. i have also decided that the deployment of volunteers will not be carried out in conflict zones, but only in countries affected by natural disasters. participation in this voluntary corps is open to all european citizens, regardless of age or professional or academic qualifications. i have also decided to open this programme to retired people who can bring real added value to the field through their various professional experiences, for example. i wanted this body to respect diversity and to benefit as many people as possible. i would also like to stress that this initiative will help to fill some of the gaps in current humanitarian volunteering and will also contribute to raising public awareness and the idea of european citizenship.

in writing. in 2011, almost 120 million europeans, or nearly a quarter of the total european population, were at risk of poverty or social exclusion. in the face of such a social emergency, the creation of a european fund for aid to the most deprived (fead) was essential. it is one of the only solidarity instruments in the european union that is directed at the poorest and it is a concrete expression of europe's commitment to solidarity with its most vulnerable citizens. for the period 2014-2020, the fead will be appropriately endowed, i.e. at an amount not below the current level of the fund. it will also retain its mandatory character, i.e. if member states decide not to use the fund, the budget must remain available for the poorest. it is essential to show citizens that the fight against poverty and social exclusion is at the heart of the european union's objectives.

in writing. i voted in favour of the groote report on the proposal for a regulation on the making available on the market and use of biocidal products, as regards certain conditions for market access. biocidal products are a group of products intended to destroy, repel or render harmless harmful organisms, to prevent their action or to combat them by chemical or biological action. the main objective of this regulation is to ensure a high level of protection of humans, animals and the environment by limiting the placing on the market of only effective biocidal products presenting acceptable risks and by encouraging the placing on the market of active substances presenting less risks.

in writing. european legislation is now negotiated on an equal footing by the european parliament and the council of ministers of the european union in almost all cases. only taxation is still the subject of legislation adopted by the council, after simple consultation of the european parliament. however, when the two co-legislators (the european parliament and the council) legislate, they sometimes decide to entrust the european commission with the task of supplementing, detailing or updating certain parts of legislation. this is the delegation of legislative powers and the exercise of implementing powers by the european commission. i voted in favour of this report because it recalls the essential role of the co-legislators and the need to limit but also to allocate properly, on the one hand, the delegation of legislative powers and, on the other hand, the exercise of implementing powers by the european commission. in any case, the european parliament and the council must remain vigilant and closely follow the measures proposed by the european commission in order to block them in the event of disagreement.

the committee on regional development has tabled a number of amendments to the proposal. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as a native of perpignan, a town on the border between france and spain, i am well aware of the problems posed by the lack of compatibility between rail systems in europe. for a long time, we had to change trains to cross the border. we opened the perpignan-barcelona line at the end of 2013 with four years of delay, mainly due to technical interoperability problems. the reform we are voting on tomorrow is essential. it will enable a train to run indiscriminately on any railway section throughout europe. the goal is to reduce the 11,000 national security regulations. the european railway agency will become the one-stop shop for all vehicle authorisations in order to avoid discrimination and unjustified delays. it will mainly open up border regions and make the territories more attractive. if we want real mobility in a european railway area that is efficient, the member states must open up, modernise and stop defending their own interests. it is the concrete europe that we are defending.
for the greens/efa group mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, outside the european railway workers are expressing their discontent with the fourth railway package. they're worried, and i think we can understand them. they are concerned that the public service will be undermined and dismantled by an open market without social rules. the commission's objective of opening up the market must not have the effect of weakening the quality of supply while lowering the working conditions of those involved in the railway sector. this fourth package inevitably involves technical progress with a view to establishing a european railway system. the technical pillar, which was unanimously approved by the committee, will greatly improve interoperability and cross-border relations. the regulation on public service obligations, under the auspices of rapporteur mathieu grosch, also found points of convergence, despite an initial proposal by the commission which was unacceptable because, as is too often the case, it was too dogmatic. the social aspect is thus taken into account and the re-employment of staff is now firmly established. thus, the position of users and the qualitative indicators of supply are also taken into account, which makes it possible today to make a direct conditional allocation. as regards the report by mr grosch, however, i strongly disagree with the question of reciprocity, which is taken out of the general context to penalise specifically a french company, a wholly independent subsidiary of sncf. on this point, i want to make it very clear that there is both a miscalculation and a political error. i believe that a wholly financially independent subsidiary which does not enjoy a monopoly cannot be prevented from applying in any member state on the european continent. finally, as regards the governance of the railway system, the rapporteur responsible for this issue has unfortunately not changed the commission's proposal, which clearly hinders the possibility of establishing an integrated model, even if it guarantees completely transparent financial rules between the infrastructure manager and an operator, historical as it may be. in the same report, i deeply regret that public service contracts are being jeopardised by open access, whereas previous legislation allowed them to be protected. commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, as you can see, i believe that this fourth package contains real technical advances, but that the political aspects are not taken into account. this makes my analysis of the work done mixed and will lead my group to express reservations on a number of points, which i have just mentioned.
mr president, i should like to begin by addressing the question of opening up to competition and public service contracts. i would like to make two main points here: firstly, transport authorities the third action programme in the field of health for 2014-2020 is finally operational. i would remind you that the european commission's proposal was dated 9 november 2011, and that we had adopted the regulation in the parliamentary committee on 24 april 2012. i would like to thank all the fictitious rapporteurs, the european commission and the various presidencies of the european union which have succeeded each other in reaching an agreement today. the first issue was budgetary, and the european parliament has tried throughout the negotiations to stress that the financial crisis has made the need to improve the efficiency of our health systems even more pressing. more than ever, we need to think of health as an investment in the future, not as a cost or a variable for adjusting social budgets. the sector must be a lever for growth and job creation in this period of crisis and emerge as a real pillar of the european economy. the european commission had earmarked eur 446 million for the budget of this third health programme. today, we have a budget of almost 450 million over seven years, for the period 2014-2020. this amount is still too small, of course, in view of the health challenges posed by the ageing of the european population, but we have managed to save it from budget cuts. this is also a significant increase of [nbsp]5.7%[nbsp] compared to the second health programme. this budget will co-finance potential applicants for funding, who will have to respond to calls for projects in areas where eu action can bring real added value in the health sector. the european parliament has been keen to ensure that this third health programme makes the best use of the resources available. four priority objectives were therefore defined: preventing diseases by addressing the main risk factors (smoking, alcohol abuse, sedentary lifestyle, poor dietary behaviour); to protect citizens from serious cross-border health threats; to contribute to the creation of innovative and sustainable health systems; and to improve access to better and safer healthcare for all union citizens. parliament also requested that the european commission submit a mid-term evaluation report on the achievement of these objectives by 30[nbsp ]june[nbsp ]2017. as regards the objective of prevention, i wished [nbsp ]and this is reflected in the agreement[nbsp ] that the main risk factors should be better identified in order to put more emphasis on prevention: smoking, drug use, alcohol abuse, poor diet and sedentary lifestyle. more effective prevention will increase the sustainability of our health care systems. many projects funded in schools to improve food education have had positive results. this type of project should therefore be continued in the new programme. i also wanted, together with my fictitious colleagues, to see the programme put more emphasis on ageing-related diseases. these diseases are affecting more and more people. more than 7 million people in europe suffer from some form of dementia. this has serious health, economic and social consequences. action is therefore imperative on both prevention and innovation. this process presents a number of issues and challenges, both for the economy and for society. by preserving the health of the individual and his ability to remain active, both physically and socially, for as long as possible, we can maximise its positive impact on productivity and competitiveness. in conclusion, improving the health of our elderly will not only save them from the aging-related suffering but also reduce the social and medical costs borne by society. this is a major challenge which we must anticipate at european level because it cannot be met sufficiently by the member states.

in writing. my report presents a set of pragmatic solutions to increase the participation of the outermost regions (ors) in all eu funds and programmes. it called on the european commission to work on solutions to bring the ors out of their isolation and recalled that the ors can make a significant contribution to achieving the objectives that the european union has set itself by 2020. this is a reversal of the approach which i asked the european parliament to support by putting forward a proactive vision, focused on the future, research, innovation, job creation and the fight against youth unemployment. i voted in favour of my report, which was adopted by a very large majority (446 votes in favour, 73 against and 47 abstentions). at the end of the parliamentary term, this vote is a strong political signal for the ors sent by all meps.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report on the outermost regions. this report rightly highlights the role that these overseas regions can play, particularly in research and innovation at european level. the outermost regions can serve as european laboratories and centres of excellence in several sectors. it is therefore important that all european funds and programmes are used in an appropriate way, promoting synergies. i regret, however, that the report does not call for more synergies with the overseas countries and territories which share many of the same characteristics and problems as the outermost regions.
in writing. the outermost regions are an integral part of the european union. they are a real asset to the european presence throughout the world. these regions have remarkable research and technology potential in a number of areas such as aerospace, renewable energy and maritime research. however, they are among the regions of europe that suffer from very high unemployment rates, particularly among young people. the flight of skills is common in the outermost regions, due to high unemployment rates and the inadequacy of the training offered. the european union must not in any case abandon these regions, but must help them to face the challenges they face. i am therefore very pleased to have voted in favour of this report. it proposes to extend the scope of the union's solidarity-based mutual assistance to them so that they become an integral part of eu strategies and policies. although remote, these regions are still european and must be treated as such.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my colleague and friend from the gue/ngl, younous omarjee, on optimising the development of the potential of the outermost regions (ors) by creating synergies between the structural funds and other european union programmes. the very technical name implies that the aim is to improve the integration of the outermost regions into all european policies, in particular by promoting a more sustainable approach to development. this report is a good initiative, since it is a reminder to the institutions that the ors can no longer be put on the sidelines and seen as a handicap by those who are shaping the european union of tomorrow. to this end, the report calls on the commission to examine the additional costs and the problem of the high cost of living in the ors and to take them into account in the formulation of european policies. it also called for better accessibility in the outermost regions, in particular by reducing the digital divide, and for a number of measures to be implemented, such as the creation of an investment framework for social housing to combat poverty and exclusion in the outermost regions.
in writing. i voted for the theurer report on the performance-based evaluation of the union's finances: a new tool for the european commission's improved discharge procedure. in accordance with article 318, the commission shall draw up an annual report on this matter. in so far as it focuses on financial results, this evaluation report complements the approach to compliance developed by the european court of auditors. it gives parliament the opportunity to assess political achievements, not just the legality of financial transactions.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this text, which gives concrete expression to the application of a new tool introduced by the treaty on the functioning of the european union in the budgetary discharge procedure. it enables the european parliament to exercise its power of political control over european public policy more effectively when assessing the union's finances. i think it is particularly important that parliament should insist that the commission should rely on accurate information for the performance of the member states when assessing the finances.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which makes it possible to assess the european union's finances in a sound manner. i can therefore only share the desire to strengthen the culture of performance applicable to the financial management of the union. this will prepare the way for the transition to a truly performance-oriented budget.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the evaluation of the union's finances, which is a new instrument for budgetary discharge with a report provided by the european commission on the evaluation of the union's finances. in order to provide parliament with relevant information as discharge authority, the commission report should provide cross-cutting information to measure the results of internal policies in relation to the europe 2020 strategic objective.
in writing. this non-legislative report praises the efforts of the barroso commission to assess the impact of european union spending. he refers to a hallucinatory statement by josé manuel barroso in 2011. the president of the commission had said that the european budget would now be determined not on the basis of the traditional headings determined by the bureaucracy and the electorate, but by taking into account the facts and objectives [...], so as to make the best possible use of every euro spent . this technocratic and anti-democratic profession of faith sums up the spirit of the 'results' and 'spending' evaluation which this report advocates. this assessment is illegitimate if the objectives assessed are not determined democratically. if general interest objectives were set, for example in terms of social progress or equality in public services, the record of this commission would be disastrous. to be at last at the service of the people, the union's finances must be completely re-funded democratically, like the rest of the treaties. this is the fundamental condition for citizens to consent once again to the european legal order which they now massively reject. i am voting against this undemocratic report.

in writing. whether for business, personal or tourist reasons, europeans are increasingly crossing the borders of their home countries to travel to other eu countries. the idea of a european-wide on-board emergency call system is therefore a good one. however, i have serious problems with the text proposed by the commission and parliament. firstly, i am firmly opposed to any delegation of public service, particularly in such a crucial area as road safety. secondly, the proposed differentiation between emergency and distress calls could be used as a pretext for a reduction in investment in ecall (and therefore in its effectiveness) as part of the austerity policies imposed on europe by the troika and mrs merkel. thirdly, as not all europeans speak globish , it would be wise to provide a permanent translation service within the ecall service. no matter what the cost of such a measure is, human life is not precious. good ideas, bad solutions: i vote against it.
in writing. e-call is an initiative of the european commission to eventually introduce a pan-european automatic emergency call system based on a public service in all vehicles sold in the eu, allowing for example a crashed car to instantly call emergency services while sending its precise location, whether its occupants are conscious or not, and regardless of the eu country it is in. this system, based on 112, thus allows for a faster intervention by the emergency services, adapted to the severity of the accident and the type of vehicle involved. it is expected that passenger cars and light commercial vehicles will be equipped with them from october 2015, with the exception of two-wheelers. at present, only 0.7% of vehicles are equipped with such a system. the report provides that the service will be free of charge, ensures that the data collected is only for traffic control and rescue purposes and plans to launch a campaign to raise awareness among motorists. i am convinced that the widespread use of this system will save lives and i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. with the opening of borders and the creation of a single market where european citizens are free to move around in all member states, many europeans are forced to travel all over europe. we have to make sure they're safe. the ecall system allows you to reach the nearest emergency services from any point in europe with a single number. the report proposes a regulatory approach to ensure the gradual mandatory presence of ecall in all vehicles. this will help to speed up the rescue of the person in danger. i am glad that i voted in favour of this report. a more effective approach will, i believe, save many lives.
in writing. in 2012, there were more than one million accidents on european roads, resulting in approximately 28 000 deaths and more than 1.5 million injuries. in addition to the lives lost or destroyed, this tragedy also represents an annual cost to society of about 130 billion euros. the eu is strongly committed to reducing the number of road accidents and mitigating their consequences. when fully operational across the eu and available to every driver, ecall will make a significant contribution to achieving these objectives. its main advantage is the reduction in the number of road deaths and the severity of injuries caused by road accidents, as the emergency services arrive at the scene of accidents more quickly. i could therefore only support this report by my vote in plenary.
in writing. the purpose of this legislation is to deploy the infrastructure of interoperable ecall call centres throughout the european union. the ecall system is an electronic emergency call system in the event of an accident installed on passenger and light commercial vehicles. this text will allow for the mandatory deployment of the system by member states on 1 october 2015 to allow the handling of ecalls. in order to finance the system, in the usual liberal logic within the eu, it is permissible to use public-private partnerships and private calling services. i therefore voted against this legislative proposal which was adopted by a large majority in the european parliament. while it is a laudable intention to prevent emergency services from being dispatched quickly in the event of an accident, it is an illusion to believe that technological measures will be sufficient to remedy the decline in public emergency services, which is a consequence of liberal policies and austerity measures. under the guise of improving the safety of drivers and passengers in vehicles, it is feared that the protection of personal data and respect for the privacy of individuals will be a win-win situation.
in writing. i welcome today's vote on the deployment of ecall: it is a real leap forward for road safety. in the event of a serious road accident, the ecall system in each vehicle will automatically dial the emergency number 112, and all new vehicle models sold in the european union from october 2015 will have to be equipped with it. this system will not prevent accidents, but it can make a significant contribution to reducing the number of road deaths. the ecall we have obtained today will be a free public emergency service for all drivers in europe, regardless of the type of car they are driving: the main benefit of the system is that it immediately alerts the emergency services to the precise location of the accident site. we can be pleased with the vote we have obtained today, but this result should not obscure the work still to be done on the implementation of the "112" system, particularly in the area of call location, on which the proper functioning of ecall depends in every respect. the ball is now in the court of the member states!

in writing. applied to all goods and services of everyday consumption, value added tax (vat) is used in all european countries as a broad-based tax source. at present there is no common framework for its collection and administrative processing, which regularly leads to errors and unfortunately to fraud. the european commission has put forward a proposal to make the collection of the levy more efficient, in particular by reducing the paperwork involved in its collection and adopting a standardised format at european level to facilitate trade between member states. the objective of this text, which i voted for, is to save time for vat returns, to avoid errors or to be able to correct them easily, and to increase the capacity of the tax administrations of the member states to carry out checks. i hope that our businesses and our member states will soon feel the positive effects.

in writing. greece is one of the member states experiencing one of the highest migratory pressures in europe due to its geographical location. although in the third quarter of 2013 the agency frontex recognised an explosion in the number of illegal immigrants in bulgaria (+600% since 2012), italy (+380%) and hungary (+260%), greece remains the second country most affected by waves of illegal immigration. this called for urgent cooperation with turkey, whose negotiations had been dragging on since 2002. it is now done and i am glad of it. with the readmission agreement, the union establishes a new form of cooperation based on full reciprocity with the obligation to readmit turkish nationals and their families if they have not obtained a right of residence in the applicant state, as well as third-country nationals and stateless persons. dialogue with source and transit countries is an essential condition for combating illegal immigration. the national response to the regulation of migration flows is necessarily european. it is by being in europe that france can influence migration policy. outside, she'll only suffer.

in writing. despite highlighting some positive effects, such as the expected decrease in cross-border trafficking in human beings, this reciprocal agreement between the european union and turkey aims to deprive irregular migrants of their rights by applying simplified and expeditious return procedures to their country of origin. the obligation to readmit nationals also covers family members, i.e. spouse and minor unmarried children. i vote against this agreement which denies basic human rights.
in writing. turkey is the main transit country for illegal immigration into the european union. it is therefore essential to reach an agreement with turkey to provide for the return of illegal immigrants to turkey or to the third country. it is of course unthinkable that the european union should become a strainer. we therefore need specific regulations in this area to prevent any illegal entry into european territory. i therefore support this readmission agreement with turkey and am very pleased to have voted in favour of this report. however, in these negotiations turkey has behaved in an unacceptable manner. the eu will only ratify the agreement if the eu introduces concrete measures to facilitate the issuing of visas. the european commission has already taken a step towards turkey by drawing up an action plan in this area and now turkey wants more. we cannot afford to respond to such blackmail, especially when an agreement like this benefits both parties. europe must not let itself be dictated to in any way.
in writing. i voted against this recommendation of the european parliament on the readmission agreement between the european union and turkey. it is regrettable that the european parliament has voted in favour of such an agreement which is aimed at strengthening the european fortress and consolidating turkey's role as the european union's super-gendarme on migration. the european parliament is fully aware of the policies of the erdogan government. ngos have alerted us to the dramatic situation of migrants in turkey. this agreement is no longer a concern for migrants and asylum seekers who are in transit through turkey or seeking refuge there. the protection of their rights is almost non-existent and varies according to the actual or supposed political, cultural or religious affiliations of migrants. this agreement is dangerous and will only increase human rights violations in a country which already has a serious record in this area. this agreement is all the more regrettable because the european union has not agreed, in return, to liberalize visas for turkish nationals, which is just a road map and not a proper agreement.

in writing. this report provides a framework for opening up rail passenger transport to competition and sets out the rules for better governance, in particular between the infrastructure manager and the railway undertakings. i supported this report, which, following the vote in plenary, takes up the french, german and italian proposals. the result is a strict framework for opening up to competition: transparency rules allow fair access to the network for a new company, but the arrival of a new entrant can be stopped if it threatens the viability of an existing public service contract. several safeguards are also provided for in respect of respect for collective agreements and the transfer of staff in the event of market opening. in addition, the states remain free to choose the mode of organization and the degree of openness of their network, the modes of organization in the form of a holding company or under that of a historical company retaining close links with the infrastructure manager as in france, are guaranteed. finally, an integrated european ticketing system must be developed for the benefit of passengers.
