in writing. - the report by mr el khadraoui is part of the fourth railway package which we have discussed a great deal in recent months. more than 50% of the european railway market is not free and rail transport within the european union still faces many technical barriers. there is a clear need to improve crossborder cooperation between operators in the sector, to ensure that all vehicles do not violate social standards and to increase the share of rail transport compared with other modes of transport. the opening up of the market must be accompanied by strict rules on passenger rights and the protection of workers, without neglecting the importance of a proper balance between the need to open up to competition and the protection of the public service obligations of each member state.

in writing. i voted against the el khadraoui report on the 'single european railway area' because it confirms a logic of complete competition which runs counter to the public service. this 'governance' aspect of the rail package aims at complete organisational, financial and human separation between the network and the provision of rail services. this separation, designed to encourage the entry of new competitors to sncf on the market, calls into question an entire organisational model, industrial culture, know-how and all the synergies that arise from it in the name of competition. opening up to competition will bring nothing to the users, let alone the railway workers. on the contrary, it is the predominance of commercial logic over that of public service that is organized by this text. the less profitable lines will be served less or even abandoned, prices will rise and the quality of service will decline with the refusal to make the necessary investments. i reject this ambition and regret the commission's lack of flexibility in its desire to open up the rail market and its lack of respect for existing national organisational models, so i voted against this report.

in writing. the report by mathieu grosch (epp, belgium) is one of the central pillars of the fourth railway package. the report also calls for a wide-ranging opening up of the markets for passenger transport, following the liberalization of international freight and passenger transport. one of the measures proposed by the european commission is the prohibition of direct award of contracts by local authorities to railway undertakings, with the obligation to go through tendering procedures. beyond the additional cost that these procedures will entail for public authorities, this is an infringement of their right to organise transport services in a way that responds as much as possible to the needs of users. the european parliament has somewhat watered down the european commission's initial proposal on this point and wants the possibility of granting the aid to continue, but under very strict conditions. national authorities will have to justify this on the basis of criteria such as punctuality of services, cost-effectiveness, frequency of services and user satisfaction. despite this small change in relation to the european commission's proposal, this text is a leap forward towards more liberalisation. we therefore voted against it without hesitation.

in writing. i voted against the grosch report on 'opening of the market for national rail passenger services' as it envisages opening as from december 2019. on that date, all new contracts from 2019 onwards or renewals of contracts expiring until the end of 2022 will follow new procurement rules. any direct award of public service contracts to sncf will therefore have to be motivated by criteria of punctuality, reliability and cost/benefit. the latter criteria would allow new competitors who do not have the same social obligations, or who do not finance the service on less profitable lines, to break market prices and thus challenge the existing cross-financing model (the most profitable lines subsidize the least profitable). the report also requires the presence of at least three competing operators in a country such as france. in view of the inherent danger of opening up railways to competition, which remains a vital service for the economy of our territories, and in view of the incompatibility of the logic of competition with the very notion of a public service, i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. the report by izaskun bilbao barandica (spanish liberal party) on the interoperability of the rail system within the european union is one of the six regulations and directives that make up the fourth railway package, which aims to complete the liberalisation of rail. the 4th railway package is divided into a political and a technical component. the question of interoperability is part of the allegedly technical aspect. what does interoperability mean? in a nutshell: the ability to run trains without difficulty on railway networks in different member states. this measure is therefore far from neutral. the french authorities even consider it to be 'one of the factors enabling effective access to the various national markets' and sncf considers it to be 'a major challenge in terms of competitiveness'. interoperability could help to improve railway cooperation at eu level, but in the context of the liberalisation policy it is just one more tool to encourage competition between railway companies at the expense of the rights and safety of users and workers. we vote against.

in writing. i voted for the cramer report on railway safety, a relatively consensual report, which includes all the measures relating to the harmonisation of technical requirements and the agency's role as a one-stop shop, in order to make certification procedures faster and cheaper for companies. this pillar is nevertheless strongly correlated with the political pillar, for what is the point of having the technical means to run trains throughout europe if market access is restricted in some countries? in addition, there are differences with the council, which is reluctant to strengthen the agency's powers.
in writing. this text establishes a common regulatory framework for railway safety. together with the interoperability text, it sets the benchmarks for the necessary harmonisation of certification and safety requirements for railway undertakings. in particular, i support the creation of a single safety certificate valid and recognised in all member states as it contributes to greater safety on the union's railways.
in writing. new legislation on rail safety is not a priority, especially at the european level, which is not adapted to the situation and is not in a position to know the reality on the ground. the work done by the member states in the field of railway safety is largely sufficient, as the rapporteur acknowledges in his explanatory statement. "rail is already the safest mode of transport in the european union and has further improved its safety performance over the past decades".adding legislation at european level increases the cost and administrative burden in the member states, making european policies incompatible with current economic problems.
in writing. the fourth railway package was voted on in the european parliament on 26 february. the package makes no secret of its objectives: to complete the liberalisation of the railways. the report by michael cramer (germany - various interests) focuses on railway safety. by dogmatically liberalizing, out of pure ultra-liberal ideology, the commission and the successive majorities of this parliament have seriously undermined the safety of rail passengers and staff. the fatal accident in brétigny, france, last july is unfortunately one of the consequences of this. this report refuses to take these realities into account. we therefore voted against this report.
in writing. - although rail transport is one of the safest modes of transport in the european union, accidents, however rare, can have disastrous consequences for human life and the environment. railway safety is critically dependent on the interaction between all actors, namely between undertakings, infrastructure managers, the railway sector and safety authorities. it is therefore necessary that safety legislation takes account of these developments and establishes appropriate information, management and emergency procedures and tools. the aim is to maintain and further improve railway safety by speeding up certification procedures and leading to savings in time and resources.
in writing. i abstained on the cramer report on 'railway safety' because the proposed standards for safety systems do not improve much on those applied by sncf. these new european standards are above all an opportunity to facilitate the movement of european trains on french soil and thus the arrival of new european competitors with their rolling stock (locomotives, wagons). however, i did not want to oppose any improvement in safety rules in other member states of the european union, so i abstained.
in writing. i voted in favour of the texts which constitute the railway package because they provide concrete elements from a technical point of view to improve the efficiency and competitiveness of the european railway area in the field of safety. the safety rules for railways would be improved by a european management of equipment certification under the european railway agency. these provisions would increase economies of scale for railway undertakings operating in the european union by reducing administrative costs and speeding up procedures. the provisions on the opening of markets should also improve competition in this sector while taking into account the public service obligation and the working conditions of the staff.
in writing. the principle of strengthening safety rules in rail transport is good and necessary. unfortunately, the commission's directive does not go in that direction. the commission has no intention of imposing a definitive anti-dumping duty on imports of certain steel products originating in the people's republic of china. the role of the states in defining safety rules is thus reduced to a reasonable proportion. there is still an unelected authority which does not represent the consumer and workers' organisations. it would be responsible for defining and guiding european security policy. this text advocates the establishment of a 'principle of equity', equity is not a measurable principle. what is the significance of this text compared with its shortcomings and the deplorable consequences for the security of european competition? i am voting against this text, which is nothing but a manifestation of the liberal technocracy of the european union.
in writing. i supported the strengthening and simplification of safety rules suggested by the european commission and am very satisfied overall with the outcome of this vote, which has allocated the responsibilities between the railway agency and the national authorities in terms of safety.
in writing. rail is already the safest mode of transport in the european union and has further improved its safety performance over the past decades. while its transport performance has risen from around 200 billion passenger kilometres in 1970 to over 300 billion today, the average annual number of passenger deaths travelling by rail has fallen from around 400 in the early 1970s to less than 100 today. although serious railway accidents are rare, enhanced railway safety in the union remains essential[nbsp]; i have therefore supported this report in the plenary.
in writing. - since 1970, rail traffic has increased by 50% in the eu (from 200 000 million passengers/km to over 300 000), while accidental deaths have fallen by a quarter (less than 100). although rail is the safest mode of transport, there are still accidents that require increased safety. since the 1990s, three major european railway packages have been adopted. continuous development of the environment and the discovery of deficiencies makes it possible to constantly improve safety. in this process, legislation has a key role to play in ensuring effective interaction between undertakings, infrastructure managers and responsible authorities. the revision of directive 2004/49/ec will introduce a 'single safety certificate' through the european railway agency and an improvement of safety procedures with the obligation to establish emergency plans for accidents and a plan for the care of victims. in this connection, i regret that the s&d group's proposal that management systems should provide for the duplication of safety systems on all sections of the european rail network, redundant systems, in order to reduce risks to a minimum and avoid tragedies such as that of angrois, did not succeed.

in writing. the fourth railway package was voted on in the european parliament on 26 february. this set of six directives and regulations makes no secret of its objective: to complete the liberalisation of rail. the reports are divided into two parts: the so-called 'political' texts and the so-called 'technical' texts. the report by roberts zīle, a latvian conservative, is part of the so-called technical strand and concerns the european union agency for railways. this report could have worked towards better control of drivers' working time, thus improving both the working conditions of employees and safety for all. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of electronic data-processing techniques, such as the use of electronic data-processing machines, and to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of electronic data-processing techniques. the introduction of common safety certification could be a positive measure if the objective were to increase safety, but the only compass is free and undistorted competition. we therefore voted against this report, which is devoid of any real possibility of improving security and which only serves to strengthen liberalisation.
in writing. - in order to ensure greater competition in the railway sector and to provide better transport services to passengers, parliament approved new rules. the eu rail market has undergone profound transformations in recent years, introduced gradually by several legislative packages. the aim today is to open up national markets and make railways more competitive and interoperable at eu level. this will also make it easier for new and small operators to access railway infrastructure by simplifying the complex authorisation procedures currently in place. national authorities will thus have the possibility to submit tenders for public service contracts through calls for tenders or directly to a railway operator, justifying the decision to award the contract directly, based on criteria of efficiency, cost-effectiveness, frequency of rail operations and customer satisfaction.
in writing. i voted against the zile report on the 'european union agency for railways' because it takes the agency out of its role of making recommendations for the issuing of authorisations to promote the technical opening up of the railway market. by allowing the agency to issue european marketing authorisations for equipment and safety certification for businesses, the aim is to facilitate the penetration of competitors and their equipment into national markets without the involvement of national safety agencies. the european railway agency will also have a role in monitoring national safety authorities and supervising the compliance of national rules with the european framework. in order to oppose this logic of exploiting harmonization to facilitate the entry of new competitors, i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. the eu is thus repealing a regulation which allowed member states to compensate railway undertakings for the costs of obligations which undertakings in other modes of transport are not obliged to bear. it is therefore important to abandon an outdated regulation since the liberalisation of the rail transport sector and to put all companies in the sector on an equal footing.
in writing. the report on 'standardization of accounts of railway undertakings' by jaromir kohlicek is part of the so-called technical pillar of the fourth railway package. a 1969 regulation authorises member states to pay financial compensation to railway undertakings, a list of which is given and of which sncf is a member, for expenditure relating to obligations such as family allowances and pension charges. the european commission wants to repeal this directive, which it considers incompatible with the directive establishing a single european railway area. jaromir kholicek tried to minimise the negative effects of this repeal during the negotiations, in particular by tabled amendments in plenary, and obtained a two-year extension of the measure. despite the efforts of the rapporteur, this text is an integral part of the fourth railway package and is part of the logic of liberalisation. moreover, by accepting the repeal of the 1969 directive, this report endangers the social conditions of railway workers. we voted against this report.
in writing. - regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings was discussed in the context of the fourth railway package. the aim is to bring railway undertakings on an equal footing with other transport undertakings. this regulation will therefore allow member states to compensate railway undertakings for the payment of obligations, such as special payments for accidents at work, pensions for railway workers or payments for equipment costs, which undertakings operating in other transport sectors do not have to bear.
in writing. i voted against the kohlicek report on the 'normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings' because it seeks to repeal a regulation which allowed states to pay financial compensation to companies which had financial obligations towards their former employees (such as early retirement pensions, family allowances, pensions for accidents at work and other special schemes for railway workers). the aim of the regulation was to compensate incumbent railway companies with such financial obligations so that they would not be disadvantaged in competition with new entrants who do not have such social obligations or who refuse to do so. rather than extending these social obligations to all, they were tolerated by compensating the costs. however, if this possibility is removed in the name of competition law rather than extending these social obligations to all railway companies, these social acquis are put in great danger. that is why i opposed this report.

in writing. i voted for the introduction of the e-call system. this text is of great importance to all drivers and passengers, who will soon be able to have vehicles equipped with emergency call devices, designed to automatically alert the emergency services in the event of a serious accident. as the minutes following an accident are crucial for trauma, it is vital to locate seriously injured vehicles quickly to allow emergency services to arrive at the scene as quickly as possible (the so-called "golden hour"). it is true that today this new system seems to be the vanguard. it is even seen by some as a threat to their personal freedom. yet, as lives are saved, i am convinced that it will gradually become "natural", as was the case with the wearing of seat belts in cars or helmets on motorcycles. i voted against the amendments which provide for the possibility of deactivating the system manually, because i see the ecall 112 as compulsory safety equipment subject to approval. this is how, by 2015, thousands of lives could be saved, and the severity of injuries to tens of thousands of victims could, i hope, be alleviated.
in writing. in 2012, there were more than one million accidents on european roads, resulting in approximately 28 000 deaths and more than 1.5 million injuries. in addition to the lives lost or destroyed, this tragedy also represents an annual cost to society of about 130 billion euros. the eu is strongly committed to reducing the number of road accidents and mitigating their consequences. when fully operational across the eu and available to every driver, ecall will make a significant contribution to achieving these objectives. its main advantage is the reduction in the number of road deaths and the severity of injuries caused by road accidents, as the emergency services arrive at the scene of accidents more quickly. i could therefore only support this report by my vote in plenary.
in writing. road accidents are one of the leading causes of death in europe. in 2012, 28,000 people died and over a million were seriously injured. the introduction of the vehicle-based ecall system, approved by the european parliament at its february 2014 session, will automatically alert emergency services in the event of an accident and locate the vehicle. the service, which is free for users and is expected to become mandatory from 2015, will also allow for faster response by emergency services and thus save more lives. the ecall system must comply with the highest data protection requirements. only information related to the accident or the vehicle, such as the type of fuel used or the number of seat belts, should be sent to the emergency centre. this should prevent drivers from being constantly monitored by the system and being able to disconnect from it if they wish.
in writing. this proposal for a regulation concerns the characteristics of an emergency call system, known as ecall, installed on certain vehicles and based on the 112 emergency number, which is intended to call for help in the event of an accident. under the guise of determining the standards for such devices to be used in the union, this legislation makes the installation and use of ecall mandatory for passenger and light commercial vehicles, whereas only 0,7% of them are currently equipped with ecall, mainly luxury vehicles using private emergency call systems. while it is a good idea to prevent emergency services from being called in at the first opportunity, it is to be feared that such measures are mainly used to compensate for the decline in public emergency services as a result of austerity policies. under the pretext of security, this legislation raises serious concerns about mass surveillance of individuals. the declarations on privacy made in plenary do not suffice to reassure against the risks of using the data collected for other purposes. i regret the rejection of the amendments calling for this system to be voluntary and that it can be disconnected if the driver so wishes. i therefore voted against this legislation, which unfortunately was adopted by a large majority in the european parliament.

in writing. the third action programme in the field of health proposes some advances in the field of care[nbsp]; he even denounces the impact of austerity measures on access to health care. but after the fine declarations, the necessary resources are not allocated, and the resolution contains odious references to the liberals' amoralism. illness is seen as a factor in lower productivity whereas health must support growth. "by preserving the health of the individual for as long as possible, and his or her ability to remain active both physically and socially, we can maximise its positive impact on productivity and competitiveness". the rapporteur, mrs grossetête, speaks of a 'high-tech industry, largely located in europe', but does not say a word about the relocated pharmaceutical industries or the closure of services and hospitals which led this week to the death of a woman in the waiting room of a parisian hospital for lack of medical care. i abstain from this so as not to share in this hypocrisy.
in writing. promoting the right of access to healthcare for all citizens in europe is a vital battle to be fought. the european union needs a common strategy to reduce the remaining inequalities between member states. however, policies must be implemented in an intelligent way. the promotion of access to health care must be accompanied by disease prevention measures and the encouragement of innovation in health care. i am very glad that i voted in favour of this report. it particularly highlights the deep need to better understand longevity as one of europe's major challenges.
in writing. this report looks at the renewal of the eu's health agenda for the new period 2014-2020, with four main objectives: to stimulate innovation, to improve access to better and safer healthcare, to promote good health and prevent disease and to protect citizens from cross-border health threats. i am pleased to see that, in the context of budget cuts affecting the eu budget, the financial resources allocated to this programme are higher than those initially proposed by the european commission (from 446 million to 449.4 million) and those for the programme covering the period 2008-2013, which was 321.5 million. i also welcome the fact that an amendment adopted by the european parliament has recognised the impact of austerity policies on access to health care and on the poorest. unfortunately, it has become almost a matter of course. however, this report does not address crucial issues for the eu, such as the relocation of the pharmaceutical industry or the risks of hospital closures as a consequence of the e-health policy, and once again endorses the logic of active ageing, in other words working more. that's why i decided to abstain.
in writing. i voted for the tosenovsky report on the guidelines for transeuropean telecommunications networks. the report covers a number of objectives: financing of broadband networks and prioritising digital service infrastructures with the overall objective of contributing to growth in line with the europe 2020 strategy; the total budget allocated to financial instruments for broadband networks should be 15% (i.e. eur 150 million); 1/3 of the broadband projects financed by the cef must reach speeds of more than 100 mbps; the first funding priority shall be given to reusable digital service infrastructures, such as electronic identification/authentication, secure electronic document distribution, machine translation for pan-european digital services, critical infrastructures supporting eu-wide cyber readiness and secure electronic invoicing. finally, europeana and safe internet for children were identified as potential candidates for funding for the disrupted service.
in writing. this text allows the establishment of trans-european telecommunications networks within the framework of the connecting europe facility (cef). it seems to me therefore important to work towards reducing the digital divide in europe and to provide access to these networks for all. the european union cannot afford to leave less populated regions on the margins of these communication technologies. although the budgetary constraints on this project are regrettable, it seems to me important to continue to stimulate investment in these high and very high-speed networks to strengthen the digital market.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which sets out the guidelines for the implementation of transeuropean telecommunications networks within the union. i welcome the increase in the competitiveness of the european economy, particularly for small and mediumsized enterprises. in addition, the promotion of interconnection and interoperability of national networks is guaranteed, which makes it possible to take account of these new constraints.
in writing. after a few phrases promoting 'a better internet for children', we see the real purpose of the recast of this directive. as always, the aim is to increase 'european productivity' and 'develop the internal market'. the market of 500 million potential users is indeed attractive. the obsession with competition as the only way to "provide competitive, affordable services and the innovation needed by consumers and businesses" is repugnant to me. the commission has not yet taken a decision on the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women. this liberalisation has increased inequality between consumers in a commercial and tariff model whose only beneficiaries are the shareholders of private rentier operators. i am voting against a text which is entirely consistent with this logic.
in writing. i voted for the report because it does not raise any major problems and is supported by all the political groups. this is a simple first reading, without a trilogue agreement, as the council has not made sufficient progress in its examination of the text. accessibility of websites is ensured by a set of principles and techniques that must be respected when designing websites in order to make their content accessible to all users, including those with disabilities. the market for website development is a relatively large economic sector: 175[nbsp ]000 companies within the european union, 1[nbsp ]million jobs, turnover of 144 billion euros (2009 figures). accessibility policy initiatives and commitments already exist at european level but will be strengthened and complemented by this report.
in writing. with this text, we are approximating the rules of the member states on the accessibility of public sector websites by setting harmonised requirements. indeed, public sector websites provide essential services. this is therefore a basic provision for people with mobility problems, such as the disabled or certain elderly people. there is a need to provide greater access to public services, such as job search services and social benefits for citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which makes it possible to stimulate the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites. to this end, i share the desire to strengthen the accessibility of the web in order to allow in particular disabled people to make the best use of websites.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites. more than 100 million european citizens, including the elderly and disabled, have difficulty accessing these websites to use online public services and less than 30% of websites are considered to be accessible to all today. the text, which was improved and brought into line with the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, was to apply only to the websites of public sector bodies, but now covers all websites operated by entities with public missions, such as those of health and education services, public transport and tourism, water distribution, electricity, or postal services. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include mobile versions of websites. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. web accessibility is essential at a time when digital technology is becoming more widespread and the internet is becoming the preferred place for information and contact with public authorities. we must accompany this change by thinking of people who may have difficulties in accessing it. this is the case for the elderly and the disabled. computer solutions exist to make websites accessible to all, but they should be implemented by the member states' administrations in the first instance.
in writing. it is essential to promote the accessibility of the web for the greatest number of people. this is part of the principles we stand for with net neutrality and the protection of data of users of services on the internet. this is a step in the right direction. however, this report (as always) is placed in the context of the establishment of the digital single market: the standardisation of accessibility rules in all eu countries to be able to appeal, potentially, to all eu agencies. in addition, the implementation of the directive will lead to enormous additional costs for national, regional and local services. finally, the proposal is premature because the european standard in this area is being developed. under the guise of improving access to websites for people with disabilities, this is actually about increasing competition and pressure on member states. the process is disgusting. i vote against it.
in writing. the report proposes many improvements to the commission's proposal for a directive and endorses the first significant step at european level in the area of accessibility of the websites of public bodies and, moreover, of all websites operated by entities performing public tasks, thanks to the s&d meps and the rapporteur, which i welcome.
in writing. we must fight against the exclusion of people with functional limitations or disabilities. the european citizens must not be excluded from the information society linked to public services. public services are responsible to the whole population. these same people are often heavily addicted to the internet. for this reason, member states should take measures to increase the accessibility of public services on the web. i am very glad that i voted in favour of this report. it is true that several member states have already proposed some measures for web accessibility. however, a harmonised approach is needed to eliminate inequalities between the various countries of the union. it is by choosing a common strategy that we will succeed in increasing competition, competitiveness and economic growth in this europe in crisis.
in writing. currently, the vast majority of public administration websites are inaccessible to blind or partially sighted people. the directive is therefore particularly important in this context: it is time to give a legislative impetus to make changes, both in terms of basic accessibility and in terms of services offered online. we also took into account the growing demand from the public to be able to access information and services online through applications and mobile devices or to have easily downloadable online forms. we also stressed the importance of effective, proportionate and dissuasive sanctions for breaches of the provisions adopted pursuant to this text. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of consumers in the event of a breach of the directive is a very good one. i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. i am the rapporteur for the socialist group and i am satisfied with the result. web accessibility is not a gadget but an essential and increasingly indispensable element in the lives of people with disabilities. but in the absence of regulation, too few websites meet international accessibility standards, depriving our most vulnerable citizens, especially the elderly, of essential access to many services, including public services. i tabled amendments to extend the list of sites concerned to include those websites which fulfil a public service mission. the list adopted by parliament is much more ambitious than originally planned and includes a large number of administrative procedures and information for the benefit of citizens. finally, the directive will make it possible to make compliance with the standards for website accessibility a matter of course and encourage private actors to follow the example of the public service for disabled persons.
in writing. less than 30% of websites are considered to be accessible to everyone today. yet 15% of the working age population in the european union has a disability, and europe has 87 million people over the age of 65. more than 100 million european citizens, especially disabled and elderly people, have difficulties accessing public service websites. this is totally unacceptable: public services' websites must be designed in such a way that all citizens can access them. technology allows us to do this, an international technical standard covers all the criteria, we just have to decide, and that is the direction we have taken today! while the european commission proposed making public bodies' websites accessible by 2015, we have gone further: all sites fulfilling public service missions, such as health-related services, primary, secondary and higher education enrolments, cultural activities and tourist information, are now covered. the european council did not, however, open discussions on this text. it's time to make this a priority!
in writing. i voted for the klinz report on the long-term financing of the european economy. it is a question of taking a long-term view of the european economy in order to anticipate trends as far as possible and not rely on speculative bubbles which, when they burst, destroy the stability of european citizens.
in writing. this paper discusses the various possible ways of promoting long-term financing of the european economy. the economic and financial crisis has created a climate of uncertainty within the european union and has undermined investor confidence in european markets. it is therefore essential to consider how the european union can become once again an attractive area for investment, which is necessary for growth and employment. it also seems to me particularly appropriate to seek to facilitate access to bank or non-bank financing for smes.
in writing. i voted in favour of this green paper, given the real need for the european union to find long-term funding for its actions. i therefore support the four pillars of this green paper, which are centred on the efficiency and effectiveness of the financial markets in their ability to provide financing instruments. finally, i share the view of the european commission in its desire to facilitate access to finance for smes, since they are the economic lungs of many of our territories and the union must be able to help them.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the long-term financing of the european economy which follows the publication of the commission's green paper and contributes with various measures to the promotion of long-term investment. improved long-term financing conditions would allow better financing of the real economy and would promote economic growth and job creation.
in writing. the report stresses the need for long-term investment in line with the needs of the real economy. it also recalls that public investment plays an essential role in long-term investment. it's time to remember. so far, everything is fine. the report even stresses that training and education costs should be treated as long-term investments. then it all goes to shit in a weird schizophrenia. on the one hand, it noted that the eu's international competitors, such as the united states and japan, maintained a high level of public investment and, on the other, it proposed that the eu should increase private investment. it proposes to turn to the financial markets to finance future investments, while at the same time noting that public financing is limited by the granting of state aid to rescue financial institutions. but above all, it avoids the simplest way of stimulating investment: the implementation of stimulus plans. this is impossible because "budgetary consolidation is the priority for public budgets". it would be sufficient, however, if the member states could borrow directly from the ecb. mr. klinz probably didn't think of that! i vote against it.
in writing. this own-initiative report, which follows the commission's green paper on the long-term financing of the european economy, is not without its obvious ambiguity. while emphasising the need for long-term investment to create jobs and achieve social and sustainable development, the text endorses and promotes all the austerity policies implemented by the eu in recent years. the report promotes public-private partnerships, without denouncing all the problems that also arise from these partnerships, which are now well known to everyone. the report supports the ongoing negotiations for an eu/us free trade agreement. i objected to this report.
in writing. the economic crisis has led to fiscal consolidation and investor protection policies. it has also revealed the perversions of a deregulated financial sector, which has led, rightly, to the tightening of prudential regulations. all these factors have made financing more complicated for the actors in the real economy. but it is our smes which are the main victims of this shrinking supply of finance. it is therefore essential that, in parallel with the management of risky behaviour, we facilitate access for our companies to sound and affordable financing. this requires action in three directions: better targeting of household savings towards investments that benefit the economy in the long term, better financial attractiveness of european companies through policies that favour their competitiveness and the reduction of administrative and regulatory burdens, and finally a stronger involvement of public authorities, for example through the development of public-private partnerships or the strengthening of public investment institutions. in the end, it is essential to support a project that combines regulation and stimulation for a sector which, despite the deviations, remains vital to the proper functioning of our economy.
in writing. i voted against this report on the long-term financing of the european economy. i would like to say that, given the current policies in this area, the title is sufficient. very little is said about the necessary long-term investments in education, research and development, innovation, the ecological transition or infrastructure. on the contrary, the report 'considers that high-quality securitisation can play a useful role in the financial intermediation of assets' believes that financial speculation can continue to flourish[nbsp ], praises public-private partnerships, 'welcomes the progress of the ongoing negotiations on ttip' (the great transatlantic trade and investment partnership) or 'stresses that a business climate favourable to investors [...] is an indispensable condition for making the european union an attractive destination for foreign investment'. in other words, no change in sight. the same policies are being pursued without regard for the consequences for social rights. we'd be disappointed if we could still be. yet the socialists and the greens voted overwhelmingly in favour.
in writing. the resolution, which punishes clients of prostitutes, proposed by mrs honeyball, is intended to be "a step towards full equality between men and women throughout the european union". in reality, this report undermines the sovereignty of the member states and promotes the gender theory. the priority should be to dismantle criminal networks, combat forced prostitution and make the sex trade more common. the report proposes the 'nordic model' to the member states and presents it as the only solution to combat prostitution. the resolution "urges the governments of the member states which reserve an alternative treatment for prostitution to review their legislation". the european union is once again seeking to infringe the sovereignty of the member states by imposing a social resolution. the text also condemns "gender stereotypes" linked to the commodification of women's bodies, a term used by advocates of gender theory. the initial fight against trafficking in women and criminal networks is supplanted by the introduction of gender ideology.
in writing. following discussions in several european countries, the european parliament has addressed the issue of sexual exploitation and prostitution through a number of networks operating within the eu. i supported the report by mary honeyball because it makes recommendations to the european commission on combating sexual exploitation, which is violence against women. the report calls on the european union and the member states to take measures to discourage the practice of sex tourism inside or outside the union. parliament called on the eu and its member states to develop a policy of prevention in the countries of origin of prostitutes through sanctions, awareness-raising campaigns and education. so the report is not against people who are prostitutes. thus, by recommending that the client be penalized and not the prostitute, it represents a further step towards full equality between men and women throughout the european union.
in writing. the issue of prostitution is a highly complex one. to draw up a catalogue of miracle solutions in a few pages of a report which has not been really debated, where ideas, approaches and experiences have not been confronted, is a clumsy if not risky undertaking. the author praises the swedish model of a total ban on prostitution and the penalisation of the client, but is unable to say on the basis of verifiable and indisputable data that this model has actually helped to reduce this phenomenon. can we not imagine that underground networks have developed, that the problem has been moved? as far as the resulting trafficking in human beings is concerned, i am in favour of the firm method. the people responsible for these networks must be hunted down and punished, these networks fought and dissolved. on social issues such as this, let us leave it to the member states to experiment with the model they consider most effective in combating trafficking and violence against women, but let us not prescribe to the european parliament a miracle and universal solution which ignores national identities and cultural trajectories.
in writing. i have decided to vote against the alternative resolution signed by several members of my political group and supported by the conservatives of the ecr, whose backward ideas on women's rights we regularly combat in this house. i have, however, supported the report by mary honeyball, which, while emphasising the gendered nature of prostitution, highlights its impact on gender equality by refusing to regard women's bodies as a commodity to be freely disposed of by men. i voted in favour of this text because it seeks to establish the link between prostitution, human trafficking and organised crime. they are intrinsically linked, trafficking not being a regrettable by-product of prostitution but the very condition of its existence. it therefore recommends that member states, in order to combat this phenomenon most effectively, should tackle demand, as provided for in the nordic model, which penalises the customer and not the prostitute. finally, and this seems to me to be a key point in this report, it stresses the need to propose credible alternatives and specific support measures to enable these people to be genuinely reintegrated into society.
in writing. prostitution is a matter for the member states. that is why i abstained on this report. we have no jurisdiction in this matter.
in writing. first reality: prostitution is an attack on the dignity of women and therefore on human rights. the report stresses that national legislation on this issue has direct consequences for gender equality and the perception of women as 'objects'. it clearly takes an abolitionist approach and advocates the decriminalization of prostitution. it establishes the direct link between prostitution and trafficking and the organised crime that organises this 'market', and demonstrates the harmful effects of the crisis on these women. the aim is to encourage member states to rapidly transpose the directive on preventing and combating trafficking in human beings and protecting its victims. i note that some greens have tabled a minority opinion against this report, referring only to 'forced prostitution'. i shall of course vote in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted for this report, on which i was rapporteur for the french delegation of the epp group. this paper examines issues such as mining and sustainable development, the role of the private sector, international trade and investment regimes and the use of revenues, and the disconnection of armed conflict from mineral exploitation. it is a question of responsibility, but also of stability in countries which can quickly become unstable because of the corruption surrounding raw materials.
in writing. this paper addresses the challenges of extractive industries in developing countries and calls for the promotion of responsible practices in these industries. it seems to me important to be sensitive not only to the environmental issues that the extractive industries represent but also to social issues. energy resources in developing countries are often linked to tensions and many conflicts. it is therefore legitimate to encourage extractive companies in developing countries to adopt transparency policies on their environmental and social standards.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which raises the opportunities and threats of mining in developing countries. a comprehensive strategy would thus make it possible to better manage mineral-fuelled conflicts and the environmental, social and human rights consequences of mining.
in writing. developing countries rich in natural resources are paradoxically often in more problematic situations than others (the phenomenon of the 'resource curse'). control, exploitation, trade and taxation of minerals can, in some cases, contribute to armed conflict. the aim is to adopt a comprehensive strategy to address the root causes of mineral-fuelled conflict, to better manage the environmental, social and human rights impacts of mining, and to better support and integrate artisanal and small-scale mining. but beyond these general and generous principles, the text lacks practical aspects. the rapporteur calls on the authorities to ban prospecting and mining in national parks and world heritage sites, without specifying the counterparts of this non-exploitation. a concrete eu support in the yasuni itt project, the first such offer in the history of mankind, would have been more effective. while european regulation on this subject is welcome, i doubt that the measures mentioned in this report will be sufficient to stop mining at the expense of people and the human ecosystem. i'm not going to.

the rapporteur. - madam president, good evening mr commissioner, good evening colleagues, and thank you for being here this late at night to discuss this important subject. i would first like to express my satisfaction with the drafting process which led to a unanimous vote in the committee on international trade on this subject. i would of course like to thank the fictitious rapporteurs, mrs köstinger and mrs bearder, mr martin, mr zahradil and mr murphy for their cooperation and to point out that we did vote unanimously on this resolution because we in the committee on international trade consider this to be a very important subject. there was this desire to send a clear signal to the commission and the council about the seriousness of our work and the ambition we have in the area of monitoring and regulating trade in timber and timber products, and the seriousness we take in this type of agreement with indonesia, in this case, and, previously, with certain african countries. it is also an opportunity for me to thank the indonesian authorities, the embassy and all the actors who have enabled us to work. as i said, we considered this a serious matter, which is why we wanted to meet as many stakeholders as possible - both indonesian and european - in the field, in order to formulate the best possible recommendations and to ensure that the agreement we want is the best possible and, above all, that it guarantees that the wood and wood products we will import into the european union meet - of course - sustainability criteria. this voluntary partnership agreement with indonesia is particularly important because the indonesian forest is a huge forest. it's one of the three largest forests in the world. it is obvious that this is a major challenge for the climate - as we know - for biodiversity and, of course, also from the point of view of the people who live in the forest or the forest. and then, it's an important agreement because we know the importance of the timber trade in indonesia, including to asia. it is therefore essential that the flegt licences to be granted can, in some way, give the right criteria on all indonesian exports and, in any case, provide a reference for timber trade. of course, once parliament has given its consent, if the vote so decides tomorrow, the commission will have to decide, on the basis of its assessment, whether the system for verifying the legality of wood is relevant, correct and meets the criteria of the european parliament. and we know that despite the efforts of the indonesian government, there are still shortcomings, and we wanted to point them out. these shortcomings are, of course, the lack of verification of a number of timber and timber products from forest conversion, whether for agriculture or for the production of palm oil. it is also known that the audit of the permitting process as carried out under the current verification system has many shortcomings. and then, finally, we know that the legality verification process does not distinguish between products that have been certified and products that are not certified in the whole chain. you can see that there are efforts; the indonesian authorities and all the actors in the sector in indonesia and civil society are clearly making efforts. but, again, since this will be the only occasion for the european parliament to express very strongly what it expects from the european commission, we wanted to do so here, and i would like to say that the european parliament's objective in this matter is really to ensure that the voluntary partnership agreement and the licences that will be granted meet the objectives of protecting the climate and protecting biodiversity, while ensuring, of course, the sustainable development of indonesia.

member of the commission. - mr president, repeated heavy rainfall and unusually strong winds since last december have resulted in flooding in a number of member states. in particular ireland, the uk, france, and to a lesser degree some other countries, were all affected. moreover, very unusual snowfall and freezing rain has led to serious damage in the southern alps, and in slovenia in particular. in all these instances, the commission’s emergency response coordination centre (ercc) was closely monitoring the situation as it developed and immediately established contact with all the countries affected. the ercc kept an overview of developments and potential needs for assistance. it regularly shared information and provided situational updates to member state authorities through the eu common emergency communication and information system. at the request of the national authorities in, for instance, the uk and slovenia, the ercc also supplied satellite imaging of flood zones. in the event that a member state requests external assistance, the union civil protection mechanism is activated via the ercc. in such cases, pre-defined civil protection assets – so-called modules, composed of specialised equipment and teams – are available for deployment if necessary at short notice. following slovenia’s request for assistance, 11 member states offered assistance, mainly through the union civil protection mechanism but also bilaterally, providing the disaster-stricken country with more than 120 power generators. while no estimates of total damage are available at the moment, we do know that considerable destruction was caused in many places, in particular in coastal areas where high tides added to the damage, and in slovenia as a result of the freezing rain. the eu solidarity fund was established after the terrible floods in 2002 to provide financial assistance, and has since proven its usefulness by providing aid amounting to over eur 3.7 billion to member states to deal with the costs of emergency measures in the event of major disasters. the solidarity fund is, of course, in principle available to those countries now affected by storms, floods and ice too, if the conditions are met. activation of the fund relies first of all however on applications being submitted by member states if they consider that the fund should intervene. the commission cannot activate the fund on its own initiative, but stands ready to give any guidance and advice that may be required in preparing applications. if and when applications are submitted, the commission will assess them as quickly as possible and, if possible, request the council and parliament to mobilise the necessary financial resources.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the private copying levy is not abolished. today the european parliament is expressing its position on this issue. for those of you who are not experts in this field, i would like to recall a few simple points. first, private copying is an exception to copyright, that is, it allows the copying of protected works without the author's permission, provided the work has been lawfully acquired and the copy is for private use only. in return for this right to copy, the user of the copy pays a royalty, that is, a contribution to the copyright. this contribution, or private copying fee, is paid when the raw media or the equipment necessary for making copies is purchased. i would like to emphasize that this is a royalty, a contribution to copyright, not a tax or a levy. the english term 'levies' is ambiguous as to the nature of this charge, and i would ask the translation services to exercise the utmost care. what is the difference between a royalty and a tax? a tax is levied by the state and goes into the state's revenue. his assignment is untraceable. the fee is instead levied by the persons entitled to it, in particular by collective management organisations; it is directly used and redistributed for the remuneration of copyright and for the financing of actions in favour of cultural creation and dissemination. i propose in my report that at least 25% of this income should be allocated to supporting creativity. that is why i say that it is a virtuous system, but one that can be improved. in this connection, i have heard and taken into account the main criticisms of the private copying levy system. the first criticism concerns the risk of 'forum shopping' since almost all member states (23 out of 28) apply this levy, but not at the same rate. i therefore ask the european commission to start thinking about harmonising the definition of the private copying levy (what is it? what does it compensate for?), the scope (what material can be subject to the levy?) and the way in which the rates are calculated. the creation of joint committees (groups of rightholders, manufacturers and consumers) could be a good practice to develop. the second criticism concerns transparency. the requirement of transparency of amounts collected and redistributed should be improved with the introduction of the directive on collective management, which we voted for. transparency can also be improved with regard to institutions and events that benefit from a share of the revenue from private copying. and i ask that this information be made public. secondly, the consumer who has paid the fee must be informed and know the amount of the spc. i am also proposing measures to this end. finally, exemptions for professionals must be effective through the development of exemption agreements and simple, efficient and effective reimbursement systems. commissioner, i have heard a lot of people say that the private copying fee system would be obsolete in a digital broadcasting environment. on the contrary, i believe that it has never been so easy and quick to make copies of protected works, and that the quality of the copies is virtually identical to that of the originals. the system must therefore be strengthened and adapted to the dissemination of works on the internet. we believe that streaming, for example, does not exclude private storage and copying, including on virtual media such as the cloud. i therefore ask the commission to start thinking about new copying practices in order to adapt the private copying fee system. commissioner, there is a consultation going on at the moment on the future of copyright. this report is the first contribution of the european parliament.
