in writing. i welcome the agreement reached on the revision of the tobacco directive. i believe that the increase in the area allocated to health warnings will have a significant impact on the attractiveness of tobacco products and tobacco use in the eu, especially among young people. i also welcome the respect for the principle of subsidiarity in the regulation of electronic cigarettes: each member state will be able to decide its own legislation, in accordance with the choice of its own citizens. the decision cannot be taken by brussels, but it is up to the member states to define their own policy on this matter. in the end, although i regret the retreat initiated by the court of justice in relation to crossborder sales, the solution found seems to me to be balanced and effective, which is why i voted in favour of it in the plenary.
in writing. i voted in favour of the compromise reached by the socialist linda mcavan on the tobacco directive. 700 000 people die every year in europe from tobacco. the main challenge, therefore, is to discourage young people from starting, because of the addiction. in fact, 70% of smokers start before the age of 18 and 94% before the age of 25. the main issue in this report was to regulate the sale of electronic cigarettes. the choice is left to the states whether to consider them as medicines or tobacco products, thus allowing france, for example, to maintain existing points of sale without forcing consumers to go to the pharmacy. electronic cigarettes sold as tobacco products will have to comply with nicotine concentration and refill size limits, which will above all protect the health of european citizens. the compromise also includes the addition of health warnings on packages, the banning of flavoured cigarettes by 2020, attractive packaging and misleading labels such as 'light'.
in writing. smoking currently kills nearly six million people a year worldwide, including 700,000 in europe, and this figure could reach eight million by 2030. i welcome this vote, which for the first time confirms concrete actions in favour of a better prevention policy for young people. the road to this ambitious vote has been long, as some of the opposing lobbies have been powerful, but it is public health that is now protected. among the progress achieved, i would particularly like to highlight the addition of a health warning (text and image) covering 65%[nbsp ] of the front and back of cigarette and rolling tobacco packages, the ban on flavoured cigarettes from 2016 (with a menthol transition period until 2020), the ban on lipstick or perfume packaging, the ban on the use of terms such as 'light' and the framing of e-cigarettes, which can be considered either as a medicinal product or as a tobacco product in order to preserve existing national regulations.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report calling for greater involvement of the european union in the fight against prostitution. prostitution is the latest form of violence where the victim is still considered the culprit in some countries. for this reason, i am in favour of prosecuting those who buy sexual acts rather than those who sell them. the resolution we have just voted on goes in that direction.
in writing. in the same vein as the socialist resolutions which are only used to argue in the european parliament, i present the honeyball resolution on prostitution. the parliamentarians were divided on the question of whether or not to penalize customers. the nordic model of banning prostitution has been promoted by some, rejected by others and why? it is not, because it is only a resolution and it is the states that decide. in short, it is a waste of time and energy, since everyone is resigned to defending his system, his model, believing that he is right. i therefore defended the french position, which is above all trying to protect prostitutes as much as possible and to fight organized crime.
in writing. i voted against the honeyball resolution which seeks to penalize customers. sex workers want rights, to be protected by the law, not a hypocritical penalty that forces them to hide more and more and live in working conditions that are dangerous to their health and safety.
in writing. i abstained in the vote on this text on sexual exploitation and prostitution. the european union must certainly continue to fight against the terrible phenomena of prostitution, such as human trafficking, child prostitution and violence against women. however, it is not for the commission to impose on the member states a legislative model for dealing with the problem of prostitution. each member state must be sovereign in putting in place the legislation it deems appropriate. prostitution is a complex issue for which there is no right or wrong solution applicable to all member states. i did not, however, wish to block the adoption of such a text which rightly emphasizes the devastating consequences of prostitution.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text despite the fact that it defends the so-called 'nordic model', a model based on the penalisation of the customer, which i do not particularly support. the report denounces prostitution and the harm it causes to all those who are forced or forced to suffer what can be considered a form of violence. we also placed a strong emphasis on the need to combat human trafficking and smuggling, which is often orchestrated by cross-border organised crime.
in writing. i welcome the fact that the european parliament has adopted this text which advocates a necessary abolitionist approach to prostitution.
in writing. i agree that a solution must be found to the problem of prostitution, which puts many women at risk every day. to protect these women from the mafia networks, we must take all necessary measures. however, i do not support the idea of imposing the nordic model or any other model on all member states. obviously, prostitution, trafficking in women and gender inequality must be tackled. however, we must fully respect the principle of subsidiarity. that is why i abstained on the final vote.
in writing. i voted in favour of the honeyball report on sexual exploitation and prostitution, which has been the subject of a lively debate in the european parliament. this report, which has no legal value but a strong political value, has made it possible to underline that a majority in the european parliament, of which i am a member, supports an abolitionist approach to prostitution. prostitution is a form of violence, exploitation of inequalities and a violation of human dignity, and 95% of those involved do not choose to engage in it. it is demonstrated that it does not reduce sexual violence in any way, it is necessary to end a demand that justifies the offer. the model of regulating prostitution has shown its limits as it perpetuates and fuels the development of human trafficking. an approach to decriminalizing prostitutes, highlighting customer responsibility and developing concrete alternatives to help prostituted persons exit the system should be given priority.
in writing. i could not vote for this own-initiative report by mary honeyball, a british labour party member on prostitution. this report catalogues the practices and legislation of the member states, which are to the detriment of some and the disadvantage of others, without demonstrating the validity of these claims, which go so far as to equate the legalization of prostitution with that of pimping. the report's bias is to see the swedish model as the panacea. neither an abolitionist nor a legalist, i do not believe that the penalisation of the client is the only solution and even fear that it increases the vulnerability of people who prostitute themselves, sending them back into hiding. the fight against prostitution networks and the reintegration of those who wish to do so must be given priority, but this requires resources which are hardly on the agenda. it is by tackling the worsening social misery that we will prevent the majority of women, but also men and especially young men, from falling prey to trafficking networks. the report has therefore not allowed an objective view to be developed on a painful subject which raises many questions in the light of the model of society in which we want to live.
in writing. another report that undermines the credibility of our parliament! what image do we give, in the midst of a crisis of confidence, in the midst of economic and social difficulties, when we take over part of our agenda with a report on guidelines for prostitution and its consequences for gender equality? i am aware that with prostitution there is a whole range of violence, humiliation and trafficking of all kinds that are brought to our attention, but national legislation is much more relevant than action by the union! i repeat once again: in matters of society, which are matters of morality, of intimacy, of the private sphere, let us leave the principle of subsidiarity in play. is it up to parliament to decide whether to penalize the customer or the service? on tolerance, regulation or prohibition? i'm sure you don't, and i'm sure i'm not the only one who thinks that.
in writing. the eu's single market offers many opportunities to the 500[nbsp ] million european citizens and the many businesses that are based in the union. unfortunately, citizens and businesses alike are not always aware of their rights. solvit has therefore been set up to provide them with rapid solutions in the event of problems. i voted in favour of this report which proposes to reform the system to make it more efficient, to the benefit of european citizens and businesses.
in writing. i voted in favour of the solvit report. solvit is an informal online help service for european citizens and businesses in the european union when their rights are being violated by the public administration of another member state, in the event that no legal action has yet been taken. several objectives are mentioned: to improve the system considerably, particularly with regard to disputes involving companies and response times; better take into account cross-border labour law, social rights and equal treatment issues (e.g. pensions); promote solvit and raise public awareness of its usefulness.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to ensure that citizens and businesses are better informed about their rights in the context of the functioning of the internal market. it also provides them with the tools they need to prevent crossborder litigation. we can also be satisfied with the modernisation of the 'your europe' portal. it is a step towards making community legislation, which is often considered too distant from the citizen, more accessible.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it recognises the full usefulness and value of the solvit system for the european single market. solvit is a tool of major importance for the union, which enables citizens and businesses to resolve disputes at european level amicably, by bringing together national authorities. the text does, however, recognise that the system needs to be improved, in particular by focusing more on the problems faced by businesses in their crossborder activities. the lack of awareness of the mechanism among citizens is also, of course, a major obstacle to its development. i welcome, however, that this report advocates the establishment of measurable criteria which will allow a better assessment of the evolution of solvit, and thus of whether any legislative measures need to be adopted to replace the informal procedure which is now at the heart of the mechanism.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on improving the online help service for european citizens and businesses who would have their rights infringed by the public administration of another member state in many areas, such as the recognition of professional qualifications, visas and residence rights, trade and services. the system, which should provide a response within 10 weeks if no legal action has yet been brought, could nevertheless be improved.
in writing. the solvit network intervenes in any crossborder problem between a company or a citizen, on the one hand, and a national public authority, on the other, concerning the incorrect application of community law relating to the internal market. solvit is therefore an instrument for enforcing the neoliberal rules of the european internal market, which i condemn. citizens and businesses are invited to submit online complaints on a portal falsely entitled 'europe is yours' to challenge states that lack zeal in enforcing the liberal rules imposed by the eu. the report welcomes the application of the 'principle of zero tolerance in the event of non-compliance with the services directive'. a whole program! this shows that if the same system existed for social and individual rights, europe could be a shield for the people. another choice is made. we will not be afraid to break the treaties to allow a rebuilding of europe. i am voting against this instrument which thinks it can stop me.
in writing. solvit is a service provided by the national administration of each eu country to help citizens or businesses in one country when their rights are not respected in another eu member state. it currently handles nearly 1 300 cases each year and manages to find solutions for about 90[nbsp ]% of citizens or businesses within 70 days. i support the recommendations in this report which are aimed at further improving the efficiency of this system and that is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the melo report on the european investigation order, which contains some good proposals.
in writing. this text introduces a new european instrument, the 'european investigation order', which then establishes a comprehensive system for obtaining evidence in cases with a cross-border dimension. by voting for this text, the european parliament is helping to strengthen cooperation between member states in criminal matters through exchanges of good practice. a strong signal is then sent. the establishment of an area of free movement is inseparable from the strengthening of security in that territory. however, it seemed important to me to establish that the issuing of the european investigation decision must be necessary and proportionate. in addition, particular importance should be attached to the protection of personal data in cross-border investigations.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive which obliges member states to enforce any european investigation decision on the basis of the principle of mutual recognition. at a time when crossborder crime is becoming a major problem, i can only encourage all the european union's efforts in this area. i also welcome the intention to add a chapter on respect for fundamental rights, which reflects the european union's commitment to ensuring fair trials.
in writing. i defended the new instrument of judicial cooperation in criminal matters in europe, the european investigation order, as it should improve the functioning of justice, especially in cross-border crime cases, while ensuring full respect for fundamental rights. the european investigation order will go a step further in criminal judicial cooperation by ensuring that judicial authorities in one country can more easily request the opening of an investigation in another eu country and thus obtain evidence more quickly, with fewer administrative formalities, through the introduction of a single standard form. drawing on the experience of several years of the european arrest warrant, we have defended the introduction of a particularly novel ground for refusal in a mutual recognition instrument in criminal law, despite the council's strong resistance: these are cases where the judicial authorities of the member states consider that this investigative decision is incompatible with their fundamental rights obligations. we need a law that allows us to act with the necessary diligence to prosecute those who have committed crimes across the border.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a directive to replace the current mutual legal assistance conventions, which are too complex and too limited to guarantee the effectiveness of investigations involving several member states. investigations will now be recognised in all eu member states to facilitate cooperation between police and judicial authorities. the judicial authority of one member state may order one or more specific investigative measures to be carried out in order to collect evidence in another member state, for example to collect witness testimony or dna samples. we have also introduced a time limit for the enforcement of decisions to ensure that the investigation is not delayed by excessive administrative complexity. i voted in favour of this text because it will help to ensure the effectiveness of the police and the judiciary in the member states, so as to better combat organised crime.
in writing. in order to create an area of freedom, security and justice, we need to strengthen cooperation between law enforcement authorities in the member states. the european investigation order is in line with this. it will allow evidence to be gathered in cross-border investigations to strengthen our fight against criminal networks, while ensuring full respect for fundamental rights.
in writing. this is a further violation of the fundamental principles of the separation of powers and the roots of democracy. the aim of this directive is to establish a procedure whereby judicial authorities ask their counterparts in other member states to conduct criminal investigations in their own country. this 'european investigation decision' would replace the existing legal framework for the collection and transfer of data between member states and would apply to almost all types of evidence. this directive introduces a wider scope than the european mandate, and also covers evidence that does not yet exist (e.g. a statement by a witness) or is not directly available (e.g. analysis of a dna sample). the number of grounds for refusal is very limited. based on treaties not democratically agreed by the people, this procedure undermines the independence of the judiciary by subjecting it to constraints outside the legal hierarchy on which its legitimacy is based in each country. i vote against it.
in writing. i supported this new instrument for judicial cooperation in criminal matters in europe. it will improve the functioning of justice in crossborder crime cases, while ensuring respect for fundamental rights.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which simplifies the conditions for obtaining short-stay visas to the european union. this simplification is not without conditions. the beneficiary states had to meet strict security and control requirements. in addition, emergency mechanisms have been provided to temporarily suspend such a facility in the event of a massive influx of third-country nationals or non-compliance by those countries with the conditions of use.
in writing. we have just introduced in june 2013 a mechanism allowing the european commission to suspend the visa exemption in case of a substantial and sudden increase in asylum applications, persons in an irregular situation or rejections of readmission applications. an effective and dissuasive suspension mechanism is essential to prevent and address abuse. however, this mechanism has never been activated. we cannot therefore support further visa waivers and further opening of our borders until this suspension mechanism has proved its worth.
in writing. i voted against this report to exempt moldova from the visa requirement to enter the territory of the european union, because it sends the wrong signal at a time when citizens expect the union to strengthen its migration policy. despite moldova's progress in strengthening its institutions and its strong links with the eu, visa liberalisation with moldova is contrary to my vision of a well-chosen immigration policy and reform of the schengen system. the recent swiss referendum shows that the eu must take back control of immigration and no longer make the principle of free movement the alpha and omega of its migration policy.
in writing. the european parliament has given the green light to the visa exemption with moldova. it is regrettable that once again parliament is extending the list of visa-free countries without taking into account the fears of citizens, many of whom are still suffering the effects of the crisis. moldova signed an association agreement with the european union in november 2013 and has made a lot of efforts to move closer to european standards. but does economic cooperation mean that borders are automatically opened? without blaming the moldovan population, we must be able to assess the visa policy of the european union as it has been for several years with realism. the benevolent, even naive, approach of the union to visa policy is not a sound political approach when it leads to a deregulation of the system. the latest analysis reveals that the visa exemption for the balkan countries has led to significant increases of up to 100[nbsp ]% increase in asylum applications in france. european migration policy is at a standstill. it's time to evolve it.
in writing. i voted against the extension of visa exemptions to certain new countries. recent experience with visa exemptions granted to countries close to the union has shown that they are accompanied by a significant increase in the number of cases of fraud and improper installation in the host country. this also raises security issues, particularly in the fight against certain trafficking.

in writing. the aim is to abolish the european visa requirement for moldovans. it is a counterpart to the establishment of free trade agreements. the signing of the eastern partnership last november was the culmination of these 'serious efforts'. in addition, the visa exemption will be limited to holders of a biometric passport. this big brother trend is disturbing. above all, it means extra costs for people who want to travel to a country with poverty wages. i cannot oppose a text which will represent a real step forward for the freedom of movement of moldovan citizens, but i do regret the neoliberal framework of our relations with our european neighbours. therefore, i abstain.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, thus giving my support to the voluntary partnership agreement (vpa) between the european union and the republic of indonesia on trade in wood products. its purpose is to establish a legislative framework to ensure the traceability of wood products, to establish a verification procedure to certify that wood products exported to the eu market have been lawfully acquired, harvested, transported and exported and to ensure the sound management and sustainable exploitation of indonesian forests.
in writing. i voted in favour of the jadot report on the voluntary partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of indonesia, as it supports the ratification of the voluntary partnership agreement.
in writing. this text improves the traceability of indonesian wood products and promotes sustainable management. it represents an important step in the fight against deforestation and forest degradation, which pose threats to biodiversity and sustainable development. i also think that this is a significant agreement for the health of the european economy and jobs, given that the union is the largest export market for indonesian wood products.

in writing. in the fight against the plunder of biodiversity, the issue of forest destruction is of the utmost importance. the agreement before us is part of the flegt (forest law enforcement for governance and trade) framework, which i supported in january 2011. but this agreement only allows partial progress towards the necessary establishment of a mechanism for sanctions for all environmental crimes. it introduces minimum regulation in indonesian timber imports to the eu. the recommendation calls on the commission to present to parliament an evaluation of the indonesian wood certification system before any eu authorisation is granted to indonesian wood products. but the independence of decisions on the granting and verification of export authorizations should be guaranteed by public services, and assistance should be provided to combat illegal logging. the absence of such measures is particularly regrettable. for these reasons, i abstain.
in writing. the objective of the voluntary partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of indonesia is to establish a legislative framework to ensure the traceability of timber products, to establish a verification procedure to certify that timber products exported to the european union market have been lawfully acquired, harvested, transported and exported and to ensure the sound management and lawful exploitation of indonesian forests, and to enhance the effectiveness of the european action plan on forest law enforcement, governance and trade. i was strongly committed to fairer and more equitable trade and could only support this agreement. but i also share the recommendations we made in the resolution: the indonesian certification system, which is currently being revised, must now rise to the occasion and seize this new opportunity to gain credibility.

in writing. the eu-iraq partnership and cooperation agreement should be categorically rejected: it should be used to end the violence, to help economic and social development, to promote effective progress on human rights, rather than to promote the expansion of european oil companies in the country. but above all, it shamefully ignores the main reasons for the state iraq is in today, and the identity of those responsible: the usa, the uk, and the rest of the coalition, in which, let us remember, france did not participate at that time! i vote against it!

in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on armed drones which calls on the european union to develop an appropriate european and global response that safeguards human rights and international humanitarian law. the text also calls on the european council to adopt a common eu position on the use of armed drones.
in writing. the use of armed drones is unacceptable. philosophically, the armed drone violates the first and most fundamental law of war: "in the context of war, it is legitimate for me to try to kill you without being considered a murderer because you are given the same right over me". from an efficiency standpoint, i favor human intelligence. this resolution opposes the use of armed drones and is within the only international legal framework: the un. i vote for it.

in writing. the european union is built around shared democratic values and affirmed fundamental rights. however, there are still too many situations in some member states where rights and freedoms are still not properly guaranteed. these include, for example, those of minorities, women, workers, the protection of privacy, the independence of the media and the judiciary. europeans must be more intransigent in respecting fundamental rights and it is essential that the union maintains a very high level of respect for rights for its citizens, but also for its image in the rest of the world. that is why the creation of a european supreme court, which would protect the values enshrined in the european charter of human rights, would be an important step in the construction of europe by protecting what we hold most precious in europe, our values.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the european arrest warrant. unfortunately, i have too many examples of the misuse of the ema, particularly in the context of binational divorces. several french parents were sued by an mae for alleged non-payment of alimony. instead of going through existing civil proceedings, some states, such as germany, use the mae and thus criminalise small-time affairs. the dea was created to fight major crime, not divorced parents!
in writing. by voting for this text, the european parliament asks the european commission to take action to reform the functioning of the european arrest warrant and other mutual recognition instruments. while the european arrest warrant is an effective instrument to facilitate the bringing of suspects and accused persons to justice, imperfections in the functioning of the system remain. the european union is an area of freedom, security and justice. it is therefore appropriate to stress that member states should ensure the proper application of union law on procedural rights in criminal proceedings relating to the use of the european arrest warrant. however, clarification of this legislation, such as a better definition of the crimes for which the european arrest warrant should be used, is needed.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the european arrest warrant. today, crime is transnational, and with cybercrime, it is increasingly common for a crime to have multiple points of connection in different countries. the european arrest warrant is an effective response to this problem. in addition, this text makes it possible to speed up and facilitate the bringing to justice of suspects and accused persons by modernising the current procedure, which i welcome.
in writing. since 2004, judicial authorities in the member states of the european union can issue a european arrest warrant to arrest suspects throughout the union. this improved cooperation between member states has considerably reduced the time taken for extraditing suspects to the countries where they are to be tried. nevertheless, the european parliament has asked the commission to make proposals to improve the respect for the rights of suspects and the conditions of detention. a european arrest warrant may exceptionally be refused if it threatens national security or if the requested measure is not authorised by national law. member states shall have 30 days to examine the request for a european arrest warrant and 90 days to execute it. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european arrest warrant is a useful instrument which needs to be improved in order to be more effective while ensuring that the fundamental rights of the accused are respected.
in writing. the european arrest warrant is an essential tool for cooperation between judicial and law enforcement authorities. we must improve it, while keeping in mind the importance of consistency of the rules of all the cooperation tools we have at our disposal, such as the european investigation order.
in writing. the european arrest warrant (eaw) adopted in 2002 replaces the extradition system by requiring each national judicial authority (judicial enforcement authority) to recognise, ipso facto, and subject to minimum checks, the request for surrender of a person made by the judicial authority of another member state. it was this arrangement that enabled france to hand aurore martin over to the spanish authorities for acts that did not correspond to any crime in france! this is an awkward situation. the report before us raises a number of criticisms of the use of the european arrest warrant and focuses on respect for human rights and the principle of proportionality. it is a step in the right direction and, to encourage these efforts, i am voting in favour.

in writing. this paper discusses the different legislation on private copying charges in europe. consumers have the right to make copies for personal use of certain legally acquired cultural works. however, in the digital age, ensuring adequate copyright protection is essential to secure the cultural sector. different national laws within the internal market sometimes raise certain difficulties. that is why i think it is important to deal with this issue at european level and to move towards harmonisation of legislation. in particular, it is necessary to establish a clear definition of the concept of private copying at european level.
in writing. in 23 of the member states of the european union, the reproduction of artistic works, such as films or music, is permitted for private use. in order to remunerate the persons holding the rights to these works, a tax is levied on multimedia devices and digital consumables. the €600 million raised by this tax is a vital supplement to the income of european artists. the european parliament adopted a report which supports the maintenance of this system of royalties while suggesting various alternatives, whereas royalties for private copying are not enough to compensate artists. i voted in favour of this text because i believe that the european union must find more appropriate solutions to safeguard cultural offerings and the rights of artists in the digital age.
in writing. i voted with a majority of my colleagues in favour of an own-initiative report on private copying, an exception mechanism for copyright, which allows those who own cultural property to make a copy of it in exchange for a royalty on the copying media. the report recommends adapting this mechanism to the emergence of new technologies, so that it is compatible with the emergence of new digital media for the consumption of cultural works and goods. the private copying system is very successful in our country, because it supports the creativity and competitiveness of our creative and cultural sectors, guaranteeing european cultural exceptionalism.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on private copying levies, which represents a balanced system between the private copying exception and the right to fair compensation for rightholders. however, the system could be improved at european level by adopting a common definition of 'fair compensation', a single charge and better visibility to consumers.
in writing. culture is seen here only as a commodity. moreover, this report is far from initiating the necessary reflection on the financing of culture. in the digital age, which is disrupting the modes of distribution and consumption, the text merely engraves in marble an outdated economic model of distribution which ultimately benefits only the artists and professionals who already benefit the most. it's time to stop pitting artists against their audiences. i vote against it.
in writing. the private copying levy is a system which exists in several member states, including france. it consists of levying a tax on the media capable of generating copies of digital works. i am committed to this mechanism: it supports a fair remuneration of authors, and constitutes an important source of funding for creation in the broad sense (allocation of part of the remuneration to actions of cultural or social interest, to the training of authors, to the deployment of festivals, etc.). it also allows the use of works by a large number of consumers without complex formalities, while remunerating the rightholders. i therefore supported this report, which places a premium on remuneration for private copying, while stressing the need to remain open to the evolution of digital technologies, to find appropriate solutions and modernise the approach to remuneration. i did not, however, support paragraph 3 of the text, which goes a little too far in advocating the spread of a fully harmonised system of charges in the eu. in the end, overall, this report shows that the eu is committed to protecting its cultural industry and wants to act to support it, and i share this conviction.

member of the commission. - mr president, on behalf of the commission, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr burkhard balz; mrs[nbsp ]sharon bowles, chair of the committee on economic and monetary affairs; the shadow rapporteurs mr peter skinner, mrs sylvie goulard, mr ashley fox and mr sven giegold; the committee on economic and monetary affairs and parliament as a whole for the work that has been done on omnibus ii. the agreement on omnibus ii that parliament reached with the council and the commission in november of last year, after almost three years of negotiations, is a very important step towards the introduction of a modern and risk-based solvency regime for the insurance industry in europe, as of 1[nbsp ]january[nbsp ]2016. it updates and completes the solvency ii directive. the new solvency requirements under solvency ii will be more sophisticated and more risk-sensitive than in the past, thus enabling a better coverage of the real risks of any particular insurer. the new requirements move away from a crude, one-model-fits-all way of estimating capital requirements to more entity-specific requirements. at the same time, unintended consequences for the real economy are avoided, because omnibus ii – thanks to the technical advice of the european insurance and occupational pensions authority (eiopa) and the insistence of this parliament – introduces a balanced package of measures that will enable insurers to provide insurance products with long-term guarantees. today’s vote also means that europe will soon have in place an insurance regime that will serve as an example for other regions in the world. solvency[nbsp ]ii will also put a greater focus on risks and their management, as well as introducing stricter rules on the public disclosure of certain information. solvency ii should thus increase confidence in the insurance market, making it both safer and more competitive. this long-awaited and vital reform is now becoming a reality. the commission is preparing the next stage of the implementation of solvency ii, which will be the adoption of a commission delegated act containing a large number of detailed implementing rules, as laid down in empowerments in the directive. important principles such as the proportionality principle, which are also very dear to this parliament, will be duly reflected on. the adoption of this delegated act is planned for the summer of this year. at the same time, eiopa is working hard on a package of implementing technical standards. everything will be ready for solvency ii application on 1[nbsp ]january[nbsp ]2016. at the request of the european parliament and the council, the omnibus ii directive contains two new articles – articles 2(ab) and 2(ac) – which amend both the esma and the eiopa regulations. the commission agrees with the substance of these amendments. however, as highlighted by the commission during the trilogue discussions, amending union regulations by the legislative instrument of a union directive is not in line with the principles of good legislative drafting. in this context, the commission also notes that the three esa regulations constitute an essential building block of the supervisory structure within the internal market for financial services, and thus for the banking union. due to the fundamental nature of the three esa regulations, and for reasons of legal certainty, it is the commission’s view that it is paramount to preserve the integrity and coherence of these regulations, avoiding subsequent or uncoordinated changes to these rules through sectoral legislation. thus, while the commission can accept the substance of these amendments, in the context of the final agreement on the omnibus ii proposal the commission is of the opinion that it would have been more appropriate to determine these issues in the context of the forthcoming horizontal review of the esa regulations. that said, i would again like to congratulate parliament on its instrumental work on this important dossier.

on behalf of the alde group. mr president, this is an important text which, in my view, is part of a much broader effort to improve transparency. in a number of texts which we have had to deal with in the committee on economic and monetary affairs, we have tried to limit tax evasion and tax evasion and to ensure that the revenue can be channelled into the coffers of the southern states in difficulty. what struck me most about my work here was that there had been a clear emphasis on budgetary discipline up to now, but that, in the end, the public authorities had been rather unconcerned about where some of the money generated by honest or less honest activities had gone. we can therefore only welcome this fourth anti-money laundering directive which goes even further and deals with criminal activities. it's good that we have central registers. the issue of trusts has been widely debated. there are major differences between member states. i hope we've found a satisfactory solution. i am struck by the fact that the text clearly identifies the people who are politically exposed; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the future of the internal market. i also believe that there are benefits to having both positive and negative lists of countries with risks or those outside the european union who are making efforts. i think that we are far from being right about this text, but that this collective work is going in the right direction. i would like to see progress also in the area of non-opportunity, not crime.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we all share the same conviction: that the rules on money laundering and the fight against tax evasion must be regularly reviewed. this should make us better equipped to cut off the sources of financial channels which may support criminal activities in europe. i therefore particularly welcome the progress that can be made with the text which the european parliament is going to vote on today. one of the best ways to put an end to the shell companies behind which some people hide to launder the dirty money from criminal activities is to have a public register of beneficial owners. it is well known that too divergent practices in identifying the beneficial owners of companies and legal persons facilitate the use of opaque structures, especially when this is coupled with insufficiently binding national regulations which encourage the development of unregulated structures. by listing the ultimate beneficiaries of companies or trusts in the public central registers of the member states of the european union, we can end the anonymity of offshore companies and accounts used by fraudsters to conceal their financial transactions. a mandatory, centralised and publicly accessible public register is therefore an indispensable tool for achieving an effective fight against money laundering. this is the same reasoning that guides me against exemptions of the gaming industry from its vigilance obligations, even in cases of low risk of money laundering. i believe that such a derogation could not only lead to serious distortions of competition but also allow money launderers to choose the territories where the legislation is more permissive. i therefore believe that it would be preferable to adopt a graduated and therefore, in some cases, lighter surveillance system to take account of the constraints of small operators, as suggested by the fatf.

in writing. i voted against the european parliament's report on the provision and quality of statistics for the macroeconomic imbalances procedure. officially, this is to ensure the quality, the speed of production and the provision of statistical data by also monitoring their quality. but in reality, these established statistics are major tools for detecting "macroeconomic imbalances". we know what that means, and we know what it means to put the emphasis on preventing and correcting excessive imbalances within the union. these are, under the guise of 'good' governance, major tools for the surveillance of national budgets as implemented in the context of austerity policies. this will strengthen the commission's upstream control and give it statistical tools to base its bloody recommendations to the member states on structural reforms, and here again we know what that means. the political group to which i belong in this parliament, the gue/ngl, rejects these policies in general and wants to promote other policies based on solidarity and a different distribution of wealth.

in writing. money laundering is a significant impediment to the smooth functioning of the financial sector. this type of criminal activity undermines the integrity of the european financial sector, represents a huge loss of revenue for the states and distorts competition. we must fight every day to eradicate this scourge. i am glad that i voted in favour of this report. the legislation will make it possible to better prevent and detect money laundering and terrorist financing at source. it will also lead to improved traceability of funds transfers and transparency, while ensuring citizens' privacy and fundamental rights are protected. a common strategy in this area is the only solution to preserve the european financial sector, which has already been badly damaged by the crisis. the harmonization and adaptation of member states' policies will be a means of ensuring safety and effectiveness in the fight against these reprehensible criminal acts.
in writing. i supported this report in my vote in plenary, as the new directive will strengthen the prevention of the use of the financial system for the conversion of proceeds of criminal activities into lawful funds. according to the international monetary fund, money laundering is widespread, amounting to almost 5% of world gdp. such criminal activities undermine the integrity of the financial sector, cause a loss of revenue for governments, distort competition, hinder the proper functioning of markets and undermine development. this scourge requires a comprehensive and coordinated arsenal of prevention and sanctions at both the european union and its member states.
in writing. this is a proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council granting a european union guarantee to the european investment bank against losses under financing operations for projects outside the union for the period 2014-2020. the council and parliament, the two budgetary authorities of the union, have reached an agreement, which i support.
in writing. this text deals with projects with third countries under the european union guarantee to the european investment bank (eib). i support such a text, which states that the eib should in particular promote investment, research and innovation projects by smes in order to support local development. i believe it is essential to help young businesses develop their innovative ideas in order to attract funding.
in writing. i voted in favour of this decision of the european parliament and of the council, which aims to bring eib financing operations more closely into line with eu policies and to strengthen their coherence and complementarity with eu instruments.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr ivailo kalfin, on the european union guarantee to the european investment bank (eib) in the event of losses resulting from financing operations for projects outside the union for the period from 1 january 2014 to 31 december 2020. the report mainly proposes to refocus the geographical scope of the eib's mandate, to set a new ceiling for financing operations, to strengthen the climate change component of the mandate and to better align eib financing operations with union policies. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. under the new multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, the eib's mandate for its external missions will amount to eur 25 billion. the proposal aims to fix the amount of the union guarantees to the eib's own resources by means of the provisioning of the guarantee fund for external actions. with a fixed ceiling of up to eur 27 billion and an optional additional amount of eur 3 billion, the main objective of this fund is to ensure that the eib maintains its aaa rating. in approving this report, we are being asked to approve the disastrous policy of the eib. i am opposed to external funding which would be better used in the eu. i am opposed to the logic of productivist projects in a lamentable indifference to the environment, just as i am opposed to the financing techniques which encourage the privatization of public services and facilities. i vote against it.
in writing. as genetic resources represent a significant economic interest, their exploitation can cause serious environmental and ethical problems. in view of this situation, the international community and the european union have decided to take action to regulate their use and the distribution of the benefits derived from them. i voted in favour of this text because it is an important issue.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to give the union the tools it needs to combat biopiracy, through the nagoya protocol. in other words, it aims to prohibit the use of illegally acquired genetic resources and thus to ensure a fair and equitable sharing of the use of these resources. this is in line with the improvement of biodiversity conservation.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which will enable the union to comply with the nagoya protocol. while the question of access to resources is left to the sovereignty of the member states, it is important to provide a clear community framework on the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits derived from the use of natural resources. the text will improve the chain of use of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, but also increase transparency and legal certainty (in particular in the fight against biopiracy). i am pleased to see that the report contains clear definitions and clarifies the obligations of users of genetic resources. the latter was a priority in order not to create excessive burdens for users and authorities. all these provisions will enable the european union to secure its place and its leading role in the current international negotiations. we must rapidly achieve an ambitious multilateral mechanism that can meet the challenges of preserving biodiversity and its sustainable use.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague sandrine bélier, which is the result of negotiations with the council and the commission on the 'apa' regulation. the aim of the new regulation is to transpose the nagoya protocol, which establishes a general framework for access to genetic resources (used for the development of new medicines, for example) and to combat illegal access to these resources (biopiracy). this transposition is necessary for the ratification of the protocol itself and constitutes a balanced compromise. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. - the exploitation of natural resources, including genetic resources, should be left to the sovereignty of the member states, but a european regulatory mechanism should be established to harmonise access to these resources and make it fair for all eu member states, as a result of the entry into force of the nagoya protocol. in this sense, i am particularly in favour of the improvement of legal certainty, the chain of use of genetic resources and the associated traditional knowledge, as proposed in the report.
in writing. this regulation provides for the transposition into member states of the nagoya protocol on genetic resources and the protection of biodiversity. i regret that the final text lacks safeguards against fraudulent exploitation of these resources by industry. moreover, it does not prohibit the patentability of living things and private companies from profiting from them. however, given the progress it has made in the fight against bio-piracy, i cannot oppose it. i vote for it.
in writing. the nagoya protocol on access to genetic resources and the fair sharing of benefits arising from their utilization was adopted in october 2010. it is a supplementary agreement to the convention on biological diversity and concerns the conditions for access and sharing for the use of genetic resources. the text put to the vote by meps aims to implement the regulation for the application of the nagoya protocol at european level. it would, for example, improve the union's position in terms of traceability, fair sharing of benefits and compliance with international obligations. i therefore decided to vote in favour of this text because it is essential that the union has a suitable regulatory framework to combat the illegal exploitation and trade in genetic resources.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which states that the objective of the regulation is to achieve a fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from the use of genetic resources, thereby contributing to the conservation of biological diversity and the sustainable use of its components, in line with the objectives of the convention on biological diversity.
in writing. three years after the adoption of the nagoya protocol on access to genetic resources and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from their use, the council and the european parliament have reached agreement on the regulation implementing the protocol in the eu, which aims to combat bio-piracy. the regulation prohibits the use of illegally acquired genetic resources (animal, plant, etc.) in the eu. it obliges users (companies, scientific institutions, etc.) to verify that the acquisition of these resources and the traditional knowledge associated with them has been legal, and to share equitably the benefits derived from them on the basis of agreements negotiated with the countries and holders of origin. a european benefit-sharing fund will be established. it is part of the goal of a more inclusive and sustainable world, preserving biodiversity and its use by local populations. but there are no guarantees on exploitation by industrialists, and no controls, as the council opposed the tightening of access conditions and sanctions. i therefore abstained in the adoption of the legislation which will allow the eu to ratify this protocol. the indigenous peoples and ngos must fill the gaps through their action.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which introduces new rules on roadworthiness tests with the aim of further improving road safety and ensuring a high level of environmental protection.
in writing. i voted in favour of the werner kuhn report because the agreement reached at first reading between parliament and the council is satisfactory. it provides for heavy motorcycles to be subject to periodic technical inspection from 2022. however, member states may exempt such vehicles from the control if they have put in place other effective road safety measures, in the light of the road safety statistics of the last five years. heavy motorcycles are covered by the periodic roadworthiness test, but the specific methods of testing, areas of testing and frequency remain the responsibility of the member states. this report makes progress towards the development of common rules harmonised at european level which promote the free movement of union citizens.
in writing. this text is a step forward for road safety and environmental protection in the union in that it sets stricter standards for vehicle tracking. it consists of making the monitoring of certain vehicles more rigorous by, for example, aligning the inspection frequency of vehicles with high mileage (over 160[nbsp ]000[nbsp ]km) with that of older vehicles. for two-wheelers, only motorcycles with an engine exceeding 125cc will be subject to a mandatory technical inspection, and only from 2022. but member states will not be obliged to make these checks compulsory if they put in place effective alternative measures. this postponement of the requirement for roadworthiness tests for two-wheelers and the margin of manoeuvre granted to member states seems to me to be in the right direction, as only a small proportion of fatal accidents involving two-wheelers are due to technical failures.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which is part of the package of measures on technical inspection, by guaranteeing better access to information. i fully support this report, one of the measures of which is to inspect old and high-mileage vehicles every year, as is already the case with taxis and ambulances. i hope that this will reduce the number of road accidents caused by technical failures.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it will improve road safety without restricting the freedom of european drivers. i am particularly pleased with the exclusion of two- and three-wheel motor vehicles from the scope of the regulation, on which i was strongly committed. heavy motorcycles will be subject to periodic technical inspection from 2022 onwards only if a member state cannot demonstrate that other effective road safety measures have been implemented. the specific methods of control and their frequency will be the responsibility of the member states. the proposal also provides that in the event of re-registration of a vehicle from one member state to another, the authorities must recognise the valid technical inspection certificate issued by the member state of origin. these common harmonised rules will facilitate the cross-border movement of european citizens.
in writing. i welcome the final adoption of the text on roadworthiness tests, which restores to member states the power to authorise a roadworthiness test for two-wheelers. it is a victory for the citizens who have been strongly mobilized, especially since the european parliament was very divided on the subject. the socialist party and the greens, in particular, were campaigning for compulsory inclusion of two-wheelers in the scope of the regulation. these technical checks will therefore remain optional in countries which at the same time pursue preventive policies and take effective road safety measures. france, for example, reduced the death rate for scooters by 46 percent and for motorcycles by 25 percent between 2000 and 2010. only 1[nbsp ]% of fatal accidents involving motorcycles are due to technical failures. it seems to me therefore inconsistent to increase the number of checks when the causes of accidents are not due to technical problems. however, two- and three-wheelers remain vulnerable on the roads and that is why it is essential that we continue to improve road infrastructure, to provide prevention and training and to punish offences such as vehicle overloading.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague werner kuhn establishing a periodic technical inspection of vehicles. the specific provisions for two and three-wheelers leave sufficient room for manoeuvre for member states by making periodic roadworthiness testing of large cylinders mandatory from 2022, unless a member state can justify other effective road safety measures, such as training of motorcyclists or adapting road infrastructure for 'vulnerable' users. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr kuhn's report because there is an increasing mobility in europe today and that is why there is a need for more harmonized legislation on technical inspections. the directive covers cars, buses, commercial vehicles and their trailers, but does not include mopeds and motorcycles. the aim is to reduce the number of deaths caused by road accidents in the eu, and to reduce emissions of pollutants due to inadequate maintenance of vehicles, by increasing the frequency and quality of periodic roadworthiness tests. the new rules require member states to use risk classification systems to identify factories where vehicles have a poor safety record and thus reduce the administrative burden for those that have a good safety record.
in writing. the commission's proposal to introduce annual technical checks for two-wheelers, regardless of the type of engine, was far too intrusive and burdensome for motorcyclists. parliament proposed a balanced solution, taking account of motorcyclists and safety requirements. it calls for technical checks every two years from 2022 and only for cylinders over 125 cubic centimetres and older than 4 years. parliament also gives the possibility to those states which so wish to push these requirements further, but without forcing others to do so. i therefore supported this text, which sets out a minimum level of security controls while significantly reducing the constraints proposed by the commission.
in writing. at the end of 2013, the lithuanian presidency of the european union committed to postpone technical checks on motorised two-wheelers until 2022 and to leave the choice to member states to exclude these vehicles from checks. today the commission and parliament want to reverse this commitment and introduce these checks as early as 2018, on the pretext that they will improve road safety. the argument is fallacious: independent studies show that technical failures are the cause of less than 1[nbsp]% of accidents involving motorcycles. in reality, it is very likely that this european change in the direction of motorized two-wheelers is being driven by large multinationals such as dekra, which see technical controls as a lucrative source of profit. in fact, dekra's influence is particularly noteworthy, since no less than three of its reports were used to write the text! in the field of technical control, only two elements must prevail: the safety of users and the fight against air pollution. the commission's and parliament's text does not improve either. i vote against it.
in writing. i was initially strongly opposed to this text, which envisaged imposing a compulsory technical inspection on two-wheelers without taking into account the particularity of these vehicles. the european parliament's vote endorses an agreement reached with the council last december which is, on the whole, a compromise in favour of two- and three-wheel vehicles. it endorses the choice of a directive rather than a regulation, as originally proposed by the european commission, and thus allows for greater flexibility in implementing the objectives pursued by the european union. the adopted directive is thus sufficiently flexible to meet both road safety objectives and concerns about the costs and constraints for two-wheelers. it will be for each member state, and therefore also for france, to decide whether or not to apply the requirement of technical inspection to two-wheelers. i voted for this compromise.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which will simplify the lives of motorists travelling in europe by mutual recognition of technical inspections. this will eventually be done without undue pressure on motorists and motorcyclists. despite the powerful lobbying of the control centers, this is a victory for the reason we are witnessing: motorcycle accidents are almost never related to a technical failure. standards must be proportionate to the context and the objective. in the end, therefore, member states will be free to decide on the methods and frequency of checks for motorcycles. this is good news for french motorcyclists, as france has already expressed its opposition to the technical inspection of motorcycles.
in writing. road safety needs to be improved in europe. too often we hear of serious accidents caused by faulty vehicles. it is important to make periodic roadworthiness tests of cars compulsory throughout the union in order to prevent such accidents as much as possible. i am glad that i voted in favour of this report. i am also glad that i fought for the abolition of the compulsory technical inspection of two- and three-wheelers. it seemed to me disproportionate, given the specific nature of these vehicles, to create an obligation for all member states. motorcyclists are generally passionate about their vehicles and are aware of their vulnerability. it is true that it is important to harmonize the laws of the various countries of our union, but europe has better things to do than to legislate on problems that are not problems.
in writing. more and more vehicles are being sold in one member state and then re-registered in another. it has therefore become necessary to provide europeans with equal guarantees regarding safety and vehicle inspection points. i supported this report, but i did not want to extend this common technical inspection obligation to two- and three-wheel vehicles under european law. in france, only 1[nbsp ]% of fatal accidents involving two or three wheels are due to technical failures. i therefore felt that it was disproportionate to impose new budgetary burdens on our citizens for their vehicles, for the sake of a small profit in road safety. the text adopted therefore states that it will be for governments themselves, depending on their safety assessments and objectives, to decide whether to apply the regulation to two- or three-wheel vehicles.
in writing. two reports were put to the vote on vehicle inspection: one by werner kuhn (epp, germany) on motor vehicles and their trailers and the other by olga sehnalova (s&d, estonia) on commercial vehicles. the first involves considerable progress in improving and developing the quality of periodic technical inspections by setting up minimum european standards. the second reinforces the application of technical roadside checks which complement the periodic technical checks and take place in an unannounced manner. i think it is important to strengthen vehicle controls: the safety of users must take precedence over the frivolity of the automobile industry. i therefore voted for both reports, although i have doubts about the real interests served by the multiplication of these standards and i regret that the proposals of my group, the gue/ngl, to place the responsibility for the lack of vehicle control on employers have been systematically rejected.

in writing. this report takes stock of the european financial surveillance system put in place in 2009 to prevent a new financial crisis like the one in 2008. the fact that the mechanisms in place are inadequate is a fair observation, and the criticisms of the commission's decision-making role in these bodies are well founded. however, the proposed adjustments do not in any way solve the problems posed by the excessive financialization of the economy. as always, the ultimate objective is to ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market and the stability of financial markets. for me, it's about governing against the banks, not with them. i vote against it.
in writing. the 2008 crisis highlighted the very unreliable nature of the financial market. the european union immediately took steps to restructure the financial system to avoid the current crisis. the european system of financial supervision is one of these measures. it ensures the stability of the european financial system. the union has not stopped there, however, and has put in place other crisis prevention and resolution mechanisms such as the single resolution mechanism. the union's objective is to harmonise these different instruments in order to protect citizens from the financial sector's abuses. the harmonization of the financial policies of the member states is also of considerable importance. let us remember that the crisis is a sovereign debt crisis. i am convinced that with the measures taken by the union, we will never again experience such a serious economic and financial crisis. i am glad that i voted in favour of this report, which sets out the various points which need to be improved in order to make the european financial surveillance system fully operational.
in writing. in response to the financial crisis, europe established three financial supervisory authorities for banks, financial markets and macro-prudential policies in 2010. the time has now come to strengthen the mandate of these three authorities, as monitoring and risk management are not yet optimal. in particular, they must be given the capacity to initiate proceedings and take decisions autonomously, as is done in the united states. the european parliament therefore calls for an immediate revision of the regulations on financial supervision, based on experience and respecting fundamental rights and the principle of subsidiarity.

in writing. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon gave binding force to the charter of fundamental rights and its articles 41 on good administration and 42 on the right of access to documents of the union institutions. with regard to the 2001 eu legislation on public access to documents, the court of justice has consistently found that the eu institutions too often abuse exceptional measures without a valid reason. the resolution therefore calls in particular for the 2001 regulation to be reviewed and for the protection of personal data not to be used as a pretext for refusing certain information. i share these views, but i abstained because this resolution is far from meeting the challenges of better democratic functioning, particularly with regard to access to documents in one's own language, transparency on trilogues and, above all, information on international and free trade agreements. the european parliament rightly denounces the practices of the commission and the council, but it must also sweep up its own door and live up to its responsibilities by fully assuming its role as co-legislator and rejecting certain council positions. this is how the democratic deficit of the union can perhaps begin to be filled.

vice-president of the commission. - madam president, the single european sky initiative is one of the most important eu projects in the field of air transport. our air traffic management system is fragmented and plagued by delays. it lacks independent oversight, relies on outdated technology and it is vastly more costly than comparable systems elsewhere. with the single european sky project we have taken the first step towards addressing these issues: creating real oversight, laying the groundwork for modernising technology and, for the first time in the history of air transport, we have halted the rise in costs. you might ask why, if we have already done all those wonderful things, we need a new proposal. the answer is that we are only at the beginning of a long road, and whilst we have made some progress, we are nowhere near our goals. the ses[nbsp ]ii+ initiative is not about a new policy, it is about moving to the next stage in the implementation of those existing policies, and that is why we need this proposal. with ses[nbsp ]ii+ we are making the safety and technical oversight authorities truly independent of those they oversee. as remarkable as it may sound, we still have an area where the authorities are part of the organisation they oversee and are sometimes even staffed by the people who have to be overseen. i am sure we can all agree that this is not a recipe for robust safety oversight. ses[nbsp ]ii also clarifies the role of the european aviation safety agency (easa), the commission and eurocontrol by focusing on their respective strengths and avoiding overlaps. we are also pushing for more transparency in how support services are procured. air traffic services today are still not procured under the normal public procurement rules, which allows unhealthy relationships to flourish. the proposal gives a new boost to the functional airspace blocks, allowing industry more freedom and more flexibility. the decision-making in the performance scheme is rationalised and made more independent. as regards parliamentʼs amendments, i fully understand that in a few countries the idea of independent oversight authorities is a difficult one, but unless the authorities are given real resources and independence, we will never have full implementation of the single sky, nor a true assurance of safety. the audits which the easa conducts have revealed some major deficiencies in oversight which we should rectify before accidents happen. similarly, we have some concerns with the amendments deleting the separation of the support service provider. this could make fair and transparent tendering impossible. there is a clear need to ensure that the choice of provider is made on clear and objective criteria and is duly justified. the commission welcomes most of the amendments to the easa basic regulation, which enhance the role of this institution. there are only limited cases where the commission does not share the point of view of the committee on transport and tourism (tran). regarding delegated acts, the commission holds that the text should follow the common understanding on delegated acts and not introduce further requirements, even if the commission has voluntarily taken to including expert groups’ views in its proposals. secondly, we would prefer to maintain an end-of-term evaluation of the executive director of easa. this is particularly important when preparing for reappointment. let me conclude by thanking parliament once more for its support. the successful completion of the first reading in parliament will turn the spotlight on the council and, hopefully, push member states to do their part.

in writing. this text revises european legislation on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data. the protection of personal data is a fundamental right guaranteed in europe by the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the current legislation dates from 1995, well before the dramatic advances of the digital age, and is no longer adapted to the challenges posed by the development of the internet. it seems to me therefore absolutely essential to adapt this legal framework to ensure adequate protection of the personal data of european citizens. in particular, it seems appropriate to adopt directly applicable legislation in a uniform manner in the member states to put an end to the fragmented approach to data protection. finally, the granting of new rights to european citizens, such as the right to have personal data concerning them erased, seems to me particularly interesting.
in writing. despite the rise of the internet in recent years, the rules for protecting the data of european citizens and consumers have been the same since 1995. the european legislation has therefore had to be adapted. new rules will now ensure a much higher level of protection and information for citizens and consumers. for example, companies will have to provide clear and understandable notices on the use of their customers' data. citizens will also finally be able to benefit from the 'right to be forgotten', i.e. the erasure of their personal data on the internet. any violation of these rules will be severely punished by fines of up to 5% of the annual turnover of the companies charged. all these measures should make it possible to better control the use and transfer of citizens' personal data.

in writing. meps adopted a text to better regulate the processing of personal data, in particular data recorded on social networks, online banking sites and in the customer registers of companies. we have improved information for citizens by requiring data controllers to inform users about the conditions for processing data and their rights, for example by indicating how long data will be kept or whether it is possible to lodge a complaint. persons who have entrusted their personal data will have a right of access to such data and a right to have it deleted. member states will have to set up one or more independent supervisory authorities, which will cooperate with each other within the european data protection board. any person shall have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority. member states will also have to clarify the liability of subcontractors and define criminal sanctions. i voted in favour of this proposal because the current legislation, dating from 1995, did not provide sufficient protection for the personal data of citizens in the context of the rapidly developing market for the processing of personal data.
