in writing. manufactured nanomaterials are created by humans to meet certain medical or food needs. although the details of possible future applications are not yet known, this is probably a future area. so far, scientific studies do not conclude that there is a danger but call for caution. however, some nanomaterials are not manufactured but have long been present in foods, such as dutch sauce or mayonnaise. the legislative framework for nanomaterials is provided by the consumer information regulation, adopted at the end of 2011 and which will enter into force on 13 december 2014. the delegated act prepared by the european commission to ensure the application of this text provides for the labelling of nanomaterials present in food, with certain limitations. today, this resolution calling for full labelling (old and new nanomaterials) seems excessive to me, creating confusion for consumers who will wonder why their mayonnaise is now described as containing nanomaterials and who will assume that this is synonymous with a particular risk, and finally difficult to apply, because a very low nanoparticle content is difficult to detect, which means that such a measure would not be controllable by the competent authorities. i therefore voted against this resolution.
in writing. i rejected the objection to the european commission delegated regulation amending the legislation on the definition of manufactured nanomaterials in food. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the proposal. requiring producers to indicate all ingredients that occur as manufactured nanomaterials on the list of food ingredients would lead to excessive labelling requirements. it is not possible to distinguish naturally occurring nanomaterials in food from manufactured nanomaterials. it is therefore very difficult to apply such legislation. i regret that, by this vote, the european parliament has chosen legislation which will contribute more to confusion than to consumer protection.
in writing. i voted against the resolution on the objection to a delegated act of the european commission on consumer information on foodstuffs as regards the definition of 'manufactured nanomaterials'. this delegated act provided for the labelling of all nanomaterials present in food, whether manufactured or natural. however, nanomaterials containing less than 50% of particles with one or more dimensions in the range of 1 to 100 nanometres, as well as food additives (already present on the official union list of food additives) were not covered by this new proposed definition. however, these limitations are the basis for parliament's objection to this delegated act, which calls for full labelling of all nanomaterials. such a provision would be unworkable in practice, as low levels of nanoparticles are very difficult to detect. it would also cause confusion and concern for consumers, who would see the term 'nano' on the labelling of certain food products already on the market, even though they are not the subject of new suspicions of health risks. i regret the adoption of this resolution.
in writing. i voted against the resolution calling on the european commission to make mandatory the labelling of food containing manufactured nanomaterials, ingredients obtained through the use of nanotechnologies. i consider this proposal to be unrealistic and unnecessary, since some nanomaterials are naturally present in food, such as fruit juices, powdered products and milk, including those from organic production. furthermore, the requirement to change all food packaging would be a significant cost to the industry. i therefore hope that the european commission will maintain its original proposal. the commission act does not provide for labelling of food containing nanomaterials but will clarify the definition of 'manufactured nanomaterials' and define an acceptable threshold of nanomaterials in food.
in writing. i voted against the objection to a delegated act on consumer information on foodstuffs as regards information on nanomaterials, as the proposal is difficult to apply and could create confusion among consumers.
in writing. the resolution aims to oppose a commission regulation which seeks to repeal the provisions on the labelling of all food additives which are in the form of manufactured nanomaterials. this exemption creates confusion between the food safety aspects and the general labelling provisions intended to inform consumers. the presence of nanomaterials in food is likely to raise food safety concerns. it is a serious mistake to remove the obligation to inform about them. i am voting for this report which seeks to prevent that.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which rejects the commission delegated regulation of 12[nbsp ]december[nbsp ]2013 amending regulation (eu) no[nbsp ]1169/2011 of the european parliament and of the council on the provision of food information to consumers (the [nbsp ]inco regulation) as regards the definition of 'manufactured nanomaterials'. such a delegated regulation would lead to discrimination between additives with similar properties, which could lead to a possible distortion of the market. it would hinder the proper provision of information to consumers and would go beyond the scope of the delegation given to the european commission.
in writing. in december 2012, the commission presented a draft delegated act to amend union legislation on the labelling of nanomaterials in food by the end of 2014. the commission wanted to exempt manufacturers from the obligation to mention 'nano' in front of ingredients used in nanometric form in food labelling. this was particularly the case with food additives which have long been used in the form of nanomaterials in our food. the reason given by the commission is that this would create confusion and a certain fear among consumers. it was thus giving in to the lobbying of the agri-food industry. i voted against this commission proposal and i am glad that a majority of members of the european parliament did the same. the european parliament has refused to allow the commission to take up the right of consumers to be informed. this exemption would have set a very unfortunate precedent in the face of the many unknowns and uncertainties in science, the environment and health related to nanomaterials, which are already abundant in our daily lives. the legislative framework on this technology is seriously lagging behind. support for technological innovation must not be at the expense of protecting health and the environment.
in writing. unlike the albrecht report on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data, i voted against the report presented by my colleague dimitrios droutsas. the rapporteur has not, in my view, succeeded in striking a reasonable balance between the right to privacy on the one hand and the activities of investigation and prosecution on the other. the council and the experts in the judicial and police community consider that the compromises are neither feasible nor close to reality.
in writing. this legislation establishes legislation on the protection of personal data processed by law enforcement authorities for the purposes of crime prevention. i voted against this text, which presents too great a imbalance between the protection of personal data, which is admittedly a fundamental right that must be protected, and the necessary exploitation of them for security purposes. it is regrettable that such a desire to protect our fellow citizens is actually detrimental to them in the sense that the authorities responsible for fighting crime will be hampered in their work. i regret that such a vote seems neither realistic nor feasible.
in writing. i voted against the report by my colleague dimitrios droutsas which sought to introduce provisions relating to the protection of personal data specifically for judicial authorities. the report places disproportionate burdens on the authorities in the member states, which will unfairly hamper their mission to prevent and combat crime. although the protection of personal data is necessary, including in the fight against crime, it is regrettable that this results in an unnecessary burden on those responsible for protecting european citizens on a daily basis. i therefore regret the adoption of this report.
in writing. we must always uphold the highest standards of personal data protection. however, it is necessary to be realistic and pragmatic and not to impose requirements that are disproportionate. we must not slow down and hamper the work of the police force by imposing unnecessary or excessive bureaucratic constraints.
in writing. the regulation on the protection of personal data is accompanied by a directive specifically on the processing of such data in law enforcement and criminal law. the report significantly improves the commission's proposal, particularly as regards the conditions for using data (retention period, transparency), transfers to third countries and profiling. it calls for a number of impact analyses (including on video surveillance). the council must now hear our demands and accept this agreement. i am voting for this proposal which gives greater scope to the protection of personal data in the criminal field.
in writing. this report advocates the creation of an effective framework for the protection of european citizens' data. while proposing some improvements to strengthen the protection of citizens as a whole, the report welcomes the efforts made by the commission to create a unified framework for data protection and to harmonise the different systems existing in the member states. convinced that the protection of personal data is one of the major challenges of the digital economy for the years to come, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which will protect the freedoms and fundamental rights of natural persons, in particular their right to the protection of personal data, and which will guarantee the free exchange of personal data by the competent authorities within the union. this regulation lays down rules on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data by the competent authorities for the purposes of the prevention and detection of, investigation and prosecution of, or execution of criminal offences.
in writing. the new legislative package merges the four regulations on the single european sky into one regulation (marinescu report). i voted in favour of this report because it brings together the four key performance objectives of safety, the environment, capacity and economic efficiency. air traffic control agencies will have to provide better services at lower cost. the new legislative package aims to improve the independence and transparency of the setting of objectives and to strengthen the control of their application. in parallel, the independence of the performance review body will be strengthened and sanctions may be applied in case of failure of member states to meet targets.
in writing. the aim of this text is to strengthen competitiveness in the air transport sector by developing the 'single european sky'. i support such legislation, which streamlines airspace management. this vote is therefore a step towards better performance in the sector, which will be favourable to growth and the creation of highly skilled jobs in europe. finally, it is important to work towards reducing the impact of air transport on the climate and the environment.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr marian-jean marinescu, on the implementation of the single european sky. the objective is to lay down rules for the establishment and proper functioning of the single european sky in order to preserve the current safety standards for air traffic and to contribute to the sustainable development of the air transport system, in particular by reducing the impact on the climate. the report proposes to improve the efficiency of support services, encourage industrial partnerships and strengthen the independence of national supervisory authorities and the role of the network manager. i'm very happy about the adoption.
in writing. i voted in favour of the reports on the implementation of the single european sky, which aim to strengthen the independence of national supervisory authorities, strengthen the role of the network manager, strengthen industrial partnerships and improve the performance of support services, such as meteorological, communication and navigation services, which could eventually be opened up to competition.
in writing. after the single european sky i in 2004 and the single european sky ii in 2009, the single european sky 2+ is now in place. what is the commission's new text? nothing new, except that the competition for airspace management services is accelerating. the commission's explanatory statement is clearer than ever on the objective pursued: 'with a workforce of 38% less, the us operator controls almost 70% of additional flights'. the commission states that 'the main causes of this productivity deficit in europe are the inadequate implementation and enforcement of the performance system, the inefficiency of the supervisory authorities and the disproportionate number of support services working for service providers'. incredible violence from this council. my priority in airspace management is the safety of the users. i cannot accept the dangerous, narrow and limited view of the commission and the marinescu report on this point. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted against this report which supports the very dogmatic approach of the european commission, which only sees the air navigation sector through a very liberal lens. beyond that, the provisions in this proposal are premature and in some respects excessive in relation to the balanced outcome achieved in the negotiations on the single sky 2 package. these reforms need to be timed.
in writing. while all the forecasts indicate that air traffic will increase sharply in the coming years, we are slow to take measures to cope with this development. as airspace remains highly fragmented, the increase in traffic is likely to result in increased congestion, with costs in economic, environmental and safety terms. i therefore voted for the marinescu report because the implementation of the single european sky will help to alleviate these problems. it will provide citizens with safer, shorter, more cost-effective flights, help our airlines to withstand international competition and support our aviation industry by improving our interoperability through the deployment of the sesar system. in particular, the implementation of the single european sky will play a positive role in growth, employment and competitiveness in europe by stimulating demand for skilled jobs, in particular in the field of air navigation and air traffic control. i hope that the diversity of actors, the complexity of procedures and the divergences between national and sectoral interests will not prevent us from achieving a genuine integration of european skies, for the benefit of all actors.
in writing. the european regulation known as the 'single european sky' is not new. it is part of the logic of the dismantling of public services. the european commission wants to go further and impose a separation between regulatory and supervisory authorities and service providers, as for railways. in france, this will mean a change in the status of the dgac, which could no longer be composed of the dsna (provider), the dsac (supervisory authority) and the dta (regulator). this may lead to operators refocusing on their core business, air traffic control, with the outsourcing of a whole series of activities, such as the design and publication of air navigation procedures, the maintenance of air navigation systems, the national civil aviation school... the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's air transport sector is not left to the mercy of the market. the unions mobilized on 30 january against this overhaul. we support their demands and have therefore voted against.
in writing. the new legislative package merges the four regulations on the single european sky into one regulation (marinescu report). the easa regulation (sassoli report) is amended: certain items that overlap with the current regulation (ec) no[nbsp ]216/2008 have been deleted in the single european sky regulations. i therefore voted in favour of these amendments because they simplify the legal corpus and thus provide more clarity.
in writing. i voted in favour of such a text adapting the provisions on the european aviation safety agency (easa) to the legislative developments under way in the context of the development of the single european sky. in particular, it seems particularly important to clearly define the role of this agency in this new context and its powers. such rationalization of legislation on aerodromes, air traffic management and air navigation services provides greater clarity and thus improved aviation safety in europe.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague david-maria sassoli on the simplification and clarification of the legislative framework for aerodromes, air traffic management and air navigation services. the report aims to put an end to the duplication of work between the single european sky regulations and the european aviation safety agency (easa). it also proposes to strengthen and extend the role of the easa. however, he stressed that security remained the agency's primary mission. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. i voted in favour of the reports on the implementation of the single european sky, which aim to strengthen the independence of national supervisory authorities, strengthen the role of the network manager, strengthen industrial partnerships and improve the performance of support services, such as meteorological, communication and navigation services, which could eventually be opened up to competition.
in writing. after the single european sky (ses) i in 2004 and the ses ii in 2009, the ses 2+ is now the ses. these legislative packages are based on a liberal approach to air traffic management. safety is always secondary. what does this text suggest? he wants to apply civil aviation rules to some of the military aviation first. i refuse to do so because it is an infringement of national sovereignty. the commission's text then explains that 'civil aviation must be regulated in such a way as to promote its development, performance, interoperability and safety in a manner commensurate with the nature of each activity'. we can see here that the liberal logic puts safety first. the sassoli report saw this and reversed the wording, moving safety to the top of the list and adding points on environmental protection. however, it does not remove the passage on 'proportionate' nor does it call into question the application of civil rules to military aviation. safety must not be provided in a 'proportionate manner': it must be provided. that's it. i am voting against this text.
in writing. the report aims to extend consumer rights in the package travel and assisted travel services sector, which is still far too opaque and unfair to european consumers.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which strengthens consumer protection in the internal market in the context of the purchase of package holidays and assisted travel services. tourism is a major sector in europe that must be promoted. it is important to close the legal gaps, in particular with regard to packages and travel services sold online, in order to give consumers confidence in these products and to strengthen this sector, which is mainly composed of smes. it is therefore essential to ensure uniform consumer protection in the single market. it is therefore a relevant proposal to regulate the responsibility of the organiser for the performance of the services included in the package.
in writing. i voted in favour of this legislative report on package travel and assisted travel services. the text allows account to be taken of developments in the tourism sector and in travellers' practices, generated in particular by the widespread use of online bookings, the liberalisation of the airline sector and the diversification of travellers' requests (personalised trips). the legislation thus adopted strengthens consumer protection (for example, through increased transparency and better information for travellers) while taking into account the concerns of professionals in the sector (organisers, travel agencies), by introducing more flexibility (in the case of business travel, for example) and by reducing excessive administrative burdens (in the case of brochures, for example). the current 1990 directive was to be revised to take account of new practices, but the aim was not to upset existing national economic models. thus, the option of making the organiser or retailer liable for non-compliance, as provided for in the 1990 directive, has been reintroduced, despite the commission's initial choice to make the organiser solely liable.
in writing. on wednesday 12 march, meps adopted a text on package travel and assisted travel services. the aim is to better protect travellers against organisers' insolvency and unilateral amendment of the travel contract by offering them the possibility to participate in an equivalent trip in the event of changes and cancellations. we have also improved the protection of the rights of travellers who purchase combinations of services for the same trip or holiday. i voted in favour of this text to ensure that european consumers can enjoy the travel services they have subscribed to, as the digital age is increasing the number of offers.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report, which proposes to modernise the legislative framework for package holidays. these new provisions allow for adaptation to the digital age, which should facilitate the work of professionals in the sector and strengthen consumer protection.
in writing. the commission's text aims to improve the safety of people buying 'package holidays', more commonly known as 'package tours'. the text's provisions, which are rare, are generally rather positive and strike a balance between user protection and the necessary long-term readability for businesses. it would have been useful, however, to add to the information requirements the recommendations of the ministry of foreign affairs of the member state concerned in the case of travel abroad. however, the real problem is the mayer report, which wants to remove the obligation for providers to inform travellers of a travel access guarantee for people with reduced mobility and instead wants travellers to apply for it. does mr mayer realise that by doing so he is making it more difficult to choose a suitable journey for people with reduced mobility? does he realize that he's breaking the equality of citizens? i can't condone such a backsliding. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which strengthens the protection of european consumers buying package holidays by introducing the obligation to promptly repatriate the traveller in exceptional circumstances and stricter provisions in favour of consumers in the event of changes to prices or other terms of the contract. this text gives member states the possibility of extending the liability obligations laid down for organisers to retailers, who, for example in france, are the final sellers of the services.
in writing. as the european union is the world's leading tourist destination and an important economic sector in europe, a suitable legislative framework is needed. the current european legislation has shown its limits. it therefore needs to be reformed to take account of the importance of digitalisation in this area, by harmonising the different laws of the member states and adapting the existing rules to the needs of consumers and traders. i am glad that i voted for such legislation. we must ensure that european tourism is attractive by guaranteeing consumers the best possible protection, information and efficiency.
in writing. the package travel contract is not a contract like any other. it concerns a set of benefits reserved for a specific period. in the event of cancellation, the seller cannot 'stock' the trip as he would for a product for later resale. so we must be especially careful in our legal choices. the sector is largely composed of very small firms, which would not be able to offer a wide range of insurance cover without significantly increasing the prices of their products. the current system, based on the tour operator's proposal for supplementary insurance to be added to the package, seems to me to be balanced: on the one hand, travellers wishing to increase their coverage can choose to take out a specific policy; on the other hand, travellers wishing to increase their coverage can opt for a specific policy; secondly, as this guarantee is not reflected in the price of the package, it allows undertakings in the sector to maintain reasonable costs. it was therefore important to me to keep this system working, and it has proved to be successful.
in writing. given their impact on the climate, fluorinated gases are a real danger and their use should be phased out, as soon as economically viable solutions are available. i had tabled several amendments in the parliament's committee on the environment because i felt it was essential to ensure this transition to solutions that were less harmful to our environment, but also to take account of the very concrete economic realities faced by those who use these fluorinated gases: we must thus fight against the legal instability that undermines our economy. i am pleased with the final text, because we have set ourselves clear objectives to protect our climate and we are taking the time to achieve them. i therefore supported this compromise and called for a vote in favour of it.
in writing. this text represents a major step forward in the fight against global warming by reducing emissions of fluorinated greenhouse gases. these gases, which are found in refrigeration systems, aerosols and insulating foams, are particularly dangerous for the environment. at a time when reducing greenhouse gases and their impact on the environment is one of the major challenges facing the european union, it seems to me legitimate to seek to replace the use of such gases. this is why innovation for sustainable growth must be encouraged. moreover, it seems to me legitimate to prohibit their use gradually in certain sectors where other effective solutions are possible.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague bas eickhout on the european regulation on fluorinated greenhouse gases. these greenhouse gases can be replaced by substitutes with lower or no climate impact, which would reduce annual emissions by two thirds by 2030 at relatively low cost. the replacement of these gases, particularly in refrigeration or air conditioning products, will be carried out differently depending on the global warming potential of the product concerned, so as not to place too much pressure on companies. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. - the montreal protocol provides for the global phase-out and reduction of most ozone-depleting substances. by 2050, the target is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 80-95% compared with 1990 levels. to achieve this, a reduction of non-co2 emissions (including fluorinated greenhouse gases) of 72-73% by 2030 is required. unfortunately, though all other greenhouse gases have been reduced, emissions of fluorinated gases in the eu have increased by 60% since 1990. the proposal maintains the current provisions of the f-gas regulation, with some adjustments to ensure better implementation and enforcement by national authorities. the most important new measure is the introduction of new provisions at european level for the phasing out of the marketing and use of hfcs, which are widely used in the air conditioning and commercial refrigeration sectors.
in writing. with the majority of my fellow meps, i voted in favour of a directive to limit the emission of fluorinated greenhouse gases, known as hydrofluorocarbons (hfcs). replacing fluorinated gases with new, less polluting products could reduce greenhouse gas emissions by two thirds by 2030 and limit global warming. we have therefore introduced a quota for hfcs and banned their use in certain appliances, such as household refrigerators and freezers, for which less harmful substitutes are already available on the market. in order to give industry time to adapt its products to the new regulation, we have guaranteed sufficient time for the implementation of the bans by 2022-2025.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report, which aims to limit the emissions of fluorinated gases, which have the greatest global warming potential, in the european union. the amendment of the rules must, however, be realistically made with a view to moving towards equipment, such as household refrigerators and freezers, containing less harmful substitutes.
in writing. reducing fluorinated gas emissions is an important and necessary measure. unfortunately, this text lacks ambition and should have proposed, for example, a general ban on the placing on the european market of new products containing fluorinated gases. the timetable for the gradual reduction of the maximum quantities of hfcs placed on the market should also have been more ambitious, in order to be in line with the objectives of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. nevertheless, it has the merit of not relying on an unlikely market mechanism to solve a major problem. only drastic reduction and control of greenhouse gas emissions, accompanied by significant public investment and financial support, will solve the ecological crisis. i am voting for this text in order to encourage interesting measures, although unfortunately not ambitious enough in the context of an ecosocialist policy.
in writing. fluorinated greenhouse gases are widely used in heat pumps, air conditioning systems and refrigeration equipment. their warming potential is 100 to 1,000 times greater than that of co2. they contributed to 2.2% of the eu-15 emissions in 2011 and could contribute to 8% of total greenhouse gas emissions in 2050. it is therefore important, as well as the fight against co2 emissions, to combat the emission of fluorinated gases. to do this, the report proposes to tax those responsible for these emissions (€10 per tonne of co2 equivalent). the text also proposes the introduction of a mechanism for reducing quotas. a more ambitious text could have been reached, but i believe that the commitments obtained are positive and constitute a first step towards reducing emissions of fluorinated gases. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. as rapporteur for the opinion of the tran committee, i voted in favour of this text which aims to ensure a high level of environmental protection by reducing fluorinated gas emissions by two thirds by 2030 compared to their current level. the main advances of this regulation are: a gradual reduction of fluorinated gases over time, a total ban on the use of these gases for a range of equipment and products, additional requirements for the training and certification of personnel and additional reporting obligations should improve the monitoring of the use of fluorinated gases.
in writing. the treaty on the functioning of the european union recognises the right of european citizens to move freely within the union (article 45 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union). the directive aims to clarify the rights deriving from the free movement of workers and defines precisely the areas in which any discrimination on grounds of nationality is prohibited. after negotiations with the council and the commission, agreement was reached to adopt the text at first reading. i am happy with the agreement, so i voted in favour.
in writing. it seems necessary to emphasise that while the free movement of persons is a right and an opportunity for the european union, it could not be done at the expense of the social law of the member states and thus constitute an unacceptable social dumping within the union.
in writing. while it contained some interesting provisions, i could not support this text, which is aimed at strengthening the freedom of movement for workers, without acknowledging the problems it creates, particularly those linked to social dumping. my abstention was also motivated by the ambiguity in the text concerning the mutual recognition of the various types of civil union and their rights, an area of law which must remain the sovereignty of the states.
in writing. i decided to abstain on the final vote on this report because it concealed the many flaws which the principle of free movement of workers can cause. of course, it is necessary to ensure that migrant workers can enjoy their rights and be protected against abusive treatment. however, the european union cannot continue to turn a blind eye to the intolerable social dumping situations created by free movement. it allows, for example, workers to be employed in a member state other than their country of origin, under less favourable social conditions than local workers. these dumping situations are tragic for our companies and our citizens and lead many of them to unemployment or bankruptcy. i regret that these aspects are not given more emphasis in the text adopted.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which, without introducing new legislation, will make it possible to apply more uniformly the rights conferred by the union on workers and members of their families in the context of free movement. contact points will be set up to provide information and assistance to migrant workers and their employers. in particular, each member state will have to provide appropriate means of redress in cases of discrimination. these appeals may be brought through an ngo or other body which supports individual workers.
in writing. on wednesday 12[nbsp ]march, the european parliament voted in favour of a directive on the free movement of workers within the european union. the text covers all union citizens working in another member state and includes crossborder workers and seasonal workers. it provides for better information to citizens who decide to go to work in another eu country about their rights and obligations, in particular through national contact points to assist such workers. the directive will also improve the protection of workers, in particular health and safety conditions at work. i voted in favour of this text because i believe that the free movement of workers must be better regulated in order to guarantee equal rights for all and to avoid unfair competition.
in writing. the mutual recognition of the various types of civil union is a matter for the member states. that is why i abstained in the final vote on this report.
in writing. regulation (eu) no[nbsp ]492/2011 specifies the rights arising from the free movement of workers and sets out the specific areas in which discrimination on grounds of nationality is prohibited. however, despite these legal provisions, there are still many problems of discrimination based on nationality and problems related to the mobility of workers (in particular with regard to access to employment, working conditions, social benefits, access to training, etc.) for 'mobile' workers. the aim of this directive is to provide a better tool to effectively protect mobile workers against such discrimination. it should be noted that this directive does not concern 'posted workers', which is tantamount to creating a situation of inequality between workers and a fragmentation of the labour market. nevertheless, this report is intended to offer workers a slight degree of protection. i vote for it.
in writing. the free movement of workers is one of the four fundamental rights of european citizens. it gives every european citizen the right to move freely to another member state in order to work there. the current text put to the vote by meps aims to strengthen the previous regulation on the free movement of workers, as many problems of discrimination based on nationality and administrative problems persist for workers on the move. the aim of this text is to be anti-discriminatory and to provide stronger support for migrant workers. i voted yes.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to improve and promote the application of article [nbsp ]45 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and regulation (eu) no [nbsp ]492/2011 throughout the territory of the european union by establishing a common general framework of appropriate provisions and measures for a better, more uniform application of the rights conferred by union legislation on workers and members of their families exercising their right to freedom of movement.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament's report on the draft directive to facilitate the exercise of workers' rights in the context of the free movement of workers. there are already european regulations on the rights arising from freedom of movement, but there are still many practical problems, as well as significant discrimination against european workers when they want to settle permanently in another member state. the new directive submitted to the european parliament aims to combat such discrimination on grounds of nationality, to close the gaps that still exist between legal provisions and practice and to strengthen rights. the report makes a number of advances, such as the recognition of the rights of family members and equal treatment with national workers in matters of employment, pay and housing. it also provides remedies where these rights are not respected. i regret, however, that posted workers (those who come to work in another member state for a short period) are not covered by this text, because it creates inequalities between workers, causes a fragmentation of the labour market and fuels social dumping.
in writing. prevention is always better than cure, including in relation to the environment: environmental impact studies are a very good thing, because they allow to predict the environmental consequences of an investment and thus protect our environment and improve the use of funds. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament. however, the problem was also to put the cursor in the right place for the obligations to be respected. we must be fully aware that additional obligations can also impede investment, growth and employment. at a time when europe is only just beginning to raise its head, my group has thrown out all unnecessary, ineffective or redundant measures so that this text remains an effective tool for improving projects with an environmental impact. the question of shale gas remains. the european parliament had called for strong binding legislation and it is regrettable that the european commission has so far only proposed simple recommendations. it is clear that we must both facilitate exploration, in order to know what wealth europe has at its disposal, and strictly control exploitation to avoid damaging environmental degradation.

in writing. certain public and private projects, such as the construction of motorways or mining sites, must be subject to an environmental impact assessment (eia) in order to be authorised by the member states. the european commission had proposed a revision of this directive to simplify procedures and take account of new environmental factors. unfortunately, the text presented to us after negotiations between the european parliament and the council will have the effect of further complicating the current procedures, while the french legislation revised in 2011 remains controversial. i regret that the european parliament has adopted this directive, thus aggravating the 'over-administration' which is already severely penalising our companies. i am glad, however, that the directive adopted provides for a reduction in the time needed for impact studies, in order to avoid the blocking of job-creating sites.
in writing. i voted in favour of the revision of the text on minimum requirements for the assessment of the environmental impact of certain public and private projects. the aim of this text is to achieve a high level of environmental protection, to simplify procedures and to reduce unnecessary administrative burdens. the report provides for a reduction in public consultations. new factors such as biodiversity will have to be taken into account, transparency and public participation will be facilitated by the creation of a central internet portal, and rules on the management of conflicts of interest will be strengthened.
in writing. this text proposes some positive improvements to the directive on the assessment of the environmental impact of public and private projects. however, the desire to simplify administrative procedures or to reduce the number of projects which at the end of the preliminary verification procedure will be subject to a mandatory environmental impact assessment is counterproductive from an environmental point of view. the text also enshrines the european union's capitulation to the oil and gas lobbies with regard to shale gas and oil. while it is necessary to ban fracking and shale gas exploitation for reasons primarily of climate, the environment committee of the european parliament has not even been able to maintain the (largely insufficient) position it had been set and to introduce an obligation to evaluate all projects for the exploration, evaluation and exploitation of shale gas and oil! the union, which has never supported the yasuni itt project in ecuador, reaffirms once again that its vision is that of the race for hydrocarbon extraction, without taking into account the immense challenge posed by the urgent decarbonisation of our 'developed' societies. i vote against it.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the assessment of the environmental impact of public and private projects, because it makes good progress in environmental matters: improving the definition of biodiversity, better management of impact studies in terms of transparency, citizen participation, precision of criteria, or strengthening the fight against conflicts of interest or penalties in case of misapplication. many environmental associations are in favour of adopting the text, considering that it largely passes the cost/benefit test. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the fact that the community is not able to meet its own needs. it also lists high impact projects, such as deep boreholes, for which an environmental impact assessment should be considered, irrespective of their size. the report, therefore, although not perfect and pending specific legislation on the issue of shale gas, has the merit of setting a framework in this area, while leaving member states free to take more ambitious measures at national level.
in writing. in october 2012, the commission presented a revision of the 2011 directive on public or private projects requiring an environmental impact assessment (eia) and on those subject to a preliminary verification procedure. the proposal specifies the criteria for choosing between the two procedures and lists a number of new projects that may be submitted to the procedure in order to ensure compliance with the union's environmental objectives. the european parliament adopted by a very large majority the agreement with the council, which makes some improvements to the 2012 directive, such as the introduction of the principle of global impact, a public consultation and the obligation for the developer to provide a dossier of up to 30 pages summarising the main information related to the project (e.g. impacts on ecosystems, use of natural resources, consideration of reasonable alternatives, etc.). however, the agreement excludes shale gas projects using hydraulic fracturing, the health and environmental consequences of which are becoming increasingly well known. i therefore voted against this revision because there is no justification for excluding the extraction of shale gas at the expense of protecting the environment and the health of europeans.

in writing. the aim of this text is to support cultural and information pluralism and to protect intellectual property. europe must adapt to the shift in the merger of traditional broadcasting services with the internet. in order to avoid any dominant position on the market, the own-initiative report proposes in particular that the competition rules be applied to this specific sector. that would be a step in the right direction. voting in favour of this text is not only a vote in favour of supporting european competitiveness in the new information and communication technologies (nict) sector, but also a vote in favour of giving citizens access to a quality offer of audiovisual and internet services.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which suggests updating the regulatory framework for the media, which is necessary to respond to the changing context of digitalisation and the internet. these issues will have to take into account consumer protection and the dual character of the media as cultural and economic assets.
in writing. this report provides a framework for the interaction between audiovisual media, electronic services and applications. it noted that the diversity of audiovisual offerings must be safeguarded in the interests of economic interests and, in this respect, 'remarked to the commission that authorising the inclusion of the cultural and audiovisual media sector in international free trade agreements is contrary to the european union's commitment to promoting cultural diversity and identity'. the report also attaches great importance to net neutrality, support for public works of quality and protection of personal data, but it also encourages deregulation of advertising and competition with the public sector. finally, it does not take into account the targeted territory and the location of the company, which is tantamount to encouraging fiscal dumping. i am voting in favour of this in order to encourage the anti-trade elements of the document, particularly on the transatlantic trade agreement (ttip).
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which recalls that the technological convergence of the media is now a reality, in particular for broadcasting, the press and the internet. european media, culture and network policy must therefore adapt the regulatory framework to new realities, while ensuring that a uniform level of regulation can be established and applied also to new market players from the european union and third countries.
in writing. the creation of european citizenship was one of the major achievements of the maastricht treaty of 1992. however, even today, citizens of the member states of the european union do not always feel that they are european citizens in addition to their national citizenship. that is why i welcome the 25 new measures proposed by the commission and supported this own-initiative report on european citizenship.
in writing. citizens' access to information about the union is a crucial issue. this text rightly encourages facilitating access to, inter alia, the solvit network and the 'europe is yours' portal, two useful tools for involving europeans more closely in the union's decision-making process. it also stresses the need to raise citizens' awareness by giving political education a more central role in european affairs in school curricula. finally, in the interests of transparency, it is proposed to facilitate access to documents of the european institutions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the 2013 report on european union citizenship because european citizens need to be able to exercise their rights more effectively in a concrete way. the proposals in this report aim to remove the barriers which still prevent people from going to live, work or shop anywhere in the european union. several measures are being taken to this end, including easier access to economic, administrative, legal and cultural matters for residents and also for nationals moving to another member state, rapid information on citizens' rights via the europe direct network and the 'europe is yours' website, the development of a common disability card for disabled people recognised throughout the european territory, the improvement of european legislation on the settlement of cross-border disputes, the recognition of voluntary work, citizens' initiatives and the right to petition the european parliament as elements of citizens' action, the protection of citizens against any form of discrimination based on nationality, precise information on the right to vote in european municipal elections and when one does not reside in one's country of origin...
in writing. the european parliament adopted a report on citizenship of the european union in 2013. i voted in favour of this text, which proposes 12 new measures to strengthen the application of the rights of european citizens. for example, we have asked for a one-stop shop in each member state to better coordinate projects with crossborder impact. we have also called for the creation of a european association status. finally, we recalled the importance of political education in european affairs in school curricula in order to promote european citizenship among the youngest.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report, which calls for the establishment in each member state of a single point of contact to coordinate projects with crossborder impact. in order to make the concept of european citizenship more tangible, member states should include political education on european affairs in school curricula. the establishment of a european association status would also be beneficial.
in writing. this report on citizenship of the union recalls the 'basic' rights of european citizens: the right to vote in local and european elections, the assistance of a european embassy in third countries, the importance of volunteering, etc., but it does not denounce the austerity that is undermining the rights of citizens, especially in the countries of southern europe. it does not claim any decisive rights for parliament, which represents the people. he also claimed that the election of the commission president by parliament would allow the europeanisation of the election campaign and thus an increase in turnout. i fear that his hopes will be dashed on this point. i don't want to encourage them, so i'm not going to.

in writing. this text constitutes an interim report on the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office as provided for in article[nbsp ]86 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. by voting for this text, i wanted to show my support for the creation of such an institution. although the debate is not over, it was important to send a strong signal to that effect. the european prosecutor would be tasked with strengthening the protection of the financial interests of the european union and filling the gaps in the current law enforcement systems. it is estimated that the european union loses almost 500 million euros every year because of budgetary irregularities. this considerable shortfall justifies the establishment of such a body. it is true, however, that it is essential not to undermine the principle of subsidiarity within the european union and to define clearly the powers of each of the judicial bodies in europe. that is why discussions must continue on the structure that this european public prosecutor's office should adopt.
in writing. fraud against the european budget is estimated at €500 million each year. in this situation, the creation of a european public prosecutor's office would certainly be an added value in order to investigate these facts more effectively. in this resolution we ask that the respective roles of the future prosecutor's office and other european agencies such as olaf and eurojust be better defined. we also stress the need for binding criteria for deciding which courts have jurisdiction in the cases under consideration. the european public prosecutor's office should be able to use the information provided by the eppo to investigate cases of serious misconduct or fraud. finally, i have spoken in favour of the creation of a european public prosecutor's office which respects a high level of protection of the rights of the defence and applies european standards of procedural rights.

the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the action of the troika raises at least two types of questions. the first question is the democratic control of proposals to the states. even within the troika, the obvious disagreements between the imf, the ecb and the commission have not been discussed in any democratic body of the union. the european parliament was never consulted. the most important decisions were taken in the eurogroup, an informal body where germany's voice was predominant. the legal basis for the participation of the commission and the ecb in an intergovernmental structure such as the troika is also a matter of debate, if reference is made to the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the ecb has, in particular, exceeded its prerogatives by imposing its views on fiscal policy and the restructuring of the irish, cypriot and greek banking sectors. the commission has not always been the guardian of the union acquis, notably in cyprus, by turning a blind eye to the eurogroup's proposal to tax deposits below eur 100 000. secondly, this lack of legitimacy is all the more serious because the policies imposed, with a gun to the head, on national governments and parliaments are the subject of many controversies. four of these can be mentioned. first, the greek debt could have been restructured immediately to avoid the recessionary impact of too brutal fiscal austerity. this was the position of the imf, which had revised upwards its estimates of the budget multiplier and which favoured internal devaluation. this remains the imf's position, which believes that further debt restructuring is necessary, while the greek debt ratio is at 175[nbsp ]% of gdp. in the event of a new restructuring, it could be suggested that the ecb, which bought 34 billion of greek debt on the secondary market, take these losses, unlike what happened during the first restructuring. this would certainly increase money creation, but it would not be harmful at a time when deflation is threatening the euro area. second and second mistake, the ecb only got its bazooka [nbsp ]the unwto program, probably too late, in september[nbsp ]2012. if this programme had been set up earlier, it might have prevented the contagion from portugal and cyprus. thirdly, the combination of severe fiscal austerity and internal devaluation, i.e. lower wages, killed demand and plunged greece and portugal into a lasting recession. fourth, the irish banking rescue package, which amounted to almost 30% of gdp, was almost exclusively borne by the taxpayer and preserved the interests of senior bank bondholders. at that time, solidarity mechanisms such as the efsf or the esm and the future banking union did not exist. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the budgetary discipline is maintained. portugal and ireland have regained access to the market to finance their debts, but the instability that existed when the assistance was requested has been exacerbated in all countries. growth remains sluggish; debt ratios have soared; unemployment, poverty and inequality have exploded. the report makes proposals to improve democratic control of the european stability mechanism, which is to become a genuine european monetary fund replacing the troika. the european stability mechanism must be placed under the aegis of the community method: codecision between the european parliament and the council must prevail for economic policy recommendations made to states in return for financial assistance. my dear colleagues, our fellow citizens blame europe for its lack of transparency and democracy. they doubt the effectiveness of austerity policies that they increasingly dislike. by adopting this report, our parliament, the only european institution elected by direct universal suffrage, can send a strong signal to our fellow citizens on the eve of the next elections. it sets a course for the next president of the commission. answer is "blue cardboard". mr president, it seems to me that the budgetary policies in all the member states are now pro-cyclical. before the crisis, these were already pro-cyclical policies. there have been stimulus plans, but it was when those stimulus plans were suspended that growth collapsed in all european countries, and particularly in those countries which asked for assistance. without growth, you have no tax revenues and you have debts that are growing. i don't have time to say more, but i suggest you look carefully at the curves in all the countries of the euro area: deficits are falling everywhere, but debt levels are also soaring everywhere. that is the paradox of procyclical policies, which you seem to be advocating.

council in exposing and condemning human rights abuses wherever they may occur, and we seek to develop the means to stop or, even better, to prevent violations. i will touch firstly on some of the eu priorities in the current main session of the human rights council. secondly, i wish to assure you, the european parliament, and anyone watching this debate, of the european union’s strong and commissioner for human rights (ohchr) country office, and we continue to call for that to be put in place swiftly. we support, too, the extension of the mandate of the special rapporteur on human rights in iran, not least given the recent spate of executions, and we call on iran to cooperate more closely with the un. we also support efforts to enhance accountability and reconciliation in sri duty to respect and protect human rights and fundamental freedoms, which are also enshrined in the new constitution, and must ensure the smooth opening of the ohchr country office. recent events in the central african republic and south sudan remind us how quickly violence can start and how suddenly human rights can come under threat. the special session on the central african republic and recent attention dedicated to south sudan also demonstrate that the council can act speedily when necessary. it is now up to all of us to ensure that the relevant reports and mechanisms are used effectively. obviously, the human rights council must tackle the most acute situations, and therefore the eu representatives – and many other high-level speakers last week in geneva – addressed the situation in ukraine, which continues to evolve rapidly. the european union reiterated its deep regret about the many deaths, injuries and human rights violations that have occurred over the past weeks. the crisis in ukraine must be resolved peacefully according to international law and with full respect for ukraine’s territorial integrity, sovereignty and independence. all citizens must be protected against intimidation and human rights violations, including persons belonging to minorities. we welcome ukraine’s resolve to investigate human rights violations, and we understand that the investigation will be carried out in line with international standards and in cooperation with the council of europe. the impact of events in crimea on the human rights situation there is of particular concern. beatings, arrests and kidnappings of journalists and civil activists must stop immediately and should be properly investigated. the human rights council, in addition to tackling country-specific issues, looks at many thematic issues, as well as human rights in the broader context, including issues of great importance for the eu and this house such as lgtbi persons’ rights, freedom of religion, belief and gender equality. all around the world, the space for civil society is being shrunk, making it easier for human rights violations to occur. in order to address them, the council itself must be a safe space for debate. reprisals against those who cooperate with the united nations system, or crude procedural moves to prevent civil-society representatives from participating, are unacceptable and betray the founding intent of the council. in closing, let me stress again that the council is a vital body for the promotion and protection of universal human rights: it deserves our full support and cooperation. in this context, we acknowledge the return of israel to the human rights council at this session and encourage it to cooperate fully with the council and its mechanisms. long-term peace and security can be sustained only if human rights and international humanitarian law are fully respected by all. finally, let me invite you to join our efforts in the pursuit of human rights around the globe, for our priorities are yours, and vice versa, as the motion for a resolution before you today so clearly shows.

i'm the reporter. - mr president, i too am very moved to take up this debate today. for more than two years we have been working in parliament in a way that is both aggressive and aggressive in the creation of an asylum, migration and integration fund. i would like to add my thanks to the fictitious rapporteurs who accompanied us and to the staff of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, who have also accompanied us throughout this work. the negotiations on the asylum, migration and integration fund have concluded that with this new financial instrument the european union and its member states are well equipped to respond in a way that is both supportive and responsible to the increasingly transnational challenges that europe will continue to face over the next seven years. in the preparation of the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020, in the area of internal affairs policies, it was essential to carry out intensive work on simplifying the old spending instruments and working towards greater flexibility, in particular to respond to urgent issues. experience has shown that, because of their diversity and fragmentation, the rules governing spending programmes have often been perceived as unnecessarily complex and difficult to implement and control. the creation of european funds for asylum and integration of migrants is a good idea, but we must have access to them! for example, many ngos have argued that delays in payment procedures have put them in difficulty, often forcing them to take out loans from banks or, worse, to close their doors. i therefore very much welcomed the new dynamic of simplification and rationalisation suggested by the commission in its november 2011 proposal. the asylum, migration and integration fund thus builds on the three financial instruments of the previous period: the european refugee fund, the european integration fund and the european return fund. among its strategic objectives, the new fund will help to[nbsp]strengthen the european asylum system, promote legal migration within the union, promote fair return strategies and deepen solidarity and responsibility-sharing between member states. in the context of these objectives, the fund now also has an external dimension, making it possible to finance actions in or concerning third countries. on the other hand, while it is positive, this quest for simplification and adaptability also raised questions. since they are now grouped together in a single instrument, how can it be ensured that member states do not give more priority to return activities than to those related to asylum or integration? how can all stakeholders, including local and regional authorities and civil society, be effectively involved in the programming, implementation and evaluation of the various activities carried out? how can a rigorous evaluation mechanism be put in place to ensure that eu funding is used appropriately and transparently, even if member states have not set appropriate objectives or indicators for their annual programme? finally, a number of questions: when it is now possible to finance actions outside the union, how can we ensure that these actions are consistent with other european policies, particularly development policies, and how can we avoid the temptation for states to adopt a carrot and stick policy which would in some way make development aid dependent on the efforts of foreign countries in the field of return and border controls? in response to the concerns raised, we have succeeded in parliament, after intense negotiation, in achieving a fair and transparent distribution of funding between the different objectives of the fund, providing for a minimum percentage of resources to be allocated to asylum and integration policies respectively. for example, of the €2.4 billion that member states will share to finance their annual programme, at least 20% should be allocated to fostering legal migration and promoting the effective integration of migrants and at least an additional 20% should be allocated to funding asylum-related measures. ngos and international organisations involved in the partnerships will be involved in the development and implementation of the fund[nbsp] and the monitoring at national level. we have succeeded in strengthening a results-oriented approach, which will not only have an accounting view of the actions carried out, but will also favour a qualitative evaluation of their achievements. i have some regrets, of course, because we have not succeeded in strengthening solidarity in the area of asylum, whether it is with third countries or between member states, and so, for example, we have not succeeded in implementing the instruments available, as contained in the treaties, for example, article 80 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, in order to guarantee more solidarity measures in the future. it is a regret that we have not found a solution in our discussions.

i would like to thank the rapporteur for the excellent report, which has been produced by the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection. as you know, the bar is a noble species of great economic value. it is highly sought after by professional fishermen and also by recreational fishermen, whose numbers are growing in europe. in the atlantic and the english channel, cod fishing is a significant activity. it is a major contributor to local economies. the techniques used by the professionals are many, but the three main ones are pelagic trawl, longline or trawl; recreational fishermen engaged in surface trawling or live bait fishing. the bar reaches sexual maturity, depending on the area, during its fourth or fifth year of life, for a size that can range from 35 to 40 centimeters. after spawning, the actual reproduction occurs after a long spawning period, which leads to the fish gathering for several weeks in tightly packed schools, which can be very large numbers of individuals. so fish are particularly vulnerable during these gatherings. the conservation of this species is now the responsibility of the member states, not the european union. france, for example, is currently implementing interesting measures in collaboration with the professionals, thanks to the work of the "bar" committee of the national committee for marine fisheries and marine farming: a biological rest of seven days during the spawning period to limit the pressure on breeding adults, a minimum mesh size of 100[nbsp ]mm for trawls and nets, and landings of pelagic trawlers limited to five tonnes per week per vessel. i welcome these voluntary measures, of course, but they are still not enough. recreational fishermen in france have responsibly decided to increase the catch size in order to contribute to the conservation of the resource. this shows that they are aware of the need to protect this species. today i am saying that the european union must take up this issue in order to organise harmonization at its level. the 2012 ices opinion indicates that the lack of reliable stock data is problematic at european level. it recommends, as a precautionary measure, a reduction of 20% of the total catches of bluefin tuna at european level, referring to the average catches between 2008 and 2010. the february 2011 ifremer opinion indicates that the lack of data is very problematic. it is therefore important that at european level the commission proposes to the member states that they intensify the monitoring of commercial and recreational fishing activities and suggests that they organise access to the resource between professional and recreational fishermen to enable sustainable exploitation. this protection must not, however, lead to a ban on the exploitation of this species but to its organisation. the aim is to adopt management measures that will enable fishermen to fish within the limits of the quotas set up by the european union. those quotas shall be established on the basis of the best available scientific advice. they will be accompanied by a multiannual management plan which will provide fishermen with a medium- and long-term view of their catch possibilities. this will also provide a global view of the market and marketing of this species, which is in high demand among consumers. at the same time, states will have to be asked to regulate recreational fishing in terms of the number of catches per fisherman per year. this will avoid the excesses seen here and there. at european level, this debate must enable the three institutions to achieve the establishment of fair and equitable quotas for commercial fishing. i therefore ask the commission to intensify research on the state of european bar stocks in order to know their biology and to provide us with a study by the end of october 2014. i also propose that the commission should set up tacs and quotas for this species. this tac implies management by multiannual plans. i also request that the minimum capture size be increased to a minimum of 40 centimetres. the european commission, commissioner, must take its responsibilities and propose concrete measures to preserve the bar. these measures will allow the commercial fishermen to continue exploiting this high value added species and the recreational fishermen to continue their activity without endangering the resource. finally, commissioner, i would like to ask you whether the commission is prepared to propose to the european parliament and the council, before the end of
