in writing. i voted in favour of approving the ratification of the hong kong international convention for the safe and environmentally sound recycling of ships. it covers the design, construction, operation and maintenance of ships with a view to facilitating their recycling without compromising their safety and operational efficiency.
in writing. this report supports the draft council decision authorising eu member states to ratify the 2009 hong kong convention on the dismantling of ships. the french parliament has already authorized ratification by france, but this question also concerns the union's competences. i have already spoken twice on this subject. i have already pointed out that the hong kong convention is imperfect in terms of protecting workers and the environment: it does not prohibit 'beaching', that is, the voluntary beaching of a ship to allow it to be dismantled on a beach. however, it marks improvements needed to better take account of the imperative of clean dismantling and recycling of ships from the moment they are built. with the renewal of orders for shipbuilding, a global phenomenon recorded since the end of 2013, and the need to deconstruct nearly 2,000 hulls per year, it is high time to put things in order. the convention must therefore be regarded as a mere text, since it does not prevent the states which have ratified it from taking stricter measures. i vote in favour, to take the lead and encourage further action.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which asks the council to invite the member states to ratify, or accede to, the 2009 hong kong international convention for the safe and environmentally sound recycling of ships, for those parts falling within the exclusive competence of the union. the aim of the convention is to ensure that ships, when dismantled at the end of their operational life, do not present unnecessary risks to the health and safety of persons and to the environment. it addresses the full range of problems associated with ship dismantling, as well as concerns about working and environmental conditions in many ship-breaking facilities around the world.
in writing. this report discusses the role of the troika in dealing with the financial crisis in the euro area. the troika is the group of the european central bank (ecb), the international monetary fund (imf) and the european union (eu). despite attempts on the left to use this report to denounce the proposed austerity measures to clean up the public finances of the countries concerned, the final report is balanced, thanks in particular to the work of my colleague otmar karas. so i voted for it.
in writing. while the troika's missions, particularly in greece, are not yet completed, it seemed important to take an initial stock of them. the report makes it clear that certain decisions were clearly not democratic, and that national governments were forced to do so. the dramatic effects of some decisions have also been noted. far from giving a blank-seing, the report reiterates that financial aid to certain european countries could not be given at any price.
in writing. i voted for this report, although i would have liked to see a stronger condemnation of the activities of the troika. the imf, the ecb and the european commission failed in their primary mission, which was to reduce macroeconomic imbalances and public debt in the countries where the troika intervened. what is worse, national parliaments have often been sidelined. it is urgent to dismantle the troika, whose conditions imposed in exchange for financial aid are suffocating the peoples, and to move towards the communitization of the european stability mechanism (esm) and the creation of a european monetary fund.
in writing. this text rightly takes stock of the activities of the troika in the euro area countries which have benefited from this programme. the troika, composed of the european commission, the european central bank (ecb) and the international monetary fund (imf), was set up to implement the rescue plans for greece, ireland, portugal and cyprus. it is important to evaluate such an instrument, which has certainly brought about economic improvements in these countries, but whose organizational weaknesses must also be recognized. it would therefore be consistent for the european union to have a sound legal basis to deal effectively with such a crisis in the future.
in writing. the troika (ecb, commission and imf) has been at the heart of the implementation of the assistance programmes for some euro area member states. after a thorough study of its role, the report presented by liem hoang ngoc and othmar karas gives a precise and reasoned account of the situation in the member states concerned, which is not satisfactory at present. the european parliament's committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy has adopted a resolution on the situation in the european union. i voted in favour of this report because i wanted us to be a force for proposals. we therefore recommend a number of measures, such as restructuring the greek debt and developing a european approach to dealing with the debt of ireland. finally, parliament called for the gradual dismantling of the troika, the communityisation of the european stability mechanism (esm) and the creation of a european monetary fund within the community framework. a civic and democratic europe must be expressed in action, especially when such important issues as the economic stability of the continent and the future of peoples who have already made so many sacrifices are at stake.
in writing. - the troika was set up as a back-up and emergency solution to save the euro area project and the economic and financial soundness of its countries. in a context of economic crisis in which decisions had to be taken urgently, a disorderly default had to be avoided, the crisis had to spread to other member states and the euro area had to be prevented from collapsing, the troika was certainly an ad hoc solution. it is true, however, that his work was at times critical and excessive, going too far beyond his mandate and his powers. we therefore believe that a mechanism should be set up focusing on the objectives of sustainable growth and financial stability, in order to prevent and avoid emergency situations as in the past, but allowing member states to implement the growth policies necessary to get out of the crisis once and for all.
in writing. the report on the troika's missions takes a critical look at the establishment of these missions and their consequences. the lack of transparency, the non-respect of the existing institutional structures, the lack of democratic legitimacy are all factors that are denounced. i also welcome the investigative work of the two co-rapporteurs, which shows the divergences of interpretation between the three institutions that are members of the troika (the ecb, the commission and the imf). these divergent interpretations have led to radical solutions favouring the interests of each of these institutions: debt reduction for the commission, bank protection for the ecb, wage cuts for the imf. the report justifies this situation by the urgency of finding a response to the risk of default by the states and supports a change of instruments through the new european texts grouped in the "six-pack" and the "two-pack". for my part, i cannot support the call for the troika's benchmark mechanisms to be incorporated into european law through these texts which give priority to deficit reduction over all other considerations, including social ones. that is why, despite the interesting points it contains, i voted against this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the establishment of programmes in response to the request for financial assistance from certain euro-area countries. the solidarity of the member states has helped to avoid a default by several states and a spread of the crisis. in order to better prepare europe for such contingencies, the union should create a european monetary fund to support countries facing insolvency problems.
in writing. this report, both informative and effective, looks back at the failures of the troika in responding to the sovereign debt crisis of 2010. it has, however, been overloaded with liberal considerations, which clearly appear as reversed pieces. he took up some of the liberal language on the so-called 'structural' aspects of the crisis and defended the usefulness of past financial assistance from the eu and the imf. on the contrary, we believe that this action has worsened the crisis as shown by the indicators of recession and rising debts in the 'assisted' countries. the report rightly points to the democratic shortcomings and the opacity of each of the three components of the troika in the elaboration and control of the plans for financial assistance to states in difficulty. in a sometimes schizophrenic way, this report also insists on the lack of positive results of the massive austerity plans and the unreality of the assumptions on which they are based. however, he went on to observe that 'the economic and social consequences would have been more severe without the financial and technical assistance of the european union and the imf'. the report does not clearly take a position for the immediate halt of austerity programmes and their replacement by a coordinated recovery policy in europe. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted for this report, which is a relentless indictment of the troika's crimes, particularly in greece, but not only. the report provides a detailed and forceful account of how the imf, the ecb and the commission failed in their dual mission of reducing macroeconomic imbalances and public debt in the countries where the troika intervened. the report continues to paint a ruthless portrait of the mistakes made, which have dramatic consequences: increased inequality and poverty, mass unemployment, decreased life expectancy, because the art of criticism is easy. there are specific proposals for breaking out of this vicious circle, accompanied by a responsible timetable in several stages.
in writing. in parallel with the work of the committee on economic and monetary affairs on the troika, the committee on employment and social affairs also prepared a report on this subject. the report deplores the social consequences of the crisis, but acknowledges that they are not due to the role of the troika but to the fragility of the public finances of the states concerned. the report stresses the need to better prepare the union for such crises, which has already been very much implemented by the financial regulation and economic governance tools that the union has had since 2009. i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. although the social models of some countries which received the troika's 'aid' required significant changes, it is undeniable that the harshness and speed of the implementation of some of its recommendations had catastrophic effects on employment and social aspects in the countries concerned. it was important that the european parliament should send this message to both the troika leaders and the peoples concerned.
in writing. this paper discusses the effects on employment and social conditions of the populations of the countries which have benefited from the rescue plans put in place as part of the activities of the troika, composed of the european commission, the ecb and the imf. it seems to me important to emphasize that the economic adjustment programmes have had a considerable impact on employment in these countries. such programmes should therefore focus more on social imbalances, in particular through return to employment plans and the creation of favourable conditions for the development of smes.
in writing. the report presented by alejandro cercas to the parliamentary committee took an uncompromising view of the troika's missions. by imposing systematic budget cuts, advocating reforms of health and social protection systems, failing to respect the mechanisms in place to adjust wages and deliberately sidelining the social partners, these missions have clearly gone beyond european competence. the right wing of parliament, however, has put aside the illegality of the troika's missions and has concentrated only on the social consequences of these missions: the rise in unemployment, poverty, inequality, emigration of the most qualified young people, the breakdown of social protection systems. clear and impartial work on the causes of this social catastrophe has therefore been deliberately reduced by the right wing, focusing only on the consequences, which are irrefutable. i support the analysis in this report of the social consequences of the troika's missions, but i regret the lack of any indication of the causes. nor could i agree with the right-wing additions to the "macroeconomic adjustments" which are so much an advocacy for competitiveness and flexicurity. that's why i decided not to.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report, which sets out the employment and social aspects of the troika's activities. the unprecedented economic and financial crisis has exposed the fragility of public finances in some member states, and the measures taken in response to this situation have had an impact on the employment and living conditions of many people.
in writing. this report is highly critical of the social record of the troika's austerity programmes in greece, cyprus, portugal and ireland. it points in particular to their effects on rising unemployment, precariousness, lower minimum wages and poverty. the report rightly deplores the absence of any right of the european parliament to influence the determination of these austerity plans. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu. several recommendations are in line with the left front's position since the beginning of the crisis, in particular the call for an end to austerity programmes and for increased spending on public health and education. nevertheless, this report is part of a framework which continues to give priority over time to budgetary adjustment. i believe, on the contrary, that social policies must always be given priority and that budgetary sustainability comes at that price. i regret that this report advocates 'flexi-security', which is synonymous with increased precariousness everywhere. i am voting against it because i do not want to endorse these wrong choices.
in writing. the european parliament has issued numerous criticisms of the troika, highlighting the disastrous methods used to manage the economic and financial crisis in four eu countries (greece, portugal, ireland, cyprus). this own-initiative report examined the economic and social impact of adjustment programmes in these countries. initially, this document was very critical and directly linked the social degradation experienced in these countries to the adjustment programmes. unfortunately, as a result of the negotiations to reach a compromise with the other institutions, the report lost its strength and the role of the troika is legitimized. i voted against this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which takes note of the unprecedented economic and financial crisis which has highlighted the fragility of public finances in some member states. economic adjustment programmes adopted in response to the situation in greece (may 2010 and march 2012), ireland (december 2010), portugal (may 2011) and cyprus (june 2013) have had direct and indirect effects on the employment level and living conditions of many people. in the light of these findings, the deterioration of employment, the disappearance of smes, a major cause of the weak recovery in these countries, and the increasing impoverishment and social exclusion in the member states concerned, this report calls on the commission to carry out a detailed study of the economic and social consequences of the economic and financial crisis and the adjustment programmes implemented to remedy it in the four countries concerned, in order to accurately assess the short and long-term effects on employment and social protection systems, as well as on the european social acquis.
in writing. the european parliament worked on the socioeconomic consequences of austerity policies in countries that requested assistance from the troika when the sovereign debt crisis was at its height in europe. many amendments have been tabled and my votes reflect my deep convictions on the matter. i would simply like to express my regret at the lack of consultation of the social partners of the european union and the international labour organisation in the preparation of the rescue plans. i also urge the european institutions, in conjunction with the member states, to set up recovery plans focused on helping smes, making good use of the european structural funds to promote employment, restore quality public services and limit all forms of social exclusion. i therefore encourage the council of europe and the ilo to propose corrective measures and incentive policies which would improve the social situation in these countries. i voted in favour of this report because i think it is a good thing that we are debating and looking back at the way in which the crisis has been handled. the european union must learn from the past and move forward.
in writing. the troika , set up in march 2010 by heads of state and government to negotiate the terms of financial assistance to greece, has contributed to a growing sense of mistrust of the european union among citizens. the response to the crises experienced by some member states must be more political and less technocratic. the european union must exercise active solidarity rather than impose inappropriate plans. the european parliament therefore recommends that transparent and binding rules be established on the allocation of tasks between the troika and the public authorities of the states concerned. programmes will also have to take account of the social and employment aspects and each country receiving financial assistance should have a 'growth task force'. parliament also called for the creation of a european monetary fund.

in writing. this report proposes guidelines for the future 2015 budget of the union. it illustrates the budgetary powerlessness of parliament, which is organised by the treaties and aggravated by the undemocratic practice of the commission and the council. the european parliament is forced to repeat for 2015 the warnings it has already made in vain for the 2013 and 2014 budgets. the collection of new priorities to be financed is only a token item, since the budgets do not even cover the mountains of unpaid debts of previous years. the under-implementation of budgets has become the commission's specialty for arbitrarily squeezing expenditure. at the end of 2013, 23.4 billion euro was outstanding, representing 16% of the current budget, for cohesion policy alone. the report nevertheless endorses the budgetary framework which is the cause of these delays. it notes that the 2015 budget will be lower than the 2013 budget. this should further increase the number of unpaid payments and make it totally impossible to spend the funds for employment and youth in advance, as announced by mrs merkel and mr hollande. like a letter from parliament to santa claus, this report shows that the european budgetary procedure is a democratic travesty. i vote against it.
in writing. as a co-author of this resolution, i voted in favour of this text which calls for support for ukraine and for stricter sanctions against russia for its repeated violations of international law in crimea. the preservation of ukraine's territorial integrity remains the priority and the european union calls for an accelerated rapprochement with ukraine to help it cope with this ordeal, which is reminiscent of the dark hours of the soviet period.
in writing. as russia prepares to welcome a 'dissident' region of ukraine, it was necessary for the european parliament to reaffirm its opposition to the forcible annexation of part of ukrainian territory, in clear violation of international law. sanctions and strong reactions from the heads of state or government and european officials are imperative to maintaining ukraine's territorial integrity.
in writing. in view of the latest developments in crimea and the threats to the territorial integrity of ukraine, the european parliament decided to send a strong message to russia, which should clarify its intentions as soon as possible. russia, i repeat, is a key partner of ukraine and must continue to be that of the european union. however, the ambiguous statements of its leaders and the military manoeuvres that are being observed pose a threat to ukraine that the union can no longer ignore. the european leaders have announced financial aid of 11 billion, the exact details of which have yet to be specified. at the same time, i urge them to intensify their dialogue with the russian authorities so that a diplomatic solution can be found quickly, that russia renounces its annexation of crimea and that the escalation of tensions which is weakening ukraine and destabilising the whole region is brought to an end.
in writing. i supported and co-signed the resolution condemning the invasion of crimea by russian military forces. this aggression by the russian federation under false pretenses undermines the territorial integrity of ukraine and is a clear violation of international law as well as several agreements between ukraine and russia. the resolution also stresses the illegitimacy and illegality of the announcement of a referendum in crimea on joining the russian federation, as it violates the ukrainian constitution and the principles of international law. in this resolution, parliament welcomes the decision to impose targeted sanctions on several ukrainian and russian officials. it also welcomed the european commission's decision to unblock an aid plan for ukraine in order to contribute to the economic and financial stabilisation of the country. europe must help the ukrainians to make a successful economic and democratic transition. the ukrainian struggle is about our interests, our values and our credibility.
in writing. i voted in favour of the joint resolution on the russian invasion of ukraine, which strongly condemns the aggression perpetrated by russia by invading the ukrainian territory of crimea. we call for the immediate withdrawal of all military forces illegally present on ukrainian territory and for full respect for international law.
in writing. this resolution is aimed at one thing only: unilaterally condemning russia, on the pretext that it has invaded crimea. that's not my view of things, nor my position. ukraine is not a member of the eu or nato. as a result, neither the eu nor nato have the authority under international law to intervene in ukraine. the atlanticist bias of the authors of this report is clear, since they call for 'close transatlantic cooperation on measures to resolve the crisis'. in a bellicose escalation, the rapporteurs welcome the sanctions already taken against russia and they are enthusiastically considering new retaliatory measures, in total denial of the risks of war that arise from them, despite the risks of unconditional support for the current de facto authorities, formed by a political coalition including neo-nazi members, which parliament formally denounced in december 2012. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text so that the union can quickly take economic sanctions against russia if the situation in crimea does not calm down, in particular by means of an embargo on weapons and technologies with both civilian and military uses.
in writing. i voted against this resolution on the situation in ukraine. there is no question of validating the €11 billion 'aid' plan, concocted in cooperation with the imf, by which the european union reaffirms its willingness to sign an entire so-called deep and comprehensive free trade agreement as soon as possible. while condemning russia's attitude, and in particular the use of military force in ukraine, i can only deplore the outbid of both sides, with ukraine becoming the battleground of geopolitical competition between two imperialisms, russia on the one hand and the western bloc, comprising the united states and the european union, on the other. it's like we're back in the good old days of the cold war. this political crisis cannot be resolved by violence or by the decisions of "transitional authorities", where far-right political groups (such as the svoboda party) hold several ministerial posts, all in a climate of widespread corruption, with neither side having anything to envy the other. a lasting solution can only be found by the ukrainian people themselves, independently of any foreign interference.
in writing. this report provides an initial assessment of the implementation of the treaty of lisbon (2009), and in particular of the new powers conferred on the european parliament. i voted in favour of this report because i think it is important in substance and balanced in its wording. the next step will now be the holding of european elections on 25 may 2014 with, for the first time, the possibility for european citizens to choose (indirectly) the president of the european commission, again an innovation allowed by the lisbon treaty.
in writing. i did not vote in favour of my friend paulo rangel's report because it contains, in my opinion, a very dangerous proposal to reduce the majority required for a motion of censure on the european commission to a simple majority of the members of the european parliament, whereas at present a double majority is required: two thirds of the votes cast and a majority of the members of the european parliament. the fact that this reduction must be made without jeopardizing the functioning of the institutions does not seem to me to be of a nature to remove the dangerous nature of this proposal. it merits a wider institutional political debate and, in my view, introduces a significant risk of institutional instability in an assembly that does not have a stable majority. i had tabled an amendment to mitigate this proposal but it was considered to be covered by the compromise, which is not true. it is in this context that i have decided not to approve this report, which contains excellent proposals.
in writing. the european parliament, the only institution directly elected by european citizens, must in future, in accordance with the treaties, play a leading role in the formulation and implementation of european policies. the next european elections in may will be an opportunity for this new assembly to weigh in on the composition of the european commission.
in writing. this report takes stock of the implementation of the lisbon treaty, which was a crucial step in strengthening the european parliament's powers as a co-legislator. it rightly stresses the need to consolidate the democratic legitimacy of the european union. the european parliament's election of the candidates for the presidency of the commission is therefore an important procedure. it is right to recall the need for good cooperation between these two institutions in order to ensure that the interests of european citizens are well represented.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which aims to assess the implementation of the lisbon treaty, which in particular strengthens the role of the european parliament. in this respect, the sharing of information with parliament should be improved, particularly in the context of international agreements, which have an increasing influence on the lives of european citizens.
in writing. this motion for a resolution reflects the anti-democratic cynicism of the european leaders and their desire to further distance the european union from the sovereignty of the peoples. the commission welcomes the lisbon treaty, which it says aims to 'strengthen the democratic legitimacy of the european union'. on the contrary, it has strengthened the role of the commission to counter the risk of 'parliamentarisation'. the authors here propose to further increase the political influence of the commission, a body devoid of any democratic legitimacy, a way of increasing the gap between the european union and the sovereignty of the peoples. i am voting against this motion for a resolution which reinforces the authoritarian nature of the present european union since the treaty, the budgetary treaty and the troika.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which assesses the implementation of the lisbon treaty, paying particular attention to the impact of the main changes it has introduced on the interinstitutional relations between the european parliament and the commission since its entry into force. the report stresses the need to strengthen the democratic legitimacy, independence and political role of the commission by linking more directly the choice of the electorate to the election of its president.
in writing. in accordance with the provisions of the lisbon treaty, the european council will have to take account of the outcome of the european elections when appointing the president of the commission. once the nominee has been appointed, he will be required to explain to parliament the political orientations of his mandate. this is a real step forward for the union, which will gain legitimacy vis-à-vis the peoples of europe. in the end, the president of the commission should even be elected by direct universal suffrage. the future commissioners should be selected on the basis of their competence, independence and european commitment. to do this, the president-elect of the commission must be able to act more autonomously in the selection process of members of an executive composed equally of men and women. finally, a majority of the members of the next commission should be chosen from among the elected members of parliament. more generally, the way the european executive works will have to be re-examined in the future. we will have to carry out a reform that leads to simple, clear, legible institutions, the designation of which the people have a say, because europe is in vital need of a genuine democratic refoundation.
in writing. the total value of illegal and unregistered goods in developing countries is estimated at over $9.3 trillion, equivalent to 93 times the total amount of foreign aid given to developing countries over the past 30 years. promoting land regimes and empowering individuals to manage their own resources could be one of the greatest successes of the 21st century, but also one of the greatest challenges ever. that is why i voted in favour of this text which examines the various possibilities for mobilising these funds and methods in order to achieve the eradication of poverty.
in writing. the lack of property rights undermines the growth of developing countries. the establishment of land schemes is a sure means of capital formation. this makes it possible to have a guarantee in order to obtain loans at reduced rates. this is the view shared by this text. i particularly welcome the desire to promote the application of property rights for women, who are often affected by inequalities in access to property in these countries.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague nirj deva on the role of property rights, property regimes and wealth creation in eradicating poverty and promoting sustainable development in developing countries. the report states that the existence of registered and recognised property rights is a driver of economic growth. it thus encourages the implementation of a roadmap for the guarantee of land rights, including property rights, and the establishment of sustainable land governance in developing countries. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. the deva report considers that the existence of registered and recognised property rights is a driver of economic growth. it confuses the possession of title to land on the one hand, with access to land and the security of exploitation on the other, which can help to reduce poverty. nor does it recognize that the root cause of poverty is the unequal distribution of wealth. the right to life is the result of the primacy of the right to private property over other rights, in particular the right to life. so it is also by putting limits on private property that poverty can be reduced. the report does have some good points, however: it denounces land grabbing and highlights that subsidies for biofuel production play a major role. it pays special attention to women's access to property. to encourage such analyses, i vote in favour.
in writing. this own-initiative report considers that the existence of property rights recognised by the collection of reliable data is a driver of economic growth. in his initial report, the rapporteur only referred in the margins to the various existing systems of 'customary rights' to land (no title deeds). ninety-two amendments were tabled to abandon this position in favour of the approach developed by the united nations habitat study (2008). it calls for the protection and strengthening of traditional forms of access to land and the defence of the rights of indigenous peoples, women and marginalized groups. the study also points out that a process of titration could lead to a concentration of agricultural land. many of these amendments were finally accepted and the final report is therefore much more satisfactory than the initial version. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which aims to develop a more comprehensive approach to the policies of the european union and its development partners. a 'macro' approach would make it possible to rationalize costs and above all to increase efficiency, which is the most important thing when we talk about development.
in writing. i supported this text which calls for greater coherence and better rationalisation of european policies for development. it is quite appropriate to define priority areas of action, such as the fight against social and environmental dumping or the coherent management of migration flows. similarly, it is appropriate to carry out evaluations of the development impact of the main union policies to ensure their effectiveness and coherence.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague charles goerens on the 2013 report on policy coherence for development. the report proposes a number of measures to make the objective of policy coherence for development operational and suggests priority areas for action, including migration management, trade, social, agricultural, energy and environmental issues. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. the report recommends the establishment of an arbitration mechanism to "prevent inconsistencies arising from the policies pursued by the union in order to avoid negative spillovers on developing countries". at least the report acknowledges the negative consequences of the union's policies. that's a good start! it even denounces social and environmental dumping and tax evasion, but the judge in this arbitration is supposed to be the president of the commission! the very same one that promotes these devastating policies. the developing countries will then be able to say, "five more minutes, mr. executioner". parliament and the states obviously have no say in this matter. i am voting against this absurd solution to problems which are so serious and so clearly established.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which recalls that policy coherence for development has become a global policy tool. the aim of the latter is to prevent inconsistencies arising from the policies pursued by the union in order to avoid negative spillovers on developing countries. this paper focuses on the method and mechanisms for ensuring optimum consistency in order to prevent certain inconsistencies.
in writing. the 25th session of the united nations human rights council is taking place from 3 to 28 march 2014 in geneva. since it is important that the european union brings its values and priorities to such international meetings, i voted in favour of this text.

on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, the clinical trials regulation can bring about a revolution in the practice of clinical trials in europe for several reasons: firstly, procedures will be harmonised throughout the union, which will greatly facilitate the development and implementation of european multicentre clinical trials. the second point is that the procedures will be simplified, which will obviously make life easier for promoters, especially university promoters m.[nbsp ]borg recalled how many they were , who will now have only one interlocutor and not a flop of absolutely anonymous interlocutors most of the time. thirdly, the procedures will be shortened. these shorter deadlines will also simplify the lives of university researchers. fourth, the results will be published. when i say results, i mean all results, including negative results. this will increase transparency and ultimately the trust of eu citizens in clinical trials. fifthly, and for the first time at european level, it is the added risk of clinical research and not the absolute risk that will be studied in the context of the formation of clinical trial dossiers. all of this is fundamental. my dear colleagues, simplification of procedures, speeding up of procedures, lower costs will probably mean more protection for patients in europe and more chances for them to benefit from new treatments quickly. for our scientists, this will be a guarantee of participation in trials that matter in the world of scientific research, while our pharmaceutical industry will find a clear advantage.
on behalf of the group . - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i thank glennis willmott for the work she has done as rapporteur, because it was urgent to propose a number of solutions to avoid, for example, the decline in the number of applications for authorisation of clinical trials, which reached 25% between 2007 and 2011 in europe. we also found that the administrative costs and time limits in europe had become a complete deterrent. unfortunately, in recent years, we have seen a shift of research to emerging countries, where the supervision of clinical trials is more flexible. patient associations, pharmaceutical companies and researchers have criticised the current legislation for imposing too heavy a regulatory framework on administrative formalities. the real improvements in the text are welcome: firstly, the guarantee of transparency in the conduct and results of clinical trials, then the strengthening of the role of ethics committees in the approval of trials, but also the proper information of patients and the increase in protective measures for vulnerable people and finally the protection of personal data. these are improvements which are a credit to the european parliament and the european institutions in relation to these human clinical trials.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, the digital single market is an opportunity for europe. we are all involved in the whole operation of removing borders and barriers, boosting our economy and showing every european what europe can do for them. today we have three very good examples of that, and i would like to thank ms del castillo vera, ms ulvskog and ms herczog – they did a great job, together with their rapporteurs, their shadows and all others involved – for their hard work. first, on eid: protecting citizens from insecurity, impersonation and hacking online, with services that are convenient and competitive, trustworthy and transparent – benefits that do not stop at the border. second, cutting the cost of network roll-out: i look forward to the vote in a fortnight. many europeans will join me in thanking you for that. they will get better broadband and fewer roadworks just by cutting the duplication – or something as simple as that. but if there is one thing i have realised, it is that the digital world is an ecosystem. it is no good having one bit without the other. it is no good having secure eid across borders without secure networks across borders; having a fancy new phone if roaming charges make you switch it off; or having fast, fixed broadband without the spectrum for wireless networks or if your operator blocks websites. we cannot accept that. that is why, ten months ago, i stood before many of you and promised new telco proposals, looking at the whole ecosystem and making a difference to the life of every person you represent. digital resources are crucial resources, especially for the 21st century. our citizens depend on them and expect them. let us not wait until they demonstrate in the streets. once we founded a community on coal and steel; now it needs to be founded on connectivity and spectrum, otherwise we are going to fall behind. it is time to liberate the billion devices in europe. that is why we need rules for a connected continent. in six short months we have made tremendous progress on this file. this shows its importance, and i am really grateful to all of you. you have suggested a number of changes – i am aware of that – but it remains in line with our objective. the market is not functioning, and you and i do not accept that. people are being short-changed when they sign a contract, and they are scared when they roam. we do not have the resources to face the future. today, with your vote, you can change all that. let me address the issue of openness and innovation online, and of net neutrality. freedom underpins a rich, vibrant online world. i know many of you have been bombarded on this issue by lobbyists, who probably said that this was a question of saving the internet as opposed to destroying it; freedom as opposed to tyranny; black as opposed to white. i know you are too wise to take those exaggerations at face value. we are not here just to come out with nice slogans. we could kill the internet with words. i want to save it with actions, and i imagine you do too. so let us take up our responsibilities and do the hard work. you know that i stand – and i fight – for freedom, openness and innovation, as we all do. this is easy to say but harder to achieve. so what does it actually mean? innovation means no more blocking or throttling services on the open internet. i am glad we all agree on that, and i agree that we need safeguards for specialised services. they must never be an alternative to the internet, never slow down the internet for everyone else, and never be forced on users against their will. that much is clear. they do not mean – and they will never mean – making people suddenly pay for youtube, but equally we must not block those new specialised services. in my opinion, that would be the opposite of openness. blocking strangles innovation and, despite what you may have been told in the last few days, that is what some of the plenary amendments will do – block specialised services. i realise the pressure you are under to do so, but we must consider the consequences. we cannot tell european businesses that they cannot have the network they need for high-definition video conferences. you do not want to tell citizens that you would not let them enjoy quality iptv. and can we tell hospitals and healthcare workers that they cannot try out new telehealth procedures? all those things depend on enhanced quality of service. i hope that tomorrow’s vote will be a good day for europe and a significant step forward for our connected continent. together, let us make sure the internet remains the platform for incredible innovation and remains an open internet.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. - mr president, today we are taking a further step towards the completion of the digital single market. the regulation on electronic identification and trust services, by digitising administrative procedures, will simplify them, while giving them the same legal value as paper documents. students, for example, will no longer have to travel to another member state to enrol in a university. companies will save time and reduce their operating costs through electronic signature, electronic stamp and electronic registered mail. as you know, the key to digital development is trust, and i must say that i am very proud that my idea for a european label has been chosen. service providers who meet the safety requirements will be able to display it, and this will be a guarantee for citizens. the committee on legal affairs and citizens' rights has adopted a number of amendments. - mr president, i will continue what i was saying about the need to give citizens confidence in the digital world. we have clearly defined the responsibilities of those who issue means of identification in order to secure the relationship between citizens and their public services. it is a fact that europeans are still too afraid of digital technology. they are full of fear, full of prejudice, but also full of contradictions, and we are here to reassure them. i hope that these texts, this important package we are about to vote on, will help to give them confidence, because if we do not fight in the digital field, if the european union is not capable of doing so, it will be the other continents that will eat us alive and that would be really unfortunate.

technological developments, namely investment, deployment, access in all its forms and on all the media for the benefit of the consumer, who will thus be able to have new services at better costs. we (the speaker agrees to answer a question on the 'blue card' (rule 149 (8) of the rules of procedure))
answer is "blue cardboard". mr president, what should be avoided is the development of specialised services and their prioritisation at the expense of basic access for all citizens, who are entitled to demand it. what we must avoid is confusion in the use of these specialised services, which is a positive thing and we are not opposed to it, but it must be organised sufficiently so that traffic congestion is not a handicap and does not force the citizen to endure the choices that would be imposed on him. that is my answer to mr rübig.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we have made many improvements in consumer information, including the obligation to provide a free consumer tracking service for both prepaid and subscription services, as well as clear and comparable information on the actual coverage of mobile networks. in addition, consumers will have to be informed of the average and minimum internet speeds they can expect at home for fixed internet and in their country for mobile internet, data that can be used against providers in the event of non-compliance with these speeds. i also welcome the progress on emergency calls and the 112 number, in particular the definition of common technical standards for call tracing, in particular for gps-enabled smartphones. however, i believe that we can still improve the conditions for termination by our vote in the event of a change in the contract by the operator or if the quality of the service is not achieved. so now i hope that tomorrow we will support a neutral and non-discriminatory internet in order to get a strong and ambitious text for consumers and citizens.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european union must therefore guarantee a free and open internet that protects the fundamental rights of europeans. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the euro against counterfeiting is a very good one. prioritizing flows is a violation of equal access to information, freedom of expression or, economically, a brake on the emergence of job-creating start-ups. the notion of a specialised service is a blow to net neutrality and is in contradiction with the positions that our parliament has defended throughout this parliamentary term to preserve the principle of neutrality. we, the environmentalists, refuse to sacrifice the freedoms of europeans and their capacity to innovate in these times of economic crisis on the altar of a few very large companies. we will vote tomorrow and when we do we will not forget who we represent: first of all the citizens, the european internet users. and it is to safeguard their interests and freedoms that we will defend the net neutrality amendment.
president-in-office of the council. - madam president, honourable members, the period covered by the stockholm programme will draw to a close this year. each of our institutions has reviewed the progress made over the last few years, and our third evaluation will play an important role as we come to look forward to the further development of the area of freedom, security and justice. the stockholm programme has played an important role in guiding and directing the european union’s efforts to implement a wide-ranging, ambitious set of actions in the area of justice and home affairs. i think we have every reason to be proud of what has been achieved. for example, in the area of asylum and migration there has been significant progress on the development of a common european asylum system, which is a particularly complex and sensitive file. we have also made progress in related areas such as legal migration and integration. a good example is the progress reached on the directive regarding the inter-corporate mobility of third-country nationals, as well as the adoption of the seasonal workers directive. this is particularly important, given the link between migration and economic growth. it also lies at the heart of many of the positive dialogues which we have with many of our neighbours. in the margins of the justice and home affairs council in march, for example, we signed a mobility partnership with tunisia. a related issue is the development of frontex, with its enhanced commitment to fundamental rights and the agreement reached on the operations-at-sea issues. the smart border initiative is now moving forward with the objective of reaching agreement by mid-2016. security issues remain of very significant concern to our citizens. our work on serious and organised crime is a highly operational part of our activities which aims at tackling a scourge which undermines our societies. key to action is this area are the european union agencies such as europol and cepol. the stockholm programme has also allowed us to make a major step forward in the area of justice, with increasing attention being given to individual citizens and to respect for their basic rights. our work on civil law is very much in line with this objective. continuing work includes discussions on the solvency proposal and the forthcoming adoption of the regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters. both are very important files. there have also been significant developments in the area of criminal law. one example is the progress in the area of criminal proceedings or victims’ rights. overall the stockholm programme has acted as a catalyst which has enabled us collectively to deliver on a wide range of legislation and actions which help protect the security and rights of all eu citizens. i would like at this point to thank the honourable members for their commitment to making progress in all these areas and also to thank both the commissioners in charge of this area. we now need to build on the success of the stockholm programme, learn from experience and draw lessons for the future. part of this will require drawing on the mid-term review of the programme, which was requested by the european council. the review was carried out in 2012 under the cyprus presidency, and this review is complementary to the work begun by parliament last summer. we particularly value the full involvement of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, the committee on constitutional affairs, and the committee on legal affairs in this process. their input is hugely significant as we collectively assess progress over the last few years, and i would like to thank the three rapporteurs once again. the european council, in accordance with article 68 of the treaty on european union, which requires it to define strategic guidelines in the area of justice and home affairs, has agreed to address this issue at its meeting in june. this work has since been taken up at a series of meetings, including the athens informal ministerial meeting in january. there have also been two full rounds of coreper discussions and a further discussion in the justice and home affairs council in march. in addition to parliament’s valuable work, and also the participation of mr lópez aguilar in the athens informal meeting, there have been two recent commission communications which have helped develop our thinking. there appears to be a significant amount of agreement about where we stand on a wide range of issues. i think we all agree that we need to put more emphasis on the quality, rather than the quantity, of legislation. the stockholm programme has been successful in laying the foundations in many areas. the priority now must be to consolidate and implement the existing framework. closely related to this, we also share similar views on the importance of evaluation, whether this is looking backwards or forwards. evidence-based evaluation is considered to be an increasingly-important tool in assessing related actions which have already been undertaken and also in helping us to set priorities for the future. this requires a greater commitment to the exchange of information between eu institutions and the member states. generating an improvement in mutual trust will also help in the further development of practical cooperation to resolve everyday issues. training in the use of information technology, such as e-justice and rapid data exchange, will be key to enabling this to happen. finally, we all agree on the need to improve the coherence between the external and internal dimension of justice and home affairs policies. this will involve closer cooperation and better complementarity in the use of resources between all those involved, but in particular the european external action service and the member states. it is clear that the future development of the area of freedom, security and justice is not just an abstract exercise. it touches on the interests, values and security of all our citizens. the council, with its particular treaty-based role, is committed to building on the considerable achievements made so far. but delivering results in this area can only ever be a collective endeavour. we therefore continue to hope for your support. thank you for the contribution which you have already made in this area and which is vital for the further development of europe.

ideas on the political priorities of these policies. i was pleased to see, by the way, that on many issues the commissionʼs assessments converge with yours. in full awareness of the post-lisbon institutional setup which puts this parliament on an equal footing with the council, we orient our policies towards citizens and their day-by-day concerns. we stress the importance of the legally binding eu charter of fundamental rights when eu law is at stake and we are also convinced that mutual trust remains the cornerstone of a common european judicial and law enforcement culture. while looking forward towards the future of eu justice policy we have identified three main challenges: trust, mobility and growth. trust is the bedrock on which eu justice policy is built and trust cannot be done by decree. it needs constant efforts by all participants. the eu has laid the foundations for promotion of this trust but this needs to be further strengthened to ensure citizens, legal practitioners and judges within the eu fully trust judicial decisions irrespective of the member states where they have been taken. mobility: eu citizens and businesses are rightly taking advantage of the free movement rights conferred upon them by the treaty but we all know that challenges remain. we all know that obstacles remain. despite significant progress achieved in this respect, citizens still experience practical and legal difficulties when trying to enjoy their rights and parliament rightly demanded that more needs to be done in this context. growth: eu justice policy should continue to make a contribution to economic recovery and tackling unemployment. structural reforms need to be pursued to ensure that justice systems are capable of delivering swift, reliable and trustworthy justice, thereby supporting the effectiveness of all other eu policies. and i appreciate in this respect the full support of this parliament for the eu justice scoreboard and its specific contribution to the european semester. eu justice policy should focus on consolidating what has already been achieved, codifying eu law and practice and, when necessary and appropriate, complementing the existing framework with new initiatives. consolidating: respect for fundamental rights is a key concern in your resolution. the commission fully shares your concern and agrees that upholding fundamental rights requires the combined efforts of all the institutions and member states. on 11[nbsp ]march the commission presented its new eu framework to strengthen the rule of law. the adoption of this communication on the same day as the eu justice agenda for 2020 shows that respect for the rule of law is an essential and key component of the whole justice policy. it also shows that the commission is determined to play fully its role as guardian of the unionʼs values. in the eu justice agenda for 2020 the commission also underlines the need for better training of legal practitioners. we have to enhance their knowledge of eu law. we have to improve cooperation. training legal practitioners in eu law is of utmost importance to ensure that the law is implemented and applied correctly, to build trust in each otherʼs judicial systems and to enable those systems to work together across borders. we will also have to explore the need for codification of certain parts of existing legislation in the justice area and of the relevant case law of the court of justice. codifying means streamlining existing legislation or practices into one single instrument for more clarity and for more legal certainty. and we all know that justice is a dynamic policy area. we have experienced that in the last month, in the last years. and it should therefore be capable of responding to changing realities and evolving expectations from both citizens and businesses. and in this context new initiatives to complement existing instruments may be envisaged if they are appropriate. the need and the added value of such complementary initiatives will have to be carefully assessed in the light of the diversity of national legal systems and traditions.

a concept that's a little bit catch-all, a little bit catch-all? how can we ensure that this global approach is not just beautiful rhetoric, disconnected from the often more complex and unfortunately often more fragmented realities of our external action? the global approach, everybody's advocating it these days. all the organisations want to take the global approach to dealing with challenges and crises: the un, nato, the european union. for the european union this is obvious, because it is the only organisation with such a wide range of instruments to carry out this policy: humanitarian, development, trade, civilian security policy missions, military missions. we have all the instruments at our disposal, so this ambition is legitimate. but the global approach is too often seen in retrospect rather than constructed a priori. i want to take as an example what is happening in the horn of africa, which is an example that you often bring up. as far as the horn of africa is concerned, all the boxes are ticked: we are carrying out military operations there, we are carrying out civilian missions there, we are providing development and humanitarian aid there. so we're on every floor. we also have a good special envoy. it's all there, all the boxes are ticked. but is this all a strategy? in writing. the eu is also funding its own channel, euronews, supposedly to strengthen its "editorial independence" and ensure the "diversity" of opinions (up to 5 billion euros a year anyway, no budget cuts here), a diversity that is never extended to me. but the point here is to encourage european radio and television to become propaganda tools for the union's policy, and particularly its foreign policy. to "orient the debate" to allow "a more uniform understanding of foreign policy among european citizens". and in the present context it is clear which way the union intends to go, the only example given, belarus, invites others. in any event, under rule 97 of parliament's rules of procedure, this text is deemed to have been adopted without parliament's opinion being sought. otherwise i would have voted against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this recommendation which calls on the european council and the european external action service to develop a coherent and comprehensive strategy for european media broadcasting in the context of the union's external relations, thereby promoting freedom of expression and media pluralism and strengthening democracy and human rights in third countries.
in writing. with this text, we are taking action on vehicle noise levels by lowering the limit values for vehicle-related noise emissions in their diversity. the report also seeks to set a minimum noise level. the stated goal is to reduce the number of people with disabilities by 25%. i am very pleased with this text, the provisions of which simply help to improve the tranquility of our fellow citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation because the objective of protecting health and the environment must be as compatible as possible with safeguarding the internal market. i also welcome the proposal to ensure road and work safety by introducing minimum noise requirements for electric and hybrid electric vehicles.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which should make it possible to combat noise pollution from motor vehicles more effectively, while preserving the competitiveness of our automotive industry. i have committed myself to ensuring that the industry, which employs almost 13 million people in europe, is not subjected to unrealistic and unworkable standards at a time when it is being hit hard by the economic crisis. the final compromise, which favours a pragmatic approach, includes a gradual reduction in the maximum permissible sound level of motor vehicles, better information for consumers when buying, and the mandatory inclusion of avas, which can alert visually impaired pedestrians, in all electric vehicles.
in writing. on wednesday 2 april, the european parliament voted in favour of regulations to reduce the noise level of motor vehicles. these new rules will have an impact on health and the environment, as more than half of the urban population in europe is exposed to noise levels of more than 55 decibels due to road traffic. we therefore plan to reduce engine noise by 4 decibels for small and medium-sized vehicles and by 3 decibels for larger vehicles. we have created sufficiently flexible rules for buses, lorries and sports cars to protect european industry while ensuring that these measures are effective. a label will be created for the least noisy vehicles to encourage consumers to favour them. i voted in favour of this text because i believe it will make vehicles more environmentally friendly and encourage innovation in the automotive sector.
in writing. the proposal aims to reduce the noise level of motor vehicles. noise from road traffic has an undeniable effect on health and quality of life. some of the proposed measures are in the right direction: imposing a maximum noise level on manufacturers, or, on the contrary, providing a minimum noise level for electric vehicles. but in the end the compromise at second reading is very disappointing. even though the surface of the road is a factor in noise emission, the commission refused to classify road pavements for noise control. the compromise is sometimes even less ambitious than the commission's proposal, particularly as regards the most powerful heavy trucks or the limits on sound which the commission advocates.
in writing. as rapporteur for the opinion in the tran committee, i voted in favour of this regulation which aims to reduce the noise level of motor vehicles such as cars, vans and lorries. according to who, traffic noise could cost 1 million years of healthy life in western europe every year. 1.8[nbsp]% of heart attacks in european countries are attributed to a traffic noise level of over 60[nbsp]db. noise from rail and road transport is therefore thought to be responsible for 50 000 fatal heart attacks and 200 000 cases of cardiovascular disease each year in europe. it was therefore more than urgent to revise this european legislation dating back to 1996.
in writing. reducing vehicle noise is important to protect public health and the environment in the european union. our citizens must be able to live in the best possible conditions. of course, the necessary adaptation time for the automobile industry must also be taken into account. i am therefore very pleased to have voted in favour of this report which perfectly highlights both of these points of view. on the one hand, the health of our citizens remains a priority, but on the other hand, we must be realistic and not set unrealistic targets which could seriously damage the european economy. this is a mistake which the greens and the socialists tend to make. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the environment is protected. in these times of crisis, we must maintain our ideals and values while being pragmatic.
in writing. the european parliament adopted my report on computerised databases by 395 votes to 216, with 13 abstentions. this is a technical text which allows account to be taken of the emergence of new technologies, in particular the electronic identification of bovine animals. this report ensures interoperability between the member states' computer systems. i am particularly pleased with the result of the call for a vote in favour.
in writing. this amendment to the current legislation is to take account of the development of new technologies in the field of electronic identification of bovine animals. the computerised databases containing information on bovine animals located in the territories of those member states should take account of that new information. it is therefore quite appropriate to adapt this european legislation which makes it possible to improve these databases by extending their fields of information in such a way as to guarantee efficient identification of bovine animals and thus better health and food safety.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive because i believe that the exchange of information on traceability of bovine and porcine animals should be a priority for the european union. this new directive only increases transparency in health matters, and i welcome that.
in writing. this text complements the proposal on the electronic identification of bovine animals by the establishment of a computerised database. the question of labelling cloned animals has not been settled, so i cannot support it. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive. the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1760/2000 as regards the electronic identification of bovine animals and repealing its provisions on the optional labelling of beef and veal requires council directive 64/432/eec to be amended accordingly as regards the computerised databases which form part of the surveillance networks in the member states. to date, the elements of the computerised databases established in directive 64/432/eec do not include any reference to electronic means of identification. in the interests of consistency of union legislation, this regulation amends council directive 64/432/eec as regards computerised databases forming part of the surveillance networks in the member states.
