in writing. i voted in favour of the rinaldi report on the application and enforcement of international trade rules. this regulation gives the european union the means to enforce its trade rights vis-à-vis third countries. it enables the commission to act quickly and effectively in cases of violations of international trade rules by using trade defence instruments. this is a real step towards the principle of reciprocity in trade.
in writing. the european union needs to be provided with effective instruments to enforce its rights under international trade agreements. that is why i support such a text which aims to make the european union a credible actor on the international scene, capable of protecting its interests. the creation of a common legislative framework setting out the rules and procedures to prevent third countries from breaching international trade rules is therefore appropriate. it is therefore important to promote systematic recourse to the most effective dispute resolution mechanisms. the european union cannot allow its rights to be flouted and competitiveness in europe to be penalized.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation which aims to create a common legislative framework to enforce the union's rights under international trade agreements. i welcome this agreement which largely safeguards the interests of the union in that it sets up instruments to respond to violations by third countries of international trade rules which affect the interests of member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr niccolo rinaldi, on the application and enforcement of international trade rules. the aim of this text is to establish rules governing how the union would enforce and defend its rights in the event of unfair or illegal trade measures taken in third countries. the eu previously lacked a single legal framework to defend its interests in a rapid, efficient and flexible manner, which did not provide an incentive for offending countries to stop their behaviour. the report was adopted by 596 votes in favour, 17 against and 16 abstentions. i am very pleased with this result.
in writing. the proposal aims to provide the european union with a horizontal legislative framework to enforce its rights under the wto and other international trade agreements. the regulation lays down rules and procedures to guarantee the union's rights to suspend or withdraw concessions in international trade agreements. does the european union want to retaliate against certain aggressive unilateral measures taken by its trading partners? unfortunately, the policy has its limits: it must not have "the slightest protectionist purpose". moreover, the many references to the wto do imply the promotion of free trade. i'm not going to. i do not want to deny europe some of the few new means of protection it has at its disposal, but i do not approve of the overall free trade framework in which this report is based.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which proposes the creation of a common legislative framework to enforce the union's rights under international trade agreements, in accordance with the treaty of lisbon. to that end, it lays down rules and procedures to ensure the effective exercise of the union's rights to suspend or withdraw concessions or other obligations under international trade agreements.
in writing. the european union has finally adopted a regulation allowing it to act as a last resort when a third country does not respect international trade rules. if one of our trading partners does not respect these rules, it is only natural that the union may defend itself by temporarily taking defensive retaliatory measures against that country when all diplomatic means of resolving disputes have been exhausted. the security of european businesses and the stability of the union's economy as a whole are at stake. i am glad that i voted for this report, for which i was the fictitious rapporteur for the epp group. the european union is increasingly opening up its market to third countries, so it is necessary to ensure that economic operators trading with the union play by the rules of the art. we must remain cautious in the face of unfair competition from third countries. the regulation will enable the union to benefit from the attractions of trade with the rest of the world while protecting its businesses.
in writing. in a move to support the development of bangladesh, this resolution sets out the conditions for marketing in europe (cultivation, packaging, etc.). rice accounts for a large proportion of the european diet.
in writing. with this text we decide to frame the respective institutional prerogatives of the commission and parliament concerning the preferential import regime for rice originating in bangladesh. this is a necessary adjustment to allow for a better reliability of the system. more generally, the union is showing its concern to adopt a rigorous approach in its action for sustainable economic development and acceptable working conditions in a country where rice cultivation is a key activity.
in writing. the commission proposal aims to adapt the regulation on rice imports to the lisbon treaty by giving new powers to the commission (delegated and implementing acts). the regulation provides for exemption from import duties for bangladesh in accordance with wto rules on preferential tariffs for developing countries (dcs). however, the rapporteur, my colleague mr paul murphy, pays particular attention to the 'overall objectives of sustainable economic development, decent working conditions in bangladesh and the eradication of poverty in that country'. it adds a reference to the gsp+ ('special incentive scheme') which grants additional trade preferences to developing countries which have signed a number of international social and environmental conventions, introducing into eu trade law the idea of a possible hierarchy of standards. i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this, but i am saying that it should be involved in the negotiations.
in writing. this report concerns a proposal for a regulation on rice imports from bangladesh. the preferential import conditions (as provided for by the wto for the least developed countries) granted to rice from bangladesh consist of a reduction in import duties within certain quantities. the commission proposal aims to align council regulation (eec) no 3491/90 on the import of rice from bangladesh with the post-lisbon arrangements for implementing the acts provided for in articles 290 and 291 of the treaty. the commission therefore proposes, for the sake of clarity, to replace regulation no 3491/90 by the new regulation, a move which the rapporteur approves. i welcome the fact that the rapporteur has finally succeeded in removing the mention that bangladesh must levy an export tax. while i am not opposed to this tax as such, i do not think it is the european union's responsibility to impose it. bangladesh is a sovereign country and should be free to decide whether or not to introduce such a tax. i therefore supported the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to apply to council regulation (eec) no 3491/90 on imports of rice originating in bangladesh the distinction introduced by articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union between the delegated and the implementing powers of the commission. we wanted this regulation to take account of the right of small farmers and rural workers to a decent income and to a safe and healthy working environment. respect for this right was fundamental to the achievement of the general objectives of trade preferences for developing countries and in particular for the least developed countries.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text on rice imports from bangladesh. since 2009, all ldcs have had access to the european market without quotas or import duties for a certain quantity of rice. this report, presented by my irish colleague and colleague from the gue/ngl group, paul murphy, has several positive aspects. it is based on the principles of solidarity farming: 'this regulation is based on the recognition of the right of small farmers to a decent income and to a safe and healthy working environment ...'. it recalls the ilo rules to be respected, 'in particular the conventions on forced labour, freedom of association, the right to collective bargaining, equal pay and the abolition of forced labour'. finally, although the commission's initial objective was to align the regulation with the lisbon treaty, the now amended regulation pays particular attention to the 'overall objectives of sustainable economic development, decent working conditions in bangladesh and poverty eradication in bangladesh'.
in writing. this resolution takes up the provisions of a report discussed in october 2013, thus aiming at harmonisation of medical devices in europe.
in writing. this review of european legislation on medical devices in europe aims to ensure strong quality and safety standards that protect european citizens. the pip breast implant scandal has highlighted the urgency of strengthening health security measures to ensure maximum protection for citizens who use these devices. i am therefore in favour of extending the scope of this legislation to include devices with aesthetic purposes. the creation of a committee for the evaluation of medical devices (cedm) is also an interesting proposal.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation, which aims to establish a strong, transparent and sustainable regulatory framework that is conducive to innovation and competitiveness in the medical device industry. i am also pleased that a clear definition of medical devices has been established. the new alignment of the definition with european and international practice will ensure a better approach to medical devices.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which aims to strengthen the safety of medical devices. the recent public health scandals involving defective breast implants and toxic hip prostheses illustrate the need to strengthen the safety controls of medical devices within the european union. the new eu regulation will strengthen the accreditation criteria for notified bodies and stricter controls will take place with random and unannounced audits in factories to ensure the safety of users of medical devices. however, parliament will have to continue its work to improve certain provisions when it reviews the regulation at second reading. i regret that in the text voted by parliament today the possibility for member states to prohibit the reprocessing of single-use medical devices such as syringes or catheters on grounds of health safety has been removed. inadequate cleaning, disinfection and sterilisation can lead to contamination or infection. i believe that the single-use medical device provides greater safety than sterilized and reconditioned equipment.
in writing. as the various pip breast prosthesis scandals have shown us, we need to strengthen health security and provide a coherent framework that supports innovation in the european medical device sector. the result adopted was a compromise, and it did not allow the most high-risk medical devices to be subject to systematic, prior and independent assessment by means of a collegial expertise on cases currently assessed unilaterally by a certified body. but this is a welcome result in view of the attempts by the conservatives and liberals to weaken the text even further. i am also in favour of maintaining the ban on reprocessing of single-use medical devices, as provided for in the text, because patient safety must not in any way come at the expense of restrictive budgetary policies practised by certain hospitals.
in writing. i abstained on the report by my colleague dagmar roth-behrendt on medical devices. while the text does make some progress in the post-market monitoring of medical devices, which is essential to prevent a new fraud like that of pip from happening again, i regret that prior marketing authorization has been adopted for certain categories of medical devices. this is a costly and time-consuming device that will burden professionals and slow down innovation, since, unlike a drug, the life cycle of a medical device is short and improvements are regular. under this system, any improvement, even a minor one, will have to wait for prior authorization before it can be placed on the market. i could not, however, bring myself to vote against the progress of this report, which is essential to improving patient safety. the report was adopted by 547 votes to 19, with 63 abstentions.
in writing. medical devices are instruments or devices which are intended to alleviate a disease or compensate for a disability without pharmacological means. they represent about half a million different products, from adhesive bandages to x-ray equipment. the 25 000 european medical technology companies employ more than half a million people and filed more than 10 000 patent applications in 2012. in response to the proliferation of incidents, such as the pip prosthesis scandal, the european parliament has revised existing legislation. i voted in favour of this text because it improves information and health protection for patients, as well as the traceability of medical devices, without hampering innovation. we have extended the legislation to include cosmetic devices (implants, lenses for aesthetic purposes). innovative risk devices or devices which have caused incidents in the past will have to be authorised by independent european experts before being placed on the market. meps who will sit after the renewal of the european parliament next july will have to negotiate with the council in order to adopt a final version of the text and implement it in all the member states of the european union.
in writing. the regulation has the merit of specifying the standards governing medical devices. the provisions against fraud have been tightened. member states are invited to provide for and enforce severe penalties. 'aesthetic devices' are added to the scope of the regulation. the report prohibits misleading statements and calls for the principle of free and informed consent to be respected. again, the report does not address the crucial question of the social and ecological conditions under which these medical devices are produced. in the absence of such social harmonisation, the free movement of medical devices encourages the relocation of manufacturers. france is largely concerned: it already imports 55[nbsp ]% of the medical devices it consumes. yet its productive capacity continues to decline, despite its productive and intellectual capacities. i vote for these legislative advances. but i deplore a further step in the liberalization of the market at the expense of workers and the objective of relocating production.
in writing. this report deals with the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on medical devices. i have decided to support this report because it presents important improvements in terms of control and certification of medical devices. it also proposes the creation of special bodies authorised to strengthen the control of medical devices presenting a high potential level of risk to patients.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which aims to ensure a high level of protection of human health and safety, to guarantee the proper functioning of the internal market and to provide a coherent regulatory framework capable of supporting innovation and competition in the european medical devices sector.
in writing. this legislative resolution, which takes up the work discussed in october 2013, aims at harmonising in vitro diagnostic medical devices in europe.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to strengthen the existing legislation on in vitro diagnostic medical devices used for the detection and prevention of diseases, diagnosis, monitoring of prescribed treatments and evaluation of medical interventions. these devices include self-diagnostics for blood glucose measurement, hiv testing and dna testing. given the sensitivity of their use, it is our duty as members of the european parliament to ensure maximum security for these devices in order to better protect citizens in the internal market. it is vital to ensure their reliability and quality. however, i recognize that this change in legislation must be made in a proportionate way so as not to impose excessive burdens on smes, which make up a large part of this sector.
in writing. i also voted in favour of this regulation, which aims to improve the safety of in vitro diagnostic medical devices intended for diagnostic use outside the human body, i.e. in a laboratory or near the patient, for example at his bedside. they cover a very wide range of tests, such as self-diagnostics for blood sugar measurement, hiv tests and dna tests. the rights and responsibilities of manufacturers, importers and distributors have been clarified, including with regard to diagnostic services and online sales. again, it will be necessary to ensure that the second reading review preserves these patient safety imperatives.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague peter liese on in vitro diagnostic medical devices. the text was voted on in october 2013, but the final vote was postponed so that the rapporteur could negotiate with the council and obtain an agreement which would then have been validated by parliament. the council was unable to reach agreement among its members on its own version of the text, and negotiations were not able to begin. parliament therefore had to decide on its own version of the text so that it could be forwarded to the next parliament and be agreed at second reading. the report was adopted by 492 votes to 21, with 117 abstentions. i am very pleased with this result.
in writing. in vitro medical devices are medical devices intended for diagnostic use outside the human body, i.e. in a laboratory or in the vicinity of the patient. they cover a very wide range of tests, such as self-diagnostics for blood sugar measurement, hiv testing and dna testing. the report proposes a number of improvements. a new risk classification system is proposed. the market surveillance and vigilance system will be strengthened. the unannounced inspections of enterprises will be mandatory. the report also allows the establishment of a network of european reference laboratories. the report ignores the crucial question of the social and ecological conditions under which these medical devices are produced. in the absence of such social harmonisation, the free movement of medical devices increases the risks of relocation of manufacturers. france is heavily exposed to this since it already imports 55% of the medical devices consumed. however, its production capacity continues to decline, as shown by the closure of the sodimedical plant. i vote for, to support the normative advances in product regulation. but i deplore a further step in the liberalisation of the goods market to the detriment of workers and the aim of relocating production as close as possible to their consumption.
in writing. in vitro diagnostic medical devices (ivds) are devices used outside the human body, in a laboratory or in the vicinity of the patient. they can be used to perform a multitude of tests, such as hiv tests and dna tests for example. the report proposes to improve the regulations governing the marketing of these devices, as the error rates can vary greatly from one device to another, which can lead to misdiagnosis and therefore to poor treatment. the report also provides an essential ethical dimension to clinical trials. i therefore supported the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which aims to establish a robust, transparent and sustainable regulatory framework that is conducive to innovation and competitiveness in the in vitro medical device industry and that allows quick and cost-effective market access for innovative devices for the benefit of patients and healthcare professionals.
in writing. the resolution aimed to present the strengths of the european environmental economic accounts in order to combat global warming and protect europe's fauna and flora.
in writing. the effectiveness of national economic policies must be assessed by taking environmental indicators into account. the impact on the environment affects the well-being of the population. it is therefore necessary to measure effectively the environmental progress made by each country. in order to obtain the most reliable and comprehensive indicators possible, it is therefore logical to extend the european environmental economic accounts to new modules such as environmental protection expenditure. however, strengthening these indicators does not mean creating new additional administrative burdens.

in writing. in april 2010, the european commission first proposed a regulation on european environmental economic accounts, which came into force in july 2011. it introduced three modules: air emission accounts, environmental taxes and material flow accounts. these three new modules were then only considered as a first step towards the establishment of a sound environmental accounting instrument. in line with this trend, this report introduces three new accounts: the environmental protection expenditure accounts, the sum of all environmental goods and services produced and the energy flow accounts. most of these statistical data are already available but need to be adjusted to ensure a sound scientific approach and more reliable comparability at european and international level. more reliable statistics and accounts will help to develop a more effective environmental and energy policy. i therefore support this approach and have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of regulation (eu) no 691/2011 on european environmental economic accounts, which establishes a common framework for the collection, preparation, transmission and evaluation of european environmental economic accounts in a modular form. at this stage, the modules to be implemented from 2013 are air emissions, environmental taxes and flow and material accounts. in accordance with article 10 of the regulation, the commission proposes to add 3[nbsp ]new modules for the environmental protection expenditure accounts, energy flow accounts and eco-activity accounts.
