in writing. the european parliament adopted on wednesday, 2 april, by 548 votes in favour, the report by my colleague, mrs agnès le brun, on european funding for animal and plant health measures for the period 2014-2020. i voted in favour of this report because it strengthens all the instruments for health protection, in particular by creating european support for national programmes for the monitoring of plant diseases.
in writing. following the scandal surrounding the presence of horse meat in frozen food, we decided through this resolution to reaffirm the basic principles of expenditure management relating to the food production chain, animal health and welfare and plant reproductive health and material. the agri-food sector must be above reproach if it is to guarantee european consumers a quality diet.
in writing. with this text, we are making it possible to rationalise the legal and financial framework of the food production chain. the aim is to establish coherent funding objectives for more efficient union assistance. this includes simplification of co-financing rates and the establishment of robust indicators to assess the effects of policies related to food supply chain security. the aim is to ensure the safety of food and feed in the production chain. this is a fundamental provision in the search for better food safety.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, the main objective of which is to contribute to a high level of human, animal and plant health throughout the food production chain. the various food scandals have recently shown the feverishness of the european food chain and this regulation will undoubtedly increase transparency in this area, which i welcome.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mrs agnès le brun, on european funding for animal and plant health measures for the period 2014-2020. the aim of this report is to contribute to a high level of human, animal and plant health, while encouraging competitiveness and job creation. the report also forms part of the reform of european health policy management and aims to simplify the legislative framework for food supply chain safety. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. my report, which was voted on wednesday 2 april, is part of a reform of european management of animal and plant health policy. as rapporteur for this text for the european parliament, i have been working to improve the implementation of this policy on the ground, in order to improve the prevention and management of health crises. major crises such as mad cow disease and avian influenza have shaken european consumer confidence. in the face of these crises, the european union must guarantee the highest standards of safety, quality and traceability, in order to ensure the stability of european production in the long term. the reform of my report has strengthened all the tools for health protection, in particular by creating european support for national programmes for the monitoring of plant diseases, the potential seriousness of which has been demonstrated by the e. coli crisis. i also insisted that the list of diseases for which european aid is provided be included in the report, in the interests of transparency. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. this regulation is part of the legislative package entitled 'smarter regulation for safer food'. this is to provide for the financing of preventive actions or responses to health risks. the regulation thus lays down the amounts of subsidies for preventive measures and the list of diseases which give rise to the right to such subsidies. a reserve fund for serious health crises at european level is also being set up. all these provisions are in the right direction. but the financing of crisis prevention and management measures is far from settled. the financial reserve which is intended to be used (the budget for direct aid under pillar 1) would not be sufficient to respond to a serious health crisis. in this context, i shall abstain on this text which raises a problem in order to avoid its solution.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation, which sets the scope and objectives of expenditure on food and feed and modernises the financial provisions in these areas.
in writing. restoring consumer confidence in the food sector is a major priority for the european union. many food crises have shown the need for adapting legislation and increasing financial support. we must be able to prevent food crises as well as to respond effectively when a problem arises. it is about protecting our producers, our consumers and our trading partners. i am glad i voted in favour of this report. it stressed the need to bring together the various legislation relating to the food sectors in order to strengthen health security. the economic recovery requires the restoration of consumer confidence.
in writing. the resolution states that wood remains one of the most widely used raw materials and that trade in wood must also meet specific standards for its use and treatment.
in writing. the flegt licensing scheme acts as a safety net to ensure that timber imported into the union is harvested legally. while the substance of the flegt scheme remains unchanged, this text makes the legal changes necessary to clearly organise the respective prerogatives of parliament and the commission in the application of the scheme. the report therefore provides the union with the institutional means to ensure the legality of imported wood. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment against pollution from industrial sources is a very good one. it is also a guarantee to the partner countries to maintain healthy trade relations with them, as the union is one of the main markets for tropical timber imports.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it will enable the union to better tackle the problem of illegal logging and the associated trade. this report sets up an authorization system for the application of forestry regulations, governance and trade related to timber imports into the european community. the text thus provides that only timber and derived products harvested legally and in accordance with the national legislation of the partner countries may enter the union. the new system will ensure better traceability of timber and derived products imported into europe. it will thus benefit the environment, european woodworking companies and consumers.
in writing. - council regulation (ec) no 2173/2005 establishes a licensing system for the application of trade rules in the forestry sector, in order to combat illegal logging and trade. in this context, the proposal under vote today is not intended to change the substantive characteristics of the flegt licensing system, but to harmonise the provisions on comitology contained in regulation (ec) no 2173/2005. under the flegt licensing scheme, partner countries will therefore be required to ensure, through controls and inspections, that timber products have been obtained from legally harvested domestically produced timber or legally imported timber from a partner country.
in writing. in the fight against the plunder of biodiversity, the issue of forest destruction is of the utmost importance. the flegt (forest law enforcement, government and trade) scheme was set up to tackle the problem of illegal logging and associated trade. for example, certain wood and wood products may not be imported from partner countries without an import licence. the proposal before us is aimed solely at adapting the flegt authorisation system to the lisbon treaty by conferring new powers on the commission (delegated and implementing acts). the french people rejected this treaty in a referendum, and i cannot accept that the sovereignty of the people should be undermined, even for minor technical adjustments. therefore, i abstain.
in writing. regulation (ec) no 2173/2005 establishes a licensing regime for 'forest law enforcement, governance and trade', referred to by the acronym flegt ('forest law enforcement, government and trade'). this scheme was set up to combat the problem of illegal logging and the associated trade. it applies to specified wood and derived products exported from 'partner countries', i.e. countries which have entered into voluntary partnership agreements with the union. the proposal adopted by the commission is not intended to change the fundamental features of the flegt licensing system. it shall be kept under constant review by the commission. it also empowers the commission to adopt implementing acts to assess and approve existing mechanisms to ensure the legality and reliable traceability of timber and derived products exported from partner countries, so that those mechanisms can serve as a basis for flegt authorisations. this report, which is very technical, is likely to make it possible to apply the flegt scheme more effectively. so i gave him my support.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which aligns council regulation (ec) no 2173/2005 on the establishment of a flegt licensing scheme for imports of timber into the european community with the new rules of the treaty on the functioning of the european union.
in writing. any product arriving in the european union must be subject to controls to ensure that it meets the various standards that guarantee maximum safety for european consumers. the flegt system for forest regulations ensures that timber and timber products entering the european market do not come from illegal logging. it is not enough to have ideas and values, but also to have the instruments to put them into music. with the flegt system, countries that have signed a voluntary partnership agreement with the union must control their timber in order to eradicate illegal trade. the union will ensure that each partner country respects its standards. i am glad to have voted in favour of this report, which will make it possible to adapt european legislation to the new institutional context. systems such as flegt must be as efficient as possible.
in writing. in order to tackle the problem of illegal logging, trade in timber within the eu is clearly regulated, especially when it comes from countries with which the eu has 'partnerships'. in 2005, a regulation was adopted to define the rules for importing timber into the european union. this regulation specifies that an import licence is required, without which importation is prohibited. since this old regulation was adopted before the treaty of lisbon, it now needs to be revised to adapt it to the new law of the european union, in particular as regards the provisions on the commission's use of delegated and implementing acts. unfortunately, these legal alignments often give the commission an opportunity to renounce parliament's powers. i am glad that this is not the case here and that parliament has managed for once to retain the control it has. on the one hand, parliament has asked to receive all the information and documentation on meetings with national experts on the preparation of delegated acts before they are introduced. it also obtained a longer period for examining these acts. i therefore voted in favour of this very technical report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the clinical trials regulation which replaces the previous 2001 directive. the old european legislation was outdated and the negative consequences were numerous, such as long approval periods, increased production costs, fewer applications for authorization and relocations. the text will harmonise the rules, giving researchers a clear and centralised authorisation procedure and making multinational clinical trials easier to set up.
in writing. although scientific research, particularly in the field of medicine, should be encouraged, it is nevertheless imperative that it should take specific precautions to avoid any practice which may amount to the commodification of human beings.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to amend the legislation on clinical trials of medicinal products for human use in order to strengthen public health while encouraging research. it is essential to promote clinical research in europe, in particular by simplifying and clarifying procedures. the competitiveness of clinical research in europe is thus being revived, whereas the number of clinical trials conducted in europe has been declining in recent years.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which allows member states to rely on a single text for assessing applications for authorisation of clinical trials. this increased transparency is part of the desire to protect participants by guaranteeing their free and informed consent. i also welcome the fact that a chapter on the protection of personal data is provided for in this regulation.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation, which includes concrete steps to facilitate the implementation of clinical trials of medicinal products for human use in europe while guaranteeing the rights of those involved in such research. it was essential to revise this 2001 directive because the complexity of the measures implementing a clinical trial has become such that investigators prefer to turn to other countries with more flexible regulations. the new rules will not only encourage the conduct of clinical trials on the medicinal product in europe through the administrative simplification introduced, but also ensure greater transparency of the trial results. simplified notification procedures will avoid researchers having to submit largely identical information on the proposed clinical trial to several bodies. a single application for authorisation for each national or multinational trial will be submitted on an eu portal by the sponsor and a rapporteur member state will be designated to assess the scientific and methodological aspects of the research. the new regulation will give european patients the assurance that they will be able to benefit from the best care and the latest medicines.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr glenis willmott, on clinical trials of medicinal products for human use. this text, to which i contributed as rapporteur for the epp group, is a major breakthrough for european clinical research, which was suffering the catastrophic consequences of a 2001 directive. with the explosion of costs and approval times, the number of applications for authorisation of clinical trials in the union has collapsed, in favour of the us and emerging countries. the report aims to restore the competitiveness of european clinical research while setting out transparency measures. the procedures for authorising clinical trials are thus harmonised and simplified, and ensure a rapid response. citizens will have access to a european database centralising information on clinical trials authorised in the european union. the sponsors of clinical trials will be required to publish summaries of the results of the trials carried out on this database. european clinical research will thus finally find its way back to competitiveness and will facilitate the rapid arrival of innovative treatments for patients on the market. i am glad that this report was adopted by a very large majority: 594 votes in favour, 17 against and 13 abstentions.
in writing. - the adoption of directive 2001/20/ec marked a major breakthrough in the development of standards for the conduct of clinical trials, both at european and international level. it is necessary to ensure that strict standards for patient care and care are maintained in the union, while promoting scientific research and innovation, through public access to data, in the form of a comprehensive clinical trial report. however, harmonisation and careful evaluation of the existing legal framework is necessary to avoid difficulties in promoting clinical trials in different member states.
in writing. on wednesday 2 april, i voted in favour of measures to simplify and make the legislative framework for clinical trials safer and more transparent. applications for authorisation for clinical trials will be simplified, with over 4[nbsp]400 applications being submitted each year in europe. we have set approval deadlines to avoid blocking clinical trials by administrative delays. we have also increased transparency and access to information through an internet portal where all test results, as well as marketing authorisations and market withdrawal decisions will have to be published. this is a particularly important step forward. finally, we have harmonised the rules on the authorisation and evaluation of clinical trials to facilitate the conduct of cross-border clinical trials. the new rules will support research in the field of rare diseases, for which there are insufficient patients in a single european country to initiate clinical trials in view of the costs generated. the measures adopted by the european parliament will save more than four billion euros between 2014 and 2020.
in writing. the report purports to strengthen scientific cooperation within the union and to increase knowledge in the field of public health. it starts from the observation of the fall of 25% of clinical trials in europe and the consequences of this brake in the search for medical treatments. the regulation aims to better define and regulate clinical trials and also to better protect and take into account patients who consent to participate in them. but once again, the economic and financial view prevails over research. the aim is therefore to reduce delays and simplify bureaucratic procedures, i.e. to increase the pace and to reduce posts. all this in order to reduce costs and bring back private developers who have gone to do their testing outside the eu. these same promoters give priority to cost-effective clinical trials, excluding those for rare diseases. in any case, the reduction in public research funding, linked to the austerity policy being pursued throughout europe, is not in any way in doubt. i'm not going to do it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which aims to revitalise clinical research in europe by facilitating the implementation of multinational trials through harmonisation of processes and coordination of evaluation mechanisms. in the trilogue negotiations, the european parliament succeeded in putting the patient back at the centre of this regulation. we have made real improvements to the text, including: ensuring transparency of the conduct and results of clinical trials by creating an eu internet portal, providing patients with good information, in particular on the potential risks of the clinical trial, and increasing protection measures for vulnerable people (children, the elderly, pregnant women, people with disabilities).
in writing. 4[nbsp ]400 applications for authorisation for clinical trials are submitted each year in the european union and the european economic area. the current directive should be replaced by a regulation in order to harmonise the rules and establish cooperation between member states. this harmonisation of rules will provide european researchers with a clear and centralised authorisation procedure with reduced approval times and a faster and simplified process in the end. in parallel, the text strengthens the transparency of clinical trials by making publicly available a european database for information on clinical trials authorised in the european union, whether their results are positive or negative. it is in this sense that i have supported this report which will make it possible to develop more transparent and competitive european clinical research.
in writing. following the fukushima nuclear disaster, there was a need to move towards a community framework for the safety of nuclear installations. finally, it seems necessary to emphasize the questions connected with the independence of the french authority for the supervision of nuclear installations.
in writing. i voted in favour of the jordan report which strengthens the community framework for the safety of nuclear installations. i voted in favour of the amendments to guarantee the independence of the national safety authorities to prevent the commission from overstepping its nuclear safety prerogatives. i regret that these amendments were rejected.
in writing. the fukushima accident has demonstrated the need for an effective community framework for the safety of nuclear installations. good cooperation between the european and national levels is essential to establish strong protection for citizens. it is essential to adopt a more preventive than reactive approach. we must be vigilant and ready to intervene in the event of an accident at nuclear installations. the independence of the regulatory authorities responsible for the assessment of nuclear safety is therefore crucial. this is the approach we wanted to support.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive, which aims to prevent radioactive discharges at all stages of the life cycle of nuclear installations. i also welcome the introduction of benchmarks and strict requirements to ensure the effective independence of the competent regulatory authorities. this is further evidence of transparency which i welcome.
in writing. i welcome the european parliament's vote on this report to improve nuclear safety in the european union after the fukushima disaster and the stress testing exercise for european nuclear power stations, which is a model at international level. provisions on the general organisation of nuclear safety, safety culture, the independence of national safety authorities and transparency are strengthened and new provisions on emergency preparedness and response are created. in addition, the creation of a european system of peer review of nuclear installations is to be welcomed. but in this particular case, it is important to ensure that the competences of ensreg as the body of the 28 european regulators are respected and to frame the role of the european commission in order to guarantee full independence of the national safety authorities.
in writing. i voted against this report which revises the european nuclear safety directive. the vote was an opportunity to send a strong signal to the commission and the member states: more safety, more safeguards to prevent a new fukushima in europe. it wasn't. the nuclear safety authorities (nsas) will still lack the necessary skills to prevent operators from taking unreasonable risks. nor will they have any real powers of sanction. in the end, this vote only reinforces our view of nuclear power as a closed environment, closed to any outside control and to any citizen's right to look.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague romana jordan on the community framework for nuclear safety. the proposal introduces new objectives of security and transparency at union level and promotes the exchange of best practice between member states. the text nevertheless proposes an increase in the european commission's remit, which blurs the chain of responsibility between the member states, the commission and the national safety authorities, which must remain independent if they are to remain the cornerstone of nuclear safety. the report was adopted by 438 votes to 154, with 37 abstentions. i am very pleased with this result.
in writing. - the safety of nuclear installations remains a priority for the european union and its institutions. however, as the report points out, there is a need to provide a community framework for the regulation of this matter which can be homogeneous and streamline the different national regulations. the nuclear policy is increasingly a policy which must concern us as the european union and therefore must be dealt with and administered by the union itself, while leaving the member states the prerogatives which they should have.
in writing. a rigorous and stable framework for nuclear safety at european level is necessary because the consequences of a nuclear accident extend far beyond national borders. in the face of such a challenge, strict measures must be taken. the first condition is an immediate ban on nuclear subcontracting. but this text is only vague measures of uncertain application. in many respects, he is sorely lacking in ambition. nuclear safety authorities must be able to impose real safety requirements on nuclear sites from the construction phase to dismantling. it's not. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the fact that the community is not able to meet its own needs. the race to extend the life of power stations in europe is a madness driven by productivist blindness and state misery. finally, it is no longer acceptable that nuclear issues should remain the sole responsibility of the european commission. i abstain in order not to oppose the few advances in this report, which is the result of a soft consensus with the nuclear operators!
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to amend council directive 2009/71/euratom establishing a community framework for the nuclear safety of nuclear installations with a view to improving nuclear safety and taking into account the lessons learned from the fukushima accident in japan. the new proposal strengthens the existing provisions of council directive 2009/71/euratom with the overall objective of continuously improving nuclear safety and related regulation at eu level.
in writing. france is one of the world leaders in civil nuclear energy. this technology also accounts for a major share of energy consumption in france. i am in favour of increased security around nuclear energy. it is necessary. but i'm against the complete suppression of technology. i am glad that i voted in favour of this report. we need a community framework for the safety of nuclear installations while preserving a certain degree of independence of the national safety authorities. this will enable us to prevent certain disasters and to respond more effectively to emergencies. we need to tame this technology to get the best out of it.
in writing. this report strengthens safety standards in some european nuclear power plants following the european exercise of stress tests carried out in plants in the european union and some neighbouring countries in the aftermath of the fukushima disaster. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. these evaluations will also be subject to union-wide peer reviews. i supported this report because it is important to guarantee the full independence of the national safety authorities and at the same time to strengthen the role of ensreg (european nuclear safety authorities group) in its role of coordinating the work of the national regulators in good cooperation with the european commission.
in writing. tax fraud and tax evasion in europe are phenomena against which the european union must fight relentlessly. it was important to approve such a text which aims to put an end, in particular, to the double non-taxation, which results from certain hybrid financial schemes, for certain companies. we cannot allow this phenomenon to generate unfair competition in europe and a loss of revenue for the member states. therefore, clear tax rules on the distribution of profits between member states should be established. the tax exemption for european companies on distributed profits must therefore be better regulated.
in writing. the proposal under consideration aims to address the issue of hybrid financial arrangements within the scope of the 'parent-subsidiary' (pmd) directive. the rapporteur proposes to strengthen the definition of a parent company: extending the duration and increasing the minimum shareholding held by the parent company in the capital of a subsidiary established in another member state will thus prevent multinationals from making illicit profits. the report also promotes an anti-abuse rule under which all member states will be required to ignore tax advantages arising from artificial arrangements or arrangements which have no commercial justification and do not reflect economic reality. all these good intentions are unfortunately in conflict with the reality of fiscal dumping in the european union, which is being promoted by the commission. i abstain in order to encourage these efforts without any illusions about their application.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to address the issue of hybrid financial arrangements within the scope of directive 2011/96/eu (mff) and to replace the current anti-abuse provision with a common anti-abuse rule, based on the similar provision in the recommendation on aggressive tax planning. in order to avoid situations of double non-taxation arising from the asymmetry of the tax treatment applied to distributions of profits between member states, that directive provides that the member state of the parent company or that of its permanent establishment should not grant to those undertakings tax exemption on the distributed profits received in so far as they are deductible by the subsidiary of the parent company.
in writing. the stockholm programme sets out the european union's priorities for the area of freedom, security and justice for the period 2010-2014. however, it is now coming to an end, and a new strategic vision is needed to define the long-term orientations of justice and home affairs policies up to 2020. that is the subject of this report. i supported the main points in this report, including eu accession to the echr, improved access to documents, the extension of the powers of the european public prosecutor's office to crossborder crime, the strengthening of eurojust, the reform of frontex, cooperation with third countries on freedom, security and justice. i voted in favour of the report on the final vote.
in writing. this mid-term review of the stockholm programme provided an opportunity to present the main developments since the adoption of the lisbon treaty, including the recognition of the legally binding nature of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, the increased participation of national parliaments in the activities of the union, and the fact that even in the absence of agreement on a uniform electoral procedure for european elections, a gradual convergence of electoral systems has taken place. i welcome the adoption of the regulation on the european citizens' initiative which gives citizens the same powers of political initiative as those already enjoyed by the european parliament and the council and also note that the stockholm programme aims to facilitate the free movement of citizens and residents of the union by defending and respecting all the rights and obligations arising from a european area of justice, while noting that judicial cooperation is the main tool to achieve this objective.
in writing. this paper examines the stockholm programme, which is the european union's roadmap for policies relating to the area of freedom, security and justice for the period 2014-2020. although he makes an interesting assessment of this programme, i preferred to abstain when voting on this text. the text contained too many unacceptable provisions, in particular on the mutual recognition of civil status documents in europe, which i oppose. the european union must respect the competences of the member states. the text also condemns any attempt to restrict the free movement of persons in europe. again, i do not support such claims. i am, on the contrary, in favour of a debate on the framework for the free movement of persons in europe, in particular to put an end to the risk of social dumping.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleagues luigi berlinguer, juan fernando lopez aguilar and carlo casini on the mid-term review of the stockholm programme. this programme, which was intended to set out the union's priorities in the area of freedom, security and justice for the period 2010-2014, had not been examined by the european commission as it should have been, leading to this examination by parliament, in order to draw lessons from this programme and to lay the foundations for the next one for the period 2014-2020. the report was adopted by 367 votes to 85, with 29 abstentions. i welcome the outcome of this vote.
in writing. this report on the justice, freedom and security programme makes interesting findings but omits the sensitive points of this policy. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data, in particular by introducing a new data protection directive. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. i take note of these paradoxical positions and i shall vote against this text.
in writing. this own-initiative report deals with the stockholm programme an open and secure europe at the service of citizens. it aims to set the framework for police and customs cooperation, civil protection, judicial cooperation in criminal and civil matters, asylum and migration matters and visa policy for the years 2010 to 2014 in the european union. this report is a disappointing compromise that is sorely lacking in ambition. i therefore abstained from voting on this report.
in writing. i voted for this report. four years after its adoption and a few months before the european council next june defines the new post-stockholm programme for the period 2014-2020, the european parliament is reviewing the progress made and the guidelines it wants to see developed for the future. the report considers that some areas of the area of freedom, security and justice require additional efforts, particularly in terms of implementation and more uniform application. in this report, parliament regrets the lack of an objective assessment of the progress made.
in writing. i abstained on the european parliament's report on the mid-term review of the stockholm programme because it is, in many respects, disappointing to say the least. apart from the fact that, contrary to what the title suggests, we are not at the halfway point of the stockholm programme but at its end, the content of this report falls far short of what one might expect from the european parliament. this report could have been an opportunity to take a real stock of the policies on justice, security and freedom and to draw constructive criticism from them in order to give the next guidelines the right course to follow, but there is no question of that. the report has been deconstructed by the right wing of this house, but it is regrettable that the majority of my colleagues have not been able to oppose this approach. this is not surprising, but it is not encouraging for the fundamental rights of individuals, which, again, are not the priority in this area. if the union is an area of security, it is certainly not yet an area of justice, and we still have a long way to go before it can become one.
in writing. this text amends the legislation establishing a community system of controls on exports, transfers, brokering and transit of dual-use goods. delegated powers are then given to the european commission to enable it to adapt more rapidly to developments in international export control regimes. i support the rationalization of the procedures applied in the european system of such export controls in order to increase their efficiency.
in writing. dual-use goods are products, including software and technology, which can be intended for both civilian and military use. they can thus enter the non-proliferation policy. any export of dual-use goods from the european union (eu) to a third country requires an export authorisation. the proposal aims to align the regulation with the lisbon treaty and to introduce delegated acts for updating annex i (list of controlled goods) and amending annex ii (general export authorisation from the union for 6 types of lower risk exports and to certain destinations). i am opposed to this extension of the commission's powers. i object to this alienation of france's sovereignty. in this order of decision, independence alone guarantees sovereignty in the choice of alliances. but under rule 97 of the rules of procedure of the european parliament, this text is deemed to have been adopted without the opinion of the members being sought. otherwise i would have voted against it.
in writing. i supported this report which amends council regulation (ec) no 428/2009 establishing a community regime for the control of exports, transfer, brokering and transit of dual-use goods. the purpose of this regulation is to ensure regular and timely updates of the union watch list, in compliance with the obligations and commitments entered into by the member states under international export control regimes. it will also allow the union to react quickly to changing circumstances concerning the assessment of the sensitivity of exports subject to union general export authorisations.
in writing. the proposal for a directive aims to establish a system for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading in the european union with a view to the implementation by 2020 of an international convention applying a global market mechanism to international aviation emissions. in other words, the objective is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the aviation sector. the challenge is to succeed in acting on a global scale. but to convince our partners, we must first act at european level. i therefore supported the agreement reached in the trilogue to limit the application to intra-eu flights for the time being. i'm pleased that an agreement has been reached. we must now succeed in acting on a global scale.
in writing. it has been brought to our attention that although the eu ets applies only to intra-european flights, some member states now seem reluctant to implement the legislation. third countries, such as china and india, refuse to refund quotas for flights to europe, for example between frankfurt and london. we considered it unacceptable to enter into discussions with the council on the results of a legislative proposal before the very limited suspensive legislation has been clearly applied. we cannot accept that third countries, such as china or india, refuse to comply with european legislation when they operate flights within the european union. we believe that it is necessary to reach agreement on an amendment to the directive and we are ready to discuss it with all the stakeholders.
in writing. this vote represents a minimal compromise by the most polluting countries on our climate policies. parliament has endorsed a compromise limiting the coverage of the european emissions trading system to intra-european flights only. by accepting this dossier, the european union has shown its weakness in relation to major powers such as china and the united states in terms of environmental legislation.
in writing. by voting on this text, the european parliament gave its opinion on the application of the greenhouse gas emission allowance trading mechanism in the field of aviation. intercontinental flights are rightly excluded from the scope of the european greenhouse gas emissions trading scheme until 2016. by limiting this mechanism to intra-european flights, we want to facilitate the conclusion of an international agreement on co2 emission reductions in the field of aviation. in this compromise we are adopting a balanced position between respect for the environment and the competitiveness of the air transport sector.
in writing. i voted in favour of an amendment to this report which would exclude flights outside the european union from the scope of this mechanism until 2016. in line with recent commitments made to the international civil aviation organisation, such a measure is intended to facilitate the conclusion of a global agreement on the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from aviation. the text as amended must therefore be able to protect the climate while preserving the competitiveness of our airlines. it also excludes flights between the union and its outermost regions from the scope of the emissions trading scheme. in these latter countries, the airplane is often the only means of transport and helps to facilitate the mobility of the inhabitants.
in writing. i voted in favour of the agreement reached with the council on the application of the carbon tax until 2016 only to flights between airports in the european economic area. indeed, i believe that a rejection of this agreement is not satisfactory because it would only provide arguments to encourage some states not to commit to an international agreement on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and would send the wrong signal to key partners such as the united states, china, india or brazil to reach an ambitious agreement at the 21st un climate change conference in paris in 2015.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague peter liese on the trading of greenhouse gas emission allowances for international aviation. the main question was whether international flights should be subject to the ets, at the risk of starting a trade war with china or russia, or whether it was better to exclude them from the ets until the international civil aviation organization meets in 2016 and adopts comprehensive measures to combat greenhouse gases. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a new regulation on the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the report was adopted by 458 votes to 120, with 24 abstentions. i am very pleased with this result.
in writing. reducing greenhouse gas emissions from civil aviation is unavoidable and necessary. the european union is showing by this text that it is absolutely not up to the challenge. it is ideologically committed to the principles of the carbon market and has given up any ecological ambition. the report also shows a glaring setback in european environmental ambitions: it celebrates the capitulation of the european union on the international scene. in the name of waiting for an international agreement, the union is increasing the number of derogations for international flights. instead of being a power that firmly imposes its principles of combating global warming, it is entering into a game of compromise with powers that have not been very prominent in recent years in the fight for environmental protection, especially the united states. i am firmly opposed to the principle of a carbon market and i am in favour of an eco-socialist policy which would involve ecological planning, in particular for the development of alternative transport solutions, in international aviation. this ecological planning is not compatible with the liberal and austerity policy of the european union which is reflected in this text.
in writing. this report focuses on the inclusion of civil aviation in the european emissions trading system. it validates a compromise reached between the european institutions which provides for the exclusion of flights to and from third countries from the application of the european carbon tax until 2016, pending an international agreement on the application of an emission trading scheme to civil aviation. it also excludes flights to and from the outermost regions of the union. until now, flights to third countries were excluded, but those to the outermost regions were subject to the carbon tax. of course, this system was particularly penalising for the ors which were in an unfavourable competitive situation vis-à-vis their neighbours. the report therefore proposes to restore a level playing field between the ors and their neighbouring third countries. i therefore supported this report which calls for the exclusion of the ors from the european greenhouse gas emission allowance trading system, as long as third countries are not subject to it.
in writing. i supported the trialogue agreement. the non-application of the aviation carbon tax to intercontinental flights is an important concession by the european union to third countries such as china, the united states, russia and india. this respite will allow them to devote their time to the development of a global agreement within the international civil aviation organisation (icao). by 2016, we must all work towards a market mechanism to regulate aviation emissions globally.
in writing. i voted in favour of the co2 tax on air travel within the european economic area. the text excluded intercontinental flights until 2016. this was one of the sine qua non conditions for china, the united states and russia to agree to develop a global agreement within the international civil aviation organization (icao), scheduled to be concluded in 2016. it is a last chance for these countries to adapt. if there is no agreement in 2016, we will not accept the continuation of such an exemption. i also welcome the exclusion of flights to the outermost regions (ors) from the scope of the directive. indeed, today the full application of the carbon tax to airlines operating in the ors would mechanically increase the cost of air tickets for passengers to and from these regions. this increases the handicap of remoteness suffered by the rup by unfairly penalising passengers, but also the flow of perishable goods.
in writing. this draft regulation, combined with the revision of the payment services directive, aims to create common rules for interchange fees, i.e. charges related to the use of bank cards. the aim here is to introduce ceilings and to improve the transparency of these charges. i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation, which improves consumer protection.
in writing. i voted in favour of the zalba bidegain report on interchange fees for card-related transactions. these are fees which have been monitored by competition authorities since 1984 in europe to ensure a fair balance between the financing of these commercial fees and consumer protection. the aim of this report is to bring the different committees in all the member states into line and eventually to abolish them. i have spoken in favour of a balanced relationship of transparency and consistency between banks and consumers. i want an economic justification for the amounts withdrawn by the banks.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which provides for a cap on interchange fees for debit and credit card payments. this cap will allow for more transparency in payments and lower prices for consumers within the internal market
in writing. this text lays down common rules on interbank commissions. they are generally applied between the acquiring payment service providers and card issuers belonging to a given card scheme (for example, between a customer's bank and the merchant's bank). the european parliament has adopted a strong position in this vote with a view to negotiations with the other institutions of the european union. in particular, it shall set ceilings for these interchange fees. i strongly support this text, which is precisely intended to facilitate card payments within the union, particularly when a citizen is in another member state.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr pablo zalba bidegain, on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions. the report aims to establish common rules on interchange fees in the european union by placing a ceiling on them for transactions carried out using payment cards. it also proposes measures to enable retailers and consumers to make better choices about their payment instruments. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. the proposed regulation aims to improve the functioning of the internal market for card payments. one of the main obstacles to card payments is the widespread existence of interchange fees. interchange fees are interbank fees charged between acquiring banks and card issuers. they constitute a significant part of the fees charged to merchants for each card transaction. merchants, in turn, pass on these card-related costs in the price of their goods and services. in practice, competition between card schemes aims to convince the largest number of payment service providers to choose their cards, which generally leads to higher costs (advertising, ancillary benefit, etc.). the regulation sets the rates applicable to payment service providers, with ceilings of 0.2% and 0.3% of the value of the transaction. in fact, it is a private consumption tax. the aim is therefore to tackle (somewhat) the profits of the banks in order to reduce the cost to consumers. i vote for it.
in writing. this is a regulation concerning the fees charged for each card payment, known as interchange fees. these fees are paid by the merchant's bank to the cardholder's bank for each transaction. the level of fees varies considerably between member states and between different types of cards. each year, 9 billion euros in interchange fees are paid in the european union. interchange fees are not the subject of specific legislation in most member states. the regulation is in fact based on the competition case law between the commission and mastercard and visa europe. the level of interchange fee caps proposed by the commission (0.2% for debit cards and 0.3% for credit cards) is the result of an agreement concluded following a competition case involving these companies. this report is a real step forward in the fight against excessive bank charges and will be of particular benefit to consumers and small traders. i gave him my support accordingly.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to establish common rules on interchange fees in the european union, by capping them for transactions made using payment cards which are widely used by consumers. it also provides for transparency measures to ensure that retailers and consumers can make informed choices about their payment instruments.
in writing. with this text, we are planning the establishment of an integrated payments market. in other words, the aim is to remove barriers to competition in the area of card and internet payments. this is to improve the interoperability of card, internet and mobile payment systems. but it is also a higher level of security and transparency of payments achieved. by voting for these amendments we are therefore in favour of diversifying the means of making immediate payments in a more secure way.
in writing. i voted in favour of my colleague diogo feio's report on payment services in the internal market, which proposes the implementation of a more transparent, innovative and secure european legal framework. this is because significant parts of the payments market remain partitioned along national borders, which hampers the development of innovative digital payment services and deprives consumers and retailers of convenient and secure payment solutions. the main aims of the proposal are to ensure a level playing field, to facilitate the provision of innovative crossborder card payment services, to align pricing practices and to better protect consumers' interests. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. the proposal aims to repeal the current payment services directive (psd). the aim is to extend the scope of this directive in order to improve the functioning of the internal market for payment services. by facilitating transactions within the eu, the commission hopes to boost growth. low consumption has little to do with means of payment but with the income available to individuals. the directive will nevertheless make it possible to support the fight against money laundering by means of increased supervision of payment institutions. i am voting with a little enthusiasm to encourage this.
in writing. the objective of this regulation is to deepen the single market for electronic communications. it should therefore enable european citizens and businesses to benefit more widely from communication services, without cross-border restrictions or unjustified additional costs. in other words, we are putting an end to roaming charges: consumers will not pay more when they make calls or send messages from another eu country. this is a huge step forward for consumer rights! i also wanted to make clear in this text the principle of net neutrality, which means that an internet service provider cannot discriminate or interfere with traffic based on user activity. this is a fundamental principle which we must defend at european level. the final text, which meets these requirements, i voted for.
in writing. the single market for electronic communications is at the heart of the digital economy. in order to enable europe to fully exploit the potential of the digital single market for growth, competitiveness and employment, the role of telecommunications in promoting innovation and connectivity in all sectors of the economy should be strengthened. after three regulations over a period of six years, we have finally proposed to abolish roaming surcharges for voice, sms and data calls. the commission notes that the measure is not intended to create a new legal obligation for operators to provide the services of a service provider in the union.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the telecoms package, which abolishes roaming charges for mobile communications from december 2015. this is a real breakthrough for european consumers. the european union is moving towards a single digital communications market. this market will enable individuals and businesses to access electronic communications services, regardless of where those services are provided in the union, without cross-border restrictions or unjustified additional costs. as for companies providing electronic communications networks and services, they will be able to operate their networks and provide their services regardless of their place of establishment or the geographical location of their customers in the european union. as regards net neutrality, i support an open definition that offers consumers a quality access service and allows the development of innovative offers.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the net neutrality part of the telecoms package and welcome the european parliament's rewriting of the commission's original text. in its initial proposal, the european commission wanted to regulate the preferential treatment that operators can offer to certain services, while guaranteeing the quality of the basic service. it was the door to differentiated internet access offers, to an internet controlled by internet service providers who themselves became content providers. with this text, the principle of net neutrality becomes explicit, general and binding. let us hope that the council will take its responsibilities and support this text which protects the fundamental rights of our citizens and supports our innovative smes against the gargantuan appetites of the large american multinationals.
in writing. the adoption of this text is a major step towards a single european market for electronic communications, whereas the current market still appears to be too fragmented. the telecommunications market is a source of considerable potential competitiveness. it is estimated that the single market for business communication services could generate profits of almost €90 billion per year. i therefore welcome the adoption of this text which lays down the principles necessary for the completion of this market. the abolition of roaming charges is one of the major successes of this text. consumers will then be able to move around europe without incurring additional charges for calls, messages and mobile internet. another important point concerns the neutrality of the internet, which is then enshrined in this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation, the general objective of which is to move towards a single market for electronic communications, putting an end to the fragmentation which currently exists in the union. i am pleased that the proposal also ensures the harmonisation of virtual access to fixed networks. this will facilitate market entry and cross-border service provision.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report and i welcome the european parliament's willingness to reject any obstacles to net neutrality. it's a victory for public and digital freedoms! we, the meps, rejected the idea of a multi-speed internet, which would no longer be open and accessible to all. the conservatives' plan was to make the quality of internet access and its content dependent on commercial agreements between internet service providers and service giants. this vote is a first step towards the final inclusion of digital freedoms and the protection of net neutrality as inalienable and unalterable rights in europe.
in writing. i supported this report because, thanks to the efforts of the socialists, we have managed to keep the principle of net neutrality intact. the european parliament's position, which the council is therefore called upon to join, is that internet service providers should not be able to block or slow down access to websites they dislike, or to give preferential treatment to one over the other. we also introduced a definition which guarantees all users permanent access to the content of their choice and adequate connection speed. these are essential elements for consumers and small telecom companies alike and this reform should encourage investment and job creation. another important element in favour of this text is the fixing of a date for the end of all roaming costs by december 2015. we want to make sure that no more citizens turn off their mobile phones abroad for fear of an exorbitant bill. the internet should remain a public space where everyone can access a service or application of their choice, without restriction or limitation.
in writing. while the european union has many flaws and imperfections, we can be happy about the concrete progress that citizens are not aware of, such as the abolition of roaming charges from december 2015. from that year onwards, when a citizen crosses the border, he will no longer be affected by surcharges on his calls, sms and data exchanges. it will be able to travel and make calls throughout europe without fear of overcharging. as regards net neutrality, which i strongly support, i regret the approach taken by the european parliament, which risks stifling innovation in the field of communications. too much regulation and supervision can sometimes be counterproductive. by strictly limiting the rights of operators to intervene in the network when we do not have a complete and precise control of the issue, we risk ultimately affecting the rights of consumers, which is the very opposite of what was intended.
in writing. i supported the report on the single market for electronic communications as it is a fundamental step forward in this field, which is still marked by the fragmentation of national markets. the text will improve the daily lives of european citizens: elimination of roaming surcharges (calls, messages or mobile internet use) by the end of 2015, facilitation of the development of very high-speed internet, etc. these are concrete steps forward that are essential for the citizens of europe. the text adopted, however, lacks coherence in terms of net neutrality. i defend the principle of net neutrality, understood as the absence of discrimination in the treatment of traffic regardless of the sender, receiver, service, etc. however, this principle should not jeopardise the existence and future development of specialised services (e.g. telemedicine, videoconferencing, etc.) which require flow management. the overly restrictive framework for these specialised services is contrary to innovation and the interests of consumers. unfortunately, the wording adopted in the adoption of the socialist and liberal amendments in this respect does not ensure the necessary articulation between the recognition of net neutrality and the preservation of the existence and development of specialised services.
in writing. defending freedom and neutrality on the internet i voted, together with my colleagues, for the texts in the european parliament aimed at defending freedom and in particular neutrality on the internet. i felt it was my duty to preserve this rare space of freedom of expression in the face of the, at least, suspicious demands of certain lobbies of telecom operators and their pro-european allies in the committee on industry. it is very important to affirm our principles in defence of our freedoms in the face of the abuses that have been observed across the atlantic and around the world, both in the scandals connected with the widespread surveillance of citizens and public actors and in the dangerous collusion between multinational companies.
in writing. the report aims to complete the 'single telecommunications market', i.e. to allow for further liberalisation of the telecommunications sector. the rapporteur nevertheless proposes some measures which will have a beneficial effect on consumers, such as the abolition of roaming charges. at the same time, however, it rejects the regulation of international calls proposed by the commission on the grounds that this market is deregulated and therefore competitive. the report is aimed at promoting 'effective competition in retail markets'. finally, the question of net neutrality, i.e. the exclusion of any discrimination as regards the source, destination or content of information transmitted over the network, would have been absent without the amendments tabled by my group. i am voting for it in order to support the progress we have succeeded in making.

in writing. public interest entities (pis) are entities that are of significant public interest because of their field of activity, size or number of employees. the proposed text aims to reform the audit procedures of these entities. the initial aim was to improve the quality of these audits by ensuring the independence of the auditors, but the compromise between the institutions concerned (trilogue) falls far short of the requirements set by parliament. the obligation to change auditors every 10 years was thus circumvented to allow for the renewal of this period and its extension to 14 years. in short, this text, which is supposed to tighten up the rules, does not. i vote against it.

in writing. the report on 'the union's global approach and its impact on the coherence of the union's external action' is parliament's response to the joint communication (commission and high representative/vice-president) to the european parliament and the council on the union's global approach to external action. this report, prepared by my colleague arnaud danjean, deplores the fact that the potential of the new post of high representative/vice-president of the commission created by the lisbon treaty has not been fully exploited and calls, in particular, for the role of the holder as vice-president of the commission to be effectively strengthened. the report also notes that in future the union should develop strategies in the regions in difficulty before engaging on the ground (unlike the strategy for the horn of africa, which was defined ex post). i fully share these analyses and have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. we believe that important geostrategic changes are underway in other parts of the world, including the emergence of a multipolar international scene characterised by the presence of new actors with competing regional and global ambitions, as well as increasing interdependence; the rise of multidimensional and asymmetric threats; the reorientation of us security policy towards the asia-pacific region; the growing struggle for energy and resource security; the increasingly severe consequences of climate change; and a severe and protracted global economic and financial crisis from which no eu member state is escaping. the strength of the european union therefore lies in its ability to mobilise resources across the full range of instruments at its disposal in the fields of diplomacy, security, defence, economy, trade, development and humanitarian aid - in full compliance with the provisions of the united nations charter - and that the use of these instruments within a comprehensive approach gives it unrivalled flexibility to deal effectively with the most difficult international issues and to achieve its own strategic objectives.
in writing. the union, if it is to assume its role as a major diplomatic and military power, cannot afford to be a blunder. the absence of a european presence in mali in the early stages of the conflict and the reservations of our partners about intervening in the central african republic prove that the copy in the field of foreign policy must be urgently revised. the european union has the tools to play its role as a power in conflict zones and in the rest of the world: diplomatic, military, humanitarian, trade and development instruments. but it is undeniable, in the light of recent events in africa, that it suffers from unpreparedness and an unfinished strategy. if we want the eu's overall approach to foreign policy to work, it is imperative that we review our strategies upstream so as not to leave room for fumbling once they are put to the test on the ground. coordination between member states is therefore essential and this role belongs to the high representative whose potential is not fully exploited. however, without genuine political will on the part of the member states to develop european defence, it is likely that we will see a strengthening of the eu in this area.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which stresses the need for the european union to have a comprehensive approach to its foreign policy in order to respond as effectively and as quickly as possible to the challenges of today's world. it is crucial to increase coordination between the relevant european institutions and to foster the development of strategies for effective anticipation and construction of the european foreign policy response. the lack of coordination and cooperation undermines both the content and the coherence of this policy. but we must also be realistic: an effective european foreign policy can only be built on the basis of a real political will, both in terms of objectives and means.

in writing. the european parliament adopted by 386 votes to 228 with 17 abstentions my two reports on electronic identification of bovine animals and simplification of optional beef labelling. one of the key issues in these reports is to have a common technology for all european farmers who voluntarily undertake the electronic identification of their cattle. on the labelling side, we are simplifying the rules for voluntary labelling, i.e. marketing labelling, so that farmers can better communicate the qualities of their meat. i am very pleased with this positive outcome after almost two years of legislative and field work.
in writing. this text will improve the efficiency and speed of beef traceability. this modernisation of identification is a fundamental step forward in strengthening consumer confidence. i fully support this text, which is in line with my commitment to mandatory meat labelling within the european union. i particularly welcome the need for compliance with iso standards, which will enable the union to develop its trade internationally and thus to access new markets.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation, which considers that competitiveness in the beef and veal sector must be preserved and encouraged. i welcome the fact that this text can contribute to improving animal and public health through a faster and more accurate system of tracing cattle. while food scandals around meat labelling and origin have been common in recent months, i very much hope that this report will increase transparency in this area.
in writing. the european parliament adopted today, in plenary session, the report on electronic identification of bovine animals. following negotiations with the council and the commission, the provisions on voluntary labelling of beef and veal are to be abolished. i voted against this report, as did my group, the greens/efa. the main reason why we voted against this text is the abolition of the current system of prior approval for voluntary beef labelling. under the pretext of administrative burdens, there will henceforth be no more control by the authorities over this voluntary labelling, which is crucial for informing consumers about quality aspects, such as rearing conditions or animal feeding.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague sophie auconie on the electronic identification of bovine animals and the labelling of beef. the report aims to amend the current identification system by providing for the optional introduction of electronic identification of bovine animals in order to strengthen food safety and the protection of animal health in the union, promote the competitiveness of the sector and simplify procedures relating to animal passports and farm registers. the report also proposes to harmonise the labelling practices. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. parliament adopted on 2 april the report on the electronic identification of bovine animals. the report aims to adopt a common technology for all european farmers who voluntarily undertake the electronic identification of their cattle. as the technology in this field is developing rapidly and its use is becoming more widespread, it is necessary to adapt the legislation in order to recognise electronic identification of bovine animals as an official means of identifying those animals. this technology has a wide range of benefits for its users, particularly in terms of traceability and herd management. however, electronic identification should remain optional in order to avoid excessive financial burdens for small producers. while i have been committed for several months to better labelling of the origin of meat, i voted in favour of this measure which will allow for more precise traceability of animals and thus guarantee better consumer protection.
in writing. the text aims to introduce electronic bovine identification (eid) on a voluntary basis and to simplify the rules on voluntary beef labelling. the aim is to improve the traceability of cattle while ensuring that farmers are not burdened with administrative burdens. however, the issue of labelling cloned animals, which is being called for by parliament and ignored by other eu bodies, remains open. this is problematic, especially since the text also aims to give the commission new powers in this area (delegated and implementing acts) under the lisbon treaty. for these reasons i am voting against.
in writing. i voted in favour of the agreement reached in the trilogue on this regulation. the latter will amend the current system by providing for the optional introduction of electronic identification of bovine animals, while allowing each member state to make it compulsory on its territory. this electronic identification system will make it possible to improve the traceability of animals and meat and thus offer greater food safety to consumers. the aim is also to reduce current administrative procedures, which will bring many benefits to the sector: competitiveness, faster controls, better outlets and reduced labour costs.
in writing. food safety must be guaranteed within the european union. this is why all measures to increase food protection must be supported. the case of beef was a clear example of food insecurity during the 1997 bovine spongiform encephalopathy crisis. we cannot go back to a situation where many cattle in the union are contaminated. electronic identification will provide more reliable data and will enhance traceability and thus food safety. i am glad that i voted in favour of this report. it supports the adaptation of existing legislation to harmonise technical standards for electronic identification and proposes a voluntary approach to the introduction of this technology.
in writing. i voted against this report by the french udi sophie auconie. whereas until now only ear tags have been considered as an official means of identification to ensure traceability of cattle, making electronic identification compulsory and creating a single labelling system within the european union could increase the traceability of beef and thus facilitate consumer information while facilitating the work of farmers. unfortunately, after months of negotiations, the proposals are not satisfactory, particularly as regards the labelling of beef from cloned animals and their offspring. while a large part of the political groups in the european parliament (s&d, greens and gue/ngl) strongly demanded this measure, no guarantees were given in this respect and the rapporteur, followed by the majority of the parliament, chose to conclude an agreement without taking this requirement into account. not requiring the traceability of cloned animals and their descendants is not the best way to guarantee the food security of european citizens, quite the contrary.

in writing. the budget of the european centre for the development of vocational training is also being cut as the budget allocated to it by the european union is being reduced. this means that the body is forced to seek an increasing share of private own resources, which may be at the expense of its independence, which is vital in vocational training and certification. i vote against this austerity drive. parliament's budgetary discharge should enable it to enforce budgetary commitments on all the european institutions and agencies. but the commission and the council take virtually no account of parliament's votes, even when it refuses discharge. because that year the commission and the council managed to put 1 billion surpluses in reserve and carry them forward, whereas the eu had accumulated 16 billion unpaid. this savage application of austerity is unacceptable and absurd.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which accepts to grant the director of the centre discharge in respect of the implementation of its budget for the financial year 2012. noting that the court of auditors had indicated that it had obtained reasonable assurance that the centre's annual accounts for the financial year 2012 were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular, we approve the closure of cedefop's accounts. we do, however, make a number of recommendations which must be taken into account when the discharge is given, in addition to the general recommendations in the draft resolution concerning the performance, financial management and control of the agencies.

in writing. this text reflects parliament's approval of the commission's new legislative framework for the fight against fraud and sets out the complementary proposals. it called for concerted and joint action by the commission and the member states in support of the european anti-fraud office in the fight against fraud affecting the union's financial interests. it is particularly well thought out to propose a computerised system for the circulation and control of products subject to a single excise duty. in short, the text takes stock of the constant increase in crossborder flows - and therefore of new risks - by referring to the introduction of common measures within the union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this realistic report which stresses the need to continue the efforts made in the fight to protect the financial interests of the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague ines ayala sender on the annual report (2012) on the protection of the european union's financial interests and the fight against fraud. this report examines the evolution of the number of fraudulent and non-fraudulent irregularities reported and their financial implications in various areas of union action. it welcomed the positive results of the vat reform launched in 2011 and called for greater efforts to assess the performance of national revenue collection systems. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. - the protection of the union's financial interests is a key element of the eu's programming agenda to consolidate and strengthen citizens' trust and to ensure the proper use of their money. in order to protect the financial interests of the union and its citizens, an integrated approach is necessary, including strategies to combat fraud and corruption through effective, consistent and equivalent legal actions throughout the union. close cooperation with member states is therefore essential, especially in this period of financial austerity, in order to ensure adequate protection against fraud.
in writing. this report seems to be a good initiative in the fight against tax evasion. but he finally appears as a masquerade. how can anyone seriously claim to be fighting tax evasion without addressing the subject of tax havens? nor does the report contain a line on tax dumping. the report also calls on the european anti-fraud office (olaf) to communicate its findings to parliament better, whereas the main problem with this office is its total submission to the commission. finally, the commission shows the extent of its hypocrisy by asking the services to improve the collection of customs duties when the single transatlantic market would remove a major part of customs duties. the free movement of capital promoted by the european union contributes more to the development of fraud. i therefore abstained on this text in order not to endorse these mechanical bearing without consequences.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report which notes that in 2012 non-fraudulent irregularities reported to the commission increased by around 6% compared to 2011, with a financial impact of around eur 2.9 billion (more than double the figure for 2011, notably in the areas of cohesion policy and direct expenditure). we note with concern that this increase mainly reflects the effect of irregularities involving large amounts, but is also due to systemic irregularities reported at the closure of programmes.
