mr president, it so happens that when the interpretation of article 50 was included in our rules of procedure, it was a case like the one we have today. that is to say, a case where the committee on employment and social affairs had exclusive competence and shared competence with the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs. following this conflict, the committee responsible for interpreting the regulation added the interpretation which is now contained in the current rule 50, according to which, where the committee on the substance has flouted or disregarded the powers of the committee having exclusive competence over another party, the second committee - in this case the committee on employment and social affairs - may table its amendment in plenary. but it only makes sense if this amendment can be voted on. the interpretation you are now giving to the rules prohibits the committee on employment and social affairs from exercising this right. and it is in this sense, i believe, that the speech of my group's chairman should be heard and the voting list corrected.
mr president, we cannot be complicit in the sham, because this report is there as if to relieve the majority groups of the historic opportunity they had to assert the powers of parliament vis-à-vis the council, in accordance with the prerogatives provided for by the lisbon treaty. how many times have we not heard that parliament has a veto, that this budget is bad and that parliament will stand by it. we know what happened in the end: this budget was approved, albeit with some marginal concessions. if parliament had stood its ground, we would not have had this kind of debate and this kind of resolution.
madam president, commissioner, mr president of the council, i am pleased to note, as most of us here are - with the exception of a few minor dissonant notes - that we have succeeded in bringing to fruition the commission's courageous proposals, which you, commissioner, have put forward with great determination. this work by the parliament and the council reflects a genuine political will to achieve greater efficiency in the economic action of the european union. the efforts of all those who have helped to get these texts ready before the end of this parliamentary term and who have managed to respect an ambitious timetable in a very difficult economic context should be commended. we have succeeded in finalising, during this mandate, the pillars of banking union, namely the banking supervision mechanism, the resolution system with a single resolution fund and the deposit guarantee mechanism. the ultimate aim of all these texts is to restore the confidence of european citizens in the banking system and to protect them against the risks of bank runs. they are the culmination of all the parliamentary work carried out under this mandate on financial regulation, which should help to keep the financial system in check, avoid the emergence of new systemic crises and put finance and banks at the service of the economy. we have succeeded in overcoming our differences on the broad or narrow conception of european supervision, or on the system of pooling deposit guarantee. all this is the result of a collective will, for most of us, to find better solutions, and you, commissioner, have played a large part in this. today's debate is, if i may say so, the icing on the cake of an exemplary regulatory activity.
madam president, mr president of the council, mr commissioner, at a time when the european union is experiencing an excess of unemployment with 26 million unemployed, it is time to tackle the banking excesses which have led to an unbearable state of public finances. i am glad that we adopted these absolutely major aspects of the three-pillar banking union at this session. first of all, i would like to congratulate my colleague mr hökmark on his report, which sets out the procedure to be followed when a banking institution is in difficulty and has to restructure its activities. the aim is simple: to ensure that european taxpayers and savers are no longer on the front line to rescue banks in difficulty, as of 1 january 2016. the shareholders and creditors will be the first to bear the losses incurred by the banks. the adoption of my colleague peter simon's report will now bring the deposit protection regime into line. in the event of bank failures, eu citizens will be able to recover up to €100,000 of their savings within seven days. it is a promise that has been kept for a long time, and it is now a reality. last but not least, the report by my colleague elisa ferreira. this is where we really get into trouble. it has been a battle for months and i welcome the support and the dynamism that my political group has brought to this debate. we have thus demonstrated that there is a european dimension which makes it possible to go beyond the approaches of certain member states, to have a real banking union, to destroy the pernicious link between bank debt and public finances. it's a real innovation, and it's finally allowing us to get some investment going. i would like to thank the commission for allowing us to tackle the real issue that concerns our citizens: investment that creates jobs.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this regulation, which is one of the major pillars of banking union, drawing lessons from the crisis and ensuring that in future the debts of banks will no longer be paid for by taxpayers. under the banking union, euro area countries will share a single resolution fund, financed by the banks themselves, of €55 billion. the text on the single resolution mechanism reduces political interference in decision-making: thus, when a bank is in difficulty, decisions on how to proceed will be taken mainly on the basis of technical grounds, allowing for a rapid, fair and coordinated response.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague elisa ferreira on the single resolution mechanism, as part of the legislative package on the 'banking union'. the regulation aims to complete the single supervisory mechanism within the banking union by creating a european resolution authority for the prevention and management of banking crises and a resolution fund fund funded by contributions from the banking sector. the text was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. this text is part of the single supervisory mechanism (ssm). in order to avoid a bank failure, the text provides that a single resolution board (srb) is to put in place a recovery plan for the institution concerned either by internal recapitalisation or by external capital injection from the european stability mechanism (esm), or from the states or the ecb. the troika is thus established as the ultimate saviour of the european banking sector. there is no need to make private shareholders pay first. the text also establishes a single bank resolution fund to guarantee deposits. but make no mistake, this guarantee fund is not one of them. these are national funds with mutual loan obligations. it is not a european solidarity fund: it is simply a generalization of the national deposit guarantee schemes, which are already in place in some countries and are backed by banks. the text does not therefore change the speculative practices that feed the crises, but prepares to deal with the effects of the next one without addressing the causes. i therefore vote against this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which establishes uniform rules and a uniform procedure for the resolution of credit institutions and certain investment firms under a single resolution mechanism and a single bank resolution fund, and amends regulation (eu) no 1093/2010 of the european parliament and of the council.
in writing. the 2008 banking crisis caused considerable economic and social damage in europe. it is unacceptable that the european taxpayers are once again paying for the mistakes of the banks and are suffering the full brunt of the excesses of the financial sector. the single resolution mechanism, the second pillar of the banking union, will put banks, their shareholders and creditors at the forefront. the end of unconditional bank bailouts will preserve the public finances of states and will be essential to protect the savings of citizens. the report by the socialist mep elisa ferreira makes the bank resolution mechanism and the institutional rescue fund credible and effective. thanks to the involvement of the european parliament, and especially the s&d group, the €55 billion rescue fund will be fully operational after 8 years, and the implementation of the bank resolution procedure will be decided in the last resort at european level, and therefore will not depend on the particular interests of the states. the banking union is a great success for europe and a historic project to bring finance to a boost and ensure the security and stability of the economy.
in writing. i supported the creation of a single bank resolution fund and the establishment of a single resolution mechanism, which are the third pillar of the banking union. a single resolution board will deal with the winding-up of euro area banks. the joint resolution fund will be financed by the banking sector and will have a budget of eur 55 billion, and parliament has also obtained a supply of the fund within 8 years instead of 10 years, the original deadline. it is therefore no longer the states that will be contributing in the event of a crisis but this fund. the package of measures adopted builds the future banking union and aims to restore european citizens' confidence in the banking system.
in writing. i voted in favour of the weidenholzer report which focuses on consumer protection in public services and targets in particular four areas: energy, postal services, telecommunications and public transport. in the energy sector, it stresses the need for an open, transparent and integrated energy market, improved procedures for changing suppliers and better information for consumers on prices and contractual changes. as regards telecommunications, it reaffirmed the importance of the digital single market and the need to make it easier for consumers to switch suppliers. finally, in the field of public transport, it emphasises the need for multi-modal transport to meet the needs of the ageing european population and of people with reduced mobility.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report on consumer protection in public services, as it aims to provide the european commission with ideas and action in four areas in particular: energy, postal services, telecommunications and public transport. the emphasis is on the need for an open, transparent and integrated energy market, on strengthening consumer rights (facilitating supplier switching, more information on prices and contract changes) and on the importance of establishing a digital single market. the report also stresses the need to take account of the ageing population and the needs of people with reduced mobility in the field of public transport. i regret, however, that any reference to the establishment of a european system of collective redress has been removed. the creation of such a system, including all the safeguards necessary to avoid abusive or unfounded requests, seems to me to be essential in order to strengthen the protection of consumer rights.
in writing. public services are services "essential to the life and social and cultural participation of citizens". "public service" is the unpronounceable word? the report does indeed note the successive liberalizations in the fields of energy, telecommunications, transport and postal services. it demonstrates the failures of this policy, which leads to 'the dismantling of existing structures to the detriment of consumers, price increases, a complication of contractual conditions and job losses'. but the socialist rapporteur's conclusions are the opposite. the state would be there just to limit the damage! while the liberalisation of public services should be questioned, the report considers that it is the role of the private sector to cover, instead of public services, profitable markets and the state remote or disadvantaged and 'unprofitable' territories and populations. these solutions are appalling. i abstain in order to encourage the denunciation of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which sets out the measures needed to improve the accessibility and quality of services provided by public utilities. the need for regulation and optimisation has been particularly acute as a result of the crisis. the public service is under considerable financial pressure and may therefore no longer be able to fulfil its mission of providing the universal service to disadvantaged groups, or only to a more limited extent. their function as social stabilisers is also threatened, which reduces the level of social inclusion. based on these challenges, this report helps to describe factors limiting universal access to public services and to examine how to take consumer needs into account in an appropriate manner.
in writing. this text deals with technical standards applicable to vessels sailing on inland waterways (rivers, estuaries, etc.). the main aim of the directive is to harmonize the technical rules applicable to these vessels, which are now different from those for vessels sailing on the rhine. the parliament's report requires the commission to set rules by 2017 for liquefied natural gas (lng) vessels. this is a good thing, because lng is less polluting than conventional fuel. but it's too late. the fleet in inland waters is renewed very slowly. so every year that passes is a missed opportunity. the directive could have been a real leap forward in the ecological conversion of the fleet. with the exception of lng, this issue is not even mentioned. i'm holding back in the face of such lack of ambition.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive which will allow the adoption of a single and uniform set of technical standards applicable to inland waterway vessels. this legislative framework will provide greater legal certainty, ensure that adaptations to technical progress are implemented within a reasonable timeframe and ensure that high safety standards are maintained on all inland waterways in the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to improve the detection and prevention of customs fraud, in the best interests of the european consumer. customs fraud is on the increase and it is essential that citizens today have access to safe and genuine products on the european market. to achieve this, we need to step up the exchange of information between member states and with the european commission, to fill the gaps in existing detection systems, while respecting fundamental rights.
in writing. this text adapts a 1997 regulation to make the fight against customs fraud more effective, particularly in the area of origin and misdeclaration of import or export transactions. the text aims in particular to strengthen the investigatory powers of customs officers. however, the stated objective of strengthening the means of combating fraud is largely incompatible with the external trade and customs policy as practised by the commission. the new eu customs code (customs 2020 programme) continues to place fluidification and market penetration as the first objectives of the union. the main consequence of this is customs dumping by some member states, which attract customs clearance on their territory by limiting controls. the commission is not at all discouraged by these practices. the strengthening of the means of combating fraud thus appears to be a minimum objective and in reality the control system as intended by the commission, which reserves a very limited place to physical control, fits very well into its liberal logic. the whole text is a sham to justify the state of the frontiers. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which will improve the detection, prevention and investigation of customs fraud by intensifying the exchange of information and available evidence and improving the functioning of the system in place.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation, which aims to provide the union with a comprehensive external policy on public procurement. with the growing weight of emerging economies, the unequal conditions of competition are creating many problems, and i therefore welcome the fact that the union has reached such an agreement, which will undoubtedly develop the internal market while preserving a certain level playing field between the stakeholders.
in writing. the proposal is a codification of the legislative acts relating to 'information procedures in the field of technical regulations and rules on information society services'. codification is the process of grouping together normative texts of various kinds into collections on a given subject for the purpose of simplification, clarity and transparency. i am in favour of making european law more accessible, i am in favour of that.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the amended proposal for a european parliament and council directive laying down a procedure for the provision of information in the field of technical regulations and rules on information society services (codified text). the advisory group of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission is of the opinion that the proposal in question is limited to a pure and simple codification of existing texts without any change in their substance. in this report, the european parliament adopts its position at first reading in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure by adopting the proposal of the european commission as adapted to the recommendations of the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission.
in writing. the arbitration agreement set out in this text provides a legal framework for the elimination of double taxation in the event of (upward) adjustment of profits of associated enterprises. due to the accession of croatia to the european union in june 2013, adjustments are necessary to proceed with its accession to this arbitration convention. i voted in favour of this text which will reduce the tax burden on taxpayers. it will also improve the conditions for crossborder activities within the internal market. the whole of the european union thus benefits from the harmonisation of european law in all the member states.
in writing. following croatia's accession to the union, it can thus accede to certain conventions and protocols of the european union. in this case, the aim is to enable it to become a party to the convention establishing a court of arbitration between states in cases of double taxation in the event of correction of profits of associated undertakings. the aim is to avoid double taxation of undertakings in different member states as a result of an upward adjustment of the profits of one of these undertakings in one member state. it would be more useful to strengthen controls on the taxation of community enterprises instead of relaxing taxation rules. i am opposed to croatia's membership and i am symbolically voting against any measure that would perpetuate it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which endorses the recommendation for a council decision on the accession of croatia to the convention of 23 july 1990 on the elimination of double taxation in connection with the adjustment of profits of associated enterprises. parliament called on the council, when fixing the date of application of the convention, to take account of parliament's concerns regarding the need to minimise the tax burden on taxpayers.
in writing. with the creation of the public-private partnership shift2rail, this text aims precisely at a better coordination of community investments in research and innovation in the railway sector. i particularly welcome the objectives of improving energy efficiency and increasing the reliability and punctuality of rail services. this is a timely measure, complementing the vote on the railway package in february.
in writing. the proposal aims at the creation of the shift2rail joint undertaking as a public-private partnership. the aim of this undertaking will be to stimulate and better coordinate investment in research and innovation in the railway sector. of course, all this is being done in the context of the creation of a single european railway area governed by free and undistorted competition. i am opposed to this new stage in the liberalization of the railways. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which advocates a coordinated approach to research and innovation in the rail sector, by proposing the creation of a shift2rail joint undertaking to support the completion of the single european railway area and to strengthen the competitiveness of the eu rail sector in relation to other modes of transport and in relation to foreign competition. the main advantage of the creation of a joint venture is that the coordination, programming and implementation of research and innovation activities would be the responsibility of a single and specific administrative structure, ensuring greater continuity and less fragmentation of research and innovation efforts.
in writing. despite its undeniable advantages in terms of safety, environmental protection and mass transport, the share of rail transport in europe is stagnating or even declining. the offer must therefore be made more attractive, in particular by increasing research and innovation in this area. but this has a cost which only a pooling of efforts can help to ensure. i therefore supported the launch of the shift2rail joint venture, which will bring together industrialists and policy makers. with €920 million until 2020, almost equally contributed by the commission and the private sector, i am sure that this initiative will bring progress to our railway system, whether in terms of infrastructure, management or freight.
in writing. mr mirsky is being sued by two latvian far-right figures for remarks he made in the european parliament's chamber in april 2011. he said: "in latvia, where more than 40 [nbsp] percent of the population is russian-speaking, it is possible [to close russian schools]. what do you think will happen if russian schools are closed in latvia? i tell you, the country will be ravaged by civil war". as i was in france, mr mirsky is a victim of the instrumentalization of his country's national justice system by fascist political groups seeking to de-demonize themselves. not only do his words not merit any prosecution, but i think it is useful to recall them today, at a time when ukraine is facing a similar situation - with consequences similar to those predicted by mr mirsky for his own country. i agree with him and join him in denouncing the influence of neo-nazis in his country. the gallo report defends the immunity of mr mirsky. i vote for it.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund to provide vocational reintegration assistance to workers made redundant by an italian company specialising in the sale of household appliances. the fund is thus helping a region whose economic health is particularly fragile. the unemployment rate in lazio actually went from 8.5% in 2009 to 10.8% in 2012. it is appropriate to provide an incentive for recruitment to these workers as one of the instruments to facilitate their reintegration into employment.
in writing. the globalisation fund is doing its job well. instead of helping workers, it encourages companies and governments to submit to the dictates of liberal thinking. an example is the italian company vdc technologies spa, a manufacturer of television sets and receivers. 1[nbsp]164 workers at vdc technologies and one of its suppliers were laid off. the application concerns 1[nbsp ]146 of these workers made redundant to finance vocational guidance/skill assessment, training, service to persons, support for entrepreneurship, recruitment bonus or participation allowance. the spanish authorities question the globalisation and the opening of the eu market to competition, in particular from china. but without daring to speak of a possible solidarity protectionism which would put an end to social and ecological dumping. i abstain in order not to deprive italian workers of this fund.

in writing. the crises of recent years have shown us the need to change european legislation on deposit guarantee schemes. it is essential to strengthen the confidence of account holders in the ability of their banks to return funds promptly in the event of default. i therefore support the proposal to reduce the time taken for depositors to repay their deposits. however, it is important to allow an appropriate transitional period for member states to implement such a measure.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which endorses the negotiations between the european parliament and the council on the framework for bank deposit guarantee schemes. the deposit guarantee of banks is essential to protect depositors and to ensure the stability of the financial system. the economic crisis has highlighted their usefulness: the widespread loss of confidence has led to the successive bankruptcies of credit institutions. it was therefore necessary to revise a number of rules governing these guarantees, and we reached a balanced agreement where parliament's position was heard. all european countries will have to ensure that their credit institutions have a deposit guarantee fund of at least 0.8% of the deposits covered by the system in less than 10 years. depositors will receive clear information on these guarantees when opening an account and once a year, and the repayment period in the event of insolvency will be reduced from 20 to 7 working days.
in writing. when, despite the high level of prudential supervision, a bank has to be wound up, the relevant deposit guarantee scheme (dgs) reimburses depositors up to a certain ceiling (the 'guarantee level'), thus meeting their needs. in the context of the banking union, the various sgss are to be generalized with mutual loan obligations between the different funds. but this guarantee fund is not one of them! this is a national fund and not a european solidarity fund. if one of these funds is in difficulty in repaying savers, it can borrow from the other funds, which will be obliged to accept the loan. it is nothing more than the organization of the domino effect! without stronger regulation of banks and without the contribution of private shareholders, this mechanism is far from being in the public interest. rather than predicting the next crisis, it would be better to tackle the causes of the current one. i vote against.
in writing. i supported this report which aims to revise directive 94/19/ec on deposit guarantee schemes, with a view to guaranteeing bank account holders, in the event of their bank's failure, a faster return of their funds, better cover and more detailed information on the application of the guarantee.
in writing. the deposit guarantee scheme is the second pillar of the banking union. it will allow savers to recover their money more quickly, up to a maximum of eur 100 000 in the event of bank failures. savers will be able to recover their savings within a shortened time of 7 business days. i supported this text which therefore requires banks to feed the deposit guarantee schemes with real funds and not just commitments. in the end, all the measures voted on build the future banking union and reflect the political will to achieve greater efficiency in the economic action of the european union.
in writing. i support the promotion of alternative fuels in europe and the development of adequate infrastructure within the european union. this is because it has the dual objective of reducing our dependence on oil and of reducing greenhouse gas emissions in the transport sector in order to decarbonise the european union. to do this, the european union must help to overcome the technological and commercial gaps in these infrastructures and develop a coherent strategy for alternative fuels taking into account the interoperability of transport modes.
in writing. i am pleased that the strategy to boost the use of clean fuels has been endorsed by the vast majority of meps. everyone is aware that electricity, hydrogen and gas are alternative energy sources that provide a credible answer to reducing our dependence on oil, pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. it is essential to develop electromobility and thus the electric vehicle fleet. however, this will only be possible if there are enough charging points. this regulation therefore commits member states to deploy public charging stations for the different types of fuel by 2020, 2025 and 2030 and to establish common standards in order to create a continuous sustainable transport network across europe.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague carlo fidanza on the establishment of infrastructure for alternative fuels. the text makes it compulsory to deploy such infrastructures, which are currently being implemented in a disparate way, with common technical standards in order to promote the interoperability of systems in europe. it also requires member states to set targets for certain infrastructures: electricity for cars and ships, hydrogen, liquefied and compressed natural gas. the report was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to ensure the establishment of an infrastructure for alternative fuels and the implementation of common technical specifications for this infrastructure in the union. this legislation proposes the implementation of common technical specifications and the establishment of minimum infrastructures for alternative fuels for transport, namely electricity, natural gas (lng and cng) and hydrogen, so that consumers can start to adopt these alternative fuels and that industry professionals can develop and deploy them.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the weights and dimensions of passenger cars. this report is satisfactory in that it highlights the objectives of the commission's white paper on a competitive and resource-efficient transport system. it emphasises the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, in particular those of carbon dioxide (co2), by 60% by 2050 compared to 1990 levels and by 20% by 2020. i voted against amendment no 70, which does not correspond to my vision of combined transport.
in writing. the vote on this text will allow the amendment of the legislation on the maximum weights and dimensions of road transport vehicles. the effort to reduce energy consumption in road transport by new aerodynamic measures for heavy-duty vehicles is noteworthy. however, i supported the rejection of the cross-border movement of these mega-trucks. a more detailed impact study is needed to assess their impact not only on the environment but also on road safety.
in writing. the proposal aims to limit pollution from buses and lorries. the text proposes, in particular, that account be taken of the aerodynamics of these vehicles. the report also takes into account the question of the material working conditions of lorry drivers, which was of course absent from the commission's text. but these measures will remain a long shot until real ecological planning will make it possible to reduce road transport to rail. i am voting against, despite the progress made in the leichtfried report, while denouncing the commission's lack of ambition in reducing greenhouse gases and its approval of the ultra-long lorries.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which revises directive 96/53/ec on the maximum weights and dimensions of road transport vehicles, in order to reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, adapt legislation to technological change and new market needs, facilitate intermodal transport and improve road safety.
in writing. in europe, we are doing everything we can to strike a balance between environmental protection and economic competitiveness. the maximum weights permitted for transport within the european territory are therefore of considerable importance. i am glad that i have rejected the question of the free movement of mega-trucks throughout europe. before we legislate, we must be sure that the decision will not have a negative impact on the safety and well-being of our fellow citizens. citizens must be informed in advance of the impact of mega trucks on road safety, the environment and the state of our road infrastructure.
in writing. the establishment of a framework for the recovery and resolution of credit and investment firms is an important step towards greater financial stability in the european union. in particular, it is necessary that competent authorities are able to act in a preventive manner in the event of bank failures in order to avoid possible contagion effects. the proposal to encourage such institutions to have recovery plans containing measures that enable them to act rapidly to restore their long-term viability in the event of a significant deterioration in their financial situation is therefore of interest.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague gunnar hökmark on the framework for the recovery and resolution of bank failures. the text aims to put in place harmonised tools to better prevent and manage banking crises and will allow for the preparation of preventive recovery and resolution plans, through mandatory structural changes in banks and, in the event of a crisis, through the forced sale of assets or the creation of a bridge bank. i welcome the wide adoption of this text.

in writing. i voted in favour of this directive which harmonises national provisions on the recovery and resolution of credit institutions and investment firms to the extent necessary to provide member states with the same instruments and procedures in the face of systemic failures. the objective of the proposed framework is to provide competent authorities with common and effective tools and powers to address banking crises in a preventive manner, to preserve financial stability and to minimise the exposure of taxpayers to losses.
in writing. this is the first pillar of the banking union: recovery and resolution of the failures of credit institutions and investment firms. during the economic crisis, many losses were borne by the taxpayers. from now on, it will be the creditors and shareholders who will be asked in the first place to bail out the banks or bear their failures, not public money, that is to say, taxpayer money. i supported this text, which is a real european victory. for example, in 2008, the french state had to recapitalise our banks to the tune of €120 billion; if tomorrow the same situation as 2008 happens, the state will not give a cent. the measures adopted are a victory for the construction of the banking union, they will prevent new systemic crises and put finance and banks at the service of the european economy.
in writing. the draft resolution provides for stricter rules on the depositary profession of undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits). the depositary of a ucits is basically the one who keeps the accounts, manages the orders and the transactions. the text appears to be a step towards financial regulation. but ultimately, the regulation of the depository profession will not prevent speculative bubbles or rotten investments. this resolution will best prevent new cases like madoff's, in short protect banks and the financial market from fraudulent depositors. we are far from the general interest of freeing the economy from the cancer of finance. i therefore abstain on this text because of the meagre progress it contains and to show that the liberals themselves recognize the inefficiency of the market alone.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive which amends directive 2009/65/ec to take account of market developments and the experience gained to date by market participants and supervisory authorities, in particular to address divergences between national provisions on depositary obligations and liability, remuneration policies and penalties.
in writing. this text promotes better access to payment account services for european citizens. in fact, consumers still too often have great difficulty opening a bank account in the internal market. it is therefore particularly important to address the lack of transparency and comparability of fees for services related to these accounts. a fee information document should therefore be provided to the consumer. moreover, it is rightly emphasised that the holding of a basic payment account should not be subject to any discrimination.
in writing. this report proposes to make access to payment accounts easier for european consumers. once again the european union is not really tackling the exorbitant powers of the banks. under the guise of harmonization, the aim is to remove obstacles to the creation of a fully integrated internal market for financial services. the aim is to remove barriers to the acquisition of retail financial products abroad in order to stimulate growth. to do this, banks will now have to provide "a comprehensive fee information document" to enable consumers to make informed choices... the financial institutions are also given a wide margin of discretion in deciding on the costs. the report also states that if a fee is charged for changing accounts, "it should be reasonable". i shall abstain, however, in order not to impede the meagre progress made in this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive which amends directive 2009/65/ec to take account of market developments and the experience gained to date by market participants and supervisory authorities, in particular to address divergences between national provisions on depositary obligations and liability, remuneration policies and penalties.
in writing. i supported this text, which will allow everyone to have a basic bank account, anywhere in the union, regardless of nationality or place of residence. at present, not everyone has the chance to open a bank account in the european union: the world bank estimates that 58 million european citizens have one, and banks have various reasons for refusing to open one. in addition, many mobile european citizens still face difficulties in opening a bank account in another eu country, for example because they do not have a permanent address. finally, it seems to me that having a bank account has become an essential part of economic and social life, especially in the era of online shopping and the opening of european borders. that is why we are calling on banks to make available a basic payment account, which should make life easier for many europeans and help to complete the single market. we have also introduced provisions to make offers more transparent and comparable.

in writing. this regulation provides new possibilities for spending money from the "reserve funds" of inland navigation (rivers, streams, etc.). these funds are managed by each state and financed by the companies in the sector. today, they can only be used in two specific cases: in the event of 'serious market disturbance' or if the organisations representing the sector unanimously request it. the balance sheet shows that not a penny has been spent. the report proposes to open up new possibilities for financing vocational training, qualification and retraining of boatmen and crews, as well as modernising the fleet 'for environmental purposes' or to improve safety, health and working conditions on board. i vote for it. one regret, however, is that nothing is being done to help the fleet adapt to the modal shift from the road to the river.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation amending council regulation (ec) no 718/1999 on a community fleet capacity policy in inland navigation with a view to promoting inland waterway transport. this legislation will make it easier for waterway carriers leaving the sector to obtain an early retirement pension or to convert more easily to another economic activity and to organise vocational training or retraining for crew members leaving the sector. it will also improve the qualification of inland waterway navigation to ensure the evolution and future of the profession.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text on information and promotion measures for agricultural products on the internal market and in third countries. it is important to increase the value of community products in a context of increased competition. we must pay particular attention to smes, which are largely in the agri-food sector. i therefore support in particular actions to guarantee the authenticity of european union products so that consumers can have confidence in their quality.
in writing. the aim of this text is to strengthen the mechanisms for advertising and promoting european agricultural products within the union and beyond. if it were only to promote products from rural, local and organic farming, that would be a good idea. but in this report, all products are eligible. the big food brands will therefore be the first to benefit. the regulation opens up the possibility of financing with european funds the promotion of processed products and not just agricultural products, including support for trade marks. in addition, the regulation sets the target of spending 75%[nbsp ] of advertising money on markets outside the eu. this is therefore a further favour to export agriculture at the expense of relocation and short circuits. one of the main objectives is to "increase the market share of european products, improve their competitiveness and open up new markets, especially in the sectors most affected by trade agreements". this text legitimizes the deregulation of the world agricultural markets and the internal market and seeks to respond to it by a race to the advertisement, a caricature of the productivist society. i vote against it.
in writing. the proposal aims to improve consumer information and the promotion of european agricultural products on the internal market and on the international scene. the aim is to encourage the promotion of distinctive labels and signs, such as protected designations of origin (pdo) and protected geographical indications (pgi) or country products. the report proposes the introduction of information and promotion measures, taking account in particular of the specific features of the outermost regions as described in article 349 of the treaty. a positive discrimination scheme is also provided for in the octs. i therefore naturally voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation, which aims to extend and modernise european information and promotion measures for agricultural products. this legislation will make it possible to carry out information and promotion measures on the internal market and in third countries, which are necessary for the agricultural sector to meet the challenges it faces in a context of increasing competition and opening up of markets.
in writing. - in these times of crisis, the european agricultural sector is particularly affected by increasingly intense competition from third countries. we must all make every effort to promote the quality of agricultural products both within and outside our borders. this european quality is recognised worldwide but we must nevertheless redouble our efforts to promote these products to consumers. it has been more than 60 years since the member states of the union decided to create the common agricultural policy in order to pool certain resources and to allow substantial aid to be provided to the european agricultural sector. we should not hesitate to continue this tradition by increasing its scope. i am glad that i voted in favour of this report. it highlights the need to act together to save the european agricultural sector.
in writing. the research and development programme on active living assistance is an important step forward in enabling european citizens to age in good health. encouraging the development of innovative services and products through information and communication technologies (ict) can help to improve the living conditions of an ageing population. these technologies can help to increase independence and reduce the feeling of social isolation of older people. i particularly support the emphasis on encouraging the participation of smes, the backbone of our economies, in this programme.
in writing. the proposal aims to establish the participation of the union in the programme for assistance to active life (aal). the main objective of this programme is to support market-oriented research and innovation projects for active and healthy ageing. the negative effects of the crisis on national health systems are taken into account. but the solutions are not the right ones. rather than creating programmes to overcome the failures of the states, it would be better to support national public services. i'm not going to.

in writing. i voted in favour of this decision, which will allow the union to participate in a research and development programme jointly undertaken by several member states to support small and medium-sized enterprises engaged in research activities (eurostars-2). this decision lays down the rules for the participation of the union in the second research and development programme jointly undertaken by germany, austria, belgium, bulgaria, cyprus, croatia, denmark, spain, estonia, finland, france, greece, hungary, italy, ireland, latvia, lithuania, luxembourg, malta, the netherlands, poland, portugal, the czech republic, romania, slovakia, slovenia, sweden and the united kingdom, as well as iceland, israel, norway, switzerland and turkey, to support small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) engaged in research activities ('eurostars-2') and the conditions for such participation.
in writing. - we now know that the greatest value of the european market lies in the potential for the creation of innovative technologies. this is the only way to remain competitive in the face of certain third countries which do not hesitate to use unfair methods to lower their prices. smes are pioneers in technology. their potential for innovation is enormous. but without europe's help, smes cannot achieve an optimal result enabling them to develop new technologies. by developing research and development policies targeted at smes, we are showing the rest of the world that we will not be bogged down by the crisis. europeans are determined to regain their leading position in the world economy. i am glad that i voted in favour of this report. it is with this kind of policy that we will succeed in getting the european economy back on its feet.
in writing. metrology is the science of measurement. it's a vital part of the high-tech world we live in. enlightened france understood and applied this. the overall objective of the empir programme is to provide metrology solutions to support innovation and industrial competitiveness, as well as to address societal challenges such as health, environment and energy. the aim is therefore to create an integrated european metrology research system with sufficient critical mass and active engagement at regional, national, european and international level. no private participation is foreseen, as metrology is recognised as a 'public good' justifying public intervention. the liberals are incapable of managing the public interest, they admit it. for once in my life, if a vital area is not sold to the private sector, i vote for it.

in writing. the text provides for the continuation of the partnership between european countries and developing countries on clinical trials. in other words, it supports clinical research and other actions to combat poverty-related diseases in developing countries, including hiv/aids, malaria and tuberculosis. closer cooperation with the countries of sub-saharan africa in particular will then be established.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague vicky ford, which extends a programme of partnership between european and developing countries on clinical trials. the initiative, which started in 2003 and is being extended under the horizon 2020 framework, aims to help develop new treatments for diseases affecting developing countries, such as hiv, malaria and tuberculosis. new medicines developed will need to be safe, effective and affordable, in order to meet the needs of the countries and populations targeted. through this programme, the union is demonstrating its determination to meet the millennium development goals set by the united nations, and i welcome this. the report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. the 'european and developing countries clinical trials partnership' was set up in 2003 in response to the global health crisis caused by the three main poverty-related diseases hiv/aids, malaria and tuberculosis. the question is to extend it for 10 years. the rapporteur recalls that "only 10% of global research funding is allocated to the diseases responsible for 90% of the world's pathologies". it therefore proposes the most open list possible for funding research into poverty-related diseases. but the fact that these diseases are on the increase in europe can only be explained by migration. the return of malaria in greece, for example, is a symptom of austerity policies. as the only remedy, this text advocates the strengthening of private actors in research, through the development of public-private partnerships and compliance with the horizon 2020 strategy. i cannot accept that health should be subjected to the commercial world, neither in these countries nor in europe under the yoke of austerity. i'm not going to.

in writing. it is estimated that each year about 2.6%[nbsp] of the turnover of european companies is lost in outstanding debts. there are now several instruments at eu level to facilitate the recovery of outstanding claims, but they are insufficient. the fragmentation of national debt recovery provisions allows the debtor to transfer or withdraw assets from a bank account held in one member state to another without difficulty. the proposal aims to create a new legal instrument of a precautionary nature, the oesc (european preservation order on bank accounts), which creditors can use as an alternative to national procedures. the proposal is balanced and provides for the responsibility of the applicant in the event of cancellation of the procedure. i vote for it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation, which creates a european preservation order for bank accounts, to facilitate crossborder recovery of claims in civil and commercial matters. the aim of this legislation is to simplify the recovery of crossborder claims for citizens and businesses, in particular smes, and to make the enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters relating to crossborder disputes more efficient. the aim is to reduce the risks associated with crossborder trade, to increase the confidence of traders, to improve the payment behaviour of debtors in situations with a crossborder dimension and to encourage the development of crossborder commercial activities.
in writing. this vote is a signal for greater comparability and transparency of information published by large companies and certain groups within the european union. it provides for the obligation for certain large companies to publish relevant non-financial information in order to create a level playing field within the union. it seems to me legitimate that these companies should publish in their management report a statement which also includes information on environmental matters, personnel management and the fight against corruption. increased transparency will only increase consumer confidence in these companies.

in writing. i voted in favour of this directive which aims to improve the relevance, consistency and comparability of information published by companies across the union. the text introduces an obligation for certain large companies to publish relevant non-financial information in order to create a level playing field for all companies in the union.
in writing. while i support the approach of this directive which aims to open legal pathways for the immigration of highly skilled posted workers, i have nevertheless opposed the compromise reached with the council because this must not be at the expense of workers' rights. i therefore opposed this compromise because it does not guarantee equal treatment between workers and could have disastrous consequences for intra-group posted workers, who could be exploited, but also for workers in the host country, who would have to face unfair competition. i voted in favour of the amendments by the committee on employment and social affairs to ensure equal treatment between posted workers and their local colleagues working in the same offices. the union cannot allow the creation of a two-tier labour market, nor the unequal treatment of employees according to their country of origin. the principle of 'equal work, equal pay in equal workplaces' must guide our action. laws should protect workers, not create loopholes to violate them.
in writing. in the case of legal immigration, it's the salami tactic. the commission classifies migrants into different categories, giving them so many different rights. so we cut the rights category by category until there's nothing left. the directive thus concerns 'the conditions of entry and residence of third-country nationals on intra-group secondment' of highly qualified employees. this is part of the logic of an increasingly unequal and selective immigration policy, designed only for the needs of countries that need skilled labour. nothing is done to provide for equal treatment between european workers and those from third countries. it is the continuation of social dumping, pitting workers against each other and throwing them out of the eu as soon as the work is done! i vote against it.
in writing. i voted against this report which lays down the conditions for entry and residence of third-country nationals on intra-group secondment. failure to guarantee equal treatment between workers will have disastrous consequences for intra-group posted workers who could be exploited, but also for workers in the host country who would be subject to unfair competition.
in writing. i voted against the directive which lays down conditions for entry and residence for third-country nationals on intra-group secondment. it concerns in particular management staff for branches and subsidiaries of multinational companies, establishing transparent and harmonised conditions for the admission of this category of workers, and improving the conditions of temporary residence for posted workers and their families. today, a number of factors limit the opportunities for international companies to use intragroup mobility, estimated at 16 500 per year within the eu, representing 4% of temporary migrant workers. this directive opens up legal pathways for immigration from third countries. but the negotiations with the council have not made it possible to include equal treatment in terms of working conditions, and in particular pay, in the applicable rights. this directive has aggravated social dumping, and i therefore voted against the report. i regret that a large majority of modem and the ump did not support equal treatment.

states did not give any hope of this compromise at the beginning of our work. as my colleagues have said, the posting of workers has become a major problem within europe. the delors directive of 1996 has proved to be ineffective, poorly applied by the member states and inappropriate for current needs. in a dynamic social market economy, this directive has had to be revised to reconcile economic freedom, fair competition and the protection of employees. the sectors most affected are construction, agriculture and services, which employ underpaid workers. intermediary companies are flourishing and cascading outsourcing makes controls too few and ineffective. the agreement reached with the council will allow for more checks. it is up to our governments to ensure that these controls are numerous and effective. a system of cross-border exchange of information between inspectors exists but in the absence of rapid administrative and judicial powers, controls remain ineffective. some countries such as france need to reform their labour inspection system, but this requires that the reform be effective and that it gives inspectors the opportunity to act quickly to suspend activities and companies suspected of abusing posted workers. it is essential to reduce administrative hierarchies and centralization, and to increase the number of inspectors. unfortunately, that is not the direction of the reforms undertaken in my country. at european level, unscrupulous business leaders will also be held accountable. it's up to them to become socially responsible. let us stop saying commission statement on the competence of the committee the commission regrets the inclusion of recital 16b that has the potential to create confusion and legal uncertainty. the role of the committees which ensure control by member states on the commission’s exercise of implementing powers is defined only by regulation no (eu) 182/2011, adopted on the basis of article 291, third paragraph, tfeu. therefore, no other secondary legislative act can alter or would need to specify further this role. in particular, the rules of procedures of committees are adopted by the committees on the basis of regulation no (eu) 182/2011. as such they are to be applied when the committee exercises its role defined by regulation no (eu) 182/2011. any reference to rules of procedures outside this context is superfluous and inappropriate. it also risks complicating the functioning of the committee. with regard to the possibility of the european parliament to be invited to meetings, the commission will implement this recital in accordance with its practice in the implementation of point 15 of the framework agreement on relations between the european parliament and the european commission. commission statement on the ‘no-opinion’ clause the commission underlines that it is contrary to the letter and to the spirit of regulation no (eu) 182/2011 to invoke article 5, paragraph 4, subparagraph 2, point (b) in a systematic manner. recourse to this provision must respond to a specific need to depart from the rule of principle which is that the commission may adopt a draft implementing act when no opinion is delivered. given that it is an exception to the general rule established by article 5(4), recourse to subparagraph 2, point (b), cannot be simply seen as a “discretionary power” of the legislator, but must be interpreted in a restrictive manner and thus must be justified. while the commission notes the agreement reached by the european parliament and the council on the recourse to this provision it regrets that such justification is not reflected in a recital. commission statement on the consultation of experts in the context of preparation of delegated acts the commission regrets the inclusion in articles 8(2), 8(2a), 11(2) and 29(6) of a provision stressing the importance for the commission to ‘carry out consultations with experts, including member states’ experts, during the preparation of such delegated acts’. the commission recalls that the commission is autonomous in the preparation and adoption of delegated acts. moreover, article 290 tfeu contains an exhaustive list of the procedural conditions which a delegation may be made subject to. the standard recital on expert advice contained in the common understanding agreed between the three institutions is a reflection of that interpretation.

i'm the reporter. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, i should like, as is the custom, to begin by thanking the fictitious rapporteurs and all those who have worked on this report, which is a technical, legal and somewhat complicated one. i would also like to thank the representatives of the commission and the council with whom we have had a fruitful dialogue. the text before us concerns the restitution of cultural property between member states. the draft directive proposed by the commission has a limited scope. it concerns only national treasures which have left the territory of a member state of the union unlawfully, and only for the purpose of returning such property between member states. it's a little more limited because it's a redesign. it is important to know that this directive was proposed in 1993 when the internal borders of the european union were abolished. it is based on article 36 of the treaties, which provides for exceptions, particularly in cultural matters. unfortunately, there was no uniform definition of what constitutes a national treasure then, and there is no such definition today. but in a way, this is normal. the 1993 directive was a serious failure, as there were very few refunds, only 7, and 46[nbsp]refunds in good faith. it is necessary to amend that directive, in particular by extending the time limits for restitution and those allowing states to verify the nature of the cultural property subject to the proceedings and to reverse the burden of proof of the possession of the unlawful property, shifting the burden of proof from the victim state seeking restitution to the possessor of the property who must demonstrate that he has exercised due diligence to verify the origin of the property and thus to benefit from compensation. the trilogue negotiations were successful and were endorsed by the council at the beginning of march and by the committee on culture and education last week. the main amendments are mainly proposals made by the european parliament. they will make it possible to define clearly, from the outset, the objectives of the directive and to promote coordination between the member states as far as possible, while respecting the specific characteristics of cultural goods which cannot be treated like other goods and facilitating the dissemination of information in order to enable the actors, and in particular those in the art market, to verify the origin of the cultural goods they are going to acquire. it also helps to clarify the lessons of good faith and due diligence, which in some legislations have rather ambiguous connotations. this is particularly the case in france. the text is intended to prevent the reckless actor from receiving compensation from the injured state which wants to recover his property. most of the art dealers are involved. so they are not casual shoppers but seasoned professionals. it may be helpful to make it clear that the judge will be the one to assess the matter and will be given full latitude to make the best possible assessment of the situation. the new text will also allow this procedure to be used for property which left the territory of a member state before 1993 - this claim has been made on many occasions - and also for cultural property and objects other than those classified as 'national treasures' provided that the two member states concerned agree. we would like to go further with a better definition by the member states of the concept of 'national treasure', a stronger incentive for the member states to ratify the unesco and unidroit conventions on the illicit trafficking of cultural property and on the information of the actors and, more broadly, the public. all these points were nevertheless incorporated in the recitals, if not in the body of the text itself. finally, we would have liked to go further with regard to the specific recognition of cultural property by relying on article 167 of the treaties, which gives the european union competence in cultural matters, in particular on the question of heritage, just as we would have liked to have made explicit reference to the unesco convention on cultural diversity. this text is eagerly awaited by our partners, particularly at unesco. it is welcome that this issue was included in the eu-africa conference. many hope that the system will run smoothly. its implementation depends to a large extent on the member states. let's hope they can move on. i would like to thank once again all those who have been willing to work on this report.

madam president, the cornelius gurlitt case in germany and the 1,400 artworks found in his attic have highlighted the difficulty of returning looted cultural property. according to unesco, the illegal trafficking of art is the third largest trafficking in the world, behind drugs and arms. the black market in cultural goods represents a loss for the member state of origin, its culture, heritage, museums and above all for citizens' access to art. worse still, when these works are found, their restitution is too complicated because of the misunderstandings and mistrust that still exist between the national judicial administrations. today we are finally modernising the 1993 european directive which sought to address these problems. the reform broadens the definition of cultural property. it will lead to better information sharing and longer time limits for making a claim for restitution. cultural heritage is a universal good that we should protect.

member of the commission. - madam president, we are here to discuss an initiative that aims to help solve a serious and often highly visible environmental problem: the over-consumption and littering of plastic carrier bags. plastic carrier bags easily escape waste management streams and accumulate in our environment, especially in the form of marine litter. for example, plastic bags accounted for 73% of the plastic waste collected by travellers along the tuscany coast. once discarded, they can last for hundreds of years, often as harmful microscopic particles that are damaging to the environment worldwide, and especially the marine environment. in the north sea, the stomachs of 94% of all birds contain plastics. the huge and growing consumption rates of plastic bags – 100 billion bags per year in the eu alone as already mentioned – also demonstrates a squandering of resources. plastic bags are a symbol of our throw-away society and unsustainable lifestyles. we use them for a few minutes but their legacy lasts for hundreds of years. public opinion is strongly behind reducing the use of lightweight plastic bags, but public behavioural change needs a nudge. this is the clear lesson from member states such as ireland, which have that shown simple measures can lead to big changes. the time has come for member states to take action across the european union, building on the successful initiatives already in place and in response to broad public concern and support. this is why environment ministers called on the commission to make proposals and it is why in november last year the commission tabled a simple and straightforward proposal to amend the european union’s packaging and packaging waste directive. the proposal contains two main elements. first, it requires member states to adopt measures to reduce the consumption of lightweight plastic carrier bags, as these tend to be used once, and frequently end up as litter. secondly, the proposal provides member states with a range of instruments, including economic instruments such as charges, national reduction targets and possible marketing restrictions, provided that they are compatible with the european union treaty rules. parliament’s draft report clearly shows that we share the same objective: limiting the consumption and littering of plastic carrier bags. i am very grateful for the support, and i would like to thank the rapporteur, ms auken, for her hard and thorough work on the commission’s proposal. thanks also to the shadow rapporteurs in the committee on the environment, public health and food safety. however, there are some amendments in the report that the commission regards as unnecessary in achieving the objectives of the proposal. the idea of the reduction target might be appealing, and indeed the commission looked into this possibility in quite some detail. our conclusion was that it would be almost impossible at this stage to design and implement an effective and meaningful eu-wide reduction target applying to all member states. the commission also does not think that it is appropriate to make exceptions for plastic carrier bags that are used to carry loose, humid and dry food or food and beverages for immediate consumption. it is perfectly possible to reduce the consumption of these bags too while respecting food safety and hygiene requirements. the commission considers that all lightweight plastic carrier bags should be treated in the same way, regardless of the type of plastic they are made of. all lightweight bags contribute to littering and can end up in the marine environment. biodegradable plastics only biodegrade within a reasonable time if they are disposed of and treated in appropriate conditions. the prefix ‘bio’ does not mean that biodegradable bags are necessarily environmentally friendly. our overriding aim should therefore be to reduce the use of all lightweight plastic bags. this would also be in line with the waste hierarchy principle and the prevention of waste in the first place. we also believe that we should not touch, in these proposals, on issues that are broader than plastic bags. for example, broader provisions relating to specific types of plastics such as the proposed ban on oxo-biodegradable plastics or to maximum concentration levels for hazardous substances and endocrine disrupters in packaging are not part of our proposal. these issues, as well as the biodegradability of plastics, which are of course important, should not be addressed in relation to a single product – the plastic bag – but in a broader context, including as a follow-up to our green paper on plastic waste. we finally believe that member states, when designing policies to reduce the consumption of lightweight plastic bags should be able to choose from a broad range of possible measures including also marketing restrictions, subject to the relevant treaty provisions. the commission and parliament, as i already mentioned, share the same objective, even though we may still need more discussion on the measures best suited to achieve that objective. in this light, the commission will carefully examine the amendments voted here these days in great detail. the commission remains at the disposal of parliament and the council with a view to finding a mutually agreeable outcome between all institutions as soon as possible.

the different committees. also thanks to the presidency for its work and the presidencies before it so that today we stand here with, hopefully, a strong agreement on this compromise. i think we can be very satisfied with the compromise. it achieves the objective of our proposal – to ensure the effective and proper functioning of frontex-coordinated sea operations and to guarantee proper fundamental rights protection during these operations. clear and binding rules should also encourage more member states to participate in these operations. this legislation, as has been said, is a response to a judgment by the court of justice which annulled the current rules and guidelines, but all three institutions have worked very hard to make sure that today, before parliament closes, we have an agreement. the draft regulation governs frontex-coordinated sea operations. it is based on a concept of border surveillance that is not limited to the detection of attempts at irregular crossing of borders, but extends also to actions such as intercepting vessels trying to gain unauthorised entry to the european union. it includes arrangements to address situations such as search and rescue that may arise during those operations and arrangements for disembarkation. the provisions on interception, search and rescue, and disembarkation must form part of the operation plan drawn up for each operation. this is an entirely binding instrument and this is one of the key points for us in the commission. it was possible to achieve this thanks to your support. according to the principle of ‘non-refoulementʼ, no[nbsp ]one should be removed or returned to a country where, directly or indirectly, there is a serious risk that he or she would be subject to inhumane or degrading treatment, where his or her life or freedom would be threatened on grounds of, for instance, race or religion. this was a very important aspect of our original proposal where we took into account recent, legal and judicial developments, and it has been further reinforced by the amendments in this parliament. the draft regulation sets out the procedures for applying the principle of non-refoulement in the event of disembarkation in a third country. an assessment is required of the situation in general of that particular third country and a further assessment of an individual nature needs to be done by the border guards during the operation itself. the intercepted or rescued persons need to be informed of the place of disembarkation and they must be given an opportunity to express any reason for believing that disembarkation in a particular third country would be in violation of the principle of non-refoulement. thanks to parliament’s amendments frontex will need to report on the practical applications of this draft regulation and in particular of the application on non-refoulement. one of the most distressing and challenging issues that we face today, and we can read about it every day in the papers, is the loss of life at sea. we have seen terrible examples lately. every effort must be made to assist people in distress and the fact that this draft regulation contains legally binding provisions on search and rescue applicable to sea operations coordinated at eu level is an important achievement. negotiations were not easy but we are here and i want to thank everybody involved. the role of frontex in coordinating the operational cooperation between member states in the mediterranean is a key element to ensure effective border control in the region and at the same time provide assistance to persons in distress. this is one way, as also identified – and as mentioned by the minister – in the work of the task force on the mediterranean, of trying to prevent similar tragedies to those we have witnessed lately. this brings me to the last point, which concerns the issue of disembarkation after interception or rescue. disembarkation after interception is based on objective criteria to ensure the subsequent adoption of the enforcement measures needed. for instance, in the case of interception in territorial seas or a contiguous zone, disembarkation takes place in the coastal member state. disembarkation in a third country is only possible when a vessel is intercepted on the high seas, subject to protection of fundamental rights and the correct application of the non-refoulement principle being guaranteed. in a rescue situation, cooperation between member states and the rescue coordination centre responsible is essential and this is also emphasised in the regulation. rescued people must be taken to a safe place and this must not only be a place where safety of life is not threatened but also a place where they would not be at risk of being subjected to any treatment in violation of the principle of non-refoulement. member states have in this respect an obligation to cooperate with the rescue coordination centre responsible, not only to identify a place of safety, but also to ensure that the rescued persons are disembarked rapidly and effectively. finally, i very much value and appreciate the provisions on solidarity introduced by parliament. the issues that we have discussed in this plenary so many times concerning refugees and migrants coming to europe are a challenge for all of us, not just for the member states immediately affected on the southern borders. both the member states and the institutions share the responsibility to do what we can to help and with this draft regulation i think that notion has been further strengthened. i thank you again for all the work that has been done on this.

vice-president of the commission. - mr president, concerning the poc report on invasive alien species, i would like to use this occasion to draw your attention to the fact that a declaration on behalf of the commission was made with regard to the agreement reached between the co-legislators. this commission declaration will be transmitted to parliament’s services in writing and inserted in the report of proceedings of this plenary sitting for your consideration.
