(applause) (sign of approval) i would like to thank the commissioner for his report. could the president explain to me the meaning of the vote in this house if the bureau does not want to respect them anyway?
in writing. the proposal aims to increase the mobility of workers by improving their pension rights. the mobility of workers is not an end in itself. however, allowing these 'mobile' workers to receive their supplementary pension rights is a minimum requirement. the council proposal incorporates parliament's amendments at first reading, in particular on the involvement of the social partners. i vote for it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive which aims to ensure that the rules governing the organisation of supplementary pension schemes do not hamper worker mobility. this text lays down common principles for improving the exercise of the right of free movement and the functioning of the internal market, principles which are part of the adaptation of the supplementary pension schemes already in force in the member states. it aims to reduce both the obstacles to free movement between member states and to mobility within a member state created by certain provisions of supplementary pension schemes.
in writing. with this text, we are putting in place a harmonised legislative framework for controls in the agri-food chain. it is appropriate to highlight the creation of a common entry sanitary document to be used by operators to prevent the mandatory arrival and dispatch of animals and goods from third countries. this is a necessary simplification of rules and controls to ensure the safety of the european agri-food chain.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it creates harmonised and coherent control procedures to ensure compliance with food safety regulations. it thus encompasses in a single legislative text the official controls concerning all sectors of the agri-food chain. the report shall introduce a minimum frequency of controls based on risk and established in a differentiated manner for each product, process or activity. i would also like to stress the importance of unannounced checks to better detect fraud. the text also suggests the creation of european reference centres with the specific task of developing and validating the control methods to be used in the case of proven food fraud. i welcome the fact that the control bureaucracy has been reduced and that micro-enterprises can be exempted from part of the payment of the contributions to the compulsory fees and charges.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague mario pirillo on official controls to ensure compliance with food legislation. the text confirms the principle of checks based on a risk analysis and consolidates the rules applicable to checks carried out in the union's trade with third countries. coercive measures in the event of infringements by operators have been strengthened, which will reinforce the dissuasive effect of controls. the report was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. this text strengthens the rules on official controls in agri-food and agriculture. parliament reinforces the requirement of independence of auditors. it is a good thing, because the european commission merely asked that they not be subject to conflicts of interest. the text also requires that these inspectors be "qualified, trained and in sufficient numbers". it is hypocritical with the austerity policies being carried out all over europe but positive. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of whistle-blowers. but the text almost completely ignores the decisive role of customs officials in combating food fraud. it merely mentions the role of customs officials in controlling pets or assisting veterinary services. however, it is the free movement of goods throughout europe and the absence of protectionist measures that make our societies vulnerable to a large number of fraudulent transactions. i'm not going to.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which will ensure a harmonised approach to official controls carried out to ensure compliance with eu agri-food chain rules. the purpose of this text is to modernise the implementing instruments as provided for in the existing regulation, in order to simplify the legislative framework. it establishes harmonised rules at eu level to ensure a comprehensive and consistent approach to official controls throughout the agri-food chain.
in writing. several recent cases have shown that, in the context of the food chain, official controls are an essential element in ensuring a high level of protection of human, animal and plant health. the legal framework that the union has developed so far remains generally effective in preventing risks: union products remain among the safest in the world, precisely because of the controls they are subject to. but the increasingly long and complex agri-food chain exposes the european union to new risks and requires continuous improvement of controls throughout the agri-food chain. the sector has thus been governed by some 15 pieces of legislation (eu regulations and directives). it was necessary to recreate a harmonized and comprehensive framework. that is why i voted in favour of this report, which proposes a thorough review of the existing provisions in order to eliminate the overlapping of the regulations.
in writing. this text rightly provides for uniform measures to be taken for the prevention and control of transmissible animal diseases. the establishment of a single and transparent regulatory framework is an effective way to ensure both animal welfare and food safety. this legislation is an effective response to preventing further food crises such as the so-called 'mad cow' crisis.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague marit paulsen which lays down rules for the prevention and control of animal diseases communicable to humans. it codifies all existing legislation, simplifying, clarifying and bringing it closer to international standards. the introduction of this system is welcome to ensure optimum protection of man against diseases of animal origin, whether new or re-emerging. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to simplify and update european legislation on animal health, in particular by taking account of new diseases. it's necessary, you know. parliament has included a reference to the fact that animals must be regarded as 'sensitive beings'. this is a good thing, because animal welfare is very much linked to the health and treatment of animals. however, this text barely touches on the main animal health risk today: the race to gigantism and agricultural productivity and the proliferation of live animal transfers. the 'regulation provides the basis for a thorough evaluation and review of existing methods'. we are a long way from what we need: a radical and urgent break. i'm not going to.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation, which lays down rules for the prevention and control of transmissible animal diseases and establishes a harmonised animal health strategy throughout the union. the purpose of this text is to establish a single, simplified, transparent and clear regulatory framework which systematically sets out the objectives, scope and principles of regulatory action in the field of animal health.
in writing. food safety must be a matter of concern throughout the european union. consumers must be assured that their products are safe to consume. this is one of the european market's surpluses. the european agri-food chain ensures that health protection standards are met. animal health is particularly important. we do not want to go back to the crisis of the mad cow disease, which caused enormous damage to the european agri-food chain. i am glad i voted in favour of this report. it will make it possible to monitor the legislation of the member states and to build up a harmonised body of rules. this will help us to strengthen prevention of animal diseases and to ensure a safer food chain.
in writing. in terms of animal health, european legislation was complex, jeopardising its effectiveness and clarity. the draft regulation brings together all the relevant european legislation in a single instrument to simplify and clarify the community framework and make it more responsive to new health emergencies. this regulation thus ensures a genuine legal framework for animal health, all the more so as it is closer to the standards of the world organisation for animal health. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. this text provides for the standardization of protective measures against organisms harmful to plants. this includes plant breeding regulations. i particularly support the idea of a plant passport so that plants can move around the union. the use of such sustainable and safe instruments not only contributes to the competitiveness of european agriculture but can also encourage third countries to align their legislation with it.
in writing. i welcome the adoption, as part of the animal and plant health package, of the regulation on protective measures against organisms harmful to plants. the regulation provides for a list of union quarantine pests and for plant health prevention and inspection measures to detect the presence of pests in imports at the earliest possible stage. the problem arises, for example, on the côte d'azur with the red palm frog. however, i regret that the report does not go far enough and that amendments nos 78 to 85 which provide for the creation of a positive list have not been adopted. the control of imports would have been even more strengthened.
in writing. the globalisation of trade and climate change are facilitating the introduction and spread within the union of new organisms harmful to particularly dangerous plants. the current legislation in the field of plant health needs to be modernised. that is the purpose of this text. the parliament's report agrees that the use of pesticides should not be systematic and that prevention and an agronomic approach (crop rotation, etc.) should be given priority. this is a "reasonable struggle" approach that dates back more than thirty years. the report is, on the contrary, very timid about biological treatments and the promise of biodynamic crops. the latter imply strict control of inputs on land and also increased control of trade in plants and seeds which are now non-existent under the free trade and free competition promoted by the treaties. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which will ensure a harmonised design of protection measures against organisms harmful to plants. the aim of the text is to establish a strong, transparent and sustainable regulatory framework to protect plant health. overall, this new framework will strengthen existing synergies with the regulation on plant reproductive material, while eliminating duplication of effort and unnecessary constraints. in order to do this, the harmful organisms which are currently regulated by the so-called directives on the marketing of seeds and plant propagating material will now be covered by the proposed regulation.
in writing. as europeans, we are in favour of opening our market to products from third countries. this should not in any way prevent us from assuring european consumers that these products are safe. plants play an important role in the food chain, so it is essential to monitor them. we must have rules to ensure that plant pests do not enter europe. i am glad that i voted in favour of this report. however, instead of a negative list of bodies with access to the european market as envisaged by the commission, a positive list would be more appropriate. we do not know what organisms may harm plants in the future. when it comes to the safety of european consumers, every effort must be made to achieve an optimal safety situation.
in writing. the aim of this report is to protect agriculture by preventing the entry and spread of pests within the european union. the current strategy, based on a negative list, lists plant products that are prohibited or subject to control before importation. by default, the rest of the plants can be imported without control. i have therefore chosen to support the approach of a more stringent positive list, which lists countries and products which do not present unacceptable dangers to agriculture and which can therefore be imported into the union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which ensures a high level of consumer safety and protection for products circulating in the internal market. it is thus aimed at non-food manufactured consumer products. the creation of a compulsory marking of origin for these products is an important step forward in enhancing their traceability and thus ensuring their quality. this mandatory 'made in' marking is also important to promote products manufactured in europe.
in writing. i voted in favour of this legislative report on the proposal for a regulation on the safety of manufactured consumer products other than food, which aims to replace the existing 2001 directive, as it increases consumer protection. the existing rules have been clarified, modernised and strengthened, in particular by taking into account products that are attractive to children, by tightening the provisions on inspections, by increasing the obligations of economic operators in relation to product safety and by creating a pan-european injury database. i also welcome the adoption of the marking of origin at european level for products covered by this regulation, after months of very lively debate. such a system, which meets a real consumer demand, will make it possible to improve the traceability of products by helping to identify defective products in the production and marketing chain. it will also enable the european union to put itself on an equal footing with many of its trading partners who have already adopted such a system, and to enhance the value of products manufactured in the union, thus benefiting our companies.
in writing. this new consumer product regulation should provide better safety for consumers. the commission's proposal does not include the precautionary principle. it provides for a clear indication of the "real place of production" of the product, the famous "made in", which the right and the liberals opposed, criticizing a "protectionism in disguise" and introduces a new ce+ labelling (in addition to the existing ce mentioning the safety of the product) indicating its compliance with the union's rules on production and imports. the regulation also introduces sanctions for companies that will be used to finance market surveillance activities. companies that don't comply will be blacklisted. it called for the harmonization of sanctions between member states to avoid attempts at dumping. a case to be closely watched to avoid harmonisation from below. in order to support this resistance to productive dumping, i vote in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which will protect the functioning of the internal market for consumer products while guaranteeing consumers a high level of safety and health protection (the 'product safety and market surveillance' package). the s&d group fought for the obligation to label the country of origin ("made in"), with a strict definition of the last processing to avoid the addition of a label to give a place of origin in europe for a product made in asia. the other key point for us is the introduction of a voluntary additional label 'safety remaining in the eu' which aims to overcome the shortcomings of the current ec marking which is only declarative and does not guarantee conformity control by an independent accredited body.
in writing. european manufactured products face significant competition from third countries. the latter use dishonest processes to lower the cost of the finished product. underpaid workers, poor working conditions, and poor product quality are common in manufacturing. consumers must be assured in some way that the product they are buying is safe. i am very glad that i voted in favour of this report. it will allow the introduction of a system of marking origin, a 'made in'. this will enable consumers to trace the origin of the product so that they can be assured of the quality of what they are consuming. european products have an excellent reputation throughout the world. we must not hide from this and instead mark our products.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on product safety, which, together with the report on market surveillance, forms a coherent package designed to make our consumer products safer. i support the main changes brought about by this legislative package, in particular the tightening of requirements throughout the distribution chain, the greater clarity of the respective obligations of manufacturers, importers and distributors, the improved arrangements for dangerous or non-compliant products and the improved traceability of products. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on the fact that he has taken the initiative in this area. i do not have time to elaborate on the legal, economic, political or even common sense arguments in favour of this provision, but i would simply point out that i have been fighting for years to support the mandatory indication of origin. the commission proposal seems to me to be very cleverly worded on this point, allowing either the 'made in pays' or the 'made in eu' label for products made in the union and i have therefore fiercely fought the attempt to remove it, as has a large majority of the house, and i welcome that.
in writing. this text concerns the revision of the general product safety directive and concerns manufactured consumer products other than food. this revision is due to the confusion between different european legislative texts among economic operators and the competent national authorities, thus affecting the good efficiency of market surveillance. the report focuses on two key measures: origin marking and safety marking. as regards origin marking, it was important to support the mandatory indication of the country of origin of the product or 'made in' on the product itself or on its packaging. this marking of origin allows products to be traced, establishes genuine consumer confidence and enhances the value of products manufactured in the european union. i am, however, against the safety label 'eu safety tested' because of the negative conclusions of the impact assessment. the labelling would not bring any benefits to consumers, the costs of such a system would be a burden on smes and a costly information campaign would be necessary. in view of these significant advances in consumer product safety, i supported this report.
in writing. i supported this report on a proposal for a regulation on product market surveillance, as it strengthens market surveillance mechanisms and thus consumer protection. the clear distinction between 'non-compliant product' and 'product presenting an emerging risk' makes it possible to apply procedures of varying degrees of strictness, depending on the degree of danger. the obligations of the supervisory authorities have also been strengthened in the context of product control. in addition, a pan-european database of consumer injuries and accidents has been set up, which will be maintained by the competent national supervisory authorities and managed by the european commission. finally, the sanctions regime was tightened, in particular by taking into account the intentional nature of the infringement and the publication of a blacklist of economic operators who had intentionally and repeatedly infringed the provisions of the regulation.
in writing. the european parliament proposed in a resolution in 2011 that the commission establish a common european framework for market surveillance covering all products circulating in the internal market, including those imported into the union. this proposal follows that request. the proposal is part of a wider package on product safety and aims to ensure that non-compliant operators do not gain an advantage in the market over compliant operators. binding provisions in the form of administrative sanctions are provided for. the ultimate aim is always to increase the free movement of goods, but for once we make sure that they meet safety or environmental standards. i vote for it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation on market surveillance which will unify the legal framework for market surveillance and border controls on industrial products and strengthen market surveillance to ensure product safety, compliance with european regulations and fair competition between operators.
in writing. the european union is committed to accepting only products on its market that are safe and harmless to consumers. this is one of the european market's surpluses. we must remain vigilant about the arrival on european territory of products which do not comply with european standards or which present any risk to consumers. i am glad i voted in favour of this report. the need to harmonise european legislation in this area was urgent in order to ensure the most effective management of market surveillance.
in writing. this report is part of the regulatory clarification for market surveillance of non-food products following the overlap of market surveillance rules between different existing legislation at european level, leading to some confusion. i have supported this report which will allow for the introduction of a clear distinction between 'a non-compliant product' and 'a product presenting an emerging risk'; the objective is that this type of product is not placed on the market of the european union. the text also introduces the use of the rapid alert system (rapex) and strengthens the obligations of market surveillance authorities in relation to product controls. finally, a pan-european injury database will be created and the penalties for non-compliance with the provisions of the regulation will be strengthened.
in writing. this text provides for measures to monitor financial markets and for requirements to publish information on trading and transactions. this draft resolution is a smokescreen, under the guise of greater transparency we are not tackling speculation itself. on the contrary, the laroisière group which drafted the document on which the draft resolution is based believes that 'excessive regulation, which would hamper financial innovation and therefore undermine the growth of the economy in general, must of course be avoided'. the former imf director, jacques de laroisière, gives us the substance of this resolution, a little transparency but no regulation. we want both transparency and supervision of the financial markets, but also strict regulation of them, so i am voting against this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation, which aims to adopt new rules for more efficient, resilient and transparent european financial markets (over-the-counter derivatives, central counterparties and central securities depositories). the text lays down requirements for the publication of information on trading and the reporting of transactions to the competent authorities and removes obstacles to non-discriminatory access to clearing systems. it also provides for specific surveillance measures concerning financial instruments and derivatives positions and services provided by third-country firms which do not have a branch.
in writing. the previous directive allowing for the emergence of free competition on financial markets was a failure. the rapporteur is surprised: 'the benefits of this increased competition have not been equally shared by all market players and have not always been passed on to final investors'. the commission is also proposing to make financial markets more transparent. it protects mainly speculative financial operations. i am voting against this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive which aims to adopt new rules for more efficient, resilient and transparent european financial markets (recast of the directive on markets in financial instruments - the mfi directive). this text amends certain requirements concerning the provision of investment services, the scope of the exemptions provided for in the current directive, the rules on the organisation and conduct of investment firms, the organisational requirements applicable to trading venues, the powers of the competent authorities, sanctions and the rules applicable to third country firms.
in writing. the alignment of the regulation on community statistics on the trading of goods between member states strengthens the coherence of european legislation with the new institutional framework. it seems to me appropriate to seek to streamline the production of community statistics on trade in goods between member states, in particular by clarifying the definition of statistical value. however, it is important that the exchange of data does not impose excessive administrative and financial burdens on member states and the competitiveness of companies established in the european union.
in writing. the report deals in particular with the modalities for the collection of annual statistics on trade and exchange between member states, which are commendable principles. but this is a transfer of power to the commission: an illegitimate and undemocratic body. moreover, the guarantees on confidentiality are too weak, whereas this is a major issue for having accurate and therefore reliable statistics. the free movement of goods is well-intentioned and does not represent an additional administrative burden. but the context of "low cost" or even "free communication of information" is absurd and illusory. public statistical quality comes at a price and must be afforded. i'm not going to.
in writing. i abstained on this regulation which amends certain requirements concerning the provision of investment services, the scope of the exemptions provided for in the current directive, the rules on the organisation and conduct of investment firms, the organisational requirements applicable to trading venues, the powers of the competent authorities, sanctions and the rules applicable to third country firms.
in writing. this draft resolution outlines a regulation on securities transactions and central securities depositories (csds). but the commission wants to regulate these areas only to achieve the single market and to ensure free competition. the draft resolution, which calls for better regulation at eu level, removes control from the member states over the national central securities depository. i therefore vote against this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which will make financial markets safer and more efficient by establishing uniform requirements for regulations and central securities depositories (csds). the aim of this text is to remedy the lack of security and efficiency of securities settlement operations and to remove the obstacles to the functioning of the internal market resulting from divergences between the national regulations applicable to these operations and the activities of csds, which ensure the functioning of the settlement systems.
in writing. this text sets requirements for marine equipment to bring it into line with international safety standards, for example by introducing enhanced control mechanisms. in particular, he pays particular attention to the tests prior to launching. i particularly welcome the introduction of a declaration of conformity which must be kept for ten years. this is a necessary step towards greater safety for european ships.
in writing. the report aims to promote the use of marine instruments complying with international safety standards on ships flying the flag of a member state of the european union. that's good. it lays down the responsibility of the flag state to ensure that only duly approved instruments are carried on board ships flying its flag. this measure of respect for the sovereignty of states seems logical. but to be effective, it should be accompanied by a drastic fight against the measures taken by some eu member states which offer flags of convenience (such as malta) or protection measures against unfair competition which endangers maritime safety and the marine environment. i'm not going to.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive, which aims to strengthen the mechanisms for implementing and monitoring its application, in order to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market for marine equipment, and to strengthen maritime safety measures. it aims to simplify the regulatory environment by ensuring the harmonised application and implementation of the international maritime organisation (imo) requirements throughout the union.
in writing. several recent disasters (erika, concordia, etc.) have reminded us of the importance of preventive measures in maritime safety. the most effective measures will be taken at european level. i therefore welcome the adoption of this directive which should both simplify the approval procedures for marine equipment and make the controls on such equipment more efficient. parliament has secured the retention of the reference to electronic labels, which will facilitate the fight against counterfeiting. these new provisions guarantee safer and more environmentally friendly ships and reduce administrative costs for our companies and administrations.
in writing. european harmonisation of legislation on pressure equipment is justified. it seems to me important to adapt these laws to the common framework for the marketing of products and to the new provisions introduced for the classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures. such a measure will in particular help to increase the confidence of producers and consumers in these pressure equipment products.
in writing. i supported this legislative report on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to the making available on the market of pressure equipment, as it allows for a technical alignment of the existing directive 97/23/ec with two texts previously adopted by the european parliament (the 2008 decision on a common framework for the marketing of products and the 2008 regulation on the classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures). the aim of this alignment is to make european legislation on health and safety more effective. the text adopted by the plenary confirms an agreement reached in the trilogue between the three institutions, the european parliament, the european commission and the council.
in writing. this report amends the european commission's proposal to revise the product harmonisation directive in the context of the implementation of the new legislative framework adopted in 2008. the text concerns pressure equipment, i.e. all equipment for the production and storage of vapours or gases at a pressure higher than atmospheric pressure. all of these equipment can present a significant risk in the event of a failure. the adoption of these texts will strengthen producer and consumer confidence by clarifying the obligations of economic operators. it will also provide member state authorities with more effective tools to carry out market surveillance checks, which will lead to an overall reduction in non-compliant and dangerous products on the market. nevertheless, the aim is as always to achieve the internal market by promoting competition. i'm not going to.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive which recasts directive 97/23/ec of the european parliament and of the council on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to pressure equipment. the text includes measures to address the problem of non-compliance by clarifying the obligations of economic operators and setting stricter traceability requirements. it also introduces measures to ensure the quality of the work of conformity assessment bodies, by strengthening the notification requirements, a revised notification procedure, the definition of requirements for notifying authorities and stricter information obligations.
in writing. this is the recast of the brussels i regulation on international jurisdiction. this regulation lays down the rules on the recognition and enforcement of judgments given by courts of other member states. for the purposes of the brussels i regulation, the unified patent court and the benelux court of justice will have to be treated in the same way as 'member state courts'. since the question of patentability of the living organism was not resolved when the unitary european patent was created in line with my position at the time, i shall abstain.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation amending regulation (eu) no[nbsp ]1215/2012 ('brussels i regulation') concerning jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters. the text is intended, first of all, to allow the entry into force of the jub agreement, since the jub agreement makes the entry into force of the agreement conditional on the entry into force of the amendment to regulation (ec) no 1215/2012. the purpose of this regulation is also to ensure that the agreement and the protocol amending the benelux treaty of 1965 are compatible with the brussels i regulation.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to define the new regulation on the organisation of a labour force sample survey in the european community, in order to bring it into line with the treaty on the functioning of the european union. one of the objectives of the european union is to work towards full employment and social progress. such a text will enable us to have reliable statistics and surveys on the situation of employed and unemployed workers in order to combat unemployment more effectively, while respecting data protection and privacy.
in writing. the advantages (subsidies to the national statistical institutes and the desire to have reliable and comparable labour market data) do not compensate for the strong disadvantages of such a proposal: the increase in the power of the commission, an illegitimate, undemocratic and blindly liberal body, will have the consequence of imposing themes of the complementary modules on the national statistical institutes (employment survey of insee in france). given the lack of interest shown by the european authorities in tax niches, the limitation of very high wages or the fight against precariousness, it is better for french statistics to retain sovereignty in the choice of the contents of its surveys. i abstain in order not to block the funds which could be made available for the development of the national statistical institutes but refuse to vote in favour, in order not to be forced to follow the commission's dictates even in our employment statistics, even down to the sample size!
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which aligns council regulation (ec) no[nbsp]577/98 on the organisation of a labour force sample survey in the community with the treaty on the functioning of the eu (commission delegated and implementing powers) and incorporates a provision on financing into the regulation.
in writing. this text ensures adequate funding for the activities of the european maritime safety agency (emsa) in the field of combating pollution at sea. this agency became essential after the erika oil tanker disaster. i therefore think it is important that it should be able to benefit from an adequate financial envelope to carry out its actions in favour of environmental protection.
in writing. this text lays down the tasks and budget of the european maritime safety agency. it gives the agency three new tasks, two to extend its action to pollution from oil and gas installations and one to intervene in the maritime space of non-eu states. the budget allocated by the commission (€165 million by 2020) was totally inadequate to deal with these new tasks. parliament proposes to increase this budget by eur 25 million over the period. that's good. but i cannot support a text which is preparing to deal with future disasters arising from the exploitation of offshore hydrocarbons, which i want banned. i'm not going to.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which will provide financial security, over a multiannual period, for the financing of the tasks assigned to the european maritime safety agency (emsa) in the field of combating marine pollution. this new envelope is intended to enable the european maritime safety agency (emsa) to maintain its network of 17 pollution control vessels spread over most european maritime areas, thus strengthening the capacity of states affected by marine pollution to intervene. these ships can intervene within 24 hours. states may apply for this assistance through the community civil protection mechanism. the emsa provides financial cover for vessels while they are on standby but the cost of cleaning operations is borne by the member states. the agency also provides satellite monitoring and detection of oil pollution.
in writing. this paper sets out how the european union can help create an environment favourable to job creation by enterprises, companies and start-ups. it is essential to focus on smes, which are the real backbone of our economies. encouraging smes to research and innovation is essential to achieving such a job boosting objective. the european union must also focus more on training and education. the skills mismatch is a real problem at a time of considerable unemployment and 1.85 million jobs are currently unfilled in the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to encourage innovative initiatives for entrepreneurs. with an average rate of 11% in the member states, unemployment is a priority and citizens expect the european union to provide concrete responses. in view of this, europe must create a favourable environment for smes, which are the main creators of jobs. we need to develop the knowledge of smes and micro-enterprises for access to finance, and encourage the development of entrepreneurship among the youngest. we also need to strengthen the skills and training of our workforce, which is a key element of our competitiveness. finally, it should be stressed that the development of smes and the creation of jobs require the reduction of the bureaucratic burdens that stifle them.
in writing. the report suggests ways to build a business-friendly environment for growth and employment. the banal litany of the liberal creed. nothing new, the solutions proposed are always the same. these include: reducing 'burdens', tax relief, removing regulatory barriers to labour mobility, keeping older workers in the labour market and developing entrepreneurship through the 'erasmus for young entrepreneurs' programme. in short, it is about "removing unnecessary barriers that impose unreasonable costs on businesses and prevent them from developing". i am voting against these liberal recipes, whose failures are evident wherever they are introduced.
in writing. public policies for economic growth are nothing without the help of the private sector. we cannot achieve the recovery of the european economy by public policies alone. we also need the companies. they are the real job creators. we must help businesses to unlock their full potential for creating jobs. we see, for example, the important role of smes in innovation and growth. improving access to finance, encouraging entrepreneurship and adapting the regulatory framework will be the way out of the crisis. i am glad that i voted in favour of this report. it stresses the importance of combining public policies and private sector improvement in managing an unprecedented crisis.
in writing. currently, 18[nbsp] to 28[nbsp]% of students in the eu have little access to and use of the internet, either at school or at home. these provisions for the development of new teaching techniques and resources would not only be of use to pupils and students but also to adult learners in any vocational training. it is also a useful tool for facilitating the learning of foreign languages. the modernisation of teaching tools is necessary, as long as it gives priority to the so-called fundamental teachings. this is what this text encourages.
in writing. what should be the role of information and communication technologies in education? the report says that this will help to reduce the "costs" of the public system further and equip future workers with "skills adapted to the future labour market". i am opposed to the narrow, utilitarian and restrictive view of this social democrat rapporteur. digital technology, and in particular free educational resources, are not just skills but can and should be a comprehensive tool for training future citizens and raising the level of skills of workers. it is also essential to explain how to use this tool to understand the social debates it raises. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report which responds to the suggestions made by the european commission. this report supports the european commission's proposals to: improve the recognition of skills acquired online and support the acquisition of digital skills by teachers, encourage open access to publicly funded teaching materials and improve broadband connectivity and ict equipment in classrooms.
in writing. some skills are essential in the labour market and yet are not taught sufficiently or properly. this is the case for digital skills, for example: it is estimated that 90% of jobs will require digital skills by 2020. but today, 40%[nbsp] of europeans aged 16 to 74 say they have limited or no skills in information and communication technologies (ict). open and free online training opportunities are effective ways of responding, as they allow for tailor-made training. indeed, these new technologies have enabled education and training institutions to reach thousands of learners in the union, including in the outermost regions, and around the world. i supported this report because it makes concrete proposals for developing this new type of education at european level, which seems to me to be a positive consequence of recent developments in the harmonization of vocational qualifications, but also of the deepening of the internal market.
in writing. the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), signed in 1973, aims to ensure that international trade in wild animal and plant specimens does not threaten their survival. trade must not undermine the preservation of biodiversity and that is why i voted in favour of this text, which is simply a legal update following the adoption of the lisbon treaty.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the groote report on the protection of species of fauna and flora through the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). the aim of the convention is to ensure that international trade in wild animals and plants does not endanger their survival. the species covered by cites are grouped into three lists. each list corresponding to a distinct degree of protection. the amendments made by the recast of council regulation (ec) no 338/97 are all motivated by the need to update the proposal following the adoption of the treaty of lisbon by replacing the obsolete provisions in the area of comitology.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to reform legislation on the protection of wild fauna and flora by controlling trade in them. regularly updated regulations on such trade are relevant because they concern a sensitive area: namely the fauna and flora that surround us, including endangered species. clearer and more comprehensive regulations will provide better protection for wild fauna and flora. the commission's role in the implementation of the treaty is to ensure that the union's institutions and bodies are able to take the necessary steps to ensure that the union's objectives are met.
in writing. i am pleased that the report on the protection of wild fauna and flora by controlling trade in them has been adopted. it is a recast of the existing regulation to enable the european commission to exercise the implementing powers conferred on it by the lisbon treaty to establish, for example, the modalities of restrictions on the import of species. parliament called for the commission's action in this area to take the form of delegated acts and not implementing acts. negotiations with the council will continue during the next parliamentary term.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to protect the health of european plants and flora by strengthening prevention, surveillance and the means of action in the event of outbreaks of organisms harmful to plants in the european union. the report proposes, among other things, to give parliament more powers to establish the list of priority pests, to strengthen public information when buying plants, and to better regulate online sales. finally, it improves border control procedures to prevent consignments of infested plants from circulating freely on the internal market.
in writing. i fully support the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cities). while the draft report allows for more effective operational implementation of the convention in some respects, the substance of the text remains an application of the lisbon treaty which aims to transfer the competences of the member states to the european commission. this is not acceptable without democratic control. especially when you know the lobbying efforts for the trade in protected species. i shall abstain on that text.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which introduces a limited number of amendments to the commission's proposal as regards the commission's implementing powers. these powers will be conferred on the commission in particular as regards the definition of the presentation, model and format of certain documents, including licences, import notifications and certificates to be issued.

in writing. i voted in favour of the hübner report authorising portugal to apply a reduced rate of excise duty until 31 december 2013 in the autonomous region of madeira and the azores to rum and liqueurs and spirits produced and consumed there. this low rate is justified by the small size and fragmentation of farms and their low level of mechanization, which undermines the economic dynamism of these outermost regions. it helps to offset the extra cost of transporting raw materials and installing equipment in these remote island regions. the renewal of that authorisation is justified in order to avoid hindering the development of those outermost regions without distorting competition within the internal market.

in writing. the commission authorises france to apply, until 1 july 2014, exemptions or reductions from the 'grant de mer' tax for a number of products manufactured in its outermost regions. the aim is to increase competitiveness and to offset the additional production costs resulting from remoteness, dependence on raw materials and energy, the need to build up larger stocks, the small size of the local market and the underdeveloped export activity. france has requested that a differentiated taxation system similar to the one currently in place be maintained until 31 december 2020. however, the commission considers that the examination of the lists of products for which france wishes to apply a differentiated taxation system is a very long task which cannot be completed before the expiry of the scheme on 1 july 2014. the absence of any proposal before that date would risk creating a legal vacuum in that it would prohibit the application of any differentiated taxation in the french outermost regions. the commission has therefore decided to extend these exemptions for a further period of six months before a new proposal is made. i vote for it.

in writing. posted workers are employees who come to work temporarily in a european union country other than their country of origin. the system applicable to these workers was laid down by a european directive in 1996. today, despite the european legislative framework, many abuses are being observed: the construction, agriculture and services sectors are particularly affected by the use of underpaid labour, thanks to the use of various schemes to evade controls (intermediary companies, subcontracting), which are also too infrequent. these abuses must be combated in order to prevent social dumping. this is the purpose of the reform, which strengthens the rules on controls, improves mutual assistance between the various competent authorities and clarifies joint and several liability in the case of subcontracting, so that it is no longer used as a means of circumventing the rules. i fully support these reforms and have voted in favour of this new directive on the posting of workers.
in writing. the agreement on the posting of workers is a major step forward in the fight against social dumping and unfair competition. the definition of a posted worker will finally be common to the 28 member states in order to fill the gaps opened by the lack of harmonisation; administrative cooperation between states will be established to prevent fraud; states will have to exchange information on the reality of service providers' activity in order to put an end to letterbox companies; the authorities will be able to require proof from posted workers themselves and not just from companies, sometimes empty shells, to verify that wages and working conditions are in accordance with the law; contracting authorities on a construction site will have to monitor the practices of their subcontractors and will be punished in the event of abuse. now we must go further, by creating a european mobile force of labour inspectors and a minimum wage throughout europe. above all, the treaty must enshrine the primacy of social rights over the freedoms of the internal market. that is why i voted for the compromise today.
in writing. - this agreement is a victory against social dumping and the exploitation of workers in europe, which is currently made possible by the implementation of the posting of workers directive, as was seen with the flamanville case. the compromise reached is not perfect, and we would have liked to go further in its binding dimension, but we have been faced with the stubborn refusal of some member states to make further concessions. among the advances made in relation to the current unacceptable situation, i would point out: the establishment of cooperation between states to prevent fraud; the exchange of information between states on the reality of the activity of service providers to put an end to the phenomenon of letterbox companies; the strengthening of controls in each country with the obligation for posted workers to provide documents proving that their remuneration and working conditions are in accordance with the law; and finally, the fact that contractors on a construction site will, throughout europe, have to check the practices of their subcontractors and be held accountable for fraudulent actions: this will be a powerful lever to ensure compliance throughout the subcontracting chain.
in writing. the posting of workers directive contains many loopholes which allow unscrupulous employers to bring in european workers without respecting labour law and current practices, and there was an urgent need for a major overhaul of this text. the text adopted merely clarifies the spirit of the directive and maintains the limits imposed on the states so that their controls do not interfere with freedom of service: the control measures remain governed by a list (which is not exhaustive), and joint liability between the undertaking and the subcontractors is maintained only in the building sector and is limited. the amendments tabled by my group to give the states the freedom to put in place the controls they deem necessary and to hold companies accountable for the practices of their subcontractors have not been adopted, so that the savage competition between workers is maintained and massive fraud will continue. that is why i refused to support this text. one of the first acts of the parliament elected in may must be to reopen this dossier to send a strong signal that dumping cannot continue to be the only horizon of european economic and social policy.
in writing. this directive on the posting of workers is a catch-all. the liberals and the ps are pretending to do something. in reality, they are organising the continuation of unfair competition and the over-exploitation of posted workers. the 1996 framework directive remains unchanged. this text is only an implementing directive intended to cover up the most intolerable. the french socialist party has been hit hard again. the french president has agreed to a european deal at a discount. and the ps chair of the committee on employment and social affairs betrayed her committee by giving the parliament's agreement to the heads of state on this content at a discount, when the committee was much more demanding. ms bérès was to demand that joint and several liability between contractors and subcontractors apply to all sectors and to all subcontractors. it accepted that it applied only to a subcontractor and only to the building sector. this hypocrisy is unbearable. the over-exploitation will continue. i vote against it. finally, to protect the rights of workers, we must break with the 1996 directive and disobey it.
in writing. although there are some substantial advances, the new 'posted workers' directive still leaves social dumping with a bright future, so i voted against it. in 60% of cases, the minimum provisions of posted workers' contracts are not respected, the small adjustments planned will not change the fate of posted workers (who see their rights violated) or the social dumping that this regulation organizes. social security and employer's contributions are still not paid in the country of secondment, or at least are not paid in the same way as in the country of secondment. there is no mention of respect for the trade union rights of posted workers. the collective agreements applicable in the country of secondment are still not respected or recognised.
in writing. i voted for this text. this is the first victory against social dumping in europe. several advances have been made and have therefore merited our support: cooperation will be established between member states to prevent fraud. it will now be possible to require posted workers themselves, and not just companies, which are sometimes empty shells, documents, in french, proving that their pay and working conditions are in accordance with the law. contractors on construction sites throughout europe will have to check the practices of their subcontractors and will be held accountable for fraudulent actions. this was the best compromise possible and available to provide an immediate response to the problem of the posting of workers. i will undertake in the next legislature to reform this issue more deeply, as the socialists have committed to in their manifesto for the elections of 25 may 2014.
in writing. - in a europe where national social policies are not harmonised, we must do everything possible to restore fair competition between workers from the different member states. the posting of workers by social dumping between the countries making up the union. fraud and abuse of all kinds are common in this field. it 's time to end this ! i am glad that i voted in favour of this report. it is by strengthening controls, empowering supply chains and clarifying the legislation in this area that we can begin to put an end to social dumping in europe. this legislation will be a first step towards convergence of social policies. i do not want a europe which leaves a part of the workforce behind in favour of unfair competition. but i want a europe that puts everyone on an equal footing.
in writing. this report deals with the issue of non-eu nationals posted to provide services within the european union. it has the advantage of strengthening the protection of such posted workers while also strengthening the protection of the union's internal market. the text makes it possible to combat fraud and, consequently, to combat social dumping. such a report is a major asset for the european union, the internal market and employment. that is why i voted for it.
in writing. given the many cases of fraud in the 1996 posting of workers directive, it was both urgent and essential to revise the text. the amendments will help to respond to abuses across europe, particularly in border regions. i could therefore only support this report which seeks to revise the directive which will affect 175,000 french employees. the new measures will make it possible to define clearly the status of posted worker and the official documents justifying it; the commission will also be discussing the prevention and sanctioning of abuses. i have supported the principle of joint and several liability of contractors towards their subcontractors in the event of non-compliance with their wage obligations. this principle is mandatory for the postal services sector, which is particularly affected by fraud, and may be extended to other sectors depending on the transposition into national law by the member states. finally, complaint procedures will be transparent and simplified for posted workers in the event of abuse or fraud.
in writing. it was imperative to vote on this text before the european elections: it is proof that we are mobilising against the flaws in the 1996 directive on posted workers. the detachment status is the stone in the shoe of european free movement. the abuses are so numerous that they have tarnished the very image of european integration: underpaid workers, no controls, safety standards not respected, unfair competition, lack of coordination between administrations, impunity and social dumping. construction workers, already in crisis in many member states, have particularly suffered from the shortcomings of the legislation. this competition is just as fierce and deadly in the border areas as it is in my region on the spanish border. the reform strengthens the possibility of controls and makes both the project owners and their subcontractors responsible. however, the text only partially addresses the problems of crossborder employment: to establish healthy competition that is beneficial for all workers in europe.
in writing. the new directive on the posting of workers, which was the result of a compromise between the european parliament and the council, will help to correct the weaknesses of the 1996 directive which helped to facilitate intra-community social dumping. it is necessary to distinguish clearly between actual situations of secondment and attempts to circumvent the law and to enable the national authorities to control secondments better. in particular, workers must be in possession of proof of their posting, such as a social security certificate, and be able to assert their rights more effectively. companies will be responsible for providing the national authorities with documents indicating the country in which they pay their taxes and contributions and where they recruit. these measures are a first step in the right direction but they are far from sufficient. it is now necessary to develop european legislation and to ensure that employers pay their social security contributions in the country where they work and that the latter benefit in their country from the rights acquired in the member state where they are posted and pay their contributions. this is the only way to put an end to social dumping in europe.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the directive on the posting of workers, which is a modest step forward, without renouncing a thorough revision of the directive. the council of the european union, which is mainly right-wing, was pushed to its limits to reach the most ambitious agreement possible. among the advances will be cooperation between states to prevent fraud. the controls will be strengthened: it will now be possible to require posted workers themselves, and not just companies that are sometimes empty shells, documents proving that their pay and working conditions are in accordance with the law. finally, contractors on a construction site will have to check the practices of their subcontractors throughout europe and will be held accountable for fraudulent actions: this will be a powerful lever to ensure compliance throughout the subcontracting chain. i regret the vote of the gue meps who preferred to vote against this progress rather than risk maintaining the current situation, that of a vacuum. it should be noted that martin schulz has committed himself to a thorough review of this directive if he is elected.
in writing. cultural heritage is a real asset which the european union must protect and promote. i voted in favour of this draft revision of the directive on the return of cultural objects unlawfully removed from the territory of a member state because the european union can bring a great deal of added value in the fight against trafficking and those who seek to profit from it, but to do this, the existing rules need to be modernised.
in writing. this text aims to amend council directive 93/7/eec of 15 march 2013 on the return of cultural objects unlawfully removed from the territory of a member state. according to this directive, only cultural property classified as 'national treasure' within the meaning of article 36 of the tfeu may be returned, that is to say, objects of artistic, historical or archaeological value. according to the commission, trafficking in cultural goods, including national treasures, has increased considerably in recent years. this is the third largest source of revenue for organized crime. the aim of the revision is to increase the number of restitutions of cultural property classified as 'national treasures'. the rapporteur proposes that the internal market information system (imi) be used to disseminate all information relating to cultural property that has been stolen or has been illegally removed from its territory. the concept of 'national treasury' is also to be extended by removing the thresholds for monetary value and seniority. i vote for it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive which will contribute to the protection of cultural property in the internal market by allowing member states to obtain the restitution of cultural property classified as 'national treasures'. the aim of the recast directive 93/7/eec is to enable member states to obtain the return of any cultural property classified as national treasures which has been unlawfully removed from their territory since 1993.

in writing. the tragic accident in lampedusa in october 2013, which resulted in the death of 350 migrants trying to reach europe, is far from an isolated case. indeed, it is estimated that several thousand have died in the mediterranean since 2000. the union must avoid such tragedies at all costs by setting up an immigration police and increased coastal surveillance. thus, the border surveillance activities of the frontex agency cannot be separated from the search and rescue obligation. it is also essential that the european values of solidarity and respect for fundamental rights guide the union's action in the field of border surveillance. intercepted migrants have often faced immense suffering and must be rescued and treated with humanity and respect. it is imperative that the european coast guard provides adequate protection to vulnerable persons, such as victims of trafficking and unaccompanied minors. they cannot send shipwrecked people back to their home countries without being sure that they will not be persecuted there. the same shall apply to the master and crew of a ship who have come to the aid of a ship in distress.

in writing. the controversy over the role of frontex, and the responsibilities involved in the agency's maritime operations, is far from new, but it has been impossible to achieve clear and binding rules in this area. i therefore supported this report which, after a legal battle and an intensive process of negotiations with the council, clarifies the rules on the interception or rescue of migrants at sea and their disembarkation. these rules should put an end to the confusion caused by differing interpretations of international law. the aim is obviously not to transform frontex into a humanitarian agency, but to provide it, within the framework of its mandate, with precise and mandatory measures in accordance with international maritime law. the success or failure of this system now depends on how it is applied. but let us not be deceived, frontex and border surveillance cannot become the alpha and omega of european migration policy. as long as the eu and its member states prefer to adopt safe and short-term responses, it is to be expected that migrants will continue to venture on increasingly dangerous routes.
