in writing. the regulations applying to 'dumped' products, i.e. products entering the european union at a price much lower than the market price, had not been revised since 1995. i have therefore supported the principle of reform and actively defended the principle of a comprehensive defence against dumping: not only commercial dumping but also social and environmental dumping. the text we have adopted today, which i amended as a member of the committee on international trade, will form the basis of the intergovernmental discussions in the council. i hope they will reach agreement quickly so that the modernised regulations can enter into force quickly, and if possible before the end of this year.
in writing. the existing legislation governing political parties at european level and their funding was adopted in november 2003. it was amended in 2007 to allow, inter alia, the financing of european political foundations from the union budget. the aim of this regulation is to increase the visibility, recognition, effectiveness and transparency of european political parties and their accountability. i consider this to be an important step towards a genuine statute for european political parties, which i wish to see. in the meantime, i voted in favour of this new regulation, which is moving in the right direction.
in writing. - i supported the creation of a legal status for european political parties because this text will enable them to contribute more effectively to the formation of a democratic european political consciousness and to the expression of the will of the citizens of the union. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, this text should support the increased role of the european parliament in the appointment of the future president of the european commission, following a campaign by political parties at european level. it will also be possible to impose sanctions, for example, in the event of misuse of eu funds, failure to comply with reporting and transparency requirements or criminal conviction. finally, by adopting rules providing for an independent structure to register these parties, we are thus removing any challenge to the application of the rules, in particular on the verification of respect for democratic values, by populist parties which are often quick to hide behind a role of victim and incapable of taking on the slippages they are accustomed to.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague marietta giannakou on the status and funding of european political parties. the aim of this text is to modernise existing legislation by increasing the visibility, recognition, effectiveness and transparency of european political parties and their accountability. an independent authority will be set up to register political parties, monitor them and apply any sanctions. the report was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. this regulation lays down more precise criteria in the statute of european political parties. national parties must be recognised by the state in question. it also called for greater representation of women in the leading bodies of these european parties. finally, it allows the financing of campaigns on european referendums. the aim is to "help citizens better understand the link between political processes at national and european level". i regret, however, that more restrictive criteria have been introduced. the 3% threshold set at the last elections has been raised to 5% as a criterion for the founding of a european party. i abstain because of this restriction of democratic pluralism.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which will improve the regulatory and funding framework for political parties and political foundations at european level with a view to strengthening and encouraging representative democracy at eu level. the main objective of these improvements is to increase the visibility, recognition, effectiveness and transparency of european political parties and foundations and their accountability.
in writing. - at a time when european citizens are constantly demanding more transparency from us, we must provide it. the political status of european parties and their funding must be an integral part of the european legislative body. we must show our fellow citizens that the activities of european political parties are controlled by an independent body. we shall thus silence criticism of the integrity of the european union. i am glad that i voted in favour of this report. one of our tasks is to restore confidence in europe. we should not hesitate to work at it.
in writing. this proposal for a regulation accompanies the regulation on the statute and funding of european political parties and european political foundations. here too, the aim is to improve the transparency and accountability of european political parties. this regulation clarifies in particular the rules on the prevention of conflicts of interest, the remuneration of external auditors and the content of calls for tender. i think that this is a timely reform and i have therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. this report concerns the regulation on the financing of european political parties. it simplifies the granting procedures. it also allows these parties to finance campaigns in the context of referendums on european issues. we avoided the worst with the right wing, which wanted to increase the distribution of funds in proportion to the number of meps. the rule remains 15% for everyone and then 85% in proportion to the number of meps in the party (not 90% as the right-wing rapporteur wanted). this leaves little room for the smaller parties. where is democracy in this context? for these reasons i abstain.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation, which will amend the financial regulation to take account of the amendments proposed by the commission in its proposal for a regulation on the statute and funding of european political parties and european political foundations. this text introduces a new title viii in part two of the financial regulation, dedicated to contributions to european political parties, and repeals the specific provisions on european political parties currently provided for under title vi (subsidies) of part one.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which takes account of the outcome of the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework (mff) for the period 2014-2020. it concerns the reserve and emergency aid for projects financed under the connecting europe facility (cef).
in writing. this report amends several european financial regulations to adapt them to the new multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. i have fought against this austerity budget and i am also against its implementation. the aim is to adapt the financing arrangements for the connecting europe facility (the cef which finances investments in networks) and for sme funds. instruments that favour public-private partnerships at the expense of the general interest and budgetary efficiency. the report also proposes adopting a model financial regulation for public-private partnerships financed from european funds. i am absolutely opposed to this privatisation of public investment to the detriment of the long-term ecological and social interest. i therefore vote against these financial regulations.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation amending regulation (eu, euratom) no[nbsp ]966/2012 on the financial rules applicable to the general budget of the union (or financial regulation rf). these amendments will make it possible to include the deferral rules for the reserve for emergency aid and for projects financed under the connecting europe facility.
in writing. shipping is a significant contributor to co2 emissions from the transport sector. it is therefore appropriate to provide for a method of accounting for these emissions and, in a second step, to decide in the future on measures to reduce these excessive emissions. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which will make it possible to take this first important step.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which aims to monitor, report and verify co2 emissions from shipping, as part of a gradual approach to reduce these emissions. the text is thus fully in line with the commitments made by the european union to combat climate change. international shipping is the only mode of transport not yet covered by the european union's greenhouse gas emission reduction commitments. with this text, the eu can finally put in place a reliable system to achieve this objective.
in writing. this text establishes a necessary system for monitoring greenhouse gas emissions. unfortunately, the proposed system is primarily declarative. but above all, it is not based on an overall political vision which would make it possible to stop treating the different freight transport sectors separately. we need a strategy to relocate the economy and create the conditions and infrastructure for rail and shipping to flourish in the face of air and lorry transport. the ambition of this text is therefore very limited. we are far from the necessary ecological planning of transport. i shall abstain on that text.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. before any legislative initiative to reduce co2 emissions from shipping is considered, this regulation aims to put in place a reliable monitoring, reporting and verification (mrv) system. the objectives are therefore to monitor, report and verify co2 emissions from ships as part of a gradual approach to reduce these emissions.
in writing. invasive alien species (ias) are initially transported by human action outside their natural range, beyond ecological barriers, and then survive, reproduce, spread and cause serious ecological, social and economic consequences. these weee are one of the main causes of biodiversity loss and species extinction. the damage caused by eee is estimated at eur 12 billion per year within the european union. i voted in favour of this text, which establishes a framework for action to prevent, minimise and mitigate the negative impacts of invasive alien species on biodiversity and ecosystem services, in particular through an early warning system.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, the main objective of which is to establish a list of invasive alien species in order to prevent and limit their spread and thus reduce their impact. the commission proposed that this list be capped at 50 species, but parliament asked that this ceiling not be set. the compromise reached between the three institutions allows the list to be drawn up without a ceiling and by means of implementing acts. parliament and the council also proposed the creation of an independent scientific body to support the decision-making process on certain aspects of the regulation.
in writing. this text represents a further step towards preventing, reducing and mitigating the negative impacts of invasive alien species on biodiversity and ecosystem services. these invasive alien species (animals, plants, fungi, micro-organisms) are one of the main causes of biodiversity loss and the extinction of some species. the creation of a comprehensive legal framework to combat these species and to preserve biodiversity therefore appears to be an appropriate response to this situation.
in writing. - i welcome the fact that the european union has finally come up with a common regulation to combat the spread and reduce the impact of invasive alien species in europe. the aim of this regulation is to curb the growth of species which are not naturally present in the ecosystems of the european territory but which, once they are imported, cause serious damage to local biodiversity. in addition to the environmental damage, the economic losses are estimated at over 12 billion euros per year in the european union. the list of invasive alien species which will be drawn up shortly will enable member states to work in synergy on this issue which is so important for our ecosystems. the text promotes european cooperation on a problem which, like the management of natural resources, knows no frontiers.
in writing. this paper highlights the problem of invasive alien species and the danger they pose to our ecosystem. it proposes a method for monitoring these species and concrete methods of control. the aim is to list these species, to eradicate them where necessary, to prevent their spread and entry into the member states. this monitoring and management will be carried out in liaison with scientists, national and local representatives of the member states and the public. i regret, however, that the text is too timid, particularly with regard to the untreated discharge of ballast water and the fouling of ship hulls. they are by far the most important vectors of introduction of invasive alien species. nevertheless, these proposals are generally in the right direction. i vote for it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation, which aims to prevent, reduce and mitigate the negative impacts of invasive alien species (ias) on biodiversity and ecosystem services. invasive alien species (ias) are a major cause of biodiversity loss and extinction of some species. they can be vectors of disease or directly cause health problems. they damage infrastructure and leisure facilities, interfere with forestry or cause agricultural losses. the damage caused by the eea is estimated to cost the union at least eur 12 billion a year and the bill is only rising.
in writing. climate change is one of the greatest threats facing the european union and the world today. in the face of this situation, the european union and a number of its partners have committed themselves to taking measures to reduce co2 emissions through the kyoto protocol. i voted in favour of this report because it allows the kyoto protocol to be properly implemented in the years ahead and thus to reduce the consequences of man-made climate change. beyond that, it is essential that an international agreement binding on all global actors is found in paris at the end of 2015 in order to reduce co2 emissions even more effectively.
in writing. at the doha conference in 2012, a new commitment period for the kyoto protocol was introduced, from 1 january 2013 to 31 december 2020. legally binding greenhouse gas emission reduction commitments were then established for this period. this text then makes it possible to implement the technical aspects necessary for the application of the kyoto protocol. it is essential that the european union takes effective measures to meet its international commitments. the functioning of the emission trading system must therefore be brought into line with the efforts to be made by each member state.
in writing. this proposal for a regulation concerns the technical rules necessary for the implementation of the kyoto protocol in the european union after 2012. the objectives of the european union are insufficient in comparison with the efforts to be made. this is all the more so after the publication of the latest ipcc report, which calls for profound and rapid changes in production and trade patterns to prevent warming well above 2 degrees. the eu would need to reduce emissions by at least 30% by 2020 while still meeting the 20% target. the implementation of these targets in europe also relies on the carbon market, which is totally ineffective in reducing emissions in a sustainable and rapid manner, and thus in combating global warming. this european implementation is therefore totally inadequate in the face of the increased ecological emergency. i deplore this european inertia and i call for ecological planning, the only effective and lasting response to global warming. under these conditions i abstain.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation, which aims to ensure the technical implementation of the kyoto protocol in the european union after 2012. this text establishes coherent rules to ensure the technical implementation of the kyoto protocol in the european union after 2012. it will facilitate the successful joint implementation of the commitments of the union, its member states and iceland.
in writing. the directive on the protection of the union's financial interests aims to establish the measures necessary to prevent and combat fraud and other illegal activities affecting the union's financial interests by developing common definitions of criminal offences and penalties. fraud cases are estimated to be worth nearly 600 million euros a year. this proposal for a directive must be understood in the wider context of all the commission's proposals for harmonized criminal law. i am convinced that the fight against fraud must be conducted at european level and that cooperation in criminal matters is essential. i voted in favour of this directive.
in writing. the damage suffered by the eu budget each year as a result of massive fraud is immense and requires measures to ensure effective protection of the financial interests of the union. despite the development of the eu acquis in this area, member states have adopted divergent rules, often resulting in differences in the levels of protection provided by their domestic legal systems. the definition of offences common to all member states should make it possible to combat fraud more effectively. this is what this text rightly proposes.
in writing. fraud and other illegal activities affect the financial interests of the union and therefore constitute a serious problem detrimental to the union budget. the commission's legislative proposal is a step in the right direction by providing for provisions which aim to bring national legal systems closer together, including criminal law measures, to combat fraud and other illegal activities. the rapporteur also proposes to reduce the threshold for infringements from eur 10 000 to eur 5 000, so that member states may, if they so wish, provide for non-criminal sanctions for fraud involving lower amounts. but as long as the fight against fraud is confined to the borders of tax havens, it will have little weight. the free movement of capital, which the european union is promoting, is a major factor in the development of fraud. i therefore abstained on this text in order not to endorse these inconsequential rotating assemblies.
in writing. this report gives a discharge on the 2012 budget of the parliament, which represents only 1 % of the eu budget and 20 % of its administrative expenditure. it is nevertheless clear that despite this 'rigor', the cracks in the ceiling of the brussels chamber of deputies almost caused a 'major catastrophe threatening human lives', in this case the lives of members of parliament and therefore my own! it also shows that the parliament's pubs and restaurants are running a deficit despite regular price increases. it is positive that this report also raises the alarm about the violations of labour rights suffered by bailiffs and local agents employed in brussels and strasbourg. this diagnosis is unfortunately undermined by the report's recommendations, which swear by the management and audit methods of private companies, without ever demonstrating their superiority in terms of the efficiency of public spending. finally, in its logic of blind pursuit and limited to extra costs, this report relays the anglo-saxon arguments against the seat of parliament in strasbourg, whereas the seat in brussels is so dangerous, abusive and costly. i therefore vote against.
the committee on budgets mr president, i shall speak in proportion to the number of members who are prepared to applaud me. i would like to speak first, with your permission, on behalf of jean-luc dehaene, who is the co-rapporteur with anne jensen, and who, unfortunately, is held back by a serious illness. i would like to take this opportunity, on behalf of the whole of parliament, to wish him a speedy and full recovery. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are to vote today on a small package of legislation which is the 'resources and financing' part of the budgetary framework for the next seven years, following the political agreement reached between parliament and the council with the commission at the end of last year. the treaty of lisbon brings two major changes to the legal provisions on the union's own resources. first, it provides for the possibility of establishing new categories of own resources or of abolishing an existing category. secondly, it enables the council to adopt implementing measures for the union's own resources system. unfortunately, the powers of parliament remain relatively limited. as regards the council's decision, parliament is merely consulted and, as regards the implementing regulation, it has the power of approval by a qualified majority or rejection by a majority. originally, in parallel with the presentation of its proposals for the financial perspective in terms of categories of expenditure, the european commission, as requested by parliament - and i thank commissioner lewandowski for this - had tabled comprehensive proposals for updating and thoroughly revising the own resources system by making full use of the new provisions of the treaty, by abolishing the current vat-based own resource and replacing it with a more modern vat resource and, above all, with the financial transaction tax, which would have limited the share of national contributions to the financing of the union budget to a maximum of 40%. as you will recall, the vast majority of members of the european parliament supported the commission's proposals from the outset, believing that they provided a solid basis for fundamental reform. unfortunately, the draft decision adopted by the council did not take this into account. it merely implements the conclusions of the european council of 7 and 8 february 2013 and amends the previous decision on resources, rather aggravating its shortcomings. for example, the own resources ceiling would be reduced slightly from 1.24% to 1.23% of gross national income for payment appropriations, and for commitment appropriations from 1.31% to 1.29%. not only are the rebates not abolished, namely the uk rebate and the rebate enjoyed by austria, germany, the netherlands and sweden, but the system is even extended in a slightly different form to denmark. as a result, we have a system of funding which is absurd and incomprehensible to the citizens. it is also deeply unfair between countries because it can be said, roughly speaking, that the richer a country is, the less it contributes to the financing of the european budget. this is the first scandal parliament has wanted to put an end to. parliament has already expressed its disappointment that the council did not want to deal with the system of reform of resources in the context of the negotiation of the multiannual framework. we have the opportunity to talk about it today. of course, our rapporteurs could have proposed a totally negative position to express the bad mood of parliament to the full, but a parliament does not express its bad mood, a parliament decides or participates in the decision. therefore, in the votes that the rapporteurs and the committee on budgets propose in plenary, we do not propose to reject or defer, we propose to approve but with amendments and a legislative resolution that recalls the position of parliament and its expectations of the work of the high-level group that was set up a few days ago, with the participation of commissioner lewandowski and the greek presidency [nbsp ] which i am pleased to welcome, under the chairmanship of mario monti, former italian prime minister and former european commissioner for italy. this high-level group is responsible, in accordance with the agreement reached in the negotiations on the multiannual framework, for reviewing the entire own resources system in order to present to parliament and the council proposals which may be taken into account in the mid-term review of the multiannual framework in 2016-2017 after they have been submitted to national parliaments. we are reminded in these amendments of the guidelines, the political guidelines for this year. we respect national sovereignty in tax matters. we proclaim the principle of constancy. the tax burden of the taxpayer must remain the same. the fact that a tax or a burden is transferred to the european level does not mean that the taxpayer has to pay more. on the contrary, he should, whenever possible, pay less. this will relieve national budgets of a burden which has become very heavy and give the union its full financial autonomy. that is the spirit in which the committee on budgets has tabled amendments and will recommend a favourable vote on these texts.
mr president, commissioner, our mandate is coming to an end and we will continue to have a bitter taste of failure on this central question for the whole institution, that of its budgetary resources. this failure is reflected in a figure, that of a multiannual financial framework which is much lower than that of the previous period. this is the first time in the history of the european union that the european budget has been reduced so much. this backsliding is not just financial, it's political. does the european parliament share responsibility for this failure? yes, and it's big! the two major parties, the right and the left, which dominate the majorities, have feigned protest. but they finally gave in without resistance. the summit of heads of state held in brussels in february 2013 took no account, not even marginally, of the wishes expressed by parliament. the most striking example is the question of own resources, which we are discussing today. the european parliament could say no. this power is derived from the treaty of lisbon, which entered into force in 2009. his duty was to enforce it. by refusing to vote on the multiannual financial framework as proposed, by saying 'no', we would have given a strong boost to the european debate and would have put this issue back at the heart of the forthcoming election campaign. we would then have made it clear to the public opinion in europe that voting in the european elections could change the course of events.

objectives are contradictory and our fellow citizens misunderstand it. we therefore have an obligation - if we want europe to fulfil the functions for which it is so badly needed - to find a way of financing that relieves the member states, that allows for the financing of community policies and that prevents our great european leaders in the european council from constantly contradicting themselves between ambitious announcements and pitiful results.

in writing. article 226 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) provides that 'the european parliament may, in the exercise of its powers, at the request of one quarter of its component members, set up a temporary committee of inquiry to examine, without prejudice to the powers conferred by the treaties on other institutions or bodies, alleged contraventions or maladministration in the application of union law, unless the facts alleged are the subject of legal proceedings and for as long as the legal proceedings are not concluded'. the purpose of this regulation is to extend the scope of the right of inquiry, to authorize field investigations and to introduce new rules for the summoning and hearing of witnesses. it also aims to ensure that clearly defined offences (unreasonable refusal to provide requested documents, unreasonable refusal to answer a summons or to appear at a hearing as a witness, false testimony and bribery of witnesses) are subject to appropriate sanctions. i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. - i have supported this report because i believe that, just as the treaty of lisbon extended the european parliament's powers as a co-legislator, we must give it stronger means to investigate effectively possible breaches of union law or mismanagement in the implementation of its provisions. while we would have liked to have been even more ambitious, this text is still the result of a compromise with a council and a european commission that feared that parliament would turn its political power into a judicial body, which was not the case at all. but this is an important step forward from the 1995 decision which has so far allowed the european parliament to set up three committees of inquiry. the new powers will therefore include the possibility for a committee of inquiry to carry out any type of inquiry and to obtain the assistance of the national authorities, if necessary, in order to enable its conclusions to be based exclusively on evidence. the introduction of the rule that member states will be obliged to sanction non-compliance with this regulation is also a definite step forward.
in writing. beyond the good intentions displayed to strengthen democratic legitimacy and parliamentary control , this motion for a resolution does not do much good. it should be remembered that committees of inquiry are the basis for drafting a resolution which is not binding, particularly for the commission. in short, the follow-up to the investigations is very limited, for example in the case of spying on the institutions of the european union by the united states, as in others. but worse, under the guise of strengthening and extending the european parliament's powers of scrutiny, this proposal is actually aimed at strengthening the power of the major groups in the european parliament. committees of inquiry may be set up only at the request of one quarter of the members of the european parliament. with the exception of the two groups which co-chair the european parliament, most groups will never be able to meet such a condition. in short, it is a matter of locking down the system to silence certain groups. i am voting against this further reduction in parliamentary powers.
in writing. this own-initiative report helps to advance the debate on the essential relationship between the european parliament and national parliaments. this relationship is crucial for the proper functioning of european democracy, as it brings european policies closer to european citizens. it has been strengthened by the lisbon treaty and will probably need to be further developed in the coming years.

in writing. this motion for a resolution concerns the relations between the european parliament and the national parliaments, presented as part of a 'european parliamentary system'. the aim is to consolidate and enhance these relations, based on the idea that national parliaments are bodies not only for their own state but also for the european union as a whole, since the governments represented in the council are accountable to them. in fact, with this motion for a resolution, the european oligarchy wants to intensify its work of annihilating democratic sovereignty. the proposal is intended to continue the work of placing national parliaments under the supervision of the european parliament, allowing the authors of the proposal to make recommendations, or even injunctions, to national parliaments on their tasks, powers or way of working. behind the avowed ambition of a 'europeanization' of national parliaments, the authors of the proposal seek to achieve a much less avowed objective: the subjection of the last frameworks of popular sovereignty, the national parliaments, to the bureaucratic standards of the european union. i vote against it.
in writing. this report is an assessment of the relations between the european parliament and national parliaments. protocol no 1 to the lisbon treaty deals with the role of national parliaments in the european union and the principle of subsidiarity is a fundamental principle of the european union. i supported this report which stresses the role of national parliaments in the legislative process of the european union. the text emphasises the role of cosac (conference of bodies specialised in community affairs), which must be maintained and strengthened. the commission is also proposing to strengthen interparliamentary relations by revising the rules of procedure and making more resources available. finally, it is necessary to strengthen meetings between political groups and european parties within this interparliamentary cooperation.

in writing. the budget of the european union is supplied by different types of resources. currently, national contributions to the union budget, based on gross national income, represent 74% of total union revenue. at the same time, the vat resource represents 11% of total union revenue and has developed in such a way that it is also perceived as a national contribution to the budget. the budget of the european union therefore has no financial autonomy and reinforces the logic of 'just return'. moreover, given the current austerity measures, some member states are reluctant to increase their contribution to the budget. in view of this information and the present context, a direct own resources system for the union is the only solution that can be envisaged. i supported this report which calls for reform of the european union's own resources system to make it simpler, more transparent and fairer. these own resources could be focused on a genuine vat-based resource and a financial transaction tax. a dedicated high level group on this issue has been set up, in line with parliament's agreement on the mff 2014-2020, and should provide proposals on the own resources system by 2016.

in writing. the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was established to respond to natural disasters and to show european solidarity towards regions facing a difficult situation. this fund is a success and an essential element of solidarity at european level. i therefore supported this text, which aims to extend its scope to natural disasters which occur over a long period of time, such as droughts.
in writing. - the european union solidarity fund was set up to respond to natural disasters and to show european solidarity towards regions of europe facing a difficult situation. the fund was set up in response to the many floods in central europe during the summer of 2002. it is used to help member states and candidate countries affected by natural disasters. from the very beginning of the fund's existence, it was clear that changes were needed to make it more effective. the instrument is generally meeting its objectives well, but its effectiveness is considered insufficient, and some of the criteria for the mobilisation of the fund are considered too complex or not clear enough. the procedure for granting aid is too long, since it is usually paid about a year after the disaster. i voted in favour of this report, which makes it possible to make this major instrument of solidarity more flexible and thus more effective.
in writing. i welcome the vote on this text amending the legislation on the european union solidarity fund to improve its effectiveness. the fund was set up to enable the european union to respond to major disasters on its territory. however, it became necessary to improve the way in which they functioned and the speed with which they responded. solidarity is a european principle which we must protect and promote. i therefore particularly support the clarification of the scope of this fund in order to put an end to legal uncertainties. the commission has also made a number of proposals to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of the reform of the european union solidarity fund. the recent severe weather events in europe, particularly in south-eastern france, have highlighted the importance of having an effective financial aid system in place to deal with the damage caused. by simplifying procedures, extending application deadlines and establishing a clear eligibility threshold, the reform is moving in the right direction. regions where damage amounts to more than 1.5% of their gdp will now be able to benefit from european aid.
in writing. since 2002, the european union solidarity fund, set up to respond to natural disasters, has been used for 52[nbsp ] events, demonstrating its effectiveness. i voted in favour of this report which clarifies the scope of the directive and suggests that it be extended to natural disasters which occur over a long period of time, such as droughts. the text clarifies the eligibility criteria for regional disasters and introduces a system of advance payments. the amendments to the solidarity fund will improve the flexibility and responsiveness of the mechanism to crises. the union must be more than a common market: it must create bonds of solidarity between nations and be able to demonstrate this in the most difficult circumstances.

in writing. the report proposes that the eusf, which provides compensation for natural disasters (cyclones, tropical storms, etc.), can now be mobilised as soon as the estimated damage is equivalent to 1% of regional gdp in the ors, compared with 1.5% for the other regions of the european union. this threshold could make a difference to europe's response to the many tropical storms and cyclones that hit overseas. the situation for mayotte has also been clarified by the text which now considers it to be a nuts-2 type region. all these measures are real advances for our territories, which are on the front line of climate change, and are increasingly affected by cyclones, droughts or threatened, as in the caribbean, by earthquakes. this fund does not solve everything, but it is an expression of much-needed solidarity and will help the ors recover more easily from natural disasters. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - reform of the european union solidarity fund became an absolute necessity. this instrument was created to respond rapidly to natural disasters that occur on european territory. although the fund generally met its objectives, its effectiveness was considered insufficient. moreover, regional disasters were hardly taken into account and too often regional authorities were left helpless by a belated refusal. i am very pleased to have voted in favour of this report. the reform of the solidarity fund will clarify the scope of the fund, tighten the eligibility criteria and speed up the administrative procedure. in addition, the regulation will provide for the possibility of an advance payment of the financial assistance. this fund is a clear testimony to the european territories that need assistance the most. we must do everything possible to preserve it and to make the best use of this instrument.

in writing. some of my colleagues, with good intentions, thought they could go against nature and deny that pollen is naturally present in honey. it is as if we were to pass laws defining egg yolk as an ingredient of the egg and making it compulsory to display on that egg the characteristics of the egg yolk that is present! i am naturally aware of the important issues behind this debate... yes, i think consumers should be informed about the presence of trace amounts of gmos in food products and i fully support the rule that any ingredient containing at least 0.9% gmos should be labelled as such. but the rules here are about ingredients, not the natural constituents of food. therefore, this rule does not apply to pollen. bees sometimes forage more than 10 kilometers from their hive in fields of all kinds and... these bees have no gps, no system to avoid contact with gmos. it would have been totally irresponsible to require all beekeepers to test every pot of honey to ensure that the bees have not been exposed to gmos. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the girling report on the amendment of the honey directive. like the rapporteur, i consider honey to be a natural product of which pollen is a natural component and not an ingredient. i also think that attention should be paid to the direct and indirect effects of this commission proposal on the beekeeping sector. the vote by the european parliament means that producers will not have to bear any additional costs for the labelling of their products.
in writing. i supported this text which defined pollen as a constituent of honey and not an ingredient which can be separated from it. as i have said before, to say otherwise would have had a negative impact on the beekeeping industry. in particular, it was allegedly subject to excessive labelling requirements and testing, which would result in an increase in the price of honey, which would be detrimental to the consumer. with pollen as an ingredient, honey would have lost its natural product status. this would have opened the door to the addition of artificial products.
in writing. - i wished to vote in favour of this text which defines pollen as a natural component of honey, rather than an ingredient. i think this text strikes a good balance between protecting the interests of beekeepers and the right to information of european consumers. the costs of testing to obtain the information needed for labelling could have had a negative impact on the competitiveness of the agricultural sector and could have led to the closure of some beekeepers.
in writing. - the european parliament has just voted on the amendment of the honey directive. following the 2011 ruling of the court of justice of the european union requiring that honey containing gmo pollen be labelled, the european commission has instead presented a revision of the honey directive that avoids this labelling by a semantic trick that allows the gmo pollen to be considered as a natural constituent of honey. we, the green group, are standing together with the associations and professionals in the sector to reject this hypocritical proposal. meps today voted in favour of not requiring labelling of gmo pollen in honey. this is intolerable ! by hiding the contamination of honey with gmos from consumers, it is the consumer's freedom of choice - as opposed to the presence of gmos in his food - but also the freedom for beekeepers to produce without gmos that are clearly violated.
in writing. i supported this first reading agreement, which maintains the definition of pollen as a constituent in its own right, not an ingredient, of the honey product. labelling pollen as an ingredient would have been technically and economically very difficult for producers to implement. it would not have contributed anything to the traceability of gmo pollen in honey, as the product as a whole is already subject to the regulations on gmos and their labelling. finally, an 'ingredient' approach could have opened the way for the appearance of fraudulent and adulterated honey on the market. i therefore welcome the fact that this text continues to consider honey as a single ingredient product.
in writing. i voted against the legislative resolution on honey because the text proposed in plenary was not improved following the last trilogue. unfortunately, by adopting it as such, i.e. by defining pollen as a natural constituent of honey and not as an ingredient, this text is concealing the presence of gmos from consumers. indeed, if pollen is considered to be a natural constituent of honey, there is no need for labelling. if, on the other hand, it is an ingredient, then beekeepers may, under certain conditions, be required to label their honey to inform the consumer of the presence of gmos in their product. the majority also did not want to adopt the alternative solution on the labelling of pollen as an ingredient in the case of the presence of gmo fields within a 10 km radius.
in writing. i call for a ban on the open-field cultivation of gmos. without going back to that objective, the report proposes to define pollen as an ingredient in honey, so that labelling of genetically modified pollen would be compulsory. this could have been a legitimate minimum consumer protection. but the amendments have had the effect of emptying the text of its substance, i.e. consumer protection against gmos, and i am voting against.
in writing. i voted against the report on honey from the agreement with the council, which raises a problem in terms of the classification of pollen. if pollen is considered a natural constituent, there is no need for labelling. if, on the other hand, it is an ingredient, then beekeepers may need to label their honey to inform the consumer about the presence of gmos in their product. in the previous votes i advocated an alternative solution: without gm crops near the beekeepers, and therefore without the risk of creating gm pollen, pollen should be considered as a natural constituent of honey. on the other hand, if there are gm fields within a 10[nbsp]km radius, the pollen had to be considered an ingredient, a status which implies extensive analyses. our approach was to support all producers who are trying to bring quality, non-gmo honey to the market, meeting consumer demand and in a spirit of proportionality of controls. i regret that the fn and ump members supported this text under the pressure of economic arguments, thus giving the report a majority.

in writing. the creation of a european market for fishing rights was the key point in the reform of the common fisheries policy. parliament abolished the possibility of selling and buying fishing quotas (transferable fishing concessions). that is a decisive positive point. the commission has also proposed that the emff should provide financial support to fishermen during the biological rest periods necessary for the reproduction of the species. it also supports young fishermen to help them settle in. it increases the resources allocated to the collection of data on the resource and fishing activity. i vote for it.
in writing. the emff contains all the aid for fishermen. the regulation provides for specific measures for fishermen operating in the overseas fishing zones: a scheme to compensate for the extra costs incurred by fishermen and a specific state aid scheme for overseas fisheries. this regulation redefines the concept of artisanal fishing to adapt it to the situation of the fisheries in the outermost regions, provides for financing for the renovation of artisanal fishing vessels and installation aid for young fishermen. all these measures are fundamental for our fishermen. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - we must support the fisheries sector, which is sometimes in great difficulty. the european maritime and fisheries fund has a budget of 6.4 billion, which is a considerable sum. the financial aspect is indeed paramount, but it must be accompanied by precise and innovative strategies in order to manage this fund as efficiently as possible. i am glad that i voted in favour of this report. it helped to define the strategic priorities of the emff: sustainable fisheries, a more competitive fisheries sector and an ambitious social dimension. by strengthening the fisheries sector and offering better living conditions to our fishermen, we will be able to increase europe's potential for competitiveness in this sector.
in writing. the emff, the european maritime and fisheries fund, is the financial component of the reform of the common fisheries policy. it will have a budget of €6.4 billion for the period 2014-2020 and will be implemented through a single operational programme for each member state. the emff will be structured around three axes. first, the development of environmentally sustainable fishing: investments will be made in more selective fishing gear and priority will be given to data collection and the implementation of resource conservation measures. the second priority is to promote the competitiveness of the fisheries sector by providing aid for the installation of fishermen under 40 years of age and investments in vessels (replacement of engines, etc.). the social part will include vocational training for fishermen and the creation of an insurance mutual fund. these three guidelines are in line with the general approach to reform of the fisheries policy and the distribution of the funds available between these guidelines is balanced, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted for the european maritime and fisheries fund. it was to be operational from 1 january 2014. the european commission is now expected to publish it in may. the emff has a budget of eur 6.5 billion and is intended to finance the implementation of the common fisheries policy. i welcome the agreement negotiated with the council, which will make it possible, in particular, to support the settlement of young fishermen by means of financial aid and the renewal of engines. mutual funds can help professionals in times of crisis. the outermost regions will receive additional compensation and, finally, the collection of scientific data and the control of fisheries will be financed in a meaningful way. i regret, however, that the discussions on aid for the renewal of ships have not been successful. they would have improved economic efficiency, safety, selectivity and reduced pollution, and i will continue to fight for a modern vision of fisheries. i also regret that the majority of my colleagues from the greens and the gue abstained.

mr president, yes, the directive which was annulled by the court of justice on 9 april was adopted following the attacks in madrid and london in 2004-05. yes, terrorism and organised crime require action to protect the public, but not just any action. the court of justice has rightly pointed out that the legislature must respect fundamental freedoms and rights and the principles governing them, in particular the principle of proportionality. that directive had imposed a disproportionate obligation on telecommunications operators and internet service providers to retain data on a general basis concerning the origin, destination, date, time, duration, type of communication, the technology used and the location. so it was mass surveillance that was put in place and we know, especially after the prism/nsa committee of inquiry, that that's not the right method. the police themselves say that only targeted approaches are effective. and that's why we're trying to find the so-called balance. the ngos had pointed this out at the time, they had denounced it, including at the time of its transposition into national law. many member states have delayed transposition for these reasons and several constitutional courts in some member states have found the directive incompatible with their constitutions. the court found that the directive was a particularly serious interference with the right to respect for private life and the protection of personal data, since it affected the retention, use and extent of data collected without the subscriber or user being informed. the court is merely repeating the complaints which many of us in this chamber have repeatedly expressed. member states which have transposed this directive must suspend their legislation without delay. if there is a review, it must be in line with the court of justice's judgment. the commission is able, in certain areas - particularly economic ones - to follow the case-law of the court. it would be good if it did so with the same zeal as the commission does for fundamental rights. i hope this decision will put an end to the security and repressive drift we have been experiencing for years, including [nbsp]it has already been said[nbsp] when adopting the swift, pnr or safe harbour agreements with the united states. all international agreements in this field must be suspended, as must all european union legislation which infringes these rights. for once, the union and the member states would be able to harmonize their actions and their words. the european citizens would welcome this, they need the values of the european union to be respected. i hope we will move in that direction.
mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in recent years our parliament has always been at the forefront of the fight on the question of the protection of personal data. the judgment last week by the european court of justice in luxembourg shows that we are not entirely alone in this fight. i know it's also shared by you. the court confirmed the legitimacy of the objective pursued by the directive on the retention of personal data, but it considered above all that the systematic and unconditional retention of the accessory communication data of all european users for a specific period of time was not proportionate. the lack of guarantees regarding the security of data, the conditions of access and the conditions for their use therefore constitutes a particularly serious breach of the privacy of europeans. we were not unaware of the weaknesses of this text, which was adopted in 2005 in a specific context following several attacks. the european commission had in fact outlined the limitations in its evaluation. we must also admit that this text has become largely obsolete in a context of big data and technological evolution which allows, as we see on a daily basis, the tracking of citizen communications by any private organization. what are the consequences of all this? this judgment sounds like a strong message to the council. the adoption of a robust set of rules on the protection of personal data seems more necessary than ever to better protect european citizens and, above all, to restore their trust in the institutions that work for their daily security. the nsa scandal and its ramifications have made it clear that the retention of personal data is subject to unacceptable abuses. while the fight against terrorism and serious crime remains a strong concern, this cannot in any case be done at the expense of respect for the privacy of our european citizens. europe that protects cannot be just a slogan. it must be translated into action. this is what we expect from the next european commission, which will be proposing a new text shortly. at least that's what we hope.

in writing. - in 2010, the member states of the european union produced more than 100 million tonnes of hazardous waste. the legislation in force prohibits shipments of this type of waste to non-oecd countries. the commission is concerned about the proportion of hazardous waste which is being illegally transferred to third countries for cheaper treatment, resulting in the shameful shipment of our hazardous waste, poor quality treatment and even serious environmental pollution. i voted in favour of this report, which supports and complements the european commission's proposal, the aim of which is of course to encourage member states to strengthen and improve controls and to limit these illicit transfers. in particular, we have provided for: harmonization of the methods for the collection and penalisation of infringements, the publication of the results of inspection plans to the general public, and the strengthening of the powers of the competent authorities in this field. cooperation between member states in the fight against illicit shipments of waste will also be promoted by the establishment of a platform for the exchange of information.
in writing. between 2000 and 2009, the production of hazardous waste in the eu increased by almost 30%. the eu waste shipment regulation prohibits the export of hazardous waste to non-oecd countries except for recovery. however, the most recent study available on this subject shows a rate of irregularity of 25% found, which would correspond to a volume of 70 million tonnes of illegal transfers per year. the fraud is the result of the very high cost of treating this type of waste, as well as the low penalties for environmental crime. there are also large disparities between eu member states: some countries carry out almost no inspections (e.g. france had a total of 26 inspections, including 24 physical inspections, while poland had 4 264 inspections, including 3 391 physical inspections). i supported this report, which makes simple and concrete proposals to improve the effectiveness of legislation in this area, including: improving the knowledge base on illicit transfers, or including a minimum number of physical checks in inspection plans and the permanent publication of inspection plans and results.

in writing. psychoactive substances are substances that affect the state of the central nervous system by altering certain biochemical and physiological processes in the brain. by altering brain function, they can cause changes in perception, sensation, mood, consciousness (altered states of consciousness) or other psychological and behavioral functions. these substances can be diverted from their original use (industrial, medical, etc.). i note that a great deal of attention is paid to psychoactive substances which escape the capitalist market. it is a pity that the same interest is not being shown in the legal, prescribed and over-used psychoactive substances in europe. the consequences for public health are near or worse. in france 1 in 10 people have used medicated psychoactive drugs in the past year. the problem in this context is therefore much wider than the 5% of young europeans who have used the 'drug' at least once in their lives. before tackling illegal consumption it would be good to look at consumption subsidized by social systems for the benefit of pharmaceutical laboratories. i am voting against this hypocritical text which does not dare to attack the main suppliers of psychoactive substances.

in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because it recalls the intangible nature of the fundamental values of the european union, namely freedom of conscience and religion. more than ever, the european union must promote this approach and recall that every man must be free to hold his own beliefs and to exercise his faith fully, provided that it does not jeopardise the freedom of his neighbours.
in writing. the purpose of this resolution is at first sight questionable: why should the union's foreign policy deal with issues of religious and cultural diversity? in a secular perspective, politics should not concern itself with religion and religion should not concern itself with politics. the freedom of the public space and the sovereignty of citizens are compromised whenever this is not the case. it is true that this text affirms principles which derive from secularism: freedom of conscience, separation of state and religion, universalism of democratic principles which should not be considered as western. but he also advocates a role for foreign policy in religious matters that is contrary to secularism. he also called for the european external action service to contribute to interreligious dialogue throughout the world. the report also advocates a dialogue between the three religions of the book as an instrument of international politics. i believe, on the contrary, that politics should not be involved in such interreligious relations to the detriment of the universality of citizens. i therefore vote against this useless report, which has no normative value whatsoever.
in writing. in the face of the many russian pressures on the eu's eastern neighbours, the european parliament wanted to send a clear message. we cannot tolerate violations of international law against our neighbours and partners. i co-signed and voted in favour of this resolution because it reaffirms the importance of respect for the territorial integrity of ukraine. it also recalls that we are strengthening our economic and political cooperation with ukraine and moldova. the european union must be firm towards russia even if it means isolating it on the international stage.
in writing. the ukrainian crisis is intensifying dramatically and the implementation of the agreement reached on thursday 17 april in geneva between the various partners seems unfortunately to be in jeopardy. the eu must be determined to take the appropriate economic and diplomatic sanctions in the face of the unacceptable destabilisation of eastern ukraine, which is being driven by moscow. at the same time, it is imperative to continue the diplomatic dialogue, which is the only way out of the crisis. but this dialogue cannot exclude firmness. the presidential elections will take place at the end of may. european diplomacy and the member states will have to ensure that these meetings take place in good conditions. the international community will have to take stock of and learn from the ukrainian crisis and the union should not be blamed for its inaction once again.
in writing. - i supported the motion for a resolution on the pressure exerted by russia on the eastern partnership countries, and in particular on the attempts to destabilise eastern ukraine. the resolution condemns the escalation of destabilisation in eastern and southern ukraine, reaffirms ukraine's right to territorial integrity and political independence, calls on the european community to tighten sanctions against russia and to step up its support and assistance measures to the ukrainian government. i welcome the adoption of this resolution.
in writing. the resolution "condemns in the strongest terms the escalation of destabilisation and provocations in eastern and southern ukraine", but clearly only russia is designated as a provocateur. what about the european union and the united states? the resolution calls for the european union to initiate a phase of economic sanctions against russia and, at the same time, calls for the signing of the free trade agreement between the eu and ukraine to be accelerated. i am voting against this resolution with its erroneous analyses and harmful objectives.
in writing. in adopting this resolution, meps call for a de-escalation of the crisis in ukraine, which is under increasing pressure from the russian government. they condemned the abuses committed in the east and south of the country by armed separatist groups, while expressing their deepest concern at the deterioration of the situation and the escalation of violence. parliament called on the russian government to withdraw its troops from the eastern border of ukraine and to enter into urgent dialogue with the ukrainian government. the only way out of the destabilization of ukraine is political and diplomatic. the european union and its member states must speak with a strong and united voice and not hesitate to impose further sanctions against russia if it refuses to engage in dialogue. the european parliament reaffirms its solidarity with the ukrainian people and its support for the country's sovereignty, territorial integrity and independence. it recalled that the future of ukraine could only depend on the choices of its citizens, in the context of a democratic, open and transparent process. finally, it is essential that the european union supports ukraine in its constitutional and economic reforms, which will bring it prosperity and political stability.
in writing. - i co-signed and voted for our resolution condemning the pressure exerted by russia on eastern ukraine as well as on the other eastern partnership countries, notably georgia and moldova. our message is threefold: - we condemn recent russian actions such as the annexation of crimea and the support for violent separatists and armed militias in eastern ukraine, and call them serious violations of existing international law; - we call on the member states and other european institutions to continue their efforts to cooperate and support ukraine so that it can complete its structural reforms and establish a democratic regime that respects minorities; - we encourage the european union and its member states to take more radical sanctions against russia, especially in the energy sector, and call for a genuine embargo on eu-sourced weapons and dual-use technologies.
in writing. i supported, by my vote in plenary, this text which condemns the escalation of destabilisation and provocations in eastern and southern ukraine and reaffirms our support for ukraine's sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence. if we continue to support the principle of including the russian side in all negotiations, we cannot tolerate its double-dealing. the resolution also reiterates that the eu stands ready to observe and facilitate the elections in may next year, if ukraine so requests. but ukraine will have to continue to move forward on the path of its political reform, in particular its constitutional reform, which should be the subject of a broad and thorough debate.
in writing. i voted against this resolution on russia's actions in central and eastern europe, in particular in ukraine. the commission's proposal was extremely unbalanced and biased. while condemning russia's attitude and in particular the use of military force, one cannot deny the outbid of both sides, with ukraine becoming the battleground of geopolitical competition between two imperialisms, with russia on one side and the western bloc bringing together the united states and the european union on the other. while this resolution recalls that the poverty rate in the country is currently close to 25%, or 11 million people, the majority of this parliament persists in not proposing to ukraine as an alternative, under the cover of a 'partnership agreement', only the development of free trade as it now does with all the countries with which it signs international agreements. what the ukrainians need is democracy and the re-founding of their institutions, so that they can decide for themselves their future, not economic tutelage.
in writing. the european union is vietnam's second largest trading partner, and in recent years the country has experienced exceptional economic growth of some 8% per annum. by voting in favour of this text, the european parliament is thus rightly promoting an increase in total exports and imports both for the european union and for vietnam. a deep free trade agreement will thus create many jobs in europe and boost the sme sector, which is particularly sensitive to the trade opportunities offered by the agreement.
in writing. the resolution aims to establish a free trade agreement between the european union and vietnam. the possibilities for social dumping will be immense if one considers that vietnam has not ratified the international labour organization (ilo) conventions on freedom of association, the right to organise and bargain collectively and the abolition of forced labour. we can see the potential for a few multinationals, but the benefits for the european and vietnamese people are less clear. the agreement also provides for the establishment of a mechanism for settling investor-state disputes, which serves only the interests of multinational firms in their fight to break social and environmental standards. i am opposed to the signing of any new free trade agreement and call instead for the introduction of solidarity protectionism. i vote against it.
in writing. - asia has become an essential player in the world economy in a very short time. while european and generally western markets are experiencing a decline in growth, asian countries are recording growth rates of 5 to 6%, sometimes even double-digit growth. we have, through naivety, and sometimes even arrogance, for a long time underestimated the potential of these economies. we are no longer dealing with emerging countries but with strong economies, with real partners. the european union must take this into account when initiating partnership processes with these powers. in 2013, vietnam recorded a growth rate of over 5%. with vietnam, we have entered the sixth round of negotiations for a free trade agreement. the agreement must strike a balance between opening up the market and protecting european companies. i am very glad that i voted in favour of this resolution. it is by encouraging these economic partnerships with asia that we are empowered to work towards a more internationally competitive europe.
in writing. trade negotiations between the european union and vietnam started in 2012, but they are the result of an initial desire to reach a more global agreement: a regional agreement between the european union and the association of southeast asian nations (asean). five rounds of negotiations have been held and the stated aim is to conclude them this year. it should be noted that in 2013, the eu trade balance with vietnam was negative: eu imports from vietnam amounted to eur 10.5 billion and eu exports to vietnam amounted to eur 2.8 billion. this trade and investment agreement will therefore help to rebalance trade volumes. however, this agreement, which respects the wto's special and differential treatment rules, should also contain binding provisions on human rights, labour and the environment. in particular, the textile sector in vietnam is experiencing problems similar to those in bangladesh. these will be taken into account in adapting the provisions of the agreement to the latest developments in this field.
in writing. i supported this motion for a resolution which responds to the european commission's communication on the 'top 10' consultation of smes on eu regulation. this is a consultation to gather the views of smes on eu legislation that affects them. parliament reiterated its support for measures to help smes, and in particular innovative smes. i would remind you that smes employ more than 65% of the private sector workforce in europe but only 25% of them export. i also support the call for a european target of 30% reduction in the cost of administrative and regulatory burdens on smes by 2020.
in writing. the resolution proposes to 'ease' the constraints on small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in order to increase their competitiveness. the aim is to 'reduce the burden imposed by labour legislation' or 'reduce the burden resulting from health and safety legislation'. proposing slavery would speed up the achievement of the resolution's objectives, namely the abolition of the right to work. i vote against it.

in writing. compromise or sovereignty ? "the principle of democracy is compromise". this statement was made on 15 july by mr weber, representative of the epp. it is radically wrong. the real principle of democracy is the sovereignty of the people, as recalled in article 2 of the french constitution of 1958. for there to be sovereignty of the people, and therefore democracy, there must also be a "people", that is to say a nation willing to assume a community of destiny. but this is not the case with the european union, which is not based on the existence of any european people. mr weber would have been better off saying that 'the principle of the european union is compromise'. because in the absence of popular sovereignty, only a system of incessant compromise can temporarily save an artificial union which the european nations will eventually dismiss.

is this not a sign of the lack of sincerity on the part of the member states in the budget negotiations of the union? in parallel, the commission is proposing two more amending budgets, this time to the community's credit. this should ultimately bring the member states' contribution to only around eur 100 million. and yet some are opposed to the application of this new arrangement. this crisis in payments is therefore neither minor nor one-off. it's a symptom of something. the symptom of a sick europe. the symptom of an outdated budgetary system that borders on the absurd. the european union must acquire new resources of its own, no longer dependent on blackmail from the member states. we, the european socialists, for example, have long been in favour of taxing financial transactions, but we must go further. we must make our budget, its expenditure and its revenue, a political instrument for sustainable growth, cohesion and social justice. this crisis is also a symptom of the failure of austerity policy. the same member states which advocate budgetary virtue are increasingly twisting and playing with words in order not to implement the policy they themselves have decided on! in writing. - i voted for the resolution on youth employment in order to bring the european parliament's proposals to the attention of the member states. the european parliament regularly proposes to invest in youth employment but the states do not always follow the recommendations. youth unemployment is a scourge, however, especially in the southern european countries, with greece where one in two young people is unemployed. i supported the proposal to include in this category of unemployed young people aged 16 to 25 also the 25-30 age group, sometimes qualified and graduated and yet unemployed. this category of young people should also benefit from investment and aid.

in writing. - the kampala compromise resulting from the june 2010 rome statute review conference of the international criminal court has led to a common definition of the crime of aggression, which is a significant step forward. states have agreed to define as a crime of aggression the planning, preparation, launching or execution by a person effectively in a position to control or direct the political or military action of a state of an act of aggression which, by its nature, gravity and extent, constitutes a manifest violation of the charter of the united nations. however, the conditions for the court to exercise jurisdiction over the crime of aggression, in compliance with the prerogatives of the security council, are not fulfilled. paragraph 8 of article 15bis of the kampala compromise is not unanimous in that it limits the role of the security council, which alone is empowered to establish the existence of a crime of aggression under the united nations charter. the consistency and complementarity between the international criminal court and the security council must therefore be sought. that is why i abstained at the time of the final vote.
in writing. the concept of the crime of aggression defines crimes committed by persons or states who have prepared, carried out or promoted an armed conflict aimed at destabilising one or more sovereign states. the definition of the crime of aggression has been laid down in the rome statute since 2010. for the international criminal court to have jurisdiction over this crime, at least 30 states must ratify the kampala amendments. the resolution calls on the member states to ratify and incorporate these provisions into their national legislation. i vote for it.
in writing. - i abstained on this text for reasons of efficiency of international policy. today, only the un security council, of which france is one of the five permanent members, has the authority to recognize the existence of an act of aggression. it is clear that justice is complementary to peace and i fully support the actions of the international criminal court. however, in the name of the stability of international institutions and the effectiveness of their action, the sole competence to characterise the crime of aggression must remain in the hands of the un security council.
in writing. - i voted on the motion for a resolution on the crimes of aggression. these crimes are included in the list of crimes within the jurisdiction of the international criminal court. but despite the lengthy process of negotiating the statute of the court adopted in rome in 1998, the states have not been able to agree on its definition. in particular, the modalities for the exercise of the international criminal court's jurisdiction in the implementation of prosecutions are not defined. i rejected the inclusion in this resolution of a reference to the kampala amendments which could lead to a choice between respect for the united nations charter and respect for the rome statute. the european union is not prepared to accept the fact that the united states is not a member of the security council, but that it is not prepared to accept the fact that the united states is a member of the security council. such a situation would be likely to undermine the efficiency and credibility of the court itself.
