member of the commission. - mr president, many questions have been put about the agreement, or the proposal for an agreement, reached last friday in brussels between ukraine, the european union and russia. what does it really mean? it means, on the one hand, that we are going to prolong the autonomous trade measures vis-à-vis ukraine. so they will continue to be able to export onto our european markets as if the agreement were already in force. let me point out that, since june when we decided on the autonomous trade measures for the first time, exports by ukraine to the european union have increased by 15% in just a couple of months. so this is a very effective tool. it is up to the council of ministers to change the decision on provisional application, and with respect to the autonomous trade measures it depends on codecision by the european parliament and the council whether or not these autonomous measures are prolonged. this is a decision to be taken by you and by the council of ministers in a very democratic process. with regard to provisional application, which is the other side of the mirror, the question of whether we have free access to the ukrainian market, and whether we can continue with sanitary and phytosanitary standards (sps) and with the technical barriers to trade, is in the hands of the council of ministers. there is currently a decision on provisional application, and the council will have to change that. we are going to make a proposal to them to do so for definite periods of time – specifically until the end of next year. why have we been working to make the agreement that was reached on friday? some have said it is non-effective, a sign of weakness or a mistake. the reason we have been doing it, ms harms, and the result of the long process which started in july, is to make ratification possible. without this agreement on friday, there would no ratification today. and what are the results of that ratification? there are at least three. first, it gives new economic opportunities to ukraine to export into the european union and to have economic growth. if we really want ukraine to become a fully-fledged democracy and part of the european house, what you will need there is economic opportunity, growth and jobs. and that, by the way, is the reason why these people protested in the maidan: because they want freedom and they want economic growth. when the soviet union split apart, the per capita income in ukraine was a little bit higher than it was in poland, and now the per capita income in poland is four times higher than that of ukraine. that has been the result of poland becoming a member of the european union. secondly, ratification establishes a bond between ukraine and the european union which is very important because that is what the people really want. they want to establish this bond with the european union, and once the ratification has taken place it is no longer merely a matter of words. it has become a legal relationship: it has become a treaty. of course, the member states will have to ratify it. six have done so already and it will be very wise for the other member states to do this as soon as possible. ratification establishes a bond between ukraine and the european union which will be very difficult, if not impossible, to undo because it establishes a treaty. at the moment, what russia is trying to do in ukraine is to create a new frozen conflict in the east of the country. that is what they are trying to do – just as happened in moldova with transnistria, just as happened in georgia with abkhazia and south ossetia, and just as happened in nagorno-karabakh. at that moment in time we, as the european union, are saying ‘ok, we will make a treaty with you, we will make this bond with you.’ this is a legal bond and we are not going to undo it, but rather we will make further discussion possible and will ensure that the elections on 15 october take place under acceptable conditions. we are ready to make a sacrifice – yes, an economic sacrifice – and delay the provisional application of the agreement for a very limited period of time. that is what this is about and i am sure that is what you are going to vote for in half an hour’s time.

president of the committee on budgets. - madam president, mr minister, mr commissioner, i would like to stress that the elections of 25 may delivered their verdict with severity and it is hardly necessary to recall how strongly euroscepticism has been. the criticism has culminated in sluggish growth and high unemployment, reaching desperate levels among young people. while populism is raging across the continent, the imf and oecd are concerned about the stagnation of the eurozone. the real question is whether the eu budget can remedy this and restore confidence. to answer this question, we need to clarify three preconditions: first, to prepare the revision of the multiannual financial framework adopted at the end of 2013. it sets the ceilings for expenditure and the level of revenue for seven years. this framework was voted on before the elections and clearly did not win the support of the electorate. democracy therefore requires us to prepare for its revision. can we expect some changes in the 2015 budget? is there no urgency in presenting a 'combat budget' in the face of the volatility of circumstances? is it reasonable to lock ourselves in a rigid budgetary tunnel, insensitive to cyclical events, such as the accidents of the road? the 2015 appropriations will largely cover operations launched in 2012 or 2013! at a time when europe is threatened by economic collapse, such inertia deprives the budget of its responsiveness. are we finally ready to implement specific and maximum flexibility as from budget 2015? secondly, i would like to sound the alarm again about the widening gap between commitment appropriations and payment appropriations. as of 31 december 2013, the balance to be paid is skyrocketing, the unpaid amounts are accumulating and growing: 5 billion at the end of 2010, 24 billion at the end of 2013. yet the treaties forbid the union from going into debt. this is a hidden debt that is taking shape and is causing difficulties for operators. this vicious circle is irresponsible. the budget of the european union is modest, representing barely 1% of gross domestic product (gdp). it is therefore necessary to design and implement it with discernment, method and consistency. i ask the council to tell us what its plan is to do to clear up the past and get us off on the right foot. finally, what will be the sources of financing for the 300 billion in investment announced by the president of the commission on 15 july? these cannot be transactions which would in any event have been financed by the markets. if europe is to have a driving effect, it means that it must take a risk, and this risk-taking must be reflected in the budget. since everyone recognizes the urgency, what will be the budget translation in 2015? the credibility of the president of the commission is at stake. in conclusion, i would like to express my strong hope that the 2015 budget will not be a mere continuation of previous budgets, with a new round of payment appropriations. europe is in crisis, europe is in danger, we were elected to put it back on its feet and to restore confidence to the europeans.

zero economic growth, zero employment, zero competitiveness except for germany, zero increase in purchasing power. the problem is the skyrocketing deficits and debts of the public sector. despite all the gifts given by governments and the ecb to listed companies and private banks, economic growth is completely stunted and competitiveness is still not there. your ultra-liberal europe is starting to take off. the other paradox is that mr juncker has appointed the least virtuous of the eurogroup's economic ministers, mr moscovici, as the commissioner responsible for deficit compliance. when will you understand that the single currency euro is a monetary aberration that goes against the other 180 countries in the world that each have their own national currency, their own central bank and their own borders. in france, the introduction of the euro coincided exactly with the reversal of the trade balance, which has become structurally deficitary; a french external deficit that broke its historical record last july, as we reached 85 billion euros at an annualized rate. as for the debt, it has doubled since 2003, reaching more than 2 000 billion euros at the end of 2014 in france. you are so desperate about the utter failure of the single currency and the decay of your economic system that you are asking member states to falsify the calculation of gdp by including the criminal economy, i.e. prostitution, drug trafficking and smuggling. the euro will not bring recovery, it will bring a new crisis! in writing. the current economic and social situation in europe requires us to help those who are losing their jobs as a result of globalisation and ultra-liberalism. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) is there to train and re-train workers who have been affected by relocations and the financial crisis. the technical assistance appropriations for this fund correspond to a maximum of 0.5% of its budget, in this case € 330000. i abstained on this vote not because i did not want to help workers in difficulty but to say that this fund would not have been needed if brussels had not pursued ultra-liberal policies and had not opened our frontiers wide to unfair competition from all over the world.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for the measures proposed by the commission under the technical assistance. this fund was established in 2006 by regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 to help workers who have lost their jobs as a result of major structural changes brought about by globalisation. in the face of the global economic and financial crisis, it must therefore provide effective and appropriate assistance. but it is still little known to the general public and little is known about its mobilisation by the member states. the commission may finance the expert group of egf contact persons which facilitates networking and exchange of information on the egf. the commission will also be able to reduce the administrative burden on member states by working on an electronic form for requesting the mobilisation of the egf. voting for this mobilisation means allowing for a simplified and effective mobilisation of the egf, which is needed in this time of crisis.

the next item is the debate on seven motions for resolutions on burundi, in particular the case of pierre claver mbonimpa [2014/2833 ((rsp)) ]
president. - the next item is the report (a4-0173/97) by mr mbonimpa, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection, on the situation in burundi. on 15 may, mr mbonimpa was arrested and placed in provisional detention following statements he made on burundian radio denouncing the imbonerakure training camps for the ruling president's party youth in the east of the drc. these camps exist and represent a major threat to peace in burundi. we condemn the provisional detention of mr mbonimpa and call for his release and for respect for the rights of the accused and for judicial procedures. we also call for the protection of human rights defenders and for an investigation into the actions of the imbonerakure. the situation in burundi is getting harsher and the ruling government is restricting protests and the rights of political opponents. but next year elections will be held in burundi and it is necessary that the political debate can take place in a calm and serene manner.
author. - madam president, burundi is one of the poorest countries in the world, with the highest hunger rate among the countries where this index is calculated. it is suffering the consequences of the crisis in its large neighbours and has to cope with the influx of thousands of refugees. a series of elections are due in 2015, and the climate is deleterious. all those who do not support the regime, who dare to criticize it, are victims of a terrible repression, whether they are political activists or ngos, journalists or ordinary citizens. pierre claver mbonimpa is one of them. a brave man, who dedicated his life to human rights. our debates, commissioner, are currently being followed in burundi. i greet those who are watching us. our discussions must be hopeful for them. the european union has the means to act. its assistance under the 10th edf has more than doubled to €432 million. this is essential for a country whose budget depends on foreign aid for more than 50 per cent. yes, the leaders of this country are corrupt. the european union must therefore press for its aid to be allocated only to the country's priority problems, conditional on respect for human rights, the release of all political prisoners, and support for the un's demand to open an investigation into the military training centres, which are at the heart of the accusation of pierre claver mbonimpa.
madam president, i apologize for my lack of experience. i wonder on what basis we are voting in the order you have chosen today. it seems to me that as usual - but perhaps i am wrong again, and i shall be glad to be refuted by you - a compromise resolution tabled by several groups is put to the vote first.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in ukraine and the state of eu-russia relations which, beyond taking account of the dramatic diplomatic situation we are experiencing, highlights the catastrophic situation facing our farmers. the crisis facing european farmers, particularly french farmers, is not a health or market crisis but a diplomatic one, caused by a standoff between the european union and russia. we therefore called on the european commission to act accordingly and to take better account of the needs of farmers while considering the possibility of using budget lines other than agriculture.
in writing. - in these recent turbulent times in relations between ukraine and the european union, we must support all initiatives for peace but also remain clear about the intentions of russia, engaged in the undeclared "hybrid war" it is waging against this country. it is in this context that i have voted in favour of this resolution calling on the european union to stand up to russia by strengthening the sanctions envisaged and to increase support for european farmers who are badly affected by the trade embargo. while we welcome the signing of the minsk ceasefire agreement, we must also deplore the fact that it has been violated by russian troops and separatist forces. but it is much more important to make every effort to find a political solution than a military one. finally, i welcome the decision of the french government to suspend the delivery of mistral helicopter carriers to russia, and other member states are expected to follow suit.
in writing. - the european parliament has rightly denounced the russian embargo on agricultural and food products, the immediate and disastrous effects of which we know in france. i am a strong supporter of french agriculture and am particularly concerned about this retaliatory measure, whose effects are now spreading to other sectors such as the transport sector. the european parliament calls on the parties to the conflict to engage in dialogue and to find a diplomatic and peaceful solution, which i welcome. however, i will remain cautious when it comes to discussing relations with our russian partner, a major economic power and member of the g8. i have read amendments calling russia an authoritarian state. it would not be in the european parliament's interest to add fuel to the fire by further aggravating the parties currently in negotiation. let us not indulge in caricature and instead support the diplomatic path if we want to end this crisis as quickly as possible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in ukraine and relations between the european union and russia. the resolution welcomes the ceasefire agreement reached and calls for a genuine peace process, while stressing the inviolability and integrity of the ukrainian territory. the ambiguous role of russia is also condemned. the resolution was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution to call for the ceasefire in eastern ukraine to be maintained and for the minsk agreements to be strictly enforced. the unity and independence of ukraine must be strictly guaranteed. to do this, it is important to work towards a political solution to this conflict and to avoid any further escalation, including by completely isolating russia at international level. nevertheless, it was fundamental in this resolution to condemn russia severely for its actions and to support the latest sanctions adopted against it by the eu. in the face of moscow's retaliatory measures, namely the boycott of eu fruit, vegetables, meat, dairy products and fisheries, it is important that european producers are properly compensated. in addition, given the current particularly complicated situation, the eu needs to reduce its dependence on russia in various fields (energy, technology, etc.). finally, with regard to the eu-ukraine association agreement, which was approved by the european parliament and the kiev parliament, it was essential to resist russian pressure by saying that nothing could change it.
in writing. - i support the ceasefire agreement between separatists and the ukrainian authorities in the east of the country and a dialogue-based settlement of the current crisis. the text of the resolution proposed to us goes far beyond relations between ukraine and russia. the european union can act as a moderator in the current crisis. but this resolution lacks impartiality as it calls for more sanctions against russia, while supporting the eu-ukraine free trade agreement. ukraine must be able to choose its own path outside of any foreign influence and interference, find a system of government that will address the concerns of a part of its population in the east, and find a modus vivendi with russia that addresses its concerns without ukraine losing its sovereignty. this must be done without any pressure, whether from russia with gas prices or from the european union with the free trade agreement.
in writing. - this unjust resolution denounces the russian aggression in ukraine and calls for the continuation of sanctions against russia. to justify these positions, it presents as established facts highly questionable claims such as the inability of investigators to access the mh17 crash site or the presence of a continuous flow of arms and ammunition from russia. but no reaction on svoboda's presence in the government. or on the azof division which makes up the bulk of the ukrainian troops and which has the same emblem as the nazi division "das reich" responsible for among other things the oradour on glane massacre. i vote against this bellicose text. i therefore welcome the defeats of the ukrainian neo-nazi gangs.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution which sets out the state of play of the situation in ukraine and eu/russia relations. parliament called for the ceasefire to be respected by all parties and for decisions to be avoided which could jeopardise it.
in writing. although the resolution acknowledges the relative improvement in the situation following the signing of the ceasefire in minsk, the text promotes solutions that take too much sides in the conflict and thus threaten the security of the region and ukrainians. similarly, the promotion of the eu-ukraine association agreement cannot serve the interests of the ukrainian people, knowing that this treaty is one of the reasons that has led ukraine to tear itself apart for several months already. i therefore did not vote in favour of this text.
in writing. - i am extremely in favour of the adoption of the european parliament's resolution on the situation in ukraine and the state of relations between the european union and russia, because it was becoming urgent for the european parliament to take a clear and precise position. in this sense, i support this resolution because it sets out a strict policy in the face of russia's actions. nevertheless, the facts of the conflict must be presented as clearly as possible in order to establish such a policy on an unshakable basis. i therefore voted against amendment no 9, because the claim that the ceasefire is a pretext for russian troops to establish a 'land corridor' to crimea and transnistria could not be substantiated.
in writing. in view of the rapid spread of the ebola virus, which has already killed 2430 people out of 4907 cases recorded as of 15 september, the outbreak has been declared by the who as a public health emergency of international concern. the commission announced an 'ebola package' worth €140 million and it was decided to launch preparations without delay for the development of a european mechanism for the coordination of medical evacuations. in total, up to 20,000 people are expected to be infected and studies suggest that 373 million euros will be needed to stop the epidemic. some airlines have suspended flights from guinea, liberia and sierra leone. the national front called for the suspension of these flights to and from these countries. i therefore voted against this resolution. whereas, in view of the current situation, it is now necessary for us to engage in a rapid action plan, whether for the deployment of medical teams, the establishment of treatment centres, the establishment of a sustainable risk management policy, vaccine research or information and awareness raising among the population.
in writing. - i voted in favor of the ebola outbreak resolution. since the beginning of this outbreak, european commission structures have already provided €147 million in humanitarian aid and treatment to help contain the virus, but our response remains slow. the affected regions of central africa do not have a health system to contain the outbreak, which has repercussions on security in the region. in a coordinated action with the un, the eu will therefore provide comprehensive assistance: not only health and logistics, but also support for the training of carers, education and prevention, health and nutrition assistance, always complementing long-term development aid. the role of the african union as a regional organisation that can provide local responses is to be highlighted.
in writing. with this vote, the european parliament wanted to highlight the critical health situation in west africa. faced with the spread of the ebola epidemic, this region of the world needs stronger international support. this has led us to call on the international community to intensify its efforts. in particular, it is important to encourage the european commission to act more vigorously in close cooperation with the united nations and the african union by conducting needs assessments and developing country-specific action plans to identify and coordinate assistance.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on ebola which calls for greater involvement of the international community in the fight against the epidemic and calls on the european commission and the member states to take coordinated action in this regard. i welcome the adoption of this resolution.
in writing. - i've asked to be a co-signer of the joint resolution on the ebola outbreak in west africa. the pandemic poses a real challenge to global security, for which the european community must mobilise humanitarian, logistical and financial resources. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the resolution also calls on the european community to strengthen medical research and to support the initiatives of the african union to combat the spread of the virus and to address the political, economic and social consequences of the epidemic for the region.
in writing. the resolution welcomes and encourages the african union's aseowa mission with the help of the european union to contain ebola. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the spread of the virus. nevertheless, i wonder whether it is appropriate to have a joint military and civilian mission of aesowa as is the case and which also includes the sending of american military personnel who are once again taking advantage of the situation. for these reasons i abstain.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution on the european union's response to the ebola crisis. through this vote, we deplore the loss of life in the affected areas. the problem is not an african problem, but a global problem. the international community must play a greater role and african states must shoulder their full share of responsibility. the resolution calls for a series of prevention measures and actions to be implemented in africa and europe. it is vital to act against the disease and its health and social consequences.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which is a step forward in the fight against one of the most serious epidemics that africa has experienced in recent decades, in particular in consolidating the support provided by the eu and its member states in terms of medical expertise and equipment. the resolution calls for the dispatch of doctors to the affected countries and for better cooperation between african and european countries.
in writing. - since march 2014, the ebola epidemic has been spreading rapidly across the african continent and the virus has already infected more than 4,000 people and caused more than 2,000 deaths. i voted in favour of this resolution, which clearly demonstrates the european union's support for the health actors involved in the fight against this virus. more resources are needed and there is an urgent need for the european commission and the member states to step up their action. this includes helping to strengthen weak health systems in affected countries, ensure better information and prevention and continue the search for an effective vaccine. it is also essential that these actions be carried out in cooperation with our international partners, the united nations and associations. the ebola epidemic is now a global security challenge.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the ebola epidemic, because the european union must become aware of this catastrophe, which has been excluded from our agenda for too long. i therefore deplore the lack of reaction from the european union, especially when it affects the health of european union citizens. so i am in favour of any action to contain this epidemic.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the eu response to the ebola outbreak. the latest figures from the world health organization for the outbreak are almost 2,630 deaths and 5,357 cases. a dramatic result, and yet probably underestimated. it is therefore crucial that the european union and its member states mobilise to stem the epidemic. the resolution stresses in particular that the international community must play a greater role in combating the epidemic and assume its responsibilities in this regard. in supporting this resolution, which calls on the european commission to step up its support for the states concerned and also calls on the member states to draw up an emergency plan to deploy the necessary personnel and equipment to the countries affected by the epidemic, i wanted to remind them that this crisis is not just west africa's but the whole of the international community's and that it is high time to mobilise.
madam president, i am glad that we are finally taking an interest in the plight of minorities and, in particular, christians in the middle east. but i regret that this interest is so belated when the situation has only worsened since the us invasion of iraq in 2003. you only mention the so-called islamic state. the islamist militias in iraq and syria are, however, just as violent and hateful to each other. how can you claim to be fighting daesh while supporting the syrian branch of al qaeda, the al nusra front? it is totally inconsistent for nato member countries to tolerate turkey continuing to arm, train, finance and buy oil from the so-called islamic state and to accept that recruitment and recruitment is organized in the streets. beyond the usual gestures, it is time for european countries to take clear positions to fight all islamist militias in cooperation with the syrian and iraqi governments.
in writing. - religious minorities continue to be persecuted in iraq and syria, massacred, and driven from their historic place of life. it is our duty to support them and to fight against terrorism and isil. the european union must take firm and concrete measures to defend eastern christians and all religious minorities. the european parliament's resolution is balanced and condemns all violations of human rights. it calls on the member states to take responsibility and to combat all forms of discrimination. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. the advance of the islamic state (often called daesh which means the same thing but shows a semantic logic) has already resulted in a large number of abuses and one could even speak of crimes against humanity (forced conversions, slavery, trafficking in women, torture, murder ...). this translates to 1.8 million internally displaced people and nearly 190,000 deaths in syria since the start of the conflict, according to the un. in these countries, areas under the control of the islamic state, a faction of al-qaeda, are in a state of growing anxiety, subject to a rigorous interpretation of sharia law and the establishment of a caliphate that violates human rights and persecutes religious minorities, especially christians. support is needed to enable them to live safely on their land and to guarantee the return of displaced people to their places of origin. in view of this situation, i voted for this resolution in order to strongly condemn these abuses, to put an end to the illicit trade of the islamic state which finances its advance, to ensure the protection of persecuted populations, to facilitate access to humanitarian aid and to prevent european citizens from leaving the territory of the union to go and fight alongside the terrorists.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in iraq and syria. we support the minorities persecuted in the conflict, especially the christians of iraq who are victims of religious intolerance. the so-called "islamic state in syria and iraq" has no legitimacy and its actions, including the barbaric murder of journalists, have been unanimously condemned as criminal. we must not allow it to profit from its oil sales on the international market. the international community is therefore supporting the legitimate iraqi authorities and is supporting the protection of the civilian population by the un. security measures will be taken to prevent foreign jihadists, including european citizens, from supporting the islamist insurgency.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this resolution on the islamic state offensive in syria and iraq and the persecution of minorities there. the european parliament voted to reaffirm its strongest support for persecuted religious minorities, especially christians in the east. it was particularly necessary to recall the right of these christian communities to continue living in their native lands while being free to practice their religion. these multiple human rights violations against religious minorities, atrocities such as the murders of journalists james foley and steven sotloff and humanitarian worker david haines, are proof that the european union must take a very firm stand against the barbaric actions perpetrated by the islamic state.
in writing. - barbaric acts, forced conversions, kidnappings, slavery, sexual abuse and torture are crimes perpetrated daily and with impunity by the islamic state (is) in iraq and syria. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the institutions and governments of the european union to take urgent measures to help and protect religious and ethnic minorities, especially christians, and to provide humanitarian aid to civilian victims. hundreds of european citizens also joined the insurgents. it is therefore urgent that the european union and the international community take legal action against anyone suspected of involvement in acts of terrorism.
in writing. - the european parliament has chosen to react by expressing its indignation at the suffering of the iraqi and syrian peoples, in particular the christian populations and the yazidi minority persecuted by the jihadists of the islamic state. in the face of barbarism, words are of little comfort but indifference would have been the manifestation of a cruel carelessness. i share the pain of these displaced people and those who are under the yoke of the islamic state. beyond the french military action, which is in response to a request from the iraqi president and which i would like to see taken up at european level, i am concerned about another phenomenon of such magnitude that threatens the security of our territories, the return of jihadist fighters, 946 of whom are french. the threats posed by these radicalised individuals must be taken into account in the formulation of our border management policies. while this remains a highly national issue, the abolition of internal borders and the de facto free movement of these people require enhanced cooperation between the european police and judicial authorities. european action is therefore needed.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution of the situation in iraq and syria. the text condemns the ongoing violence and persecution, in particular by the terrorists of isil, and calls for support for the iraqi government and protection of the civilian population. the resolution was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. - as a co-signer of this resolution, i wanted to emphasise the tragic situation of eastern christians who are victims of the religious and cultural cleansing carried out by the islamic state. it is our civilized heritage, our values, our culture that is being murdered with them. this is a crime against humanity, a crime against the diversity of the world, a crime against the identity of the middle east but also of europe. the eu must commit itself to allowing the christians of iraq and syria to remain in their homeland or to return safely, because to condemn them to exile would be to recognise the end of their civilisation. in the face of the emergency, the eu must act to: increase its humanitarian aid to persecuted communities; organise a massive military response to defeat the islamic state; supporting political transitions in iraq and syria ensuring better institutional representation for christians on the lebanese model; we must stop the jihadist contagion by protecting vulnerable neighbouring countries like lebanon, but also our own countries which are threatened by the return of jihadists from europe, whose numbers are growing. for these jihadists, we are the target to shoot because, like the christians of the east, we are the face of otherness. let us face their barbarity relentlessly.
in writing. - this resolution is unconditional support for the coalition formed by the united states, without any mention of responsibility for this disaster. the blame for the situation is placed on syria, while isil was created in iraq in 2006 following the us intervention. there are some calls for the protection of civilians, but they are not being taken into account. the european parliament is dishonoring itself by adopting the us military's war leaflets as a resolution. i vote against it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution which strongly condemns the offensive of the islamic state in iraq and syria and the abominable persecution of minorities. i have called for a real mobilisation of europe and the member states on this issue since june when the islamic state took mosul. through this vote, we condemn the cruel and cowardly executions of journalists, and denounce the caliphate established in the region. i am glad that the resolution refers to the 'paris appeal' of the muslim organisations in france which denounce the actions of the islamic state.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the persecution of minorities in syria and iraq because in the face of the atrocities witnessed by the european union, we must support these populations and condemn their persecutors. the massacres committed by the islamic state cannot go unpunished. in this sense, i support the european parliament's initiative to denounce this situation. it is therefore vital to encourage any action that promotes stability in the area and the silencing of terrorists. the urgency of such action is all the greater because such a situation is fostering the indoctrination of young europeans to religious hatred and terrorism.
in writing. - i am deeply shocked by the events taking place in iraq and syria. i supported this resolution so that the european union can step up its action to help the national and local authorities in iraq to combat extremists. it is essential that a solution be found to combat the rebel and jihadist groups and to achieve a political solution. attacks on civilians must cease and the perpetrators of barbaric acts must be severely punished.
in writing. - i voted against this resolution on the current situation in iraq and syria which, as too often, ignores the causes of the problem and proposes simplistic solutions and goes to war. first of all, let us remember that the so-called islamic state, now the richest terrorist group in the world, could not have prospered without the financial support of rich private donors from the gulf countries, to whom the governments turned a blind eye - something which this resolution does not emphasize. the resolution also 'welcomes the call by the united states for an international coalition against isil' and 'calls on all eu member states to assist the iraqi authorities ... including by providing military assistance'. this obstinacy not to take stock of all the military interventions with the united states at the head, not to see that the sources of crisis are multiplying, can only contribute to the chaos that reigns in the region.
madam president, i myself voted in favour of this resolution because it takes account of the impact on the catastrophic situation in libya and also highlights the problems we are facing, but which had to be mentioned, namely the circulation of arms, the presence of terrorist groups and the mass arrival of migrants on the italian coast. however, we would like to emphasize the role of france, my country, and nato, which plunged libya into this hell, and also to emphasize that libya is first and foremost the victim of this risky diplomacy - we cannot say more about europe and the west - and that, in the current situation, there is no lasting solution.
in writing. the situation in libya since the arab spring and the fall of dictator gaddafi remains very deteriorated. benghazi is hit almost daily by deadly clashes and many libyans and foreigners are leaving the country (150,000 between mid-may and late august according to the un). moreover, the democratic situation in the country is catastrophic. the parliament, which was elected in june last year and is recognised by the international community, is currently in tobruk for security reasons. on the other hand, in tripoli, the general national congress (gnc) considers that the current government is not legitimate and libya may therefore end up with two parliaments and two governments. the return to stability in libya will also prevent the mass arrival of asylum seekers and migrants on the maltese and italian coasts. the priority therefore remains the restoration of the political and military situation and it is essential that the eu supports the mediation efforts currently being carried out by the united nations on the ground. for these reasons i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in libya. the violence generated by the conflict has led to thousands of refugees fleeing the country, creating a catastrophic and difficult to manage humanitarian situation, including the mass arrival of migrants and refugees in italy and malta. the motion recognizes the house of representatives elected in june 2014 as the legitimate representative of the libyan people in their political transition from the gaddafi regime. the european union thus wishes to promote stability and democracy so that libyan citizens can live in security, in compliance with international law and human rights. the proliferation of weapons in the country is a threat to regional stability and international security, as is the presence of terrorist groups linked to al-qaeda that must be combated.
in writing. in libya, the security, political and humanitarian situation has deteriorated very seriously. that is why i supported the european parliament's call for all stakeholders to end the violence, to engage in a national dialogue in order to build a democratic state based on respect for human rights and the rule of law. with this vote, i also wanted to draw attention to the dual threat posed by the libyan crisis to our continent: on the one hand, the increase in migratory pressure at the union's external borders, and on the other, the presence of terrorist groups linked to al-qaeda on its territory.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption on 18 september 2014 of the resolution on the situation in libya. the return to sustainable security and political stability will inevitably require the establishment of an inclusive national dialogue between the libyan parties and the restoration of credibility to the political process. it is in this context that we call on all national actors to recognize the legitimacy of the only parliament that emerged from the elections of 25 june. we therefore ask the commission and the eeas to focus their support on strengthening the state and the institutions. the mediation efforts of neighbouring countries or the united nations and their new special representative should also be encouraged. parliament also expressed concern at the impact of the deterioration of governance in libya on regional and european security. in the chaos that continues to claim hundreds of victims and displaced persons every day, a significant number of migrants fall prey to smugglers and traffickers, with the tragic end that we unfortunately all too often experience. it is time for the european union to have a genuine migration policy, including by strengthening the synergies between the eu's internal and external policies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on libya which supports the libyan central government and calls for an end to violence between the various factions and for the protection of the civilian population. i welcome the adoption of this resolution.
in writing. - i am a co-signer of this resolution, which is justified by the sharp deterioration of the security, political and humanitarian situation in libya in recent weeks. every day libya sinks deeper into chaos as rival militias clash, some of them linked to extremely dangerous islamist armed groups. at the political level, it is essential to avoid the emergence of two competing parliaments as a result of the non-recognition of the tobruk parliament by the general national congress. the eu should therefore support un initiatives to foster constructive dialogue between the different parties and support the strengthening of the libyan state in the context of the post-gaddafi democratic transition process. it should also contribute to the reform of the security sector in libya to combat terrorism and take the necessary measures on migration in cooperation with libya and regional actors. as requested at the cairo conference on 25 august 2014, the involvement of neighbouring countries is essential to ensure stability in libya.
in writing. - libya is a place of militia fighting. many civilians are subjected to abuses simply because of their ethnicity or religious affiliation. but as is often the case, this text does not seek to establish any responsibility for the manufacture of this chaos. what about the nato intervention which went beyond the un mandate (to protect the people) by bringing down the regime, and moreover without any strategy for the future? the proposals are condolences, wishes and formulae full of good feelings, without any kind of concrete solution. the text calls on the parliament elected in june to assume its role, in particular to provide the country with a constitution, without specifying that this parliament, which had no influence on the country for a long time, recently took refuge on a ferry in the tobruk bay... in these circumstances, the mere mention of nato as a 'partner' to help the libyan leaders build state security forces capable of restoring security leads me to vote against this text whose authors are pitiful copyists of north american propaganda.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution which condemns the escalation of violence against civilian populations and legitimate institutions in libya. the european parliament calls for the restoration of the rule of law in the country and the bringing before the competent courts of all those guilty of war crimes and crimes against humanity. the current situation in libya has important effects on europe and particularly on the migratory pressure. europe and the member states must play an important role in restoring peace, in order to ensure security in the country and to stop the migration at our borders as soon as possible.
in writing. the resolution on the situation in libya is biased on a crucial point: it makes no mention of the interventions of nato and eu countries which have unquestionably led to the current destabilisation of the country and its fracturing along ethnic lines. although the resolution contains an important point on irregular immigration and asylum seekers, which is of course an issue on which the eu must play a major role, the resolution seems to me to obscure europe's responsibility for the situation in the country, and does not deal with the root of the problem with sufficient force. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the deteriorating situation in libya. it is therefore the responsibility of the european parliament to point the finger at the atrocities taking place there in order to arouse the interest of all the actors of the international community and to encourage any initiative aimed at promoting peace in that country.
in writing. - the current situation in libya is worrying. despite the parliamentary elections in june 2014 and the formation of a government, the situation in libya remains critical from a political, economic and security perspective. i supported this resolution so that the european union can strengthen its commitment to stability and the transition to democracy in libya. the use of violence against civilians is unacceptable and a ceasefire between the various parties must be established as soon as possible. it is also important that the european union acts in coordination with the international community, in particular unamid and the recently appointed united nations special envoy for libya, bernardino leon.
in writing. - the resolution on the gaza war and the situation between israel and palestine welcomes the ceasefire brokered by egypt in august. it is essential that the two sides continue to dialogue to ensure that this ceasefire is sustainable and to achieve a lasting resolution of the conflict. the european union recalls the 1967 borders and the creation of two states with jerusalem as their common capital. the european union must strengthen its support and diplomatic, humanitarian and political assistance for a viable long-term solution in the middle east.
in writing. with this vote on the situation in israel and palestine, we recall that the european union's priority following the ceasefire is to respond to the humanitarian crisis there. an adequate water supply is urgently needed. the european union cannot simply welcome the ceasefire agreement brokered by egypt. it must also commit itself to participating in the reconstruction process.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the conflict in gaza which welcomes the ceasefire agreement reached through egyptian mediation and calls for the rapid reconstruction of gaza. the resolution was adopted by a large majority. i welcome the outcome of this vote.
in writing. - i welcome the fact that the european parliament has supported this joint resolution on the situation in israel and palestine after the gaza war, in which meps welcome the ceasefire agreement reached on 26 august 2014 through the mediation of egypt and call for the rapid deployment of emergency humanitarian aid to the gaza strip. the resolution also calls on the commission to take all necessary steps to ensure that the eu's external borders are not encroached upon by the countries of the region. in this context, the resolution calls on the european union to assist in the reconstruction of gaza and to participate in the international donors' conference to be held on 12 october 2014.
in writing. - the joint resolution before us is too timid in its condemnation of israel's illegal actions and marks a retreat from the european parliament's positions on the settlement of the israeli-palestinian conflict. this text puts the two belligerents on an equal footing, while everything from human losses to material destruction to the causes of this conflict, points to a blatant imbalance in favor of israel. the absence of a clear condemnation of the massive israeli bombing, the collective punishment it inflicts on an entire people, the continuing siege of the gaza strip, its responsibility for the worsening of the situation and its parallel continuation of settlement in the west bank, cannot be justified. that is why, in the absence of sufficient support for our amendments which were intended to correct these deliberate errors, i have preferred not to support a text which absolves israel of its responsibilities and refuses to call into question european diplomacy in relation to the many abuses and distortions of international law perpetrated by israel.

for the gue/ngl group mr president, mr president barroso, when you talk about your satisfaction with your ten-year record, it is hard to understand why so many europeans do not realise that they live in the best of all worlds and why they refuse to vote now. in your plea, you talk about yourself, all the time, but very little about those millions of hardworking people, those who are burdened by unemployment, poverty and austerity every day. in ten years you have succeeded in making people hate the very idea of europe, by your efforts to privatize the large public sectors, to deregulate railways, energy and the postal service, and to make the management of the single currency almost exclusively a matter of speculation rather than giving priority to work and productive and ecological investment. not content with that, you and the governments have succeeded in this feat of transforming private debts into public debts and have even had the audacity to call upon the international monetary fund and its shock therapies to settle them, the consequences of which are now being borne by the youth and the peoples of greece, portugal, ireland, spain and now italy and france with unprecedented violence. we were told that the lisbon strategy was a resounding failure; so is the europe 2020 strategy. you have refused to include any criteria of social progress and ecological progress in the major european decisions. you have recently rejected the draft european minimum income, the extension of the maternity leave directive and a genuine positive amendment to the directive on posted workers. not content with the fierce competition between workers and firms within europe, you have proposed to widen the field of exploitation by activating the transatlantic single market project. the future depends on the exit from these austerity and regressive choices which are leading every european project into a dead end. we must instead invent a humanist europe. we must now imagine a policy of social recovery, replacing the relentless pursuit of lower labour costs with a hunt for capital waste and attacks on the environment. the european central bank's rigidity should be countered by what we have stopped defending here: a new fund for social, human and ecological development and a large cooperative investment plan, without which there will be no future for our european project.
in writing. mr barroso has violated democracy by imposing the treaty of lisbon on the french people; law by saving the euro in defiance of the treaties; and our values by starving people. a terrible record of oligarchy.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, mr president-in-office of the council, mr commissioner, as you have said, the council meeting on 23 and 24 october will have to deal with important and topical issues. it will, inter alia, decide on the objectives to be set for the new climate and energy action framework, and address the key issues of strengthening energy security, europe and interconnection needs. let us be clear: our aim is not to wage an ideological war against climate change, which would leave the mangled bodies of our companies and their employees on the battlefield. it is really - and i say this emphatically - that europe is committed to combating climate change while preserving its competitiveness and ensuring its security of supply. the situation in ukraine is a good reminder of the importance of ensuring the security of our energy sources. europe faces major challenges: high energy prices - in some sectors up to 40% of production costs - national policies are not sufficiently coherent and the internal energy market is still fragmented. finally, we have an obligation to move towards a decarbonised economy. to meet these needs, we must therefore diversify our sources of supply: renewable energy must be supported until it is technologically mature. we also need to strengthen energy infrastructure. interconnection between member states will be the key to building a genuine common european energy policy, an energy union, so dear to the new president jean-claude juncker, who has made it one of his priorities. the objectives set by the european council will be important in informing and guiding the investments of our companies. we need to provide them with a stable framework and visibility. let's stop changing our goals all the time. i take the example of the list of sectors exposed to carbon leakage: it should not have led to hesitation and our group, the epp, has shown its unity on this essential subject. the support given to enterprises to change their production methods and the use of their resources must not be mere words, but a concrete act and a promise to be kept. today, many european industrial sectors are world champions in energy efficiency and emission reduction. in building construction and transport, the potential for efficiency gains is enormous. in contrast, carbon capture and storage technologies have not really taken off. the storage of electricity must also mobilize us. it is the only way to make the development of renewable energy credible. europe cannot be left behind in these vital areas. the european union must therefore give strong support, first and foremost, to our companies in their research and development efforts. this will enable them to use ever more innovative and less polluting technologies to meet the challenges of sustainable development. in december, at the lima conference, we will have to engage with our partners in a frank, serious and pragmatic dialogue. we must not impose our goals on others because acting unilaterally is not the solution. while the eu is currently responsible for only 11% of global co2 emissions - a share that will decrease in the coming years - it cannot take the decisions on its own. europe must not be the great naïve of the climate negotiations. the lima conference must therefore be a real preparatory phase for the great paris conference. in 2015, we have a good chance of reaching a concerted international agreement, which is therefore sound and respected by all. you have mentioned many challenges, commissioner, and there is an urgency to solve the ukrainian problem. there is an urgent need to combat terrorism. there is an urgent need to stem the spread of ebola. we all have to be determined. as jean monnet said - and i conclude - 'the important thing is not to be optimistic or pessimistic, but to be determined'. and in the epp group, on all these issues, we are.
mr president, in 2008 the european institutions adopted the first climate-energy package and europe was in fact taking a leading role in energy, climate and industrial matters. unfortunately, this ambition has been exhausted and the package proposed by the european commission, on which our european leaders will be working, considerably reduces this ambition. with a 30% efficiency target, this is an ambition reduced by a third between the decade of 2010 and the decade of 2020. with a target of 27% renewable energy, that's a reduced ambition by half. so how can this new commission see that with such a package we are going to be the world leaders in climate and energy? we talk a lot about economy and realism here, but the reality is that with 40% efficiency, we do without russian gas. the economic reality is that two thirds of new electricity capacity installed in europe is renewable energy sources. there is economic realism, there is climate realism. let us have the ambition to be pragmatic, to save the climate, to save european industry and to create jobs!

in writing. - with my gue/ngl colleagues and 200 other meps, i voted with a heavy heart against the commission proposed by jean-claude juncker. the majority of the european parliament approved it by 423 votes to 209 with 67 abstentions, far fewer than the commission under manuel barroso in 2004 and 2009. but this is only a continuation of the same dogmatisms, which are far removed from the message of the citizens in the european elections. the new commission is therefore not up to the challenges, particularly the democratic and social challenges of the present day. its architecture puts market in almost every commissioner's portfolio; the commission has not taken account of the few requests made during the cartoons of the hearings of the commissioners-designate before the european parliament. while the actual evaluation of the candidatures before the parliamentary committees quickly gave way to blackmail between the main political groups, the epp, s&d and alde, the majority of the european parliament has thus finished ridiculing itself and will bear a heavy responsibility in the situation to come. the maintenance of mr navracsics and mr canete are two sad caricatures of what should not have been done. let those who supported it not come and lecture us.
in writing. this draft amending budget for 2014 on the surplus resulting from the implementation of the 2013 financial year aims to record more than eur 1 billion in surplus for the 2013 financial year, eur 771 million from positive revenue (including fines and interest on late payment) and eur 276 million from under-implementation of expenditure. i would like to remind you that the 2014-2020 multiannual framework does not take into account the outstanding amounts, which at the end of 2013 amounted to eur 23.4 billion. the growing gap between commitments and payments has led to the emergence of a european debt even as brussels is sending letters to the member states on their budgets. it is also interesting to note that european competition policy is not so perfect, as evidenced by the high level of fines and interest (an additional 1.331 billion for 2013 but surely more than 3 billion in 2014...). finally, as this draft amending budget does not in any way change the budgetary and political guidelines adopted, i voted against it.
in writing. - i welcome the efforts of sound budgetary management which have resulted in a surplus of around eur 1 billion in the 2013 budget. given the very high pressure on the budget of the european union, this surplus will be entered as revenue in the 2014 budget. in a context of budgetary difficulties, it is essential to ensure the proper allocation of surpluses.
in writing. the eu financial regulation provides that the commission presents each year a draft amending budget to budget the surplus resulting from the previous year's budgetary exercise, in this case 2013. the payment situation is becoming critical from year to year. so, at the end of 2013, there were more than 23 billion unpaid and today they would be approaching the amount of 30 billion. this is of course a cause for concern, as the european budget is financed by 75% national contributions. although the treaty gives the council and parliament the same power over expenditure, in practice the states have the final say on payments. an agreement on the 2014 amending budget is therefore both an urgent necessity and a prerequisite for the final adoption of the 2015 budget. we will be vigilant, as europe needs a consolidated budget to invest in growth. more deeply, the recurring crises are a reminder of the urgent need for a substantive debate on eu resources in order to increase the eu's budgetary autonomy.
in writing. - the draft amending budget is only intended to budget the surplus for the financial year 2013. however, we are again facing a deficit in payment appropriations this year. we must find a lasting solution to the recurrent problem of unpaid debts and stop this snowball effect from becoming paralysed in a budgetary crisis. the credibility of the european union is at stake.
in writing. this report endorses the 2nd amending budget of the union for 2014. it aims to enter in the 2014 budget the 'surplus' of the 2013 financial year of eur 1 005 000 000. sign of chaotic eu management: the budget shows a surplus while at the same time all existing indicators show a shortage of payment appropriations, both in the 2012 budget and in the 2013 budget. the report proposes to allocate this 'surplus' to finance a new budget line, numbered 40 04 01, entitled 'reserve for additional payment needs'. a cat won't find her kittens there! a surplus to pay for a non-payment of the same budget. i shall abstain on that text.
in writing. this draft amending budget no 2/2014 does not solve the serious underlying problem of unpaid debts. at 31/12/2013, these amounted to more than €23 million and, taking into account the expected snowball effect, the outstanding invoices will exceed €27 million by the end of 2014. worse, the eu has 220 billion ral (commitment appropriations not covered by payment appropriations) on its hands. clearly, the eu has made commitments it cannot honour and is therefore unable to apply to itself the budgetary rigour it requires of the member states. today, it is practically on the verge of default. finally, in such a context, what credibility can be given to mr juncker who announces a major multiannual programme of additional investments of eur 300 billion? who 's gonna pay for this ? the member states ? or should we expect the creation of a european direct tax which will put a further strain on the purchasing power of the european people, already crushed by the austerity measures imposed by brussels... this draft amending budget is therefore only a small backstop to contain a hemorrhage. for all these reasons, i voted against.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution on the protocol to the eu-republic of korea free trade agreement to take account of croatia's accession to the european union. since 2010, the eu and south korea have strengthened their ties through a strategic partnership that ensures a high level of mutual commitment. these relations are based mainly on two major agreements: the eu-south korea framework agreement adopted in 2010 and the eu-south korea free trade agreement adopted in 2011. this is the most ambitious trade agreement ever negotiated by the european union and the first signed with an asian country. it provides for the abolition of customs duties on almost 99% of traded products within five years, as well as the disappearance of many non-tariff barriers. it will stimulate bilateral trade, based on the principle of reciprocity. it will also improve the penetration of european companies into the korean market and, more broadly, throughout asia.

in writing. - when croatia acceded to the european union (1 july 2013), the additional protocol to the eu-korea free trade agreement was signed on the same day to take account of this accession and has been provisionally applied since that date. the current council decision aims to ensure that croatia can continue to participate fully in the eu-korea agreement. i therefore supported this report, which will help to complete the process of ratification of the additional protocol.
in writing. this report on the european semester for economic policy coordination and priorities for 2014 perfectly reflects the whole 'europeanist' thinking that currently dominates the european union. even as the peoples are suffering from an economic crisis that is not going away, this report suggests nothing less than continuing the policy of austerity, the harmful effects of which are clear. he insists on the need for member states to respect brussels' budgetary requirements under penalty of legal proceedings and elevates the euro, the single currency, to the altar of prosperity (even though the eurozone is in worse shape than the european union itself!). the report recognises an increase of 10 million people living in poverty between 2010 and 2012, but offers its own solutions to boost growth: structural reform including health systems and reducing the retirement age, a common, modern and inclusive immigration policy, stimulating labour mobility and free movement, restoring a favourable environment for business... in short, a descent into hell with ever more federalism and ultra-liberalism, which is why i voted against.
in writing. - the european semester is the european mechanism for economic governance. it provides an overview of the economic and financial policies of the european union and a roadmap identifying weaknesses on which each country needs to make progress. following the serious consequences of the crisis, it was important to develop a mechanism for harmonising the economic policies of the member states in order to avoid a situation similar to that experienced in 2008. i voted in favour of this text, which sets out the progress that each member state must make in order to emerge definitively from this economic recession. each state must be aware of its economic influence on the rest of europe. we have chosen to integrate our markets to form the european single market. if one state fails, others will also suffer the consequences. it is therefore essential to coordinate national fiscal policies and to implement the structural reforms needed to restore the european economy.
in writing. - the report on the european semester, the cycle of coordination of economic and budgetary policies within the european union, raises many very interesting questions in a constructive spirit. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the euro as a currency for the purpose of monetary policy. if france is not mentioned, we know that it is targeted. i regret that because of the current government's inability to carry out ambitious reforms, our country is once again lagging behind. nevertheless, the report proposes balanced solutions: to continue structural reforms while investing in research and development for better quality products. it contains proposals which are in the right direction, which is why i am in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the text reminds the member states that the necessary structural reforms must be implemented: they require courage but they are indispensable! i believe that the way to stimulate growth is to modernise our social security and health care systems without hindering patients' access to medical innovation and our pension systems by taking account of the ageing population. we must avoid imposing too heavy a burden on future generations. this is an emergency! the european commission will have to submit quarterly reports to parliament on progress in the follow-up of country-specific recommendations; and the eurogroup president will have to include a follow-up report in his assessment of the national budget plans for 2015. it is time for some member states to get to work at last!
in writing. - the reorientation of european economic and budgetary policies was to be reflected in the recommendations made in the context of the european semester. the final text of this report, which i support, contains important proposals from the socialists and democrats to reorient the union's economic and budgetary policies. the draft of automatic sanctions is finally excluded and the flexibilities of the stability and growth pact are put forward. we have also been able to get the report to stress the €300 billion investment plan needed to boost public and private investment in europe, the fight against unemployment, particularly youth unemployment, and the need to create a common unemployment insurance scheme for the euro zone. i regret that the energy transition issues, which are important for a return to sustainable growth, have not been included, but this text provides a basis on which the european parliament can base its support for the reorientation of economic and budgetary policies.
in writing. - it is important that the economic and budgetary policy recommendations be better implemented. we must remain vigilant in the face of the recent market crisis and not hesitate to carry out the necessary reforms.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this report on the european semester for the coordination of economic policies in 2014. it is important that the commission seizes the opportunity offered by the europe 2020 mid-term review and the revision of the integrated guidelines to strengthen the role of the single market for growth, innovation and jobs. the union's competitiveness needs to be strengthened in key areas such as the services sector, the energy sector, the transport sector and the digital single market. more determined efforts are needed to guide and coordinate national and union policies in order to complete the single market and reap its benefits, while continuing on the path of ambitious structural reforms in the member states. financing the real economy, and in particular smes, must be a priority and targeted and strategic investment, whether public or private, is essential to this end. i therefore welcome the €300 billion investment programme proposed by the president of the european commission, jean-claude juncker, which is due to be presented by the end of 2014.

in writing. - the coherence of the european union's policies needs to be strengthened more than ever, given that jean-claude juncker, the future president of the european commission, is promising a €300 billion investment plan. this report, which sets out the priorities of the european semester, thus attempts to highlight such consistency. i am grateful in this respect for some of the guidelines promoted by the european parliament, such as the coherence of the european union's investment in innovation, and access to finance for small and mediumsized enterprises. in the light of current international developments, there is an increased urgency to establish a sound common energy policy and to strengthen coordination in the economic and monetary union. it is therefore necessary to be vigilant about the development of the successive common policies of the union and to ensure the greatest possible involvement of the european parliament in their elaboration.
in writing. - the european semester is the european union's economic governance cycle which allows member states to coordinate their economic policies to stimulate growth and employment and balance their budgets. however, only 10% of the country-specific reform recommendations issued by the commission for 2013 have been fully implemented, and little progress has been made on 45% of them. the implementation of the country-specific recommendations is essential to ensure economic coordination within the economic and monetary union and that is why i voted in favour of this report. genuine democratic accountability could also be established by the commission presenting quarterly reports to parliament on progress in implementing country-specific recommendations; in addition, member states which are falling behind in implementing the recommendations could come to explain their situation to the european parliament.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr de backer's report on the economic and budgetary policy recommendations made in the context of the european semester. the removal from the report of the blackmail of the states to make the allocation of structural funds conditional on compliance with the 3% rule was decisive in my vote. as was the removal of automatic eu economic sanctions on member states that do not comply with this rule. we have therefore secured the adoption of some of our priorities, such as increasing public investment and using the flexibilities of the stability and growth pact. i regret, however, that this report did not go far enough. it does not include the withdrawal of the member states' contributions to the union budget, which is essentially investment expenditure, or the questioning of the austerity policy, despite its flagrant failure. finally, i denounce the political positions of a right-wing party which has still not realised the importance of the energy transition and the potential for growth and job creation that it would represent in this context of crisis and mass unemployment.
