in writing. this report, which aims to amend regulation (eu) no 374/2014, aims to reduce or eliminate customs duties on goods originating in ukraine. following the negotiation of an association agreement between the eu and ukraine for the period 2007-2011 on the establishment of a free trade area and its signature on 27 june, the regulation should therefore be extended until 31 december 2015. even though ukraine is experiencing significant tensions, the current eu policy can only lead to a deterioration in our relations with russia. the report states that according to statistics, ukraine's exports to the eu increased sharply in early 2014 (+25% or usd 587 million) while those to russia decreased (-24.5% or usd 592 million). the report highlights the opportunity for ukraine, through these trade measures, to diversify its outlets and encourage its adaptation to the standards required in the eu, ahead of the full free trade agreement in 2016. in view of the economic crisis we are experiencing, however, reason would have us reject this agreement both from the political point of view (our relations with russia risk deteriorating) and from the economic point of view (the total opening of borders and free trade have only caused relocations, unemployment and deindustrialisation in the countries of western europe). that is why i voted against it.
in writing. - the european parliament has taken the irresponsible decision to strengthen trade relations between the european union and ukraine. the economic association policy with ukraine, as it is being pursued today, has the direct effect of worsening relations between the eu member states and russia. france has no economic or political interest in maintaining a nato-desired cold war climate. worse still, while we see everywhere that the enlargement of the union to include the eastern european countries has created unfair competition between workers and caused massive relocations to these countries, the european parliament proposes to continue this suicidal policy by extending the application of regulation (eu) no 374/2014 on the reduction or elimination of customs duties on goods originating in ukraine, a country where the average monthly salary is barely usd 292! this reduction in customs duties will mean even more job losses and unemployment for our compatriots. that is why i voted against the extension of this regulation.
in writing. - this text aims to help ukraine cope with the political, economic and security crisis in the country. it will eliminate or reduce customs duties on goods originating in ukraine and thus support its external trade. moreover, in the current context, the swift approval by parliament proves that the union is capable of acting promptly and decisively while respecting its political commitments.
in writing. after several months of political crisis, aggravated by the conflict in the west of ukraine, the country is experiencing a dramatic economic situation. it therefore needs the help of the european union. until the entry into force of the eu-ukraine association agreement in january 2016, the union should continue to grant tariff preferences to ukrainian products exported to the european market. these unilateral trade preferences remove 94.7% of the eu customs duties applied to imports of industrial goods from ukraine. they also remove eu customs duties on over 80% of ukrainian agricultural exports. however, the eu has restricted zero-duty amounts for 'sensitive' products such as cereals, pork, beef, poultry and processed foods so that they do not harm the interests of european producers. in return, ukraine is obliged to respect eu health standards, as well as human rights, fundamental freedoms and the rule of law. this process aims to enable the country to modernise, reform and actively fight against corruption. the large victory of pro-western ukrainian parties in the parliamentary elections is, from this point of view, a guarantee.
in writing. - i voted in favour of extending until the end of 2015 the lifting of customs barriers for ukrainian exports to the european union. this exceptional measure responds to the exceptional nature of the situation in ukraine. the union has a moral duty to this partner, which is under immense pressure from russia in the economic, military and energy fields. while these measures have, according to initial estimates, kept the activities of ukrainian enterprises and industries afloat, with exports increasing by between 10 and 25% in the first part of the year, they must not create the conditions for unfair competition with our own enterprises and place further burdens on european farmers. on this last point i shall be firm and if i find that our support is endangering the commercial activities of european firms, industries and agriculture, i shall consider these measures again in the sense of rebalancing.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr gabrielius landsbergis on customs duties on goods originating in ukraine. the measures adopted will help to alleviate the burden of russian sanctions on the ukrainian economy.
in writing. this text is in continuity with the desire of the european institutions to integrate ukraine economically, forcing it to make the absurd choice of development prospects with the eu countries at the expense of its main external market, russia, with which it is de facto united by strong cultural ties. as the application of the eu-ukraine association agreement has been postponed until 31 december 2015, the commission proposes to extend the eu regulation on the reduction of customs duties in trade between the eu and ukraine to 1 november 2014. as i am opposed to this association agreement which was the trigger for the ukrainian crisis, i am voting against it. in addition, this text is conditional on ukraine respecting fundamental principles related to human rights, democracy and the rule of law. but these conditions are clearly not being met in ukraine: the use of cluster munitions banned in civilian areas, the banning of the communist party, the banning of certain television channels, censorship laws, the presence of neo-nazis in the government. i am therefore surprised that such a proposal has even been put to us.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text which goes hand in hand with the association agreements we voted last month. the eu-ukraine association agreements, which were approved at an extraordinary meeting, will take effect in december 2015. in order to avoid a legal vacuum and the loss of our trade gains in ukraine, we have extended the free trade agreements in force until 31 december 2014 until the end of next year.
in writing. - i voted to extend favorable customs measures to ukraine. it must be understood that if ukraine falls economically, europe will suffer too. we are therefore temporarily helping ukraine to resist the russian embargo by facilitating access for its products to the european market. for now, it shows its effectiveness and yet we do not feel invaded by ukrainian products! it's a small gesture for europe, a giant support for ukraine. we must at all costs prevent ukraine from being able to pay its gas bills to russia, and thus prevent the collapse of the country. because if the taps shut down, we're at the end of the reservoir as winter approaches. this is a situation that must be avoided at all costs.
in writing. the commission notes that the measures were imposed on the basis of the information provided by the goc and the sampled exporting producers. however, following the trilateral meeting between ukraine, the european union and russia, the eu agreed to delay the implementation of the trade part of its association agreement with ukraine until december 2015. i voted in favour of this report so that ukraine can continue to benefit from trade preferences without interruption and so that the european union can prove that it can act quickly and decisively. in addition, the european union continues and reaffirms its objectives, as ukraine will be required to respect eu health standards as well as human rights, fundamental freedoms and the rule of law in order to benefit from these preferential trade measures.
in writing. the purpose of this report is to give a discharge to the management committee of the office of the body of european regulators for electronic communications on the implementation of the 2012 budget. in view of the comments which are an integral part of this discharge, i have voted against this vote. the comments call for the office to exercise better control over its future budget, given the budget implementation rates of 89.55% and the payment appropriations rates of 76.57%. as with the general eu budget, the rate of committed appropriations cancelled and carried over to 2013 is worrying: 28% (against 45% in the previous budget year!). similarly, unused appropriations still amount to 14,6% in 2013 (17% in 2012). finally, i would also like to deplore the lack of transparency in the office and note that it has just included in its financial manual a detailed and binding checklist for the award of contracts and the appointment of a contracting officer...

in writing. inland waterway professionals are subject to irregular work patterns. the ships sail an average of 14 hours a day, often for several consecutive days. hence the need to implement a specific legislation on working time for cabin crew, as the general working time directive does not allow for these specific needs to be taken into account. the transposition of the agreement between the social partners on minimum requirements for working time on ships is a good answer. workers in this sector will now be able to benefit from legislation adapted to their activity. the proposal for a directive makes compulsory the agreement of 15 february 2012 between the social partners (european union of inland navigation, european shipowners' organisation and european transport workers' federation) on the organisation of working time in inland navigation, which sets out certain minimum guarantees for workers (working time, rest periods, annual leave). the text thus endorses the principle of increased use of dialogue between the social partners to develop union social law. this is a necessary step towards enhancing european social democracy, which i am committed to.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution, for which i was the rapporteur for the french delegation of the epp. the aim of the report is to recommend the introduction of a directive implementing the european agreement concluded by the social partners in the inland waterway sector. the agreement will fill the void left by the working time directive for inland waterway carriers and will help to combat social dumping. it includes working and rest times, holidays, seasonal work and the safety and health of workers. this text sets minimum requirements for the member states, which will remain free to set their own rules.
in writing. - the text which has been tabled is a resolution setting out parliament's position on the agreement between the trade unions and employers on the working time of boatmen. these seafarers are in a bolkestein-type situation in that they can practise their profession in a state other than the one in which their contract is established, which can create a situation of social dumping on their working conditions. the agreement negotiated between the trade unions and the employers on the working time of boatmen is a step forward, as it introduces minimum working and rest times. however, this agreement does not solve the problem of dumping in the profession which will continue because of the differences between the various labour rights. i therefore abstained in order not to block this minimum resulting from the european social dialogue, which is still lower than that practiced in france and therefore leaves open the possibility of unfair competition between european shipbuilders.
in writing. an agreement was reached on 15 february 2012 between the social partners (european inland navigation union, european boat owners' organisation and european transport workers' federation) on the organisation of working time in inland navigation. it lays down certain guarantees for workers: working time, rest periods, annual leave. the proposal aims to give effect to the terms of the agreement following an initial opposition by the council. i vote for it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text, which now ensures minimum harmonization of working time in the inland waterway sector. this text is the validation of an agreement between the social partners which sets a maximum ceiling for hours worked. this is not a regulation of working time in the traditional sense, but rather an agreement to eliminate social dumping and the most extreme practices. the inland waterway sector (mainly river transport) has an important future in achieving our environmental objectives and reindustrialising europe. the text provides flexibility for workers in order not to penalise them and to maintain the competitiveness of the sector.
in writing. - i supported this resolution which recommends adopting the european commission's proposal on specific regulations on working time in the inland waterway sector. this text is the result of an agreement reached at european level by the representatives of employers and workers in the sector. this agreement lays down minimum requirements for working time on passenger and cargo ships. it will enable satisfactory working conditions and adequate rest periods for workers in the sector to be established; essential conditions for the health and safety of the crew and cabin crew. the agreement was urgently needed, given that more than 75% of inland waterway transport within the european union is transnational. these measures would ultimately contribute to better working conditions for 31000 workers and to fairer competition between the 9645 companies in the sector.
in writing. - i voted against this european parliament resolution on a proposal for a commission directive on an agreement between the social partners on the organization of work in inland waterway transport. in this area, the european parliament can only give an opinion on this sector excluded from the working time directive. i found that not all the unions had participated in the negotiations and that while this agreement could improve social provisions in some member states, it was very regressive for the law applicable in france. although the agreement provides that more favourable provisions in the member states will be maintained, the provisions of the country where the vessel is moored will apply when navigating on a 'cross-border' river route. there is no doubt that the societies which can apply the most favourable law will seek the solutions which will enable them to be the most competitive at the expense of social rights. i can therefore only see it as an instrument of social dumping to the detriment of french employees and dockers in particular. the agreement, although it is accompanied by improvements in some member states, is a means of levelling down the social acquis.

in writing. the court of auditors' report on the 2013 eu budget shows that almost €7 billion was spent 'by mistake' (€6.97 billion to be exact), which still represents 4.7% of the total budget. the 'errors' are particularly important in rural development (6.7%) and regional policy (6.9%). the court even cites a few examples of "wrongly made errors" when, in many cases, these are actual frauds. for example, a slovenian sme was subsidised while being a subsidiary of large automotive groups. even better, in several countries, land that was subsidized as permanent pasture has been partially or completely covered with wood. the european union requires member states, subject to the budgetary treaty, to control their public expenditure, but it does not apply to itself the principles of good management which it advocates. in the face of this overwhelming observation, i would be even more vigilant about the use of european public funds, the waste of which is an affront to the thousands of taxpayers subject to austerity and ultra-liberal policies. it is high time that we demand from this technocratic europe exemplary transparency in the management of public money.
in writing. the court of auditors' report underlines, in its section on regional policy, that of 180 operations audited, nearly 102 were affected by irregularities, or almost 57% of the total number of operations audited. as such, breaches of public procurement rules account for more than 30% of the error rate estimated by the court. these figures reflect the failure of cohesion policy, which, far from promoting the convergence of member states' economies, finances projects that are too often oversized and not effectively monitored by the certification authorities. many member states have a financial envelope that is not adequate for their administrative capacity to absorb european funds. the court noted that this tension increased as the end of the period of eligibility approached. unspent funds are used to reimburse ineligible costs or to finance projects that are too expensive or unlikely to produce the expected results. the court's report shows that a complete overhaul of regional policy must be carried out in the primary interest of the contributing member states.
in writing. the european court of auditors' annual report for the financial year 2013 demonstrates that once again the european union and its institutions are operating in complete disconnection from reality. this gigantic administrative and technocratic machine is being run irresponsibly. it is clear that the union's expenditure is only too modestly subject to the logic of performance and efficiency. without a clear objective, it is a question of spending appropriations to spend appropriations. such an illustrative absurdity of the european union. more importantly, the expenditure side has almost €7 billion in errors, partly due to the lack of rigour in the distribution of eu funds. this is equivalent to one third of france's contribution to the community budget. this is all the more shocking given that the european union has nearly €30 billion in unpaid bills. finally, there is little hope that the system will be reformed, as the court's recommendations rarely reach the ears of european leaders, but let us remember that this insane technocracy lives on the backs of the people.

in writing. - this agreement is presented as a prelude to moldova's accession to the european union. i am opposed to any further enlargement under the present conditions, as i do not want to subject other peoples to the austerity of the peoples of europe. it would also be a way of relieving moldova of russian pressure by strengthening its access to the european market. so this is clearly another act of preparing hostility with russia. the report nevertheless claims to assert that the eastern partnership does not constitute a threat to russia's political or economic interests . i'm sick of your hypocrisy. i vote against it.
in writing. with this association agreement, moldova has taken another step towards joining the european union. president juncker had announced at his inauguration that there would be no enlargement. the report is very clear. it shows all the risks faced by the other member states in the event of moldova's accession, the main one of which will obviously be social dumping. the european union (and therefore the member states) has already been very generous to moldova. between 2007 and 2014, €1 billion was distributed to this country, which is, let us recall, one of the poorest on the continent (30% of its population living below the poverty line). in addition, there is a common element: corruption and the underground economy that is ravaging moldova. i also do not forget the human rights that are openly violated in this country, including the proven facts of human trafficking. the peoples are sovereign and must be consulted by referendum on any new enlargement project.
in writing. this agreement follows the proposed partnership between ukraine and the european union, which has contributed to deepening divisions between pro-russian and pro-european parties. almost all of ukraine has now been plunged into violence and division. this new agreement with moldova raises a number of doubts as to its validity. it is up to the european union to take the measure of history and to find a consensus with russia that will allow the development and future of the border countries and of europe and russia to be consolidated, and not to establish agreements with these countries that compete with russia and that could lead to their internal destabilisation. i therefore abstained on these two texts.
in writing. the european ultra-liberal system is not working and ruining the peoples of europe, so its grip is being extended even further. the arrival of moldova in a bleak economic zone with no future is bad news for the moldovans, the french and the other peoples of europe. i therefore vote against this association agreement.
in writing. - the conclusion of an association agreement between ukraine and moldova is a key element in stabilising the area, where important political choices are being made for the future. i therefore vote in favour of better cooperation between the european union and moldova, because in the long term both will benefit from increased rule of law and trade cooperation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution which supports the ratification of the association agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova, including a comprehensive and in-depth free trade agreement. this agreement was made possible by political and economic reforms in moldova, but it is not an end in itself. the eu and moldova have agreed to continue to work together in the field of economic and political reforms, and to maintain and deepen their relations.
in writing. - the association agreements with moldova (in preparation) and ukraine (already voted) have a significant geopolitical impact: they demonstrate the aggressiveness of european diplomacy towards russia. the white house's shadow is hanging over the file. i am also opposed and will be opposed with all my strength to the enlargement of the european union, which is already too large to be viable. the european union is destroying itself from within, not only by emptying the nation states of their sovereign marrow, but by giving itself body and soul to a declining us power with gigantic nuisance capabilities.
in writing. - i abstained in the final vote on the eu-moldova association agreement. as always, this agreement contains first and foremost a free trade agreement between the two parties, which i am opposed to. these agreements are mainly beneficial to certain european economic interests by obliging the associated state to pursue policies of economic liberalization and structural adjustment. we know what this means in terms of social consequences! the moldovans will probably be killed, as will many others. however, this agreement is also expected by many of these moldovans who hope in particular for greater freedom of movement between their country and the member states of the union, thanks in particular to a minimum of visa liberalisation. i therefore wanted to give them a signal by abstaining, even though i know that the eu's association agreements with the various states in the region are hardly intended to bring democracy and development, and are instead full of ulterior motives, as we have seen with ukraine (to mention only the most caricatured of the most recently adopted agreements).
in writing. i voted against because the conditions for an association between the european union and the republic of moldova are far from being met: the underground economy accounts for more than 40% of the gdp of this country whose minimum wage is only 43 euros per month. at a time when the peoples of the member states of the european union are experiencing great economic difficulties, i refuse to see the eu embarking on new, costly and dangerous adventures.
in writing. - this report on an association agreement between the european union and moldova, which provides for a large free trade area and closer economic ties, is only a preliminary to a planned eu accession. the country received more than €1 billion from the eu between 2007 and 2014, yet 30% of its population still lives below the poverty line. the worrying level of its underground economy (40%) and the endemic corruption that prevails there will obviously not promote compliance with european rules on health, food security, respect for fundamental rights or the good management of the european public funds allocated to it. finally, the eu, so quick to condemn the measures taken by russia, forgets that moldova is the leading country for human trafficking with over 3000 cases recorded between 2000 and 2012 and that russia's sanctions measures are only the logical follow-up for any sovereign state of the retaliatory measures taken against it by the eu upstream. for all these reasons, i voted against this report.
in writing. the conclusion of the association agreement between the european union and the european atomic energy community and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of moldova, of the other part, is a strong sign of recognition of the reform efforts and ambitions of the moldovan authorities. i support this association agreement, but i stress that a continuation of constructive dialogue with russia remains necessary if moldova is to develop in a peaceful neighbourhood.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation of my colleague petras austrevicius on the association agreement with moldova, an important step in relations with that country which, as in the case of ukraine, has been under pressure from russia in the form of trade embargoes and increased russian support for the secessionist territory of transnistria.
in writing. - i voted in favour of ratifying the association agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova, signed at the european union summit on 27 june 2014. i am pleased that this agreement has the support of 535 members.

in writing. moldova is facing the russian embargo. it therefore wants to sell its fruit and vegetables in the european union without paying any customs duty. this is the principle of this eu-moldova free trade agreement. the european union will thus mobilise some €445 million to support moldovan agriculture, to the detriment of european farmers who are suffering the disastrous effects of the russian embargo and falling prices. encouraging imports from moldova without any customs duties is a heavy penalty for our farmers. moldova, which, it should be recalled, does not apply the same standards, particularly environmental standards. the european union is therefore openly mocking the suffering it inflicts on its farmers. bankruptcy and suicide is the future the eu is offering farmers, and all in the name of ultra-liberal dogma. i voted against it.
in writing. rejecting the economic agreement, it would be absurd for me to endorse this agreement in the specific field of atomic energy. i therefore vote against.

in writing. this convention on international guarantees for mobile equipment is part of the drive to liberalize the railway sector completely, which i strongly oppose. the ratification of the protocol by the european union, on behalf of the european union, is also contrary to the idea i advocate of cooperation between sovereign states. these are two good reasons why i could only vote against the adoption of this convention.
in writing. this convention on international guarantees for mobile equipment is closely linked to the fourth railway package, the ultimate aim of which is the total liberalisation of the railway sector, with the social and spatial consequences that we know (see the united kingdom). but here the united kingdom will not be part of the protocol, nor will denmark. the situation is quite different for the other countries, since a regional economic integration organization will have the same rights to approve the protocol. the european union is therefore entitled to ratify this protocol in place of the member states, which are still renouncing their sovereignty, and for these reasons i voted against this convention.
in writing. - the protocol on international guarantees relating to mobile equipment, article 22 provides: 'a regional economic integration organization constituted by sovereign states and having competence over certain matters governed by this protocol may also sign, accept and approve this protocol or accede to it. in such a case, the regional economic integration organisation shall have the same rights and obligations as a contracting state.' without prejudice to the technical provisions of this protocol, the problem is the extension of the scope of ratification. it is not acceptable that the european union can ratify such a convention binding on sovereign states without their respective agreement, instead of the sovereign states. it should also be recalled that those powers conferred on the european union are based on its exclusive competence in certain matters relating to the railway sector and on article 3 of the feu treaty, which provides that 'the union shall have exclusive competence to conclude an international agreement where such conclusion is necessary to enable it to exercise its internal competence'. as a fierce opponent of this article of the lisbon treaty, i naturally voted against the approval, on behalf of the european union, of the new protocol.
in writing. the european parliament voted in favour of the council decision approving the agreement on the protocol on railway rolling stock-specific matters to the convention on international guarantees of mobile equipment. the protocol encourages capital investment in the railway sector. this is in line with the objectives of the fourth railway package to encourage innovation and increase investment in the union rail system. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the european parliament approved the protocol on specific questions relating to railway rolling stock to the convention on international guarantees of equipment for mobile equipment. i have given my approval to a text which will encourage the offer of funding for railway rolling stock. the protocol will create an international guarantee for creditors, which will in particular encourage capital investment in the railway sector.

in writing. i voted in favour of the recommendation by my colleague heidi hautala on the protocol on specific questions relating to railway rolling stock to the convention on international guarantees of equipment for mobile equipment. the text supports the council conclusions on the ratification by the european union of the luxembourg protocol signed in 2007, which sets international standards for the railway sector. the recommendation was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. i supported the report on the approval of the luxembourg protocol on railway rolling stock-specific matters to the convention on international guarantees of equipment for mobile equipment. the purpose of this protocol is to facilitate the offer of financing for high value railway rolling stock by creating a strong international guarantee in favour of creditors. it also establishes a single international registration system for international guarantees and thus contributes to the establishment of a common judicial area based on the principle of mutual recognition of judicial decisions, which will encourage capital investment in the railway sector.
in writing. - the aim is to approve the council's proposal for the establishment of a railway protocol in connection with the fourth railway package, which i had opposed. the purpose of this protocol is to facilitate the offer of financing for high value railway rolling stock by creating a strong international guarantee in favour of creditors. the commission stresses that this protocol should encourage capital investment in the railway sector and contribute to the creation of a private market for the rental of mobile equipment in europe. this is to intensify competition at the expense of the public service. all of which i condemn. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted against this convention, which transfers our national sovereignty even more into the hands of the european union. article 22 of the protocol on international guarantees for mobile equipment states that 'a regional economic integration organisation consisting of sovereign states and having competence over certain matters governed by this protocol may also sign, accept and approve this protocol or accede to it. in such a case, the regional economic integration organisation shall have the same rights and obligations as a contracting state.' the extension of the scope of ratification poses a problem here, since it allows the european union to ratify, in place of the sovereign states, the convention which will bind them, obviously without a respective agreement. it should also be noted that article 3 tfeu (treaty of lisbon), which provides that 'the european union shall have exclusive competence to conclude an international agreement where such conclusion ... is necessary to enable it to exercise its internal competence', has given the european union exclusive competence in railway matters.
in writing. i supported this report which provides for the ratification by the european union of the convention on international guarantees for mobile equipment. the convention applies when the debtor is located in a contracting state and strengthens the rights of creditors if the debtor fails to perform his obligations. the application of this convention is likely to strengthen investor confidence in the field of mobile equipment.

in writing. i voted against the adoption of this convention which, under the pretext of resolving international commercial disputes, contributes to the dispossession of states of their judicial sovereignty in favour of a so-called 'international justice' of dubious legitimacy.
in writing. this 2005 convention on choice of court agreements, which the eu already signed in 2009, is here to be adopted by the european union. it is a private international law convention (the only country to have signed it so far is mexico) that clearly erodes the sovereignty of states. an exclusive choice of court agreement may be concluded by two or more parties to designate courts (or one or more specific courts) of a contracting state with jurisdiction to hear disputes arising from a particular relationship of law. the convention aims to ensure that the courts chosen by the parties to a transaction will hear the dispute and that the resulting judgment will be recognised in other countries. i therefore voted against this recommendation, rejecting any weakening of the sovereignty of the states of the nations, including that of my country, france.
in writing. - the hague convention signed on 30 june 2005 states that 'an agreement on the choice of court allows the parties to designate in advance a court of a contracting state which has jurisdiction to hear and determine disputes arising or to arise in connection with a particular area of law'. in principle, the approval of such a convention is an act of judicial sovereignty which must belong exclusively to the states recognised by international law and not to an organisation sui generis, even if it has legal personality. the hague convention will oblige signatory states to accept that a dispute between two parties is decided by a court of a state party to the convention, whether or not it is a member of the european union. the european parliament's unusual approval of the hague convention reflects the european union's desire to have greater powers in the field of foreign policy. as a defender of the full sovereignty of france, i naturally voted against the approval of the hague convention by the european parliament.
in writing. the european parliament voted in favour of the council decision to approve, on behalf of the european union, the hague convention on choice of court agreements. these agreements stipulate that both parties agree that any dispute will be submitted to the courts of the indicated state. the convention is very important as it defines the choice of court agreements, covers matters of jurisdiction, recognition and enforcement and also regulates several procedural matters. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the approval by the european parliament of the hague convention of 30 june 2005 on the agreements for the election of the forum is a positive step. it will ensure legal certainty without the need to change the legal framework already in place in the european union. the object of the convention is identical to article 25 of the brussels i regulation already in force at european level.
in writing. the spirit of this text is to strengthen the supranational level in areas which fall within the competence of the states. the european union's accession to such a convention also helps to consolidate the eu's legal and political position, which i deplore, and for which reason i voted against this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the recommendation of my colleague pavel svoboda on the ratification of the hague convention on the election of forums. this agreement reduces the degree of legal uncertainty for european companies trading outside the union, while allowing for the creation of a harmonised set of rules at european level. after its signature in 2009, the council must now ratify the treaty, which the recommendation agrees to do. the text was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the approval of the hague convention of 30 june 2005 on choice of court agreements. the convention aims to enhance legal certainty and predictability for parties to inter-company agreements and international disputes by creating a global, optional judicial dispute resolution mechanism. the convention thus guarantees european undertakings operating outside the union that the choice of court agreements included in their contracts are respected and that judgments given by the courts designated in those agreements can be recognised and enforced in the other states parties to the convention.
in writing. - the hague convention deals with agreements on the election of courts in civil and commercial matters. in these types of agreements, the parties decide together in which country the dispute should be settled, thus allowing the parties to decide which law, which national legal body, should be relevant to resolve their disputes. the aim is to ratify the hague convention on private international law, which the union signed in 2009. the convention's wider ratification could provide greater legal certainty for international agreements. it should be noted that so far only mexico has ratified it. however, there are few safeguards to prevent market competition in the legislative systems. in view of the risks of dumping, i shall abstain.
in writing. the hague convention of 30 june 2005 provided that 'an agreement on the choice of court' allows 'parties to designate in advance a court of a contracting state which has jurisdiction to hear and determine disputes arising or to arise in connection with a particular legal relationship'. the hague convention thus clearly disregards the sovereignty of states. thus, in the event of a dispute between two parties, it will have to be decided by a court of a state party, whether or not it belongs to the european union. i am absolutely opposed to the recommendation to approve the hague convention on the election of forums, as i do not want france's sovereignty in legal and foreign policy matters to be further weakened and confiscated by the eu.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which provides for the ratification by the european union of the agreements on the election of the court (the hague convention of 30 june 2005). they concern exclusive choice of court agreements in civil and commercial matters. these agreements are those whereby two parties agree that any dispute between them will be submitted to the courts of the state indicated. this ratification will increase legal certainty when contracts are signed, since the parties will agree in advance on the courts with jurisdiction. this decision excludes insurance contracts concluded by consumers from the scope of the directive, in order to prevent consumers from accepting a choice-of-court clause without their knowledge.
in writing. the hague convention deals with the choice of courts applicable to disputes in international private and commercial law, and its objective is to ensure greater legal certainty. however, these agreements do not guarantee maximum protection for citizens and consumers; i therefore abstained from voting.
in writing. this convention should be signed by sovereign states that so wish and not by an institution such as the european union. the fact that the member states are deprived of their legislative powers is unacceptable and contrary to any democracy. i therefore vote against the adoption of this convention.

in writing. i welcome the vote on this resolution to set out an ambitious and universal post-2015 agenda to go beyond the millennium development goals (mdgs) set out in the united nations framework in 2000. a number of quantified sub-goals are to achieve the following eight goals by 2015: reducing extreme poverty and hunger, ensuring primary education for all, promoting gender equality and women's empowerment, reducing child mortality, improving maternal health, combating hiv, malaria and other diseases, protecting the environment, and establishing a global partnership for development. a new generation of mdgs should be promoted, giving greater prominence to environmental issues as factors for development, in view of the changing global challenges and the link between environmental protection, improved health, prosperity (green growth) and peace.
in writing. - in september 2000, the united nations adopted a millennium declaration setting out specific goals to be achieved by 2015. the millennium development goals (mdgs) have brought about a significant improvement in certain human situations. within a year of the target date, extreme poverty was reduced by half worldwide, and impressive progress was made in the fight against malaria and tuberculosis. the european parliament is continuing its work towards the adoption of an ambitious development agenda for the period after 2015. the report sets out the objectives of the programme: eradication of poverty, human rights, health, education, combating global warming, and so on. even if this is largely wishful thinking in view of the union's devastating free trade policy, i am voting in favour.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in your overall approach to the european union's migration issue, mr moraes and mr avramopoulos are careful to avoid the fundamental problems, which are really not reassuring for the future. we know that in italy, out of 12 identification and detention centres, 8 have been closed down because of the illegal migrant revolts. the situation there is explosive and, as mr salini said, italians have suffered the arrival of 150,000 to 160,000 illegal migrants on their shores in 2014 alone. despite the frontex loophole and the budget that goes with it, the union's policy has turned italy into a gigantic sorting centre before the dispersal of these illegal migrants in the various schengen countries and in particular in my own country, france. as a member of parliament from nice, close to the italian border, i can see that we are overwhelmed by the influx of illegal immigrants: more than a thousand a week. the council said in october, and i quote: 'measures must be taken to better manage migration flows'. the only way forward is to immediately reverse these immigration policies, suspend the schengen agreements and return sovereignty and control of borders to the states.
mr president, we are concerned about the dispatches on migration issues. between the calls for solidarity, firmness and a rapid revision of european rules, there is as much information as misinformation. one thing is certain, however, and many colleagues have mentioned it before me: the union is struggling to adopt a comprehensive, long-term, strategic and, above all, legible migration policy. it's not unusual for vision to be fragmented and short-term. so, as a new era opens for our institutions, we must achieve a profound change in migration policies. i believe that we must be committed and proactive and propose another policy which promotes, for example, better movement of people and skills, existing or to be promoted legal migration routes, which also promotes effective access to asylum procedures and the development of alternatives for people seeking international protection, and which also promotes a renewed partnership with third countries. i listened to you very carefully, commissioner, and i have noted many points of agreement. i therefore look forward to your concrete proposals to respond to the urgency, but also to take action in the long term.
mr president, i think that if there is one major issue which requires a common european response, it is the question of migration. i think it is high time that the heads of state or government realised this and moved forward to build a common immigration policy based on four pillars. the first pillar is that we must have real security, real surveillance and protection of our external borders by air, land and sea, with, why not, european coast guards. the second pillar is the corollary of the first: we must have a regulated right of entry into the european union with, why not, country quotas in immigration. the third pillar is urgent, as you all said; we need to harmonize our right to asylum. we cannot continue with countries where it takes six months to get something and where it takes five years for others. this is not reasonable. the fourth pillar is that we need a development policy, a genuine partnership with the countries of origin and a foreign policy which contributes to the stability of the countries around us.
in writing. the european union's migration policy should not escape the scrutiny of the european parliament and civil society. democratic control is essential to ensure that the fundamental rights of migrants and asylum seekers are respected. however, frontex is not known for the transparency of its actions. the working agreements concluded by the agency with third countries, because they are technical, are not subject to any external control. they would enable frontex, in cooperation with the police authorities of the countries concerned, to set up return and surveillance operations in non-european territorial waters. there are legitimate doubts as to whether these agreements respect the fundamental rights of migrants, in particular the right to seek asylum and the principle of non-refoulement. the commission can no longer turn a blind eye and remain inactive in the face of practices that do not respect the rights of migrants. what does it intend to do to inform the european parliament of these general agreements between frontex and third countries? does it intend to ensure that these agreements are in conformity with european law and the charter of fundamental rights?
mr president, despite the very long plea of mr díaz de mera garcía consuegra, what an irony of fate and perhaps even what a schizophrenia for europe! we have just concluded the previous debate which, in general terms, reflects the need for a comprehensive approach to migration by the european union. at least that is what i understood, and our discussion now turns to summary expulsions of migrants to spain and the spanish government's attempts to make these practices legally possible. how can we succeed in the challenge of a truly coherent, protective and effective migration policy if, at the same time, there are attempts to unravel european legislation and values? more specifically, with regard to the situation in ceuta and melilla, the questions we are asking are simple and quite straightforward, and the answers must be as simple and straightforward. what is the reason for a member state not to comply with the safeguards provided for in the return directive? what is the basis for exempting oneself from the principle of non-refoulement and effective access to the asylum procedure? if europe and its member states simply apply the logic of 'everyone at home' or 'everyone for themselves', we will not be able to meet the challenges posed by migration, and i believe we will not be able to meet the collective challenges of our continent.
for the greens/efa group mr president, ladies and gentlemen, my report in 2011 was aimed at improving the health and safety of europeans at work with ambitious targets. that was three years ago, ladies and gentlemen. three years! and today, for 2014-2020, the commission's framework is light years away. every year, 168 000 people die in europe from work-related accidents and diseases. more than half of these are cancers and a quarter are cardiovascular diseases. it is a moral fault to turn a blind eye to suffering at work. it is an economic mistake because accidents and illnesses cost our social security systems and also our businesses. so what indicators do you intend to put in place, particularly to measure the inequality between men and women in relation to work? do you really intend to involve the social partners, which was not the case in 2006? will you give a definition of occupational accidents and diseases? your strategic framework is not up to par, and mr juncker often says that his commission is the commission of last resort. i would rather say that this is the european commission's last chance to reconcile europeans with work, simply because european citizens can no longer lose their livelihood by earning it.
mr president, health and safety at work is a pillar of the operation of a company and the well-being of employees. in the face of the proliferation of techniques and the emergence of new occupational risks, more than ever, regulatory requirements in this area must be maintained. the crisis we are going through and will continue to suffer as a result of the still fragile economic environment is dealing a severe blow to prevention and safety at work in companies, which are costly but essential. let us not be mistaken, ladies and gentlemen, the european union is not the answer. the ultra-liberal commission has no intention of supporting health and safety at work, and attempts at harmonization will result in a clear social disadvantage. the technocracy at the behest of the multinationals dreams of a large free labour market in europe, to the detriment of the rules protecting workers. let us be on our guard, the european union is not the doctor, it is the disease.
mr president, the satisfaction shown by the ecb and all the policies when reading the stress test results at the end of last october must be qualified. indeed, 13 of the 130 largest banks still need to be recapitalised, but there is more to worry about. the financial stability board the fsb published about two weeks ago, on the sidelines of the g20, its annual list of the thirty private mega banks, including european and french banks, which would not withstand the next crisis, a crisis that is no longer a question of when it will happen but if it will happen. the fsb calls for stricter solvency standards than the current basel iii rules and recommends that these banks increase their capital to 20% of their assets. who's right? the ecb, who tells us to sleep well? or the fsb, which is raising fears of another catastrophe? the stakes are high because, when you realise these systemic risks, you will now have to enforce, as in cyprus in april 2013, the frankfurt mur the single resolution mechanism and its famous bail-in that will pump out customer deposits and savings to allow the countries concerned to bail out their own failing banks. count on us to alert our french compatriots to this financial crackdown that is being prepared.
mr president, commissioner, we must consider this lima conference as a springboard conference, since it is to prepare the great paris conference in 2015, during which we will have to obtain a binding agreement that is widely supported by our international partners. so in lima we have to work on a result for the planet, not just for the european union, because the european union only accounts for 10% of co2 emissions. this requires us to take a global approach to the climate problem. at the same time, we cannot sit back and wait for other countries to act to move forward. the european union must be at the heart of the negotiations to send a clear message. it must affirm the interest of everyone in committing themselves, without delay, to reducing co2 emissions. developing countries that fear that reducing emissions will hamper their growth have a vested interest in doing so, because they will be the first to suffer the consequences of climate change. so we should be especially attentive to their concerns. developed countries also have an interest in this because reducing co2 emissions can be done by innovating more and creating jobs. there are encouraging signs, although caution is warranted. on the international level, we see this with the agreement between china and the united states, but we must not have a mere catalogue of good intentions. i therefore trust our commissioner, mr arias cañete, to convey this message and to promote the spirit of dialogue with which the european union must go to lima. i would like to end by quoting the english writer samuel johnson, who said: "it is not strength but perseverance that makes great works". i hope that's what we get in lima.
mr president, the european union is making a worthwhile effort to combat climate change. it applies the kyoto protocol and the doha amendment. it now sets itself the target of reducing its greenhouse gas emissions by 40% by 2030 and 80% by 2050. the european union will no doubt try to persuade the world at the lima conference in december to respect the objective set by the durban agreement, namely the adoption in paris at the end of 2015 of a binding treaty to limit global warming to a maximum of two degrees by the end of the century. the failure is unfortunately predictable because china and the united states, the two biggest polluters, are not willing to make the effort. i want to see proof of this in the fact that on 12 november these two countries have just concluded an agreement by which they are putting the durban process to rest. i draw two conclusions. firstly, the european union has failed in this area as in others. second, european states must prepare themselves to face the consequences of this failure, as the ipcc announced in its march 2014 report: food insecurity, water scarcity, mass displacement of populations and the risk of conflict.
mr president, commissioner, first of all i would like to congratulate you, mr cañete, on your victory, the victory of europe, at the meeting in paris on 20 november last, bringing together the parties to the montreal protocol on substances that deplete the ozone layer. this is a victory because it is your proposals, those of the european union, that have been validated to combat hydrofluorocarbons and hydrochlorocarbons, whose impact on the destruction of the ozone layer and, therefore, on climate change and warming is, it should be noted, 23 000 times greater than that of co2. a question in this connection, mr cañete: how will these proposals be implemented in practice in the coming weeks, particularly at lima? the second point, which was also raised at the berlin conference on 20 november, concerns the green climate fund: again, we need to know how the lima conference will define the terms of allocation of the fund.
mr president, commissioner, on the way to paris and lima, we have three pieces of good news. firstly, the agreement reached at the european council, which has one binding objective and two optional objectives, must be welcomed. secondly, the agreement between china and the united states should be welcomed as a joint decision to reduce their emissions. finally, the meeting on the capitalisation of the green fund should also be welcomed. however, as europeans, it seems to me that we cannot stop there and that, even if we go to lima, we must continue to mobilise here on the basis of the european parliament's positions in favour of a triple binding objective which would add to the objectives accepted by the european council those of energy efficiency and renewable energies. finally, when we discuss the 300 billion investment plan, we must also make the issue of the ecological transition the guiding principle for the mobilisation of these new investment capacities in the european union.
mr president, commissioner, today people all over europe and the world have become aware of the reality of climate change. some companies have adopted climate-friendly investment strategies. cities, municipalities and regions have committed themselves to climate plans. so we have a society that's moving forward and ready and a climate-friendly economy that's already in place. it is therefore up to you, commissioner, to take the initiative. the commission has the power of initiative to purge the carbon market, to end fossil fuel subsidies and to strengthen energy efficiency and renewable energy targets. that is how we will be less dependent on russia, that is how we will create smes in all the territories to respond to mr juncker's speech, and that is how we will create jobs. let's show that we'll live better in a society that fights climate change.

in writing. - regulation (ec) no 2533/98 of 23 november 1998 lays down the procedures governing the collection of statistical information by the ecb from banking and similar institutions in the union. the purpose of the collection of statistical information is to enable the compilation of macroeconomic data which are essential for the ecb's monetary policy. the 1998 amendment to the regulation allows the ecb to use confidential statistical information for the performance of its new supervisory functions. while we can welcome the strengthening of transparency requirements for banks in principle, we cannot support this for the benefit of the ecb, whose legitimacy in monetary governance we question. that is why i abstained on this vote.
in writing. the new role of the european central bank in the supervision of credit institutions is a significant step forward in the establishment of the banking union. in order to ensure the highest possible efficiency and coordination of its supervisory tasks, the ecb needs to have confidential statistical data on the bodies under its supervision. this report makes it possible to adapt the current legislation on the ecb's prerogatives in relation to the use of confidential statistical data to its new supervisory function. i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - following the adoption of the single supervisory mechanism (ssm regulation), the aim here is to amend regulation (ec) no 2533/98 in order to take account of the ecb's new tasks in the field of the prudential supervision of credit institutions. the recommendation submitted by the european central bank (ecb) aims to give it access to confidential statistical information. this is to enable the identification of the reporting agent for the performance of its surveillance functions and to allow the transmission of this data to the european stability mechanism (esm). the report by parliament endorses these recommendations. it specifies a few points such as the obligation to take the necessary regulatory, administrative, technical and organisational measures to ensure the physical and logical protection of the confidential statistical information concerned. however, technically speaking, this is a transfer of sovereignty allowing the ecb to obtain statistics before the national central banks. as i am opposed to the independent power of the central bank, i vote against.
in writing. - the new supervisory tasks entrusted to the ecb in the framework of the banking union logically imply a strengthening of the obligations to report statistical data provided by credit institutions. in so far as this text aims to increase the transparency, even partially, of financial actors who prosper the more they are in secrecy, it could be supported. however, even if the national central banks also benefit from the information received, this text is part of the logic of a divestment of the national authorities of banking supervision tasks, which should be firmly opposed. the abstention is therefore justified in the present case.
in writing. the procedures governing the collection of statistical information by the ecb and by banking or similar institutions in the european union are laid down in regulation (ec) no 2533/98 of 23 november 1998. the collection of statistical information by the european central bank enables the collection and analysis of macroeconomic data. the latter are therefore used for the adjustments of the monetary policy decided by the ecb. however, the proposed amendment to the regulation here grants the ecb increased supervisory powers with access to confidential statistical information. while we can accept in principle that greater transparency is necessary for the proper functioning of banking institutions in general, we believe that this should not be done to the benefit of the european central bank, whose guidelines on monetary governance and ultra-liberal dogmatism we reject. that's why i abstained.

in writing. i am voting in favour of a regulation to take account of the evolution of the prerogatives conferred on the european central bank. the supervisory authority must be able to fulfil its role as a prudential supervisor. it must therefore be possible to collect statistical information, while respecting the principle of proportionality.
in writing. regulation 2532/98 of 23 november 1998 gave the ecb the power to impose sanctions on banks or similar institutions which failed to comply with an obligation arising from a european law or ecb decision (e.g. the constitution of legal reserves). these penalties were limited to €500k and €10k per day of stress, which is not deterrent given the balance sheets of the banks. it was therefore obvious that the sanctions should be increased, in proportion to turnover and not capped in absolute terms. this is what the text does, which is in the right direction, namely to strengthen the obligations imposed on banks. however, unusually, this text is part of a supranational logic which subjects the decisions of the member states to the ecb's green light and, therefore, risks seriously hampering our banking and monetary sovereignty. that's why i abstained.
in writing. the purpose of this report is to entrust the ecb with tasks relating to policies relating to the prudential supervision of credit institutions and, in particular, to sanctions. thus, after the introduction of the single supervisory mechanism (ssm), the large banks (approximately 130) should be directly supervised, 13 of which still need to be stabilised. the financial stability board (fsb) has published its annual list of 30 private banks that would not withstand the next crisis. it thus requires these banks to have capital in excess of 20% of assets and to meet solvency standards that are stricter than those of basel iii. in addition, national banks will also be subject to ecb supervision to initiate a sanction procedure, losing even more powers to frankfurt. i therefore abstained on this vote, considering nevertheless the need for supervision of the large european banks.
in writing. i abstained from voting on the draft council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 2532/98 concerning the powers of the european central bank with regard to sanctions. the strengthening of prudential standards and the sanctions against credit institutions which fail to comply with them is consistent with the implementation of this ecb's mission. however, i condemn the supranational logic which governs the economy of the text. thus, national authorities must obtain the ecb's approval to initiate a sanction procedure.
in writing. - the ecb has been given the power to impose sanctions on credit institutions for breaches of eu law or its own decisions. the eu resolution raises the amount of the penalties from a maximum of eur 500 000 to twice the profit made or 10% of annual turnover. in addition, national central banks lose the possibility of initiating proceedings on their own initiative, which was possible when the infringement was committed in their jurisdiction. the national authorities will now be given the green light by the ecb to initiate a sanction procedure, thus demonstrating the supranational logic of the technocrats in brussels and frankfurt. i abstained on this vote in order to show my desire to strengthen the power of control over the banks and to reject the technocratic and supranational leap forward.
in writing. the european central bank has recently started its new role as the supervisor of credit institutions. this function is crucial to regain investor confidence in the european market. its supervisory role is separate from its monetary policy prerogatives. the ecb therefore needs a new mandate to be able to sanction bodies under its supervision. when credit institutions do not meet the various criteria developed by the european legislator, the ecb has to act. we have put in place mechanisms to prevent citizens from being in a crisis situation similar to that of 2008. as a supervisor, the ecb is now in a position to ensure compliance with these mechanisms. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the regulation on the sanctions powers of the european central bank (ecb), adopted in 1998, needs to be amended. in the wake of the banking and financial crisis, the european union has undertaken a series of ambitious reforms. in this context, we have been obliged to entrust the ecb with new tasks, particularly in the context of prudential supervision. it is to take account of these changes that an amendment to the regulation is proposed. because it will help to build a more coherent and integrated regulatory environment, i support the adoption of this text.

in writing. - this report is part of the banking union and the single rescue mechanism which entered into force on 4 november 2013. the report aims to clarify and strengthen the ecb's powers. the aim is to give it the means to impose administrative and financial sanctions on financial market players and banks. the sanctions, which could previously be delayed indefinitely, will thus take effect after a maximum of three years. the limitation periods are amended. the revenue from the penalties shall be at the disposal of the ecb. this strengthens the ecb's independence and powers vis-à-vis national banks. the ecb will no longer be able to sanction banks that it will supervise. the supervisory criteria in the name of which these sanctions will be taken remain geared to the development of financial competition, far from any objective of financialisation of the economy. as i am opposed to the independence of the ecb, whose objectives are contrary to the interests of the european people, i am voting against this text.
in writing. - regulation 2532/98 of 23 november 1998 gave the ecb the power to impose sanctions on banks or similar institutions which failed to comply with an obligation arising from a european law or a decision of the ecb (e.g. the constitution of legal reserves). these penalties were limited to €500k and €10k per day of stress, which is not deterrent given the balance sheets of the banks. it was therefore obvious that the sanctions should be increased, in proportion to turnover and not capped in absolute terms. this is what the text does, which is in the right direction, namely to strengthen the obligations imposed on banks. however, it is noted that the proceeds of the fines remain in the ecb's budget, which makes the ecb directly concerned by its sanctions policy and is not in accordance with the principle of universality. secondly, the national authorities lose the possibility of initiating sanctioning procedures on their own initiative. this is only one consequence of the development of economic and monetary union, but it is a further loss of sovereignty which must be denounced. in the end, the abstention was justified by the fact that the text was being neutralised.
