in writing. the united nations framework convention on climate change - cop 20 - is being held in lima, peru from 1 to 12 december 2014. the european union needs to speak with one voice at this convention. that is why the european parliament has proposed a resolution to make a coherent statement to the rest of the world. i voted in favour of this resolution. i would like to remind you, however, that it is important to remain pragmatic in our approach to climate change. we must do a lot of work on the environment, but not at the expense of our economy. we are currently in a serious economic crisis. we cannot set environmental objectives that are too restrictive for our companies and thus make them less competitive with the rest of the world. the european environmental standards are already very high, and we must now ensure that they are working properly. we must find the right balance between competitiveness and environmental standards in order to get out of the economic crisis we are currently experiencing.
in writing. as a major player in the fight against global warming, the european union must turn its example into leadership. under the kyoto protocol, the union reduced its emissions by 19% between 1990 and 2012 while increasing its gross domestic product by more than 45%, demonstrating that environmental improvement and economic development are not contradictory. it is with this conviction that i believe it is essential to support everything that can create a positive dynamic on the road to the paris conference.
in writing. - the european parliament recalls with this resolution our ambitious objectives in the fight against climate change. the european union must speak with one voice in lima at the un climate change conference, to contribute to an international agreement at the paris conference in 2015. stakeholders at the conference need to agree on binding targets and financial means to keep temperature rise below 2°c. i am particularly pleased that the resolution recognises the certain exposure and vulnerability of the agricultural and forestry sectors to climate change. in particular, it calls on stakeholders at the conference to include in their national contributions a farmland component, consisting of appropriate common data to monitor, trace and quantifiably verify the achievement of several productivity, mitigation and climate resilience objectives. for these reasons i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. the union must be ambitious and persuasive at the cop20 conference in lima. concrete and rapid action is needed because, as things stand, our commitments are not likely to minimise the damage of climate change. the union must play a leading role in the negotiations by speaking with one voice to weigh in against the other countries of the world. the recent agreement between the united states and china is a step in the right direction, but it is still not enough. the lima conference is to set the conditions for a binding global agreement to be concluded in paris in 2015 to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. we also need to get a commitment from industrialized countries to developing countries, which contribute the least to emissions but suffer the most from them, to help them fight and adapt to climate change. finally, we must at european level set up a genuine 'environmental belt' to reconcile stimulating growth with reducing greenhouse gases. the eu budget should support green growth by promoting energy and raw material-efficient activities.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because it was important that parliament had a voice on climate change because the lima conference is a stepping stone conference before the paris conference in 2015. however, we must not shoot ourselves in the foot by setting ourselves far too high targets without our partners having the same ones, we must be careful about the competitiveness of european companies. the european union must be at the heart of the negotiations, it must have a strong message and it must push as hard as it can for a reduction in co2 emissions, but our representatives must not forget that this is a global problem that requires a global response and not just a european one: it is good to lead by example but we must make sure that we are followed.
in writing. in line with my position in the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, i will not vote in favour of the motion for a resolution which appears to be based on vague ideas and vague objectives, with some policies projected too far in the future to be realistic. the text also provides for legally binding provisions for states and proposes the release of large amounts of money without defining precisely the objectives and means of controlling this expenditure. it is therefore unacceptable to support such enterprises which are otherwise based on ideologically marked work. finally, this draft resolution contains aberrations which are part of communist planning, where it is assumed that achieved objectives are synonymous with unambitious objectives. these policies are leaks forward that are out of touch with reality.
in writing. i would like to recall the contradictions of the european union's climate policy. on the one hand, the draft resolution considers that climate change represents an imminent and potentially irreversible threat to human societies, biodiversity and the planet. on the other hand, europe is devoted to deregulation and liberalization of international trade, which have the mechanical effect of increasing energy consumption and the flow of goods. in short, global trade is the biggest contributor to greenhouse gas emissions. the lima conference is therefore doomed to failure in advance, since environmental policies, however binding, are being overridden by free trade policies. that is why i voted against this resolution.
in writing. like the majority of my colleagues, i voted in favour of the resolution on the 20th united nations climate conference (cop 20) to be held in lima, peru, from 1 to 12 december 2014. given the seriousness of the threats posed by climate change, urgent action is needed. the text proposes binding targets for 2030, namely, among other things, to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 40% compared with 1990, to increase the share of renewable energies to 30% of the energy mix, and to achieve 40% energy savings. the european parliament calls for increased funding to combat climate change, including by inviting member states to contribute to the green fund in order to raise $100 billion annually by 2020. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. indeed, governments around the world must assume their collective responsibility, especially towards future generations, and take appropriate action to effectively combat climate change.
in writing. should we have ambitions so high that we will achieve nothing or should we set achievable goals that can be followed by all? the lima conference must not be a repeat of the failure of copenhagen, because the future of the planet and the interests of all are at stake. lima will be an essential step as it will prepare for the major meeting in paris in 2015. that is why i believe that we must set ambitious but not excessive targets. i am concerned that by setting binding 2030 targets for greenhouse gas emissions reductions of at least 40% compared to 1990 levels, 40% in energy efficiency, in line with research on the potential for cost-effective energy savings, and for at least 30% of total final energy consumption to be generated from renewable sources, we are embarking on a path that will be difficult to sustain and that will discredit us in the eyes of our partners. moreover, does such a stance not run the risk of our companies and industries moving their activities to countries with less stringent regulations?
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the un climate change conference taking place in lima from 1 to 12 december 2014. the text underlines the need to take action in the fight against climate change by addressing the question of how to finance the fight against climate change and by indicating how different economic sectors can contribute to improving the situation. the resolution was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. the vote on the 2014 un climate change conference (cop 20 in lima) comes against a favourable political backdrop following the submission of the fifth report of the intergovernmental panel on climate change at the un secretary-general's heads of state summit in september, the european climate and energy agreement of 24 october on a 40% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 compared to 1990 levels and the bilateral us-china climate agreement of 12 november. in order to reach a comprehensive agreement at the paris conference in december 2015 to limit the rise in global average temperatures to 2°c, it is now up to all parties to the climate convention to demonstrate their credibility by making their official contributions known by the beginning of 2015 and setting out the precise terms of their commitment. the european union must obtain strong commitments from its partners in order to guarantee a balanced international agreement that does not penalise the competitiveness of european industry.
in writing. - the european parliament could have used this resolution to strengthen europe's role in promoting a binding climate agreement. but, full of good intentions and incantations about the will to keep global warming within the 2 per cent limit by 2050, it offers no innovative measures. worse still, it is the carbon market, which has proven itself inefficient time and time again, that is the cornerstone of its policy. the fight against global warming is not a business or a competitive one. as long as the european parliament and world leaders remain locked into this vision, no fight against global warming will be possible or effective. i vote against it.
in writing. the united nations climate change conference, to be held in lima in december, will clearly not solve the serious problems of greenhouse gas emissions. the un intergovernmental panel on climate change estimates that global emissions have risen from 38 billion tonnes in 1990 to 49 billion tonnes in 2010. the ipcc also noted that these emissions should be reduced by more than 50% within a short time! the kyoto protocol's target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 5% for the period 2008-2012 has already not been met because of the non-participation of the united states. the failure of this conference is therefore foreseeable, as china and the united states reached an agreement on 12 november last which clearly buried the objectives of the duban platform (a protocol following the kyoto protocol). the consequences of this predicted failure will be dramatic: water shortages, pollution, increased risk of conflict, not to mention the increase in migration flows. for all these reasons, i voted against.
in writing. i abstained on the final vote on this resolution. i am in favour of an ambitious international climate agreement. however, this agreement must be balanced between europe and the other regions of the world. the european union cannot continue to set itself stricter environmental standards than elsewhere, because by doing so it sacrifices its companies and its employees by imposing on them an additional distortion of competition. increasing our carbon reduction targets without our partners doing the same would only encourage relocations to areas of the world where the legislation is less restrictive. this would also create additional emissions when repatriating finished products to europe. it is possible to reconcile industry and the environment.
in writing. i supported this text, which is a useful reminder of the european union's efforts to combat climate change and the importance of reaching a binding global agreement in paris in 2015. as for the mention of sea and air transport, if i fully support their contribution to the reduction of greenhouse gases, it must be through the development of new, cleaner technologies and not through the reduction of flows of these modes of transport which are essential for global growth.
in writing. this text is a good basis for an ambitious eu position in terms of combating climate change and for greater environmental protection. i voted in favour of this report in order to push the european commission to adopt the most ambitious position possible at the international climate forum in lima.

in writing. i am voting in favour of a resolution to allow the european union to play a full part in the lima conference on climate change. in doing so, it was necessary to adopt a common position between the european union and all the member states. it is also worth emphasising the main objective, namely reaching agreements with all international partners at the major conference in paris in 2015.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the 2014 united nations climate change conference, to be held in lima from 1 to 12 december. the house is therefore calling for an ambitious global agreement by 2015 and encouraging member states to move forward with their negotiations ahead of cop 21 in paris in 2015. we stress the importance of the eu's contribution to the fight against climate change and call on other states around the world to do the same, including by contributing to the green fund set up at the copenhagen conference in 2009. the special situation of developing countries (ldcs), which emit the least co2 but suffer the most from its consequences, is also taken into account, through a call for a smarter development aid policy. these provisions are in line with my vision of the role of the european union on the international stage in the face of the challenges of climate change.
in writing. the lima negotiations will take place next month and could lead in the long term to an ambitious climate agreement in paris in 2015. the european union will thus be forced to negotiate with its global partners to increase their investment in climate policy in order to contribute to environmental protection, the development of sustainable technologies and the creation of jobs. following the recent agreement between the united states and china, we appear to be on the right track to reach an agreement, but the european union will have to remain firm on its objectives during the negotiations. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution which supports the forthcoming lima conference and prepares the way for the future conclusion of a global agreement in paris in 2015.

in writing. the luxleaks case showed that powerful corporate tax avoidance schemes, such as the so-called tax ruling practice, involve the creation of a subsidiary or a holding company (a company that itself is a shareholder of other companies) in luxembourg. generally, it is a simple office with few or no employees. then tax arrangements are made, ranging from simple vat rate rebates to more complicated arrangements such as the "patent niche". in some cases, the company avoids tax altogether, as is the case, for example, with ikea. all this to enable 340 multinational companies to avoid paying a large part of their taxes, particularly in france and europe. during this period of research (2002-2010), mr juncker was prime minister of luxembourg. today, mr juncker is president of the european commission, backed by a large left-right-center-environment coalition, and it is not acceptable that a person responsible for the establishment of this system should be kept in that position. that is why i have signed this motion of censure, and of course i have voted in favour of it.

in writing. since the outbreak of the financial crisis in 2008, the european commission has pursued numerous initiatives to save the single currency, the euro. with the deepening of the euro area debt crisis and the interdependence of the euro area countries, the european commission and the european institutions, in the framework of the banking union, agreed to establish a single supervisory mechanism (ssm) and a single resolution mechanism (srm) for banks. the banking union applies to euro area countries, but countries outside the euro area may also participate. the single resolution board has broad powers to analyse and define the approach to be adopted for the resolution of a bank, including the instruments to be used and the intervention of the european resolution fund. we are therefore asked here not to object to the provisional system of advance payments on contributions to cover these expenditure of the cru over the transitional period and thus to support this system, which is why i voted against this recommendation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european commission's recommendation for a delegated act on the provisional system of advances on contributions from the single resolution board. that delegated act establishes the funds allocated to the single resolution board to cover its administrative expenses. the recommendation supports the establishment of these funds. the recommendation was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. - i opposed the single resolution mechanism which establishes the troika as the ultimate saviour of the european banking sector. i therefore oppose the introduction of provisional financing for the single resolution board (srb) which is organising it. i vote against it.
in writing. since the financial, economic and banking crisis of 2008, the commission has been doing everything it can to save the single currency. the dramatic increase in the debt of the member states in the euro area and the devastating domino effect observed in the countries sharing the euro led the commission and the european institutions to put in place control tools to maintain the banking union. this is the case of the single supervisory mechanism (ssm) and the single resolution mechanism (srm). the single resolution board has significant powers, such as deciding which instrument to use and how much of the european resolution fund to grant to a bank. we are here asked to accept the provisional system of contributions to cover the expenses of the cru. the rescue of the euro has led to austerity plans and the impoverishment of the european people, so i voted against it.

in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution on the delays in the launch of the cohesion policy for 2014-2020. the text underlines the worrying delay by the commission in the validation of operational programmes, a necessary step in implementing the new cohesion policy. the commission will have validated only half of the programmes by the end of the year, whereas it should have validated all of them in autumn 2014. this delay will create significant difficulties for projects requesting pre-financing in 2014, as validation will extend until 2015 and may potentially require a revision of the multiannual financial framework (mff). the resolution therefore calls on the commission and the member states to take all measures to validate as many programmes as possible before the end of 2014 and to prepare as far in advance as possible with parliament the procedures for revising the cfp before the fateful date of 1 may 2015. this resolution was adopted by a very large majority, which i welcome.

in writing. in order to gather useful data and assess whether the objectives have been achieved, the commission carries out evaluations to determine the effects of the policies implemented and to assess their impact. the conclusions of these evaluations are used to refine policies. the impact assessment is carried out before the decision is taken and implemented. these analyses are carried out in particular in the context of employment policies, as is the case here with this resolution on the revision of the commission's guidelines on impact analysis and the role of the sme test. the european union currently has more than 20 million smes, representing 99% of all european enterprises. in this resolution we are reminded that smes often have more difficulty than large companies in complying with a legislative act and the commission does not hesitate, not without irony, to state that it has made the principle of 'thinking first of smes' the 'cornerstone of the small business act for europe'. the reality is quite different, however, and the european market is still dominated by multinational companies and financial powers. nevertheless, i voted in favour of this recommendation because it will have a positive impact on smes, which i support, and this text guarantees independence from the commission.
in writing. - the purpose of this resolution is to call for the strengthening of the impact analysis of the sme test. impact assessment is a tool for providing information on the economic, social and environmental effects of eu legislation. the draft resolution recalls that the costs incurred by smes to comply with an eu legislative act can be up to ten times higher than those incurred by large companies. the new regulations on helicopter transport activities, which now prohibit the flying of single-engine aircraft over populated areas at risk, could double the cost of purchasing and operating a helicopter. anything that helps to better assess the impact of legislation and regulation and to avoid economic and social disasters is a good thing. however, the strengthening of impact analysis will not produce the expected results. the technocratic structure of the european union is the main cause of the production of laws and regulations which are totally inapplicable by the member states. however, in order to support our smes, i voted for this resolution.
in writing. the impact assessments of the european commission are a prominent feature of european legislation. these analyses are carried out in advance of a legislative proposal to determine whether the direction taken by the commission in the preparation of a legislative proposal is relevant. this process is determined by guidelines on impact assessments. parliament believes that these guidelines should be amended to make them as effective and transparent as possible. the same applies to the sme test. it has long been established that smes are a key player in the european economy. the same should apply to european legislation. any legislative act must take account of the specificities of the nature of smes. it is therefore also necessary to amend the commission guidelines on the sme test. i voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. i wished to be a co-signer of this resolution on the revision of the commission's guidelines on impact assessment and the role of the sme test. in order to avoid costly and counterproductive regulation, impact assessments are an important means of decision-making in all european institutions. they are also an essential part of the regulatory improvement process that the new commission's first vice-president will be responsible for. where legislative proposals are amended before adoption by the college of commissioners, the impact assessments should be updated to ensure consistency between the points discussed and the proposals finally adopted. as part of parliament's legislative work, a parliamentary impact assessment would be necessary when substantive changes are made to the commission's original proposal. in addition, it is regrettable that the sme test is not mentioned in the commission's draft guidelines, whereas the commission has made a clear commitment, in the context of the review of the european small business act, to strengthen this test. the test, which is to be applied before any new european legislation is adopted, aims to prevent new obstacles to the smooth functioning of smes in the eu.

in writing. i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution which reaffirms its commitment to the universal protection of the rights of the child. adopted by the united nations general assembly on 20 november 1989, the convention sets out the principles, rights and freedoms to which every child is entitled in all the major areas of his or her life (health, education, citizenship, etc.). it is thus the backbone of the universal protection of children. taking stock of progress and setbacks in all the fields concerned, this resolution sets out a framework for action in the years ahead. i welcome the fact that the gue/ngl group has succeeded in imposing a large number of amendments calling for the full and effective implementation of the convention, including by insisting that 'all policies on children's rights incorporate a gender perspective', by calling for an 'urgent break' with the austerity policies that have been calling into question the progress made over the last 25 years, and by recalling that the protection of children must be at the heart of our asylum system for unaccompanied minors.
mr president, i voted against this digital single market, which is presented to us as having considerable potential and which should stimulate growth and strengthen confidence. after article 3 of the 1992 treaty on european union, which established the european single market and free movement, the commission now wants to liberalize digital circulation. it is true that new technologies are a constantly developing sector and that europe is lagging behind the united states in this respect. for example, one in five citizens in rural areas still has no access to the internet. however, it will be necessary to monitor the development of this agreement, which seems to be the trojan horse of the commission sweeping away national sovereignty. finally, it is clear that the establishment of the freedom to provide services and the freedom for all europeans and businesses to benefit from the digital services of their choice, wherever they come from in the union, will have to be monitored in order to avoid any risk of dumping, as is already the case with video-on-demand platforms such as netflix.
in writing. i abstained on the motion for a resolution on strengthening consumer rights in the digital single market. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the body of the person who is infected. the growth prospects are extremely ambitious. this market is, by its very nature, cross-border. in the absence of tax harmonization, which is the exclusive competence of the council, there is only the fear that the current distortions will be amplified by the exploitation of the weaknesses of this system by multinational companies which repatriate their profits to member states with preferential tax treatment.

in writing. this resolution is first and foremost a declaration of intent. it overlooks a major cause of malnutrition - the export of food to the international market. in countries affected by malnutrition, there is competition between local food agriculture and monocultures for export to developed countries. it is more profitable for developing countries to export animal and plant products in order to benefit from more promising markets. this leads to the disappearance of local subsistence agriculture, which the population needs to feed itself. the gradual disappearance of trade barriers in the agricultural sector is exacerbating this phenomenon, as food exports are still favoured at the expense of local populations.

madam president, this convention, even if it is imperfect, is a useful instrument as long as its objective of protecting endangered species remains unchanged. at present, member states vote individually, on their own responsibility, on projects submitted to cites. they are certainly in line with a common position defined by the council, but they are legally free to vote in any other direction. what will change with the accession of the european union is that the european union will be granted the voting rights of all member states at the conferences of the parties. the transfer of voting therefore constitutes a transfer of sovereignty, which we are opposed to in principle. but there's more to it than that. we do not trust the european union to resist lobbies, because lobbies will demand restrictions or, on the contrary, the removal of restrictions on trade in certain endangered species. there is a particular concern that certain fish species for human consumption may be included in the cites register, which would pave the way for a ban on fishing for them. at present, this is not the case, as it is the regional fisheries management bodies that regulate commercial fisheries. but there have been calls for fish for human consumption to be included in cites. the danger is that under the influence of certain lobbies, the european union prefers to simply ban fishing for certain species rather than regulate it. that is why we refuse to sign a blank cheque to the european union.

in writing. following the economic and financial crisis, the european union wanted to strengthen its economic governance through the six-pack and two-pack regulations which are here reviewed. the six-pack authorises the commission to request budgetary corrections for member states whose expenditure is falling short. worse, after two reminders, it can fine states that disobey brussels' injunctions, fines of up to 0.1% of gdp. the latter is supplemented by the two-pack which strengthens the commission's powers in the budgetary surveillance of the member states. moreover, the two-pack requires states to rely on independent growth forecasts and submit their budgets to a budgetary control body. finally, the budgetary pact (bpsc) should become a reality in 2018. this 'golden rule', a genuine austerity plan, will put a little more control on national budgets and kill growth in the member states. after depriving us of our monetary sovereignty, these regulations and treaties sacrifice the freedom of the peoples to decide for themselves on the altar of european federalism. it's a victory for the rating agencies and the financial markets over the states!
in writing. since the economic crisis, the union has decided to increase its economic governance , through the six-pack and two-pack regulations. an intrusive instrument by nature, the six-pack allows the commission to require budgetary corrections from member states whose expenditure is falling short. after two reminders, the states which were not complying with the brussels injunctions were then fined. the two-pack further strengthens the commission's powers in the field of budgetary surveillance. member states are thus obliged to rely on independent growth forecasts and to submit their budgets to a budgetary control body. the budgetary pact (bps), which was called for by the merkel-sarkozy duo, will come into force in 2018. this 'golden rule' or another austerity plan will end the control of national budgets and will destroy any idea of growth in the member states. these two regulations are contrary to our monetary and budgetary sovereignty and to the interests of the french people. with the union, there is more and more submission to the dogma of the single currency, to ultra-liberalism, federalism and the financial markets!

in writing. the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is an intergovernmental agreement signed on 3 march 1973 in washington. cites must ensure that international trade in cites-listed species, parts and derivatives thereof, does not undermine the conservation of biodiversity and is based on the sustainable use of wildlife. this convention, although imperfect, is very useful in its goal of protecting endangered species. at present, each member state sits individually within cites. the accession of the european union to cites will entail a further loss of sovereignty for the states since the union will now have the vote of all the member states at the conferences. i therefore voted against the union's accession to cites.

in writing. ‒ the sea concession is a tax on goods which affects both imports of goods into the five french overseas departments and production activities within these territories. this tax allows local authorities to benefit from a significant financial contribution (€1 billion) and stimulates the economic development of local products. this local protectionism works well and is tolerated by successive governments, which refuse to apply the same methods at french or european level. the commission proposal for a council decision aims to renew the possibility of applying tax differentials for the period 2015-2020, while providing for a framework for this practice in order to compensate for the disadvantages faced by these remote regions. i voted with the members of the front national in favour of this text, which protects french citizens living abroad.

in writing. ‒ the financing of the french outermost regions is largely dependent on decisions taken in brussels. one issue of particular concern to the ors today is the future of the sea grant regime. the council decision of 10 february 2004 authorising the current scheme for 10 years expired on 1 july 2014. this improves the competitiveness of the local industry, which is suffering from the particular constraints listed in article 349 tfeu: remoteness, dependence on raw materials and energy, the need to build up larger stocks, the small size of the local market combined with a poorly developed export activity. it is the recognition by the european union of a kind of local economic protectionism. however, this exorbitant system of internal market law is threatened by the european commission, which now sees it as a so-called "situational benefit", when in reality it is the guarantee of the survival of the economic fabric of the overseas regions. as such, it demonstrates by its very existence that the dogma of free trade is an unparalleled threat to the most deprived regions. that is why i voted for the resolution of the parliament approving the maintenance of the tax regime for the granting of maritime concessions in the french outermost regions.

in writing. the srb is the cornerstone of the single resolution mechanism, which will soon be responsible for implementing the dismantling of distressed banks. the institution will be able to rely on a range of instruments, including a resolution fund being set up and new rules on the hierarchy of creditors in the event of bankruptcy. the single resolution board (srb) is the cornerstone of the single resolution mechanism (srm) which will soon be tasked with implementing the dismantling of 'banks in distress' through various instruments, including the bank-supported single resolution fund. the srm will apply to banks covered by the ssm, which makes the european central bank (ecb) the central supervisor of banking institutions in the euro area (approximately 6 000 banks). the mru will react in cases where a bank should fail despite its enhanced supervision. it will be based on a council of six members, which we must approve here. we are aware of the need to prevent the failure of banks, but we are still opposed to the loss of sovereignty of the member states through these mechanisms, which is why i voted against this report and these appointments.

in writing. ‒ rejecting the single resolution mechanism and its banking union, which are part of financial socialism and do not seem to be able to address the shortcomings of the banking system in europe, i opposed the nomination of the candidates nominated to the single resolution board for reasons of consistency and with the firm conviction that this board has neither the means nor the legitimacy to perform its duties.
in writing. ‒ the members of the single resolution board will have the overwhelming responsibility to decide, in the event of a banking crisis, whether to trigger the resolution mechanism provided for in the second pillar of the banking union. they can decide to bankrupt a bank, split it up into several entities, and decide to set up the mechanism that can go as far as dispossessing savers of their savings to pay for the banks' mistakes. the personalities presented for the post come from the world of banking supervision, which has so far failed to prevent and anticipate risks. although the french candidate was precise and rather convincing in his answers, the single-list vote forces a negative opinion on this issue.
in writing. ‒ the single resolution mechanism (srm) which will enter into force on 1 january 2015 should allow for the recovery or reorganisation of banks that are likely to fail. in this context, the single resolution board (srb) is responsible for putting in place a recovery plan for the institution either through internal recapitalisation or through external capital injections from the european stability mechanism (esm), or from the states or the ecb. the troika is thus established as the ultimate saviour of the european banking sector. candidates for the cru have the job profile: the german elke könig, who is aiming for the presidency, is currently director of the german financial markets authority, the finn timo löyttyniemi is director of pension funds, the dutch joanne kellermann is president of the central bank of the netherlands... this mechanism will not change the speculative practices that feed the crises: it is preparing to deal with the effects of the next one with those who usually produce them. i vote against.

president of the council. mr president, members of the european parliament, vice-president georgieva, ladies and gentlemen, it is an honour for me to address today's plenary session for the debate on the political agreement reached on 8 december by the council and the european parliament on the budget of the european union for 2015 and on the package of amending budgets for 2014. the council formalised its agreement on 12 december and we look forward with confidence to the outcome of the european parliament's vote scheduled for tomorrow. as you know, the agreement was reached in a particularly complex negotiating context because of the many issues we had to deal with. i believe that this year there have never been so many amending budgets to be approved and i also believe that we have never had to deal with such a high level of unpaid invoices from the european union. this has led to an intense debate at the end of which we have agreed, also in agreement with the commission, to embark on a process which will enable us to bring the european union's debt to more acceptable and sustainable levels in the coming years. there were different views on how to reduce the level of non-payment and late payment and i think we have finally found a good compromise. i am therefore sure that the european parliament will also agree that the allocation of an additional eur 3.5 billion from the 2014 budget is an important achievement for the functioning of the european union, since it puts an end to the growth in the stock of invoices to be paid and at the same time lays the foundations for its gradual absorption in the years to come. specifically, the total amount for 2015 is made up of eur 2 818 million, by activating the contingency margin, eur 361 million resulting from the use of the margins available against the expenditure ceilings in the 2014 budget and a further eur 350 million relating to the so-called special instruments which are added to the contingency margin, postponing to a later stage an agreement between our institutions as to whether or not they are included in the expenditure ceiling. i believe that this amount is a fair balance between the public financial constraints on the member states and the financial needs of the european union for the implementation of its spending programmes. as regards the 2015 budget of the european union, a total of eur 145,3 billion is foreseen in commitment appropriations, +1,8% compared to the 2014 amended budget, eur 141,2 billion in payment appropriations, +1,6% compared to the 2014 amended budget. the amount of the appropriations thus identified allows for sufficient margins below the ceilings of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 to allow the european union to have sufficient room for manoeuvre to react to any unforeseen event. i am convinced that in this respect the 2015 budget will provide the necessary resources for the smart and effective implementation of the new programmes, given that this is the second annual budget under the new financial framework 2014-2020. just to give a few examples, i would like to highlight the payments for heading 1a (competitiveness for growth and jobs), where resources are allocated to research, training and small and medium-sized enterprises, which show an increase of 33% to eur 3.9 billion compared to the 2014 budget including the adjustments granted. the budget for the european union's external policy also saw a significant increase in payment appropriations, amounting to some 8.5%. other increases include additional resources allocated to external border control and migration flows, and to the newly established financial supervisory agencies. as regards agricultural policy, the requests of the operators in the sector affected by the russian embargo of agricultural products from the european union have been accepted, who will receive additional support financed by the higher earmarked revenues, without therefore affecting the reserve for agricultural crises, which will remain available for any additional needs that may occur during 2015. i believe that these results should also be assessed in the light of the extremely tight timetable we have had at our disposal for defining the budget of the european union for the coming year. following the failure to reach agreement in the conciliation procedure on 17 november, the commission presented a new draft budget for 2015 and on 28 november proposed a new compromise on the outstanding amending budgets for 2014. nevertheless, we managed to reach an agreement on 8 december in time to allow it to be adopted before the end of the year and thus to avoid the use of the provisional twelfths at the beginning of 2015. the negotiations were therefore very intense and the agreement reached is a very positive sign of the ability of our two institutions to find the necessary intensity in the interests of our citizens. i would like to express once again my satisfaction with the results achieved and i thank all the parties involved in the negotiations. i would like to thank in particular president arthuis and the three rapporteurs, mr gardiazabal, mr hohlmeier and mr deprez, who have been deeply involved in the negotiations, taking a constructive and cooperative approach when necessary. i would also like to thank vice-president georgieva and her team for their very impartial facilitation of the successful conclusion of the negotiations. i would like to conclude by expressing my conviction that the agreement reached with parliament is a perfectly coherent response to the three crucial challenges facing us next year: continue to reduce the backlog of unpaid invoices, not to undermine the efforts made by member states to consolidate national finances and to provide the necessary resources and incentives to promote economic growth and the creation of new jobs with benefits for all european citizens.

people around the world in desperate situations. on the 2015 budget, let me outline what we believe is particularly valuable in the agreement. first it is focused on investments in our core policy priorities. it underpins what we have to do to strengthen the competitiveness of europe and of course underpins the eur 350 billion investment plan that we have presented. secondly, vis-à-vis the 2014 budget, we have a modest step up but it is sufficient to help us adjust to the two pressure points i spoke about. for commitments the increase is 1.8% – eur 2.6 billion – and for payments the increase is 1.6%, which translates into eur 2.2 billion. that allows us eur 3.9 billion more for heading 1a and eur 581 million more for heading 4 where the pressures on europe are so strong. as the presidency mentioned, we managed to meet the needs of our farmers affected by the russian ban and by falling price levels in the milk and meat markets without tapping into the crisis reserve. we also have – and this is a very important point to recognise – a healthy development on the ratio between commitments and payments. for 2014 and 2015, as a result of what we have done, this ratio is 97% vis-à-vis an average of 89% in previous years, 2009 being 83% for example. what does that mean? that means that it will be easier to get on top of the issue of the ral that is going too far and too fast for our budget comfort. we are very pleased with the demand from parliament, which was accepted by the council, to have a payment plan, because this would lead us towards sustainability and i can inform you already that the latvian presidency – the forthcoming presidency – is taking this task very seriously. i met with the minister of finance and also with the minister of foreign affairs who will be the front minister for the presidency in the next six months. the payment plan is for us to bring to an end what we have been experiencing this year in terms of unpaid bills. our discussions in the coming months will also touch upon the issue of special instruments. in these negotiations we have agreed to disagree and leave the issue open. we placed eur 350 million in special instruments above the ceiling for 2014 but with an understanding that this is not the final call, so we have to engage in discussing it and hopefully bring it to a final call. we, as you all know, in this period of time had to deal with the issue of exceptionally a large gni adjustment, eur 9.5 billion in adjustments, that had come as a surprise to some of our member states. we have a very limited proposal for an amendment to address this issue and i want to inform you that eight member states are opting for deferred payments as provided by the amendment. given that, i hope parliament tomorrow will provide an opinion on it and it will be a positive opinion. let me conclude with three points. firstly, we have a budget and now we have to make the best use of the money we have. this for us in the commission is a top priority to focus on results, on the quality of spending. secondly, we, in the midst of negotiations, had a meeting of the high level group on own resources – i am very honoured to be one of the three commissioners now added to this group, which has very critical work which it has to continue to deliver on. and last but not least, we in the commission – you heard it in the new work programme – are very determined to drive towards this alignment of priorities and budget so we can show our citizens that the european union delivers where it matters the most to them.

in writing. the european union and ecuador have just concluded negotiations on the conclusion of an accession free trade agreement with peru and colombia, which is already in force. pending the entry into force of that agreement, the commission adopted on 1 october 2014 a proposal ensuring that the customs duties applied will not increase. the commission notes that the export price of the product concerned to ecuador was established on the basis of the price undercutting calculations. as a result, the trade balance for france is in deficit of eur 221 million for 2013. it therefore seems inconsistent to conclude trade liberalization agreements when the guarantees of opening the ecuadorian market are not met. the european union is not the only country to have a policy of unbridled globalisation. that is why i voted against this agreement on the tariff treatment of goods originating in ecuador.
in writing. during the trade negotiations for ecuador's accession to the trade agreement between the european union (eu) on the one hand and colombia and peru on the other, ecuador has made efforts which, in my opinion, merit these temporary provisions pending the approval procedure of the eu-ecuador trade agreement. these measures are designed to maintain the current levels of customs duties applied to products imported from ecuador. this transitional arrangement will enable the ecuadorian economy to be competitive with other latin american importers.

in writing. this resolution proposes that the european parliament oppose the publication of the delegated regulation adopted by the european commission to supplement regulation (ec) no 1071/2009 of the european parliament and of the council as regards the classification of serious infringements of union rules which may damage the reputation of road haulage operators. the mandate given to the european commission was to establish common rules on the conditions for the exercise of the occupation of road haulage operator. however, a close examination of the document reveals that its contents and form do not answer the question. the procedures in force in the 28 member states are still too diverse and the assessment of the level of seriousness and the enforcement of infringements are still subject to the national supervisory authorities or the competent authorities concerned. the act in question does not propose any harmonisation of existing rules, lacks clarity and does not bring any real european added value. furthermore, no mention is made of the problems of cabotage which must be examined. for these reasons i opposed the adoption of this delegated act and voted in favour of the resolution.

in writing. i wanted to defend road cabotage. the purpose of the regulation is to prevent unfair competition on the part of foreign road hauliers, in large numbers, between road hauliers, who would be favoured by lower cost prices (labour, fuel, vehicles) than those borne by our road hauliers. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the transport of dangerous goods by road. this vote is a clear warning to the european commission: cabotage is a sensitive subject with serious economic consequences. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a welcome step towards the creation of a european patent.
in writing. regulation (ec) no 1071/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 21 october 2009 lays down common rules on the conditions for the exercise of the occupation of road transport operator. the commission proposed the addition of the list to classify cases of serious breaches of eu rules which could damage the reputation of road hauliers. the commission proposal remains very vague in this classification. this makes it even more difficult for the authorities to interpret the types and levels of serious crime competently. it also failed to provide a complete list of serious offences. the report calls for us to reject the commission's proposal, so i am voting for it.
in writing. we are asked to give an opinion on the draft commission regulation on the classification of serious infringements of eu rules which may damage the reputation of road hauliers. regulation (ec) no 1071/2009 thus provides for the harmonisation of fair competition rules in order to reduce disparities between european countries which do not have the same rules in terms of working time, social charges on businesses or wages. the text also provides for stricter penalties in the case of illegal work. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. i voted against the commission's proposed act for two reasons. the first is technical: the act was draft and did not bring european added value. the second is political: it was a matter of telling the commission that road cabotage is an important subject and that we remain strongly involved in this subject in order to avoid social dumping between carriers.
in writing. i voted against this text. this list of infringements of eu rules for transport operators did not prohibit social dumping, in particular illegal cabotage, which is when a carrier operates in a neighbouring country without having the appropriate authorisations, and therefore without any guarantee that it complies with its social and environmental standards. for the socialists, social dumping and its corollary, unfair competition, are major societal problems in europe, which have only worsened with the crisis. i am very pleased with this vote: the european parliament has used the powers conferred by the lisbon treaty to the maximum to advance social progress. social dumping is not a subject that can be compromised with. it is in the general interest of our citizens.
in writing. i am pleased that a large majority of my colleagues have rejected this text from the european commission. road cabotage must be limited, and the european commission's position must be clear. we must protect french companies against social dumping. to do this, we must restrict the deliveries of a european carrier to a country which is not its own. it's the survival of our own carriers.
in writing. the list submitted to us by the commission is moving in the right direction. clarifying serious infringements in the field of road transport is to strengthen road safety and fair competition between companies. unfortunately, this list is far too restrictive from my point of view and that is why i did not support it. it does not sanction illegal cabotage, which can have a significant impact on road safety. today, some companies do not comply with the applicable national social legislation and employ drivers in inappropriate conditions which, in addition to damaging human dignity, can seriously affect attention and responsiveness at the wheel (e.g. the weekly rest in the cab). of course, this will have to be addressed through a wider reform but we must seize every opportunity to tackle the problem. without this, we will not be able to establish healthy competition between companies in the sector on the one hand, and between road transport and other more environmentally friendly modes on the other. i now invite the commission to come back as soon as possible with a new proposal.
in writing. i supported this resolution on serious breaches of eu rules which may damage the reputation of road hauliers. in voting this resolution, parliament rejected the delegated act proposed by the commission and which was being contested by the members of the french delegation to the epp. the text directly concerned road cabotage and had to be rejected for technical reasons: it did not add any value to the classification of the proposed offences and it also had worrying shortcomings in terms of the transport of dangerous goods. on the other hand, it was important for us to reiterate our vigilance as regards any possible reform of the road sector in the future. cabotage remains a sensitive and economically important subject, and special attention and action is needed to prevent social dumping.
in writing. i undertake to support any proposal to severely punish unfair competition. the fn mps had voted in 2009 in favour of the basic text from which the new regulation derives.
in writing. i voted against this text, which seeks to impose even stricter conditions on our industries, which are already heavily penalized in relation to competition from outside the community.
in writing. the european union is introducing environmental fuel specifications to reduce polluting emissions from cars. directive 98/70/ec aims to meet the commitment of directive 94/12/ec, which provided for the subsequent adoption of target values involving a substantial reduction in polluting emissions from motor vehicles. the motion for a resolution calls on us to oppose the adoption of the draft council directive, on the grounds that it does not set sufficiently strict requirements, particularly on emissions according to default averages of the intensity of greenhouse gas emissions during production itself (which is undeniably impossible to assess). the proposal therefore introduces additional standards for fuels which are far too restrictive and, in view of these explanations, i have spoken against it.
in writing. the european parliament has just voted by a very slim majority on directive 2014/0286, which will not penalise the import of oil from the oil sands by means of a european tax. as you know, the extraction of these deposits alone releases 23 percent more carbon than traditional hydrocarbons. in addition, oil sands mining techniques are very water intensive and have irreversible effects on soil destruction, particularly in canada's boreal forest. an increase in imports facilitated under the ceta agreement will result in an increase in production of this type of hydrocarbons. the adoption of this proposal for a directive shows in a very clear way that the european union is sacrificing all its social, health and environmental standards on the altar of free trade with canada and the united states. that is why i voted against the adoption of this text.
in writing. the directive on the quality of petrol and diesel fuels is the result of an acceptable compromise reached on the methods of calculating the intensity of greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions. the epp group therefore opposed the adoption of a resolution which would have required a further revision of the directive. in the run-up to the paris climate conference in 2015, this directive already shows the european union's efforts to reduce ghg emissions. for example, it requires suppliers to reduce ghg emission intensity over the entire life cycle for all fuels by 6% by 31 december 2020.
in writing. the european union has set itself the target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 20% by 2020. the transport sector is concerned with this perspective at the level of 6%. indeed, oil sands are one of the most polluting sources of energy supply, releasing 23% more carbon into the atmosphere than conventional fuels. by refusing to take into account the harmful effects of diesel, the commission is therefore contradicting european objectives and is draining the draft directive of its substance. with less than a year to go until the cop21 climate change conference in paris, this decline sends a bad signal to the international community. i hope very much that this is only a temporary delay and that we can continue our efforts to combat global warming in 2015.
in writing. the proposed resolution is built on an ideological vision of ecology by calling for the calculation of greenhouse gas emissions released during fuel production. i voted against this resolution, which would have been to tighten the directive and increase the burden on our industries and companies, particularly in the oil sector, a burden that is synonymous with loss of competitiveness and weak economic dynamism.
in writing. i voted against this motion for a resolution which seeks to reverse the compromise reached by the european commission. the authors of the resolution would like to be able to trace each fuel back to the crude oil from which it is derived, so as to give each fuel a rating in terms of its unit intensity of greenhouse gas emissions. this would be very expensive, especially for all the smes in the oil sector which are after the refining stage, and would be very difficult to implement. refined products are indeed subject to many mixtures and changes of ownership. the system proposed by the european commission to use a default average value representing the unit greenhouse gas emission intensity by fuel type is more balanced. it has the merit of not disadvantaging fuels produced in the union in favour of imported products, the traceability of which is more difficult to ensure. in conclusion, it is better to have the compromise text proposed by the commission, which is imperfect but satisfactory, than no text at all for the coming years. the compromise reached is the result of several years of negotiations.
in writing. i voted against this resolution on the proposal for a council directive laying down calculation methods and reporting requirements under the directive on the quality of petrol and diesel fuels. this resolution challenged the compromise reached by the european commission, which was to use a default average value representing the unit greenhouse gas emission intensity by fuel type.
in writing. the revised directive 98/70/ec requires fuel suppliers to report annually the life cycle greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions produced per unit of energy supplied in each member state. the proposal for a council directive aims to establish the methods of calculating these ghgs. the parliament's report strongly criticises the method used. it does not take into account recent changes in the infrastructure and the oil market, in particular the spread of fuels from non-conventional sources (tar sands, shale, liquefied coal, etc.). what is the point of setting targets for ghg reductions of 6% by 2020 if the methods of calculating emissions do not even allow the results to be measured? i vote for this report.
in writing. the european union is introducing environmental standards for fuels to reduce greenhouse gases. directive 98/70/ec aims to meet the commitment of directive 94/12/ec, which provided for the subsequent establishment of target values contributing to a substantial reduction of polluting emissions from motor vehicles. with this motion for a resolution we are asked to vote on five highly technical and mathematical calculation methods to meet increasingly stringent requirements, particularly on emissions, using default average values of the intensity of greenhouse gas emissions during production itself (which is undeniably impossible to assess). the proposal therefore introduces additional standards and clauses which are far too restrictive in respect of fuels and which ignore the general interest in favour of a spirit of shopaholicism; i voted against it.
in writing. the stated aim of this resolution is to ask the council to withdraw its proposal for a directive and to make a new proposal to parliament. the commission considers that the council proposal is contrary to the objectives of the revised directive 98/70/ec which requires 'fuel suppliers to declare annually the life cycle greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions per unit of energy supplied in each member state and to reduce by 6 per cent by 31 december 2020 the life cycle ghg emission intensity for all fuels supplied in relation to the average value in the union of life cycle ghg emissions per unit of energy attributable to fossil fuels in 2010'.
in writing. i voted against this text. i am well informed on the subject since my work on the biofuels directive in 2013, and i believe that the revision of the fuel quality directive threatens to strengthen the market shares of oil from tar sands, de facto encouraging more production. we have strongly opposed its adoption and we condemn the european parliament's vote in favour. in the current and future trade negotiations, we will not compromise on european environmental standards: the fight against climate change is everywhere and all the time! we deplore the fact that a conservative majority has supported the commission in its lack of political courage, when the consequences for the climate will be catastrophic if the european union does not take the necessary measures to reduce polluting emissions from transport.
in writing. the european parliament voted against a motion rejecting the council's draft method for calculating fuel quality. however, this proposal for a directive is the opposite of the direction the european union should take in the fight against climate change. on the contrary, this project is in the interests of the oil lobbies and will favour the dirtiest hydrocarbons, such as oil sands. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the transport of dangerous goods, which is a matter of principle for the member states. it is urgent that the european union finally work towards a real energy transition policy, which favours alternative fuels, which are more environmentally friendly, and clean modes of transport.
in writing. the resolution rejects a proposal for a directive and asks the committee to come forward with a more binding text which would have serious consequences for our industries and businesses.
in writing. the draft resolution calls on the council to make a new proposal for a directive on the calculation methods and reporting requirements under directive 98/70/ec on the quality of petrol and diesel fuels. this proposal goes against the european commitments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions as set out in this directive. the directive requires fuel suppliers to report their greenhouse gas emissions annually, with the aim of reducing them by 6% by 2020 compared to 2010. the directive is therefore a fundamental tool in the european fight against climate change. but with this proposal the commission is deliberately weakening it. by removing the possibility of distinguishing between the raw materials used for the fuels, it opens the door to the massive use of shale gas and oil sands, to the great happiness of the canadian lobby, whose influence we have seen in recent weeks. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution. but it was rejected, to my great regret, because the right-wing and far-right members, particularly the french, including the liberals, voted against it, paying attention to the industrial and economic lobbies.
in writing. the purpose of this motion for a resolution is to object to the commission's delegated regulation establishing a discard plan for the baltic sea, which aims in particular to reduce the conservation reference size for cod in the baltic sea, thus affecting the reproductive capacity of the stock. in addition, the regulation requires a reduction in the conservation reference size for cod from 38 cm to 35 cm. this regulation thus represents the technocratic vision of this european union which is incapable of understanding the real concerns of fishermen by imposing cumbersome and counterproductive standards. that is why i voted for this proposal.
in writing. the purpose of this motion for a resolution is to object to the commission's delegated regulation establishing a discard plan for the baltic sea. the plan includes a reduction in the conservation reference size (from 38 cm to 35 cm) for cod in the baltic sea, thus directly affecting the species' reproductive capacity. the result of the technocratic thinking of the european union, this regulation takes no account at all of the real concerns and needs of fishermen and is simply aimed at imposing ever more rigid and counterproductive standards on them. for these reasons, i voted against this proposal.
in writing. i voted against the resolution objecting to the delegated act establishing a discard plan for the baltic sea. in the light of scientific advice, the commission proposes a reduction in the minimum conservation reference size for cod in the baltic sea. this decline is justified and validated by scientific advice and does not pose a threat to the species. the resolution was therefore not justified. firstly, this baltic sea discharge plan has been accepted by all the member states concerned and is based on sound scientific advice. secondly, the objection would have delayed the implementation of the reform of the common fisheries policy. finally, the objection was also contrary to the regionalisation provided for in the reform of the common fisheries policy. the delegated act is to be adopted before the end of the year. it will provide operators and national authorities with visibility into the implementation of the landing obligation and the de minimis exemption provided for in the reform of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. the european parliament voted in the last parliamentary term for the reform of the common fisheries policy, including a ban on discards or landing obligations. the principle of compulsory landing is a fundamental change for fishermen; the commission has also proposed that the fishing opportunities for the stocks concerned be increased by a further 5% in the case of the fisheries sector. because i prefer this approach, i support the proposal for a delegated regulation and have therefore voted against the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ensuring the economic sustainability of the fisheries sector while preserving the sustainability of fisheries resources is a crucial challenge from both an environmental and an economic point of view. the council's decision to reduce the total allowable catches by 26% in the celtic sea and by 22% in the eastern baltic for the cod stock in 2015 are measures that can protect the species. it therefore seemed to me that adding to these measures a reduction in the minimum conservation reference size for cod in the baltic sea would pose a substantial risk to the socioeconomic balance of the fisheries sector. that is why i rejected this commission delegated regulation.
in writing. a commission delegated regulation of 20 october 2014 aims to amend the minimum conservation reference size for cod in the baltic sea. the resolution put to the vote opposes this amendment. the reduction in the size from which cod can be caught (from 38 to 35 cm) has the potential to harm the reproduction of the stock by creating a market for juvenile fish. i vote for the resolution which opposes this ecological nonsense.
