in writing. this motion for a resolution on the commission delegated regulation of 10 october 2014 supplementing directive 2009/138/ec of the european parliament and of the council on the taking-up and pursuit of the business of insurance and reinsurance (solvency ii) is contrary to that commission delegated act, which weakens the effectiveness of legislation. the commission is constantly revising downwards the risk weight and i have therefore voted in favour of this text which objects to the delegated act.
in writing. the commission is constantly revising downwards the risk weight, which of course weakens the effectiveness of legislation. since the resolution opposes this delegated act, i voted in favour.
in writing. directive 2009/138/ec ('solvency ii'), as amended in 2014, will enter into force on 1 january 2016 and will replace 14 existing directives. in line with the so-called 'bâle ii' requirements, its objective is to create a single european-level prudential regime for insurance and reinsurance undertakings in order to strengthen the risk-taking and to oblige insurers to set aside sufficient capital to meet these risks. the proposal, which was put forward by vice-president michel barnier in the last parliament, aims to make our financial system more robust and capable of coping with crises, thus better protecting our citizens from the vagaries of finance. i believe that the implementation of this legislation is of paramount importance and i am voting against this resolution, which, if adopted, would call into question the very heart of this new european body of prudential rules for insurance and reinsurance undertakings in the union.
in writing. the solvency ii directive, which was voted on in november 2009, is due to enter into force on 1 january 2016. applicable to the insurance sector, the directive aims to encourage organizations to better understand and assess their risks, in particular by adapting regulatory requirements to the risks that companies incur in their activities. the commission's delegated regulation which this motion for a resolution seeks to reject will allow the timetable to be followed and will be in line with the framework of the basic legislative act. that's why i didn't want to be associated with it.
in writing. the solvency ii directive regulates the insurance sector in terms of capital and risk-taking. in this context, the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts. on 10 october 2014, the commission adopted a delegated regulation which deviates significantly from the submitted technical opinions. in particular, it provides for a much lower calibration of the risk factors used to calculate the solvency capital requirement (csr) compared to the recommendations. this shows once again that the commission is at the service of the financial markets rather than the citizens. the resolution before us is opposed to this delegated act which underestimates the risks. i vote for it.
in writing. as regards the solvency of banking institutions, the rules established at european level fall short of the requirements of the bale iii agreements, in particular because of the poor account taken of the risk of default of a sovereign state or a public body. once again, in the context of the texts implementing the solvency ii directive, which concern insurance companies, the commission is weakening the effectiveness of legislation and risk prevention. parliament must ensure that delegated acts do not call into question the principles adopted at level 1 and must also do everything possible to avoid a miscalculation of risks and a solvency crisis in the insurance sector. in the present case, the technical committees called upon to deliver an opinion state that the draft delegated act presented here represents a retreat from both of those points of view. the rejection of the commission delegated regulation should therefore be supported.
in writing. the commission is constantly revising downwards the risk weight, which of course weakens the effectiveness of legislation. since this resolution is against this delegated act, i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which objects to the commission's delegated regulation on 'solvency ii' because it considers that the commission has deviated significantly from the technical advice presented and therefore provides for a far too low calibration of the risk factors used in the standard formula for calculating the solvency capital requirement compared to the ecscr/esacr recommendations.
in writing. solvency ii is a european reform whose official objective is "to better adapt the capital requirements of insurance and reinsurance companies to the risks they incur in their business". the main aim of the proposal, which is intended to provide better protection for insured persons, is to create a single insurance market in the eu and to improve the control of pan-european insurers (55 articles of the directive are devoted to groups). it is in fact penalizing small and mediumsized structures, and particularly mutual societies, by once again denying their specific features. i was already opposed to the adoption of such a directive last march and with its new proposal the commission wants to bring it into force by means of a delegated act, which gives it all the power and removes all control from parliament. i do not think that this is acceptable in substance or form. that is why i voted for this resolution which refused to give the commission any powers and i therefore regret that it was rejected by a large majority of the ppe, s&d, alde and ecr groups.
in writing. the will to renew the eu's internal security strategy will unfortunately not pass through these proposed measures, which are far too weak and far from reality in the face of the security problems facing the member states. the fight against terrorism and jihadism will not be fought by measures of tolerance or social cohesion but by a voluntarist policy that dares to re-establish controls at the eu's borders and abolish the schengen agreements. it is now more than urgent to put an end to this policy of good feelings which endangers the security of the citizens of the union. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. i voted against this motion for a resolution on the renewal of the internal security strategy of the european union because the measures envisaged here are ridiculously weak in the face of the serious problems facing the member states. to believe that a policy of 'promoting political and religious tolerance, strengthening social cohesion and openness to all and simplifying reintegration opportunities' will be effective in combating the rise of jihadism is the most culpable naivete because it endangers the peoples of the member states. only the re-establishment of national borders and serious controls will prevent the free movement of established and would-be criminals. it is clear that the eu is incapable of managing its borders, which are like sieves. we must therefore break with the schengen agreements and re-establish our national borders as a matter of urgency.
in writing. the eu's internal security strategy comes to an end this year. it is therefore essential to put in place a new strategy for the next four years that is better adapted to the current security challenges. the problem of european citizens going to conflict zones to fight alongside terrorists must be dealt with as a matter of priority. in this resolution, parliament sets out to the commission the various lines of a coherent internal security policy. i voted in favour of this resolution. the european union was built to provide greater security for european citizens, and this principle must be guaranteed.
in writing. with this very large majority vote, the european commission has been given more than a signal, it is a real order to adapt its internal security strategy to the new challenges facing europeans. the eu must take a strong initiative to respond to the challenge of european jihadists who have joined the ranks of daesh in iraq or syria and who are likely to return to european territory. we need a comprehensive internal security strategy, adapted to the priorities we have set for it, with effective legislative instruments and adequate financial resources.
in writing. the new threats facing europe today are much more diffuse and difficult to understand. i am thinking in particular of the issue of foreign fighters and their radicalisation, of international criminal networks responsible for various forms of trafficking and of cyberattacks. these are threats that ignore national borders and now rely on new technologies to better evade police and judicial controls. to ensure the safety of our citizens, the union must modernise its security strategy and focus on the underlying causes of violence, which are often intolerance and radicalisation, but also the sources of funding for criminal activities. this new strategy must be based on the pooling of member states' resources and must also go hand in hand with the development of a genuine common foreign and defence policy. in this context, parliament will have to ensure that this new security strategy is fully in line with the european charter of fundamental rights.
in writing. the new internal security strategy (iss) will be formally adopted by the council; it is therefore crucial that the european parliament affirms its priorities and reservations in terms of internal security, in advance of the presentation of the new ssi. the development of a union internal security strategy is an ambitious agenda and should provide the necessary foundations for a more multidisciplinary, coherent and long-term approach in this area. in this new year, however, the commission must undertake a more critical evaluation of previous actions and a more forward-looking analysis in the light of new emerging threats. another challenge for the commission is to shape the new ssi by effectively integrating fundamental rights safeguards into all developed policies.
in writing. with the number of jihadist candidates exploding, increasing by 116% since the beginning of the year, it is imperative that europeans jointly review their internal security strategy to integrate these new forms of threats. the european parliament is already taking a position on the forthcoming european commission proposal on the strategy for 2015-2019. however, parliament is not free from confusion and ambiguity. i would remind you that a few weeks ago the liberals, supported by the socialists and the national front, adopted a resolution delaying the entry into force of the pnr with canada, which is an indispensable partner in the fight against terrorism and crossborder crime. the pnr is an agreement that allows for the transmission of transient data to better detect suspicious behaviour. it is not big brother as we like to think in the collective imagination but a way for the empowered authorities to better protect citizens from possible attacks and attacks. the decision to delay this agreement, which has been negotiated for several years, is reckless and certainly does not meet the demand of citizens to feel safe in their homes.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the renewal of the eu's internal security strategy. the current strategy is coming to an end, and the text considers that new threats have emerged and must be taken into account in the renewal of the strategy. priority areas such as cybercrime, trafficking in human beings, the fight against terrorism or the issue of eu-national 'foreign fighters' should be at the heart of the new internal security strategy. i welcome the broad adoption of this resolution.
in writing. i supported the resolution on the renewal of the european union's internal security strategy. the resolution also calls on the commission to take action to ensure that the eu's internal security strategy is more closely aligned with the eu's external security policy. in order to meet these new challenges, increased operational cooperation between member states and the provision of appropriate financial resources will be necessary.

in writing. the first eu internal security strategy adopted in 2011 is coming to an end. in anticipation of a future proposal from the european commission, the european parliament (ep) took the initiative to propose its guidelines. the resolution adopted by the majority of the ep is again marked by a largely repressive approach, focusing mainly on the fight against terrorism without taking into account the many violations of fundamental rights which it has given rise to, as the us senate report on the use of torture by the cia after the attacks of 11 september 2001 has just shown. i regret the rejection of the amendments i tabled on behalf of the gue/ngl, calling in particular for the adoption of preventive measures, a multidimensional approach to security that includes the fight against inequalities and discrimination and an independent and contradictory evaluation of the current strategy. i therefore voted against this resolution, which does not take stock of the current policies which are increasingly undermining fundamental rights without demonstrating their effectiveness.

in writing. following operation mare nostrum and now operation triton, the european union is opening a route for migration from africa through the mediterranean. thousands of migrants risk their lives on makeshift boats and these rescue operations only encourage them to take the first step towards the 'european eldorado'. it is through these operations that nearly 150 000 illegal immigrants arrive in europe each year, thus entering the schengen area and moving about freely. on operation triton, the british foreign secretary, joyce anelay, very clearly announced that britain would not support the operation, stating: "we believe that (these operations) create an unintended 'attraction factor', encouraging more migrants to attempt the dangerous sea crossing and thus leading to more tragic and unnecessary deaths". it is becoming more than urgent to be as firm on immigration as australia is, to re-establish our borders, to fight criminal networks and to allow each state to decide its own sovereign migration policy. that is why i voted against this text.

in writing. if there is one big issue that requires a common european response, it is the issue of migration. it is really time for the heads of state and government to move forward to build a common immigration policy which must be based on four pillars. the first is a real security and a real surveillance and protection of our external borders, by air, by land, by sea, with, amongst others, european coast guards. the second point is the corollary of this: we must have a regulated right of entry into the european union with, why not, country quotas in immigration. the third point is perhaps the most urgent: we need to harmonize our right to asylum. we cannot continue with six-month to five-year deadlines for an answer depending on the country. this is not reasonable. fourthly, we obviously need a development policy, a real partnership with the countries of origin and a foreign policy which contributes to the stability of the countries around us.
in writing. on wednesday morning i voted in favour of a european parliament resolution on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for a comprehensive approach to migration by the european union. according to the international organisation for migration, 3 072 people died in the mediterranean in the first nine months of 2014, which once again illustrates the imperative for each member state to carry out its search and rescue operations in accordance with our moral and international obligations. however, i would like to stress that the european union must also strengthen its border controls in order to avoid, in particular, the air calls which most often lead to dramatic situations.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for a comprehensive approach to the issue of migration by the union. while the european commission and the council have presented a series of actions to be taken, notably in the context of the mediterranean task force, it is essential that parliament in turn adopt a more proactive strategy, not merely reacting to the various commission communications or even to the council conclusions, but affirming its role as a force of proposals in the migration debate. on the basis of the findings and recommendations of this inquiry, parliament should propose an alternative migration policy for europe that addresses these issues in a comprehensive and cross-cutting approach that includes: legal migration pathways, whether existing or to be promoted; effective access to asylum procedures and the development of alternatives for persons seeking international protection; and a renewed partnership with third countries on the basis of equal cooperation and mutually beneficial interaction. in any case, it is the impetus and the reorientation that we socialists intend to defend in the european parliament.
in writing. meps adopted a resolution on the situation in the mediterranean on wednesday, calling for a comprehensive approach to migration. this resolution is a good initiative, but i regret that no significant progress has been made since the adoption of the european pact on immigration and asylum, which i was the architect of in 2008. what major initiatives have been undertaken since the pact, which brought together governments of the right, the left and the communist parties? i welcome the adoption of this resolution which recalls the urgent need to develop a comprehensive approach to better manage migration flows. however, this appeal from the european parliament also shows that europe is now more reactive than active. the resolution proposes a fair sharing of responsibility and greater solidarity with the member states receiving the largest number of refugees and asylum seekers, financial and operational reinforcement of frontex, a comprehensive strategy for cooperation with third countries, in particular on resettlement and return, and the criminalization of human trafficking and illegal immigration.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in the mediterranean. the text calls for a fair sharing of responsibility, greater solidarity with member states receiving the largest number of refugees and asylum seekers and strong criminal sanctions against trafficking in human beings and illegal immigration. the resolution was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. faced with the repetition of human tragedies linked to illegal immigration in the mediterranean, the european response has been long overdue. i therefore welcome the vote on this resolution which insists on a fair sharing of responsibility and greater solidarity with the member states which receive the largest number of refugees and asylum seekers. it was also important to advocate the financial and operational strengthening of frontex and the european asylum support office (easo) and to call for strong criminal sanctions against the channels of human trafficking and illegal immigration. in addition, the eu must commit to a comprehensive strategy of cooperation with third countries in aid, co-development and enforcement to discourage illegal immigration.
in writing. this resolution was the result of a long battle against the right. it was not to replicate the position adopted during the tragic events in lampedusa, which was centred on an exclusively police vision of migration. this time, increased funding for the committee responsible for migration policies was obtained. it is proposed to "explore other legal immigration routes", to ensure the reintegration of migrants and to improve the means of rescue at sea. however, this is not required by the international obligations to which the member states have acceded. the resolution seeks to recall that migrants are victims of human traffickers and smugglers. but it fails to point out that they are also victims of the eu's aggressive trade policies. i abstain in order not to prevent a text which has the merit of allocating a research mandate and funds to the committee of parliament to look at another migration policy. it's a start.
in writing. the migratory pressure at europe's borders has been increasing unprecedentedly since the beginning of the year. the lucrative smuggling networks exploit human misery, as do some unscrupulous employers. the european approach is intended to be balanced in its content, between condemnation of these networks and the need to develop return assistance. nevertheless, it demonstrated in practice that the mass arrival of illegal immigrants was perceived as inevitable. the union is imposing on the member states a burden that economies already on the verge of social asphyxiation can no longer bear. in addition, the influx of illegal immigrants destabilizes political asylum procedures, which are hijacked for economic reasons. in the end, it is necessary above all to unite the forces of the member states to fight with means that are incomparable to what the mafias are today and to show signs of firmness to those who are seeking exile. the solution also lies in development aid and the cessation of support for corrupt regimes, rather than in naive and passive reception policies. faced with the demographic pressure of the african continent, europe in recession cannot continue to take in more economic refugees.
in writing. the european union's attitude to the situation of illegal immigration in the mediterranean is completely unacceptable. with operations like mare nostrum and now triton, which aim to retrieve migrants in the middle of the mediterranean and bring them directly to european soil, the european union has created an air of appeal to those seeking illegal immigration. it has also sent a signal of encouragement to unscrupulous smugglers, who are not afraid to deliberately put in the sea vessels in bad condition so that migrants can be rescued. as australia has recently strengthened its migration policy, solutions must be national and firmly enforced. i voted against this resolution, of course.
in writing. in the context of the critical situation of migration in the mediterranean, this resolution focuses on the establishment of a committee of inquiry and calls for greater solidarity and responsibility on the part of the eu member states. the eu's capacity for rescue at sea needs to be improved urgently to prevent the mediterranean from continuing to be a huge graveyard for refugees. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the tragedies taking place in the mediterranean need to be given greater attention by the european union, which must strengthen the coordinated action of its member states. i therefore welcome this resolution, which also calls for an increase in the financial resources of frontex and for the union's cooperation with third countries on this issue.
in writing. on the eve of international migrants day, the european parliament adopted a resolution on the situation in the mediterranean which defends the need for a comprehensive european approach to migration. according to the united nations high commissioner for refugees, the mediterranean has become the world's deadliest route for migrants. this sad fact calls for an urgent and coordinated response by the european union and its member states. meps call for a coherent and supportive migration policy, a more humane and protective policy towards migrants and asylum seekers. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem, and i am sure that the commission will take them into account. the european states must become more aware of this by making greater financial commitments to search and rescue at sea and to the reception of migrants. ensuring safe routes for refugees and asylum seekers to europe and opening new legal channels of migration will also improve the situation in the long term. faced with the challenge of migration, europe must finally do everything it can to succeed.
in writing. i supported this resolution which is a first step towards a comprehensive approach by the european union to the situation in the mediterranean and the issue of migration. this comprehensive approach to migration will allow for a fair sharing of responsibility and greater solidarity with member states receiving the largest number of refugees and asylum seekers. the commission is also proposing to set up a comprehensive strategy for cooperation with third countries and to strengthen the financing and operation of the frontex agency and the european asylum support office. i welcome the adoption of this resolution; the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances.
in writing. more and more migrants are dying in the mediterranean. this year has been one of the most disastrous in this respect: more than 3 200 people have died on the way to europe. it is therefore welcome that several political groups in the european parliament have mobilised to try to call for a committee of inquiry to take stock of the situation and propose a number of responses to this tragedy. unfortunately, the right wing of this house has been engaged in indecent blackmail to limit the scope of this resolution, trying to limit it to the same old slogans: more cooperation with third countries, more return and readmission, strengthening the mandate of frontex (and therefore more and more closure of borders). this resolution is therefore not as ambitious as we had requested, but it will allow the european parliament to continue its reflection on these issues, in particular by giving more resources to its committee on civil liberties. we therefore abstained in order to denounce this overly restrictive approach, but also to demonstrate our willingness to continue to work and to fight against these deadly policies.

in writing. the purpose of this motion for a resolution is to object to the granting of gsp+ tariff preferences to the philippines. the union's generalised system of preferences (gsp) offers tariff reductions or duty-free access to the union market for exports from 178 developing countries and territories. for example, for competing imports of canned tuna, the granting of gsp+ tariff preferences to the philippines would reduce the customs duties to 0% from the current 24%. this will lead to increased unfair competition at the expense of european fishermen who are already hit hard by the commission's flimsy regulations, even though the country has not yet demonstrated that it complies with all the conventions required to benefit from gsp+. in addition, the philippines is under an investigative measure concerning illegal, unreported and unregistered (iuu) fishing. that is why i voted for this text.
in writing. the purpose of this motion for a resolution is to object to the granting of gsp+ tariff preferences to the philippines. the union's generalised system of preferences (gsp) allows tariff reductions or duty-free access to the community market for exports from 178 developing countries and territories. thus, for competing imports of canned tuna, the granting of gsp+ tariff preferences to the philippines would reduce the customs duties to 0% from the current 24%. such a measure could actually increase the unfair competition that european fishermen are already suffering from. european fishermen already subject to abusive and very restrictive regulations. in addition, the philippines has not yet provided guarantees regarding compliance with the conventions required to benefit from gsp+. finally, the country must respond to an investigative measure concerning illegal, unreported and unregistered fishing (iuu fishing). in view of these various factors, i voted in favour of this text.

in writing. regulation (eu) no 978/2012 on the generalised scheme of preferences (gsp+) empowers the commission to adopt delegated acts to establish or amend the list of gsp+ beneficiary countries. on 19 august 2014, the commission adopted a delegated regulation applying a scheme of generalised tariff preferences to the philippines, which consists of exempting certain imports from that country from customs duties. the philippines is a "non-cooperative" actor in the fight against illegal fishing. furthermore, the united nations report on human trafficking notes that "trafficking in human beings, especially women and children, for the purpose of exploitation as labour is proliferating in various sectors, including agriculture, construction, fishing, manufacturing and services". it would therefore be illogical to grant the philippines a scheme of generalised tariff preferences, as they do not meet the conditions for access to gsp+. i am voting for this resolution which is against the commission's delegated regulation.

in writing. the srb (single resolution board) is the cornerstone of the single resolution mechanism (srm), which will soon be responsible for implementing the dismantling of 'banks in distress' through a series of instruments, including a single bank-supported resolution fund and an arsenal of rules on the hierarchy of creditors in the event of bankruptcy. the srm will apply to banks covered by the ssm, which makes the european central bank (ecb) the central supervisor of banking institutions in the euro area (approximately 6 000 banks). the mru will react in cases where a bank fails despite enhanced supervision. it will be based on a six-member board. conscious of the need to prevent bank failures, i remain, however, firmly committed to national sovereignty; that's why i voted against it.
in writing. under the single resolution mechanism, the national competent authorities are required to levy contributions to financial crisis resolution mechanisms. those contributions shall be adapted to the risk profile of institutions and undertakings in accordance with the criteria to be specified in a delegated act of the commission. however, in the delegated act adopted by the commission, the contributions do not adequately reflect the level of risk of the banks. the 'healthy' banks must therefore contribute as much as the most speculative financial institutions. i am voting against the recommendation approving this delegated act.
in writing. the srb (single resolution board) is the cornerstone of the single resolution mechanism (srm), which will soon be responsible for implementing the dismantling of 'banks in distress' through a series of instruments, including a single bank-supported resolution fund and an arsenal of rules on the hierarchy of creditors in the event of bankruptcy. the srm will apply to banks covered by the ssm, which makes the european central bank (ecb) the central supervisor of banking institutions in the euro area (approximately 6 000 banks). the mru will react in cases where a bank fails despite enhanced supervision. it will be based on a six-member board. i am aware of the need to prevent bank failures, but i remain firmly committed to national sovereignty; that's why i voted against it.
in writing. this proposal for a non-legislative resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the association agreement between the european union and the european atomic energy community and their member states, of the one part, and georgia, of the other part, is intended to eventually allow georgia to accede to the european union. that's the hidden side of this agreement! on the principle of 'more funds, more reforms', the union intends on the one hand to squander european taxpayers' money in georgia when we are in great need of it and, on the other hand, to impose on georgia its ultra-liberal vision, which has still not been proven. this agreement is a new attack on russia, with which our relations are more than strained: demands for respect for georgia's territorial integrity, insistence that russia reverse its decision to recognise the secession of the georgian regions of abkhazia and tskhinvali in south ossetia, and for russia to end its occupation. for these reasons, among others, i voted against the conclusion of this association agreement.
in writing. the rapporteur 'commends georgia for having contained the pressure from other countries, notably russia'. is this really useful and timely given the geopolitical situation in the region and the current tensions between the european union and the russian federation? that is highly doubtful. as regards the economic consequences, lessons should be drawn from past experiences of the convergence of structurally very different economies. look at our german neighbors. the report promises georgia "a european perspective and [the possibility of] applying to become a member of the union". that's not reasonable. i therefore voted against this text, which, on the one hand, can have disastrous economic consequences for the member states and, on the other hand, is particularly delicate in the geopolitical context.
in writing. i voted against all the proposed amendments. the conclusion of the association agreement with georgia is just another maneuver by the european union to isolate russia. this association agreement is part of a very worrying leap forward by the european union, which has no major interests.
in writing. i voted against this eu-georgia association agreement which is nothing but a hasty attempt to encircle russia by vassalling its strategic partners. the european union is once again showing its willingness to trample on the sovereignty of nations, despite the accumulation of good intentions: the motion for a resolution thus calls for the compulsory 'conformity' of georgian legislation. what is worse, the european parliamentarians are advocating a 'consensual european choice', in other words, they are calling for a real negation of the democratic principle! this interference is all the more scandalous because it is also harmful to the citizens of the member states: it calls for intensive liberalization of both markets and visas. for example, according to a recent report in the economic journal, immigration has cost a country like the uk £150 billion in 17 years, despite being one of the countries that is best able to contain the effects of the economic crisis thanks to its monetary sovereignty. the eu-ukraine association agreement therefore shows once again that the decisions taken by the european institutions are dictated by ideology and not common sense.
in writing. the eu-georgia association agreement was committed during the eastern partnership summit in vilnius on 29 november 2013 and signed on 27 june 2014. the georgian parliament ratified it on 18 july, allowing the agreement to enter into force provisionally on 1 september 2014. the agreement aims to significantly deepen georgia's political association and gradual economic integration into the eu's internal market. the association agreement also provides for numerous opportunities for sectoral cooperation and focuses on support for key reforms, economic recovery and growth, governance and sectoral cooperation in 28 areas, including agriculture and rural development. given the current geopolitical context in eastern europe and the caucasus, this association agreement sets out a european path for georgia. that is why i am voting for the conclusion of this agreement.
in writing. the union must develop stronger partnerships with its neighbours. the association agreement will strengthen political ties with tbilisi, while georgia has carried out a key reform of its judicial system to improve its governance. the agreement will enable europeans and georgians to continue cooperation and dialogue on the reforms still to be carried out to consolidate democracy and the rule of law. this enhanced cooperation in the political field will go hand in hand with the establishment of a free trade area between the union and georgia, which will promote trade links between the two groups. this agreement must eventually make it possible to modernize and stabilize the country so that it can freely chart its future. in this connection, it should be remembered that the agreement covers the entire territory of georgia and that in the future a lasting diplomatic solution will have to be found to the situations in abkhazia and south ossetia.
in writing. i welcome the conclusion of this association agreement, which is a significant step forward in relations between the european union and georgia. the agreement is supported by 69% of the georgian population, which shows the attachment of this people to cooperation with the european union. i also welcome the fact that the european parliament, through this resolution, reaffirms its support for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of georgia. it is also important to encourage the georgian authorities to continue their efforts in the area of democratic reforms, including the reform of the judiciary, and to work towards national reconciliation.
in writing. described as "one of the most ambitious free trade agreements the european union has ever negotiated with a third country", the agreement is also presented as a prelude to georgia's accession to the european union. i am opposed to any further enlargement under the present conditions, as i do not want to subject other peoples to the austerity of the peoples of europe. moreover, this is a new act of preparation for hostilities with russia, even though the report states that "the association process poses no danger to russia's political and economic interests". the fact that it is referred to is enough to illuminate the empty lens in reality. i hate that hypocrisy. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted against all the proposed amendments. the conclusion of the association agreement with georgia is just another maneuver by the european union to isolate russia. after the promises of accession made to ukraine, will the union do the same with georgia?
in writing. i opposed this report, which plays the georgian provocation against the russian neighbour, a situation which is very similar to the proliferation of european association agreements with moldova or ukraine. in view of the geopolitical tensions in the caucasus region, i cannot endorse this report on the conclusion of the association agreement with georgia.
in writing. i vote in favour of such a resolution, as it commends georgia and encourages it to continue its efforts against corruption and poverty. this country has made great progress despite past military events. i also support this resolution because it recalls georgia's strategic interest in the european union and its ever closer and more fruitful cooperation with the west.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, which supports the ratification of the eu-georgia association agreement, which includes a comprehensive and in-depth free trade agreement. this agreement was made possible by the political and economic reforms undertaken by georgia, but it is not an end in itself. the eu and georgia have a long-standing relationship, and the eu is committed to the development of relations with georgia.
in writing. i voted against this association agreement, which is above all a part of the strategy of encircling russia by enslaving its historical and strategic partners. i am shocked that the former georgian president was forced to be present at the voting: mr saakashvili, who led his people into open war with russia, is now living in exile in the united states, apparently to escape prosecution by the judicial authorities in his country.
in writing. the recommendation on the eu-georgia association agreement should allow for the creation of a large free trade area (another after those recently voted for with ukraine and moldova) to the benefit mainly of georgia, whose gdp growth, according to meps, is expected to be 4.3% as a result of the agreement. from a european perspective, there are no figures on the concrete contribution of this agreement to the european economy. moreover, it will only increase tensions between the union and russia, and i therefore voted against it.

in writing. with these association agreements, the european union is pursuing its diplomatic missions which, in the current context of geopolitical tensions, are more akin to alignment with us positions than to the search for prospects for peaceful international relations in the caucasus region. i reject the idea of france and the european union being used as a vehicle for us ambitions in georgia and i voted against this text.

in writing. this eastern partnership agreement is only aimed at weakening russia. for the last ten years, georgia has been the neoliberal laboratory of the united states and the soviet union on the borders of russia. the agreement aims to create a "deep and comprehensive free trade area" with the european union, which should bring happiness to the people. when one sees the results of the policies pursued in europe, one may wonder why the georgian authorities are so eager to see the same suffering inflicted on their own people. i am voting against it out of sympathy for the georgian people.
in writing. the european union is at a loss as to what to invent to try to isolate russia. the association agreement with georgia is part of the arsenal of anti-russian measures developed by the union. it should be noted that the european union has also already concluded free trade agreements, notably with moldova, and has indicated a future accession to ukraine. i voted against this association agreement with georgia.

in writing. strengthening relations with georgia is of great interest to both the european union and georgia. it is a strategic country, with 30% of its imports coming from europe. i therefore vote in favour of such a recommendation. closer relations should allow for increased trade and confidence in the union's eastern partners, along with the establishment of common commercial and democratic standards.
in writing. i supported this recommendation of the european parliament, which represents the ratification of the association agreement between the european union and georgia. following the signing of the association agreement between the european union and georgia on 27 june and the ratification of the agreement by the georgian parliament on 18 july, the european parliament was required to approve the agreement. i welcome that approval. the association agreement will strengthen economic and political relations between the european union and georgia and also contains a trade component which will provide free access to the markets of both parties in the long term. it will be important to remain vigilant and to ensure that the agreement is fully implemented and respected.
